Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and the Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program.
Title: Higher Education - Student Financial Assistance - Dependents of State or Local Public Safety Employees (Maryland Fallen Heroes Tuition Benefits Act)

bill_summary: The bill exempts spouses and financially dependent children of Maryland public safety employees who died in the line of duty from paying out-of-state or out-of-county tuition at public institutions of higher education. It also restructures the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and the Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program by shifting from an entitlement-based system to a budget-capped system. The Maryland Higher Education Commission is required to develop a formula for allocating scholarship funds, and renewal applicants are given priority over new applicants.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Spouses and financially dependent children of deceased Maryland public safety employees, current and future scholarship recipients under the Conroy and Cryor programs, and Maryland public postsecondary institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to cause a significant decrease in State general fund expenditures by eliminating the entitlement aspect of the Conroy and Cryor scholarship programs and capping total awards to the amount provided in the State budget. For context, while FY 2025 scholarship expenditures were approximately 9500000, the FY 2027 budget is set at 7000000, and the statutory minimum mandate is 4000000. Consequently, higher education revenues and expenditures at public colleges and community colleges will decrease as fewer or smaller awards are distributed. The tuition exemption for nonresident dependents of fallen public safety employees is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact due to the small number of eligible individuals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget, which includes the mandated minimum appropriation for the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund and influences funding for the tuition exemptions.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund and receive deposits for the program.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and state higher education institutions regarding the implementation of new tuition exemptions and regulatory changes.
DBM is responsible for the state budget and fiscal planning; the bill changes scholarship funding from an entitlement to a budget-capped program and mandates specific minimum budget appropriations.

The bill and related scholarship programs provide financial assistance to disabled public safety employees and their dependents, aligning with the department's focus on service delivery to residents with disabilities.
The Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program specifically provides financial assistance to the dependents of school employees killed or disabled in the line of duty.
The definition of 'State or local public safety employee' includes law enforcement officers, such as the Natural Resources Police, whose dependents are eligible for the benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's benefits apply to correctional officers and law enforcement officers, who are primarily employed or overseen by DPSCS.
The bill affects law enforcement officers within MDOT's modal administrations (e.g., MDTA Police) whose dependents are eligible for the tuition exemptions and scholarships.
The Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program provides significant benefits to veterans and the survivors of military service members.
The bill specifically includes members of the Maryland National Guard in the definition of public safety employees eligible for scholarship and tuition benefits for their survivors.
MHEC is the primary agency responsible for administering the scholarship programs, developing the new allocation formula, and adopting implementing regulations.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, its employees are key subjects of the bill, and their survivors are eligible for the Maryland Fallen Heroes Tuition Benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and tracks law enforcement officer fatalities, which determines eligibility for the benefits established in this bill.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state fiscal integrity, including the management of funds and contracts related to state higher education property and capital projects mentioned in the fiscal context.
MCSS, an independent unit within MSDE, is relevant as the bill addresses financial assistance for school employees who are victims of acts of violence in the line of duty.
Members of the Maryland National Guard are explicitly defined as public safety employees whose dependents may receive scholarship and tuition benefits under the bill.
As a public institution of higher education, MSU must implement the tuition exemptions and manage the distribution of scholarship funds to eligible students.
OLA conducts audits of state agencies and would be responsible for auditing MHEC's management of the scholarship fund and the new allocation formula.
As a public institution of higher education, SMCM must implement the out-of-state tuition exemptions and administer scholarship awards provided by the bill.
USM institutions are directly impacted by the tuition exemption requirements, and the scholarship award cap is benchmarked against USM resident undergraduate tuition rates.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to collect student-level data regarding the parental status of students from public institutions of higher education, excluding the University of Maryland Global Campus. It mandates that public institutions, including community colleges, adopt and post plans to support pregnant and parenting students by providing referrals to resources like childcare, healthcare providers, and government assistance programs. The bill also expands the definition of 'student data' to allow MHEC to share parental status information with the Maryland Longitudinal Data System.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC)
stakeholders: Pregnant and parenting students, public senior higher education institutions, and Maryland community colleges.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $51,900 in FY 2027 for MHEC to hire a part-time staff specialist to manage data collection and reporting. Public four-year institutions and community colleges are expected to experience minimal cost increases to collect data and develop required support plans. There is a potential significant increase in general and federal fund expenditures for state assistance programs like Medicaid if institutional referrals lead to increased enrollment in those programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the primary regulatory body tasked by the bill to develop data collection questions, collect student-level parental status data from institutions, adopt implementing regulations, and submit annual summary reports to the General Assembly.

As the state's central coordinating board for postsecondary education, this agency is responsible for the bill's core mandates, including establishing a common format for reporting parental status data and ensuring public institutions comply with the new reporting and planning requirements.

The bill specifically alters the statutory definition of 'student data' to include parental status, authorizing this agency to collect and analyze this new data point from the Higher Education Commission to inform state policy.

The bill requires USM's public senior higher education institutions (with specific exceptions like UMGC) to collect demographic data on parental status and adopt comprehensive support plans for pregnant and parenting students.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is required to modify its demographic data collection forms and develop and post a plan to support pregnant and parenting students consistent with Title IX.
As an independent public honors college, the agency is mandated by the bill to collect and report parental status data and implement support plans for its pregnant and parenting student population.

The bill requires higher education institutions to provide referrals to health-related government programs administered by this agency, including Medicaid, MCHP, and WIC, which may lead to increased participation and administrative expenditures.

The fiscal note indicates a need for increased general fund expenditures for a new personnel position at the Maryland Higher Education Commission to implement the bill's data collection and reporting requirements.

Institutions must refer students to the Child Care Scholarship Program, which is managed by this department; additionally, the department coordinates with community colleges that are now required to adopt support plans under the bill.

This agency administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), which is explicitly listed as a government assistance program to which institutions must provide referrals for parenting students.
The bill reinforces the rights of students to be free from pregnancy-based discrimination, a protection enforced by the Commission under state anti-discrimination laws.

The bill's focus on supporting parenting students and ensuring they have access to benefits like SNAP and child care directly aligns with this office's mission to reduce child poverty and support underinvested communities.

This agency determines eligibility for Medicaid and MCHP, programs specifically identified in the bill as resources that institutions must include in their required support plans for parenting students.

The bill's data-driven approach to supporting parenting students and enhancing their economic mobility mirrors this team's mission to pilot novel initiatives that reduce poverty and improve outcomes for Maryland families.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists to issue a limited license to practice music therapy. The limited license allows an individual to practice music therapy under the supervision of a fully licensed music therapist while they complete the necessary requirements for full licensure, specifically the required examination.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
stakeholders: Individuals seeking licensure as music therapists, licensed music therapists qualified to supervise, and the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board can issue limited licenses using existing budgeted resources. While the board will collect application and renewal fees for the new limited license category, these fees are not anticipated to meaningfully impact board special fund revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the Department of Health and signed this bill into law. The office is also responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which includes funding for the regulatory boards.
As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller manages the collection of state revenues, which includes the licensing and renewal fees authorized by this bill.
The Treasurer's Office is responsible for receiving and depositing state funds. The fees collected by the Board for limited music therapy licenses will be managed and protected by this agency.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to all state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the Board of Examiners as they implement new limited license regulations.
DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and personnel management. It oversees the fiscal resources allocated to the Department of Health and its constituent boards.

The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech–Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists is located within the Department of Health. The department is the primary entity responsible for implementing the licensing requirements and regulating the practitioners mentioned in the bill.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. Any disputes regarding the denial, suspension, or revocation of the new limited licenses authorized by this bill would be heard by an Administrative Law Judge from this office.

responsible_party: Sheriff of Anne Arundel County and Anne Arundel County Council
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office and the residents of Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County expenditures may increase by as much as $822,300 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $730,000 annually thereafter. These costs account for salaries, benefits, start-up equipment (such as vehicles and uniforms), and ongoing operating expenses for three new major positions. There is no material impact on State operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing legislation into law and overseeing the implementation of state statutes. This bill involves structural changes to the office of a constitutional officer (the Sheriff) via state law.

This bill directly amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Sheriffs serve as the primary law enforcement officers for the state's judicial branch, and the Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the operational and legal framework in which they serve the courts.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state on the interpretation of laws and the powers of constitutional officers like the County Sheriff.

bill_summary: This bill updates the reporting and data collection requirements for bullying, harassment, and intimidation in Maryland public schools. It requires reporting forms to identify motivating factors such as race, sex, or disability, and mandates that county boards of education report disaggregated data on these incidents to the State Board of Education under certain conditions and make this information available upon request.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and County Boards of Education
stakeholders: Public school students, parents, school staff, and county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no estimated fiscal impact on state or local government. The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and local school systems can update forms, establish standards, and report data using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, MSDE (the Department) is responsible for creating the standard bullying report form, establishing standards for determining motivated incidents, collecting data from county boards, and submitting an annual summary report to the General Assembly.

An independent unit within MSDE, the Center is responsible for school safety coordination, administering related grants, and managing reporting systems like Safe Schools Maryland. The bill's requirements for anonymous reporting and safety data collection fall directly within their mission.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include funding in the state budget for grants to county boards to establish the anonymous reporting programs mentioned in the legislation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and the State Board. The bill includes specific provisions related to the federal Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and confidentiality of student records that require legal oversight.

The bill requires tracking bullying incidents motivated by protected characteristics such as race, religion, sexual orientation, and gender identity. This data is relevant to the Commission's mission of monitoring and preventing discrimination in Maryland.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM would oversee the execution and allocation of any budget grants authorized by the Governor for the implementation of anonymous reporting systems.

The MLDS Center links student data from MSDE to performance and workforce outcomes. Changes in how MSDE collects data regarding student environment and safety incidents are relevant to the longitudinal datasets they maintain.

The office coordinates efforts to improve the well-being of Maryland's children. Improved reporting and mitigation of bullying and harassment in schools are core components of child well-being and support network building.

The bill specifically tracks bullying incidents motivated by a student's actual or perceived physical or mental disability, aligning with the department's role in advancing inclusive settings for residents with disabilities.

bill_summary: This bill updates the criteria for determining the legal venue for the probate of estates belonging to individuals not domiciled in Maryland, particularly those residing outside the United States. It also specifies that for Maryland inheritance tax purposes, the legal location (situs) of intangible personal property is defined as the decedent's domicile and repeals certain reciprocal inheritance tax exemptions for nonresidents.
responsible_party: Maryland Register of Wills, Orphans' Courts, and the Comptroller's Office
stakeholders: Estates of non-resident decedents, heirs and beneficiaries of those estates, personal representatives, and Maryland financial institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease minimally starting in fiscal year 2027 because certain intangible personal property of nonresidents may no longer be subject to the Maryland inheritance tax. The Register of Wills expects no significant fiscal impact, and local government finances are not affected. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable, though the impact is characterized as minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency responsible for administrative probate and the collection of inheritance taxes. This bill directly alters venue rules for probate and inheritance tax application, which are core functions of the Register's offices in each county.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judicial Branch, including the Orphans' Courts which handle judicial probate. The bill modifies the venue criteria for judicial probate proceedings.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller oversees the collection of state revenues and monitors tax laws. Changes to the inheritance tax situs and exemptions directly impact the state's tax regime.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes regarding state and local taxes. Changes to inheritance tax rules, such as the determination of the situs of intangible personal property, may lead to appeals within this court's jurisdiction.
DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The bill's impact on general fund revenues, though estimated as minimal, falls under DBM's fiscal monitoring responsibilities.
The State Treasurer is the custodian of state funds, including inheritance tax revenues deposited into the general fund. The agency manages the receipt and distribution of these state revenues.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Registers of Wills and the Comptroller, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of changes to estate, trust, and tax laws.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and various departments involved in implementing the bill's tax and probate changes, and the Governor is responsible for signing the legislation into law.

bill_summary: This bill reestablishes a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City, specifically for social events organized in conjunction with the annual CIAA Basketball Tournament. It defines related events and promoters, outlines a specific application process requiring approval from Visit Baltimore, and sets permit fees based on venue capacity. The bill also establishes penalties, including fines between $1,000 and $3,000, for noncompliance.

stakeholders: Event promoters, alcoholic beverage license holders in Baltimore City, and attendees of events related to the CIAA Basketball Tournament.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal impact. Baltimore City revenues are expected to increase minimally from FY 2026 through FY 2029 through a $50 application fee and permit fees of either $500 or $1,500 per event depending on venue capacity. Local monitoring and enforcement costs are expected to be absorbed within existing budgets.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing the bill into law and overseeing the executive agencies involved in the regulation of alcoholic beverages and economic development.

The Comptroller is the primary state official responsible for regulating the alcohol industry. The bill involves state caterer's licenses and penalties for alcoholic beverage violations which fall under the Comptroller's broader regulatory and tax collection mandate.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Governor and the executive director mentioned in the bill, regarding the enforcement of alcoholic beverage laws and licensing regulations.

The Department of Commerce is responsible for economic development and tourism. The CIAA Basketball Tournament is a major economic driver for Baltimore, and this bill facilitates social events and promotions that contribute to the tournament's success.

As the agency tasked with stimulating Maryland's tourism economy, the Office of Tourism Development is directly impacted by legislation that regulates promotional events related to the CIAA Basketball Tournament, a premier travel event for the state.

Synopsis: Altering provisions related to the rates the Department of State Police sets for towing companies involved in police-initiated towing of motor vehicles to include the towing and recovery of light-duty vehicles; defining "light-duty towing" as towing and recovery of a vehicle including trailers or semitrailers with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or less; and altering the duties of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.
Title: Public Safety - Department of State Police - Police-Initiated Towing - Alterations
bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of State Police (DSP) to establish maximum rates for police-initiated towing and recovery of light-duty vehicles (10,000 pounds or less) based on recommendations from a renamed and expanded committee. It sets a rate cap for light-duty towing at 80% of the maximum medium-duty rate and mandates the committee examine insurance matters related to out-of-state vehicles and debris cleanup.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police
stakeholders: Towing and recovery companies, light-duty vehicle owners and operators, the Department of State Police, and motor vehicle industry associations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of State Police can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, and state revenues are not materially affected. Local government finances are not impacted. There is a potential meaningful fiscal impact on small business towing companies due to the implementation of regulated maximum rates for light-duty vehicle towing.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (Department of State Police) is the primary implementing agency. The bill requires the Department to establish towing rates for light-duty vehicles, maintain the tow list, provide staff support for the rate-setting committee, and develop a process for investigating and adjudicating towing complaints.

The Secretary of Transportation is responsible for appointing a representative from the Maryland Transportation Authority Police to the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution. The department also oversees the State Highway Administration, which is also represented on the committee.

The bill requires a representative from the Maryland Transportation Authority Police to serve as a member of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.
The bill requires a representative from the State Highway Administration to serve as a member of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.

The bill requires a representative from the Maryland Insurance Administration to serve on the rate-setting committee and tasks the committee with examining and reporting on insurance matters related to out-of-state vehicles and cargo cleanup costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly alters the name, membership, and statutory responsibilities of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery, which functions as an advisory body within the executive branch.

As the chief executive, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of State Police and the Department of Transportation. The Governor signed this legislation and oversees the broader executive policy regarding public safety and regulatory rate-setting.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of State Police and the rate-setting committee regarding the development of regulations, the adjudication process for complaints, and the implementation of rate-setting standards.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to regulate the sale, planting, and growth of 'tree of heaven' and other trees listed on the Maryland Prohibited Invasive Plant List. It allows local governments to create bounty or native tree replacement programs to encourage the removal of these invasive species and authorizes the use of civil fines and mitigation requirements for enforcement.
responsible_party: Governing body of a county or municipality
stakeholders: Property owners, landscaping businesses, nurseries, and local governments in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is authorizing in nature and does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local government expenditures may increase if they choose to establish bounty or native tree replacement programs. Local revenues may increase if governments implement civil fines for ordinance violations. Small businesses may see increased costs for compliance or increased demand for landscaping services related to tree removal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines regulated invasive trees based on the "Maryland Prohibited Invasive Plant List" which is maintained and posted by the Department of Agriculture.

The agency is responsible for conserving and managing the state's forests and natural resources which are directly harmed by invasive species; they are also listed as an information source in the fiscal note.
The bill mandates that local governments use identification and eradication methodologies published by the University of Maryland Extension, which is a unit of the University System of Maryland.
The bill authorizes new local land-use and growth-related ordinances, aligning with the department's mission to promote sustainable development and resource management.
The fiscal note indicates a potential meaningful impact on small businesses, specifically landscaping and nursery companies, which fall under the department's economic support mission.
The bill's preamble cites environmental harm as a primary reason for the regulation of invasive trees, which relates to the department's mission of environmental protection and restoration.
The Governor signed the bill into law and oversees the executive departments (Agriculture and DNR) involved in managing invasive species policy.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the implementation of regulatory lists and the legal parameters of local government ordinances.
The bill authorizes the establishment of civil fines by local governments, which may eventually lead to increased adjudication within the state court system.
The bill's preamble notes that invasive species can cause harm to human health, which is the primary focus of the Department of Health.

bill_summary: The bill allows registered massage practitioners to continue practicing beyond October 31, 2026, and modifies the educational requirements for massage therapy licensure, particularly for out-of-state applicants. It also updates procedures for registration reinstatement and reactivation, including requiring criminal history records checks for reactivation, and removes hearing requirements for the imposition of administrative penalties related to failure to notify the Board of name or address changes.

stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and applicants for massage therapy licensure, including those from out-of-state.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's changes do not materially affect State finances and there is no local fiscal impact. A $100 administrative penalty for failing to report name or address changes remains, but the requirement for a hearing before imposition is removed. Small businesses may experience a meaningful impact as registered practitioners can continue practicing beyond the previous 2026 phase-out deadline without meeting additional licensure requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees all executive departments, including the Department of Health, which houses the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners. The Governor also signed this bill into law.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners. The bill's changes to administrative penalties and hearing requirements involve legal procedures and statutory interpretation overseen by the OAG.

The Maryland Department of Health regulates health care professionals and facilities. The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a health occupation board, and the MDH was cited as a primary information source for the fiscal note.

The bill explicitly requires that applicants for a massage therapy license must have graduated from an institution of postsecondary education approved by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). The bill also creates educational standards for out-of-state programs based on their approval by similar higher education entities.

The bill requires applicants for the reinstatement or reactivation of a license or registration to submit to a state and national criminal history records check, which involves data maintained and processed by state law enforcement agencies.

The bill repeals the requirement that the imposition of a $100 administrative penalty (for failure to notify the Board of a name or address change) be subject to hearing requirements, which reduces the potential administrative hearing scope for contested cases.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program to recognize public high school students for their civic readiness and engagement. The State Board of Education is required to set criteria for awarding a 'Seal of Civic Excellence' to students who meet specific requirements, including the completion of a capstone project focused on civic service within state or local government. Local school systems may choose whether or not to participate in the program, but if a system does participate, its high schools must implement the program and award qualifying students with the seal and a corresponding cord, medal, or other insignia for their diploma.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the State Board of Education
stakeholders: Public high school students and local school systems in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Education can implement the program using existing resources. Local school systems that choose to participate may experience increased expenditures related to staffing for extracurricular supervision and the cost of award materials (cords, medals, or insignia). However, because participation is voluntary for local school systems, these fiscal impacts are considered discretionary. No state or local revenue impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies like MSDE and coordinates policy initiatives related to the Governor's priorities for Maryland's youth and public education system.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the State Board of Education, and would likely review the regulations required to be adopted under this bill.

DBM oversees fiscal planning and personnel policies; the bill's provision for new extracurricular activities supervised by paid staff could have marginal personnel or budgetary implications for state-run educational programs.

MSDE is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Civic Excellence Program, receiving reports from local school systems, and supporting the State Board in developing the necessary regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's mission to promote service and civic engagement is directly aligned with the bill's goal of recognizing students for civic readiness and requiring a civic service capstone project.
GOCI oversees community affairs and volunteerism, providing a framework for the types of civic service and community partnerships encouraged by the bill's capstone requirement.
The bill explicitly authorizes participating local school systems to collaborate with institutions of higher education to support the implementation of the program.
As the coordinating board for postsecondary education, this agency oversees the institutions that may collaborate with local school systems on civic excellence initiatives.
As a state agency providing tuition-free public education to Maryland students, the school may implement the program to recognize the civic engagement of its high school students.
The agency's mission to promote fair and transparent elections aligns with the bill's focus on civic literacy and engagement, which often includes education on the electoral process.
As a public university, Morgan State may serve as a partner for local school systems seeking to implement civic service capstone projects or other civic excellence criteria.
As Maryland's public honors college, it is a potential institutional partner for school systems implementing the Maryland Civic Excellence Program.
The University System of Maryland institutions are potential collaborators for local school systems in developing and supporting the civic readiness goals established by the bill.
Volunteer Maryland coordinates service opportunities and volunteer management systems, which directly correlates with the bill's requirement for a civic service-focused capstone project.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a communication between an attorney and a client that acts as a fiduciary is subject to the attorney-client privilege even if fiduciary funds are used to compensate the attorney for services rendered to the client.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Fiduciaries - Attorney-Client Privilege
bill_summary: This bill clarifies that attorney-client privilege applies to communications between an attorney and a client who is acting as a fiduciary, such as an executor or trustee, even if the attorney is compensated using fiduciary funds. It further establishes that the fiduciary relationship between the client and a beneficiary does not waive this privilege.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Fiduciaries (including trustees, executors, personal representatives, and agents under power of attorney), beneficiaries of estates and trusts, and attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judicial Branch by codifying rules regarding the attorney-client privilege, an evidentiary standard applied in judicial proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides legal and operational support to the state's courts, including the Orphans' Courts where fiduciary matters are frequently adjudicated.

The Register of Wills is the primary state agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and overseeing personal representatives and executors, who are explicitly defined as fiduciaries under the Estates and Trusts Article. This bill clarifies legal protections for communications between these fiduciaries and their counsel.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies that may act in fiduciary capacities (such as guardians or trustees). The bill clarifies the application of attorney-client privilege in these scenarios, particularly when fiduciary funds are used for compensation.

The Department of Human Services frequently interacts with the legal system in fiduciary roles, such as serving as guardians for vulnerable children and adults. This bill clarifies the legal protections afforded to communications between the agency's representatives and their legal counsel in those capacities.

The Department of Aging oversees programs for older adults and individuals with disabilities, including long-term care advocacy and support for guardians. The bill's clarification of fiduciary attorney-client privilege is relevant to the legal environment surrounding the populations and advocates the department serves.

The Department of Disabilities is concerned with the legal rights and services provided to individuals with disabilities, many of whom have fiduciaries such as guardians or agents with power of attorney. This bill clarifies the privacy of legal communications for those managing the affairs of disabled residents.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland nonstock corporations to convert to cooperative limited equity housing corporations (CLEHCs) and establishes the procedures for such conversions. It sets requirements for voting, documentation, and notice to residents. To preserve affordability, the bill limits the resale price and appreciation of cooperative interests and requires that at least 75% of members be from low-income households. Additionally, it mandates that CLEHCs reimburse low-income households for moving expenses between $375 and $751 if they are required to vacate, and it authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish a grant program to promote the creation of CLEHCs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Low- and moderate-income households, residents of residential rental facilities with five or more units, Maryland nonstock corporations, senior citizens, and disabled persons.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase to support a new grant program and additional administrative staffing at the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), though total costs are indeterminate. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) expects a minimal increase in revenue from filing fees ($120 for articles of incorporation and $100 for articles of conversion). There is no direct fiscal impact on local governments. CLEHCs are mandated to pay moving expense reimbursements of at least $375 but less than $751 to qualifying low-income households forced to vacate due to conversion.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish additional rights and requirements for cooperative limited equity housing corporations, create a grant program to promote their establishment, and adopt implementing regulations.

The fiscal note indicates that general fund expenditures may increase for DHCD to hire administrative staff and fund the newly authorized grant program, which falls under DBM's fiscal and personnel oversight.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Department of Housing and Community Development during the development of regulations and the individualized assessment of cooperatives authorized by the bill.

The bill contains significant provisions preempting local government zoning and building code restrictions regarding cooperative limited equity housing corporations, which impacts the land use policy and local technical assistance functions of the Department of Planning.
The bill provides specific statutory protections for senior citizens, including extending the minimum period they can be required to vacate a unit during a conversion from 90 days to 12 months.
The bill provides specific statutory protections for disabled persons, including extending the minimum period they can be required to vacate a unit during a conversion from 90 days to 12 months.
The establishment of new legal rights for cooperative members and specific notice-to-vacate requirements may lead to increased litigation in the state court system, as noted in the fiscal note.
As a major policy initiative related to affordable housing and economic mobility, the Governor's Office would coordinate the interagency implementation of these new corporate structures.

bill_summary: This bill extends the expiration and renewal periods for handgun permits issued to retired law enforcement officers who served in good standing. It increases the initial permit duration from two years to five years and sets the subsequent renewal period to every five years instead of every three years.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police
stakeholders: Retired law enforcement officers of the State or a county or municipal corporation of the State who retired in good standing.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures will increase by approximately $170,000 in fiscal 2027 for one-time computer programming changes to automate the new expiration and renewal timelines. There is no impact on State revenues because retired law enforcement officers are exempt from handgun permit application and renewal fees. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State Police is the authority responsible for issuing and renewing handgun permits in Maryland. The agency is directly tasked with implementing the new five-year expiration and renewal cycle for retired law enforcement officers and requires $170,000 for necessary updates to its automated permitting system.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the oversight of general fund expenditures, including the $170,000 required for the Maryland State Police to update its computer programming to accommodate the bill's requirements.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland State Police. It provides legal guidance on the enforcement of public safety laws and the administrative procedures for handgun permit regulation.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Maryland State Police. The Governor signed this legislation into law and oversees the policy initiatives related to public safety and law enforcement retirees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy. The regulation of handgun permits is a component of the state's broader public safety and firearm policy framework.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, from 19 to 21 members, to include one representative of the Greater Baltimore Chamber of Commerce, one representative from the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees Local 3, Council 434, and one representative of the Citizens Advisory Council for Gifted and Talented Education.

bill_summary: This bill increases the membership of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission from 19 to 21 members. The bill also updates the existing chamber of commerce seat to be filled by the Greater Baltimore Chamber of Commerce and establishes a staggered schedule for the expiration of member terms.

stakeholders: Residents of Baltimore County, potential candidates for the Baltimore County Board of Education, and members of the organizations represented on the Nominating Commission including AFSCME and the Citizens Advisory Council for Gifted and Talented Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. The addition of two members to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission is not expected to materially affect Baltimore County local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor holds the statutory authority to appoint eight members to the Nominating Commission and is responsible for making the final appointments to the Baltimore County Board of Education from the list of names provided by the Commission.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions and would be responsible for advising the Nominating Commission on the legal implementation of its revised membership and term-staggering requirements.

The bill amends the Education Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland, which falls under the leadership and oversight of the Department of Education, and directly impacts the governance and selection process for a local school board.

The Office of Appointments is primarily responsible for recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates to the Governor for positions on state boards and commissions, including the members of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission and the local Board of Education.

Towson University, a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, is a permanent member of the Commission and is explicitly tasked by the bill with appointing a member and managing their term requirements.

stakeholders: Dependent children of active service members and their families relocating to Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances. The Department of Veterans and Military Families and local school systems can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Multiple school systems have indicated that their current advance enrollment procedures already conform to the bill's requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is explicitly mandated by the bill to publish and maintain information regarding advance enrollment procedures, the Purple Star Schools Program, the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children, and available assistance for active service members.

The bill amends the Education Article and directly impacts the enrollment procedures for public schools. MSDE provides oversight and leadership for local school systems and administers the Purple Star Schools Program mentioned in the bill.

The bill requires the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to consult with the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council, both of which are located within the Department of Commerce.
The bill contains specific provisions for the advance enrollment and educational continuity of dependent children with disabilities, including requirements for IEP and 504 plan implementation.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General represents the active service members and their families whose educational rights and enrollment procedures are being updated by this legislation.
The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives across executive branch agencies, and the bill involves cross-agency collaboration between the DVMF, Commerce, and Education departments.

The Maryland School for the Deaf is identified as an agency that may be impacted or involved in providing educational services to military dependents with hearing impairments who utilize the bill's advance enrollment and IEP provisions.

The Secretary of State serves as the custodian of official state records and is involved in the coordination of interstate compacts, such as the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children referenced in the bill.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits consumer contracts from waiving, limiting, impairing, or disclaiming certain legal remedies authorized by federal or state law, including statutory damages, punitive damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief. It also prohibits contract provisions that shorten the statute of limitations for bringing a legal action and repeals several previous exemptions for licensed businesses and regulated utilities. Violations of these provisions are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers and businesses that enter into consumer contracts for goods or services used for personal, family, or household purposes.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business effects are expected to be minimal. Although violations are subject to enforcement and civil penalties under the Consumer Protection Act, no specific revenue or expenditure figures were provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that a violation of its provisions constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article. The Office of the Attorney General, specifically its Consumer Protection Division, is the primary agency responsible for enforcing Maryland's consumer protection laws and prosecuting such violations.

The bill sets standards for the validity of consumer contract provisions and explicitly directs courts on how to handle illegal provisions (rendering them void and unenforceable while maintaining the rest of the contract). It also defines available remedies such as declaratory and injunctive relief that may be pursued in court.

The bill specifically identifies services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission as exempt from certain prohibited contract provisions, thereby defining the agency's jurisdictional boundaries regarding these consumer protections.

The bill repeals a broad exemption for businesses operating under a license issued by a State agency. Since the Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various professions, industries, and financial institutions, this change expands the scope of consumer contract regulations to many businesses under its supervision.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the administration of state laws and policy initiatives. This bill relates to consumer protection policy and requires the Governor's approval.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) System Pilot Program, requiring individuals whose driver's licenses are suspended or revoked due to speeding, reckless driving, or racing violations to participate. Participants are issued a restrictive license and must install an aftermarket ISA device that actively prevents the vehicle from exceeding the posted speed limit for a period of one year.
responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA)
stakeholders: Drivers with speed-related license suspensions or revocations, the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration, and certified intelligent speed assistance system manufacturers and service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are estimated to increase by approximately 61,020 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2031 based on program participation fees. The MVA is required to set fees at a level sufficient to cover program costs. The MVA may incur costs of approximately 100,000 per year for an outside consultant to develop program standards. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary agency responsible for establishing, regulating, and administering the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program, including issuing restrictive licenses and monitoring participants.
As the parent department of the MVA, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund, which is impacted by the bill's program fees and administrative costs.

The bill explicitly requires the District Court to ensure its fine schedule is updated with separate entries for specific types of reckless driving violations; the AOC provides the necessary operational support for such changes.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and the MVA, and is a required recipient of the program implementation report due by December 30, 2030.
DBM oversees state personnel and fiscal execution, including the management of the Transportation Trust Fund and the resources required for MVA to implement the new pilot program.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the MVA regarding the adoption of new regulations and the legal framework for data retention, privacy, and sharing mandated by the bill.

The program provides access to state correctional facilities for volunteers, specifically including formerly incarcerated individuals and organizations led by them. The DOC is required to establish a registration protocol, approved by the Office of the Attorney General, to manage volunteer records and schedules while allowing volunteers to opt-in to public disclosure of their participation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (Division of Correction)
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, formerly incarcerated individuals, volunteer organizations, and the Maryland Division of Correction
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can handle the bill's requirements using existing resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances and has no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the parent agency of the Division of Correction, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services is the primary body responsible for establishing, implementing, and managing the Volunteer Services Program, including creating the registration protocol and maintaining records of volunteers.
The bill explicitly requires the Division of Correction to submit the protocol for the new Volunteer Services Program to the Office of the Attorney General for formal approval.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note links this bill to the Performance Incentive Grant Fund managed by GOCPP, which provides funding for reentry programs designed to reduce recidivism, aligning with the bill's goal of release preparation for incarcerated individuals.

GOCI oversees the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism and Volunteer Maryland; as this bill establishes a new statewide volunteer program within the executive branch, GOCI may provide guidance on volunteer management and coordination.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees workforce development and adult learning programs; since the Volunteer Services Program focuses on release preparation, it directly intersects with the Department's mission to assist formerly incarcerated individuals with labor market readiness.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note highlights the existing Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services, whose work and recommendations are directly relevant to the establishment of the Release Preparation Volunteer Services Program.

The Governor's Office provides administrative oversight for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and coordinates the policy initiatives related to public safety and corrections addressed in this bill.

bill_summary: The bill requires the State Board of Elections (SBE) and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) to establish a process for the automatic restoration of voter registration for individuals released from State correctional facilities. Under the bill, DPSCS must transmit monthly lists of released individuals to SBE, which must then promptly restore the registration of those who were previously registered to vote in Maryland. The bill also mandates the provision of notice to these individuals regarding their registration status and prohibits the public disclosure of the registration agency source.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals released from State correctional facilities who were previously registered voters in Maryland, the Maryland State Board of Elections, and local boards of elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances. These costs, billed to local boards of elections by the State Board of Elections under a cost-sharing structure, are required for modifications to the statewide voter registration system to enable automatic reactivation of registrations and update voter notification cards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the State Board of Elections is mandated to jointly develop restoration procedures, manage the electronic transmission process, and promptly restore voter registration for eligible individuals released from State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is a primary implementing agency responsible for monthly data transmission to the State Board of Elections and for jointly developing the electronic transmission and restoration procedures for released individuals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to both the State Board of Elections and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services regarding the development of new inter-agency procedures and the bill's specific restrictions on public disclosure under the Public Information Act.

The bill requires the development of an electronic transmission process and modifications to the statewide voter registration system, which falls under the strategic IT and infrastructure oversight of this department.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (DPSCS) involved in implementation, signed the bill into law, and directs the broader policy initiatives related to voting rights and correctional services.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors the budget and resource allocation for the implementing agencies, especially given the system modifications and local board billings mentioned in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor's Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) is the primary regulator for the Maryland Money Transmission Act. The bill directly alters the definition of money transmitters that OFR licenses, resulting in a direct decrease of $6,000 in special fund licensing fee revenue for the department.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Department of Labor and would be responsible for providing guidance on the legal implementation of the modified licensing requirements and representing the agency in any related legal challenges.
DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and estimating revenues. This bill has a noted fiscal impact on state special fund revenues which DBM must track for fiscal planning.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases involving state agencies. If disputes arise regarding whether a specific payroll processor meets the new criteria for exclusion from the Money Transmission Act, OAH would likely handle those administrative appeals.

responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders (restaurants and bars) and alcoholic beverage consumers in Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local fiscal impact is not expected to be material as the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners is prohibited from charging an additional fee for the permit. Small businesses operating as restaurants or bars in Baltimore County may experience increased revenues from expanded off-premises sales.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry and is responsible for enforcing tax laws and regulating industry practices, which are directly affected by changes to off-premises sales authorizations.

The Governor's Office oversaw the approval of this legislation and is responsible for the overall execution of state laws and the administrative oversight of executive branch functions related to the bill.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state and local boards regarding the interpretation and enforcement of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

The bill explicitly requires the local licensing board to consider the public health impacts of off-premises alcoholic beverage sales, which directly aligns with the Maryland Department of Health's mission to set health policy and ensure resident safety.

The bill is identified as having a meaningful fiscal impact on small businesses, specifically restaurants and bars in Baltimore County, which falls under the Department of Commerce's purview of economic development and business retention.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in appointing members to various state and local boards, including the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County responsible for implementing this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud; requiring the Task Force to review the incidence of deed fraud in Maryland, including the number of complaints, resolved deed fraud cases, amount of restitution awarded, and geographic and demographic trends; requiring the Department of Legislative Services to provide staff for the Task Force; and requiring the Task Force by July 1, 2028, to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.
Title: Task Force to Study Deed Fraud

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Task Force to Study Deed Fraud to analyze the prevalence of deed fraud in Maryland, study prevention methods used in other states, and recommend strategies for intergovernmental coordination to detect and prevent fraudulent property transfers.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland property owners, victims of deed fraud, law enforcement agencies, the Judiciary, and legal service organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services can staff the task force using existing budgeted resources. Any expenses for member travel reimbursements are expected to be minimal and absorbable within current budgets. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud, a new temporary body tasked with conducting a specific study and providing recommendations on governmental issues.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or a designee) is a mandated member of the task force, and the study of deed fraud is directly relevant to the agency's mission of ensuring safe and secure housing.
The Governor is responsible for appointing two members to the task force and designating the chair.
A representative of the Judiciary is a mandated member of the task force, and the task force is charged with studying court-related data such as resolved cases and restitution awarded.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of the two appointed positions on the task force.
The Secretary of State regulates notaries public, and the task force is required to include an individual with experience as a notary to study fraud prevention.
As the chief legal representative for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to the agencies involved in the task force and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.
The Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating criminal fraud and will be impacted by the task force's recommendations for improving deed fraud detection and prevention.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The task force's findings and recommendations regarding criminal deed fraud strategies align with GOCPP's role in coordinating public safety and criminal justice policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The task force's study of deed fraud trends and recommendations for combatting it may impact the caseload and defense strategies for indigent individuals represented by the OPD.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees the rehabilitation of individuals involved in the justice system, including those convicted of crimes like fraud, and was consulted for the fiscal analysis of the bill.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency and was involved in the fiscal note analysis; it may also manage budget reimbursements for task force members.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of a political subdivision to designate certain noncontiguous blighted areas as development districts.
Title: Economic Development - Tax Increment Financing - Noncontiguous Areas

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill allows local political subdivisions, including Baltimore City, to designate noncontiguous blighted areas as development districts for Tax Increment Financing (TIF). It defines a blighted area as one where a majority of buildings have declined in productivity because of obsolescence or depreciation to the point that repairs are no longer justified.
responsible_party: Local governing bodies of Maryland political subdivisions and Baltimore City
stakeholders: Local governments, property owners in blighted areas, and small businesses in the construction and development sectors
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Local revenues and expenditures are expected to increase starting in fiscal 2027 as local governments utilize TIF bonds for noncontiguous blighted areas. Increased revenues will come from bond proceeds and eventually increased property tax revenues from redevelopment, while expenditures will cover project costs and debt service. Baltimore City is expected to have no impact as its charter already allows for noncontiguous TIF districts; however, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) is a quasi-governmental entity that provides financing and real estate development services. The fiscal note specifically mentions that local revenues from Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts may be pledged to debt issued by MEDCO, making them a primary vehicle for implementing the financing enabled by this bill.

The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) is responsible for community revitalization and municipal infrastructure projects. TIF is a key tool for financing the infrastructure and revitalization of the 'blighted areas' defined and addressed in this legislation.

The Maryland Stadium Authority's mission includes economic development initiatives such as the removal of blight, specifically in Baltimore City. As this bill defines 'blighted areas' and expands TIF authority for such areas in political subdivisions including Baltimore City, it directly aligns with the Authority's revitalization work.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce oversees programs to attract and retain businesses. TIF is a major economic development tool, and the agency is listed as an information source for the fiscal analysis of this bill.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and land use planning. The authorization of noncontiguous development districts is a significant land-use planning change that affects how local jurisdictions manage growth and resource allocation.

TIF districts operate by 'freezing' a property tax base and collecting revenue on the 'incremental valuation.' Disputes regarding property assessments within these new noncontiguous blighted districts would be heard by the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.

The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from the final decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board. Cases involving property tax assessments and credits within these specialized development districts would ultimately fall under its jurisdiction.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state agencies (such as Commerce and DHCD) that coordinate economic development policy and may be required to interpret the new statutory definitions of 'blighted area' and 'noncontiguous development districts.'

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a 'potential meaningful' impact on small businesses located in or adjacent to blighted areas that receive TIF-funded improvements. This office monitors socioeconomic procurement and business opportunities that may arise from such development projects.

The Rural Maryland Council advocates for the interests of Maryland's 18 rural counties. The expansion of TIF authority to noncontiguous blighted areas provides rural jurisdictions with a more flexible tool for regional economic development and community revitalization.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on community revitalization and sustainable development. The bill's focus on blighting and sustainable growth through TIF districts directly relates to the initiative's coordination of land use and resource conservation.

The Authority advises on the use of impact aid for revitalization in neighborhoods surrounding the Pimlico Race Course in Baltimore City. The expansion of TIF authority for noncontiguous blighted areas provides a potential additional mechanism for the community development projects they oversee.

Synopsis: Providing collective bargaining rights to certain graduate assistants  at certain public institutions of higher education; defining "graduate assistant" as a graduate student at the University of Maryland, College Park or the University of Maryland, Baltimore County who is a teaching, administrative, or research assistant or in a comparable position, a fellow, or a postdoctoral intern; and establishing a separate collective bargaining unit for the graduate assistants.
Title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Graduate Assistants

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill grants collective bargaining rights to graduate assistants, including teaching, administrative, and research assistants, as well as fellows and postdoctoral interns, at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP) and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). It establishes separate collective bargaining units for these employees and tasks the Public Employee Relations Board with overseeing the bargaining process, including the certification of employee organizations.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board, University of Maryland, College Park, University of Maryland, Baltimore County, and the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Graduate students at UMCP and UMBC serving as teaching, administrative, or research assistants, fellows, or postdoctoral interns.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for UMCP and UMBC will increase minimally beginning in FY 2029 to reimburse the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) for collective bargaining expenses. Administrative and personnel expenditures at these institutions may also increase if negotiations result in higher salaries or fringe benefits for the approximately 3,600 eligible individuals. Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for PERB will increase minimally as elections and disputes occur.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates PERB as the regulatory body responsible for overseeing the new collective bargaining units, administering elections for exclusive representatives, and adjudicating disputes.
USM is the primary administrative entity for UMCP and UMBC, the specific institutions where graduate assistants are granted collective bargaining rights under the bill.
As the central personnel and fiscal agency, DBM oversees state personnel policies and the budget execution impacted by negotiated salary and benefit increases.
This agency coordinates statewide policies for public universities and ensures institutions adhere to financial and academic standards which may be influenced by collective bargaining.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including PERB and the public universities, regarding the implementation of the new collective bargaining laws.
Morgan State University is explicitly named in the bill's amendments to the statutory structure requiring the creation of separate bargaining units for eligible graduate assistants.
The college is explicitly included in the bill's provisions requiring higher education institutions to establish separate bargaining units for graduate assistants.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies involved and is responsible for the final approval and policy coordination of the legislation.
The Board oversees significant state expenditures and contracts, which may be impacted by the fiscal outcomes of collective bargaining agreements at state institutions.
The department enforces labor laws and manages workforce development, providing the broader regulatory context for the expansion of collective bargaining rights.
As the state's principal tax collector and payroll officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the administration of state employee payments and revenue tracking.
The agency manages retirement benefits for state higher education employees, which may be subject to change through the collective bargaining process.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county or municipal corporation to designate assistant fire marshals with the approval of the State Fire Marshal or to request that the State Fire Marshal designate certain fire marshals and requiring the State Fire Marshal to adopt certain regulations governing the qualifications, training, standards, and certification of designees; requiring, by October 1, 2026, the installation of certain automatic fire sprinklers in certain high-rise residential buildings; etc.
Title: Fire Prevention - Assistant Fire Marshals, Residential Rental High-Rise Property Fire Safety Equipment, and Fire Alarm System Technicians

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the installation of automatic fire sprinklers and other fire safety equipment in residential rental high-rise buildings undergoing substantial renovations starting October 1, 2026. It also establishes a licensing and regulatory program for fire alarm system technicians and companies and sets new standards, training, and certification requirements for assistant State fire marshals designated by local governments.
responsible_party: State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission
stakeholders: Owners and tenants of residential rental high-rise buildings, fire alarm system technicians, fire alarm system companies, local governments, and the Office of the State Fire Marshal.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $311,100 in FY 2027 for hiring three administrative staff members, IT system upgrades for licensing, and NFPA certification for Office of the State Fire Marshal employees. Annual expenditures are projected to be between $231,400 and $264,500 in subsequent years. General fund revenues will increase from new licensing fees for fire alarm system technicians. Local government expenditures will increase to cover training and certification for assistant fire marshals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (MSP) houses the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission, which are the primary entities responsible for implementation, regulation, and enforcement of the fire safety standards and technician licensing programs created by the bill.

The bill has a significant fiscal impact on the state budget, requiring the addition of three new administrative positions and funding for information technology upgrades, which falls under DBM’s oversight of personnel and fiscal planning.

The OAG will provide essential legal counsel to the State Fire Prevention Commission and the State Fire Marshal in drafting the new regulations and establishing the licensing and enforcement procedures mandated by the bill.
