The bill regulates fire safety in residential rental high-rise properties, which aligns with the department's mission to ensure safe and secure housing for Maryland residents.

The fiscal note indicates that the University System of Maryland may face substantial costs (estimated at $2 million) to upgrade older high-rise residential housing facilities (dormitories) to comply with the new fire safety and sprinkler requirements if they undergo substantial renovation.

As a state-governed university with residential high-rise facilities, Morgan State University may be impacted by the new requirements for automatic fire sprinklers and safety equipment in the event of substantial renovations to its dormitories.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland operates residential facilities that may be subject to the bill's updated high-rise fire safety standards during future renovations.

DGS is responsible for the design, construction, and maintenance of state-owned facilities. It would be involved in overseeing the installation of mandated fire safety equipment for any state-owned residential high-rise buildings undergoing substantial renovation.
The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues, including the new licensing fees for fire alarm system technicians and companies established under the bill.

The Commission coordinates policy for Maryland's higher education institutions, many of which own residential high-rise buildings that are specifically identified as being potentially impacted by this legislation.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and the State Fire Marshal. The office is responsible for coordinating the policy initiatives and regulatory changes proposed in this bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax on real property if use of the real property has been converted from a retail service station to other certain uses; prohibiting the application of the credit unless the underground storage tanks located on or formerly located on the real property have been permanently closed; and applying the Act to all taxable years after June 30, 2026.
Title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: This bill authorizes local governments in Maryland, including Baltimore City and other counties or municipalities, to establish a property tax credit for properties converted from retail service stations to residential, retail, or mixed-use purposes. The credit is intended to help property owners cover the costs of removing underground storage tanks and remediating environmental contamination. Certain uses, such as discount stores, self-storage facilities, and businesses selling tobacco, electronic smoking devices, or alcoholic beverages, are excluded from the retail definitions for the credit.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City, or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation
stakeholders: Property owners of former retail service stations, local governments, and developers or small businesses involved in property conversion and environmental remediation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no impact on State finances. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 if local governments choose to grant the property tax credit. The exact fiscal impact is indeterminate as it depends on the number of properties converted, their assessed value, local tax rates, and the specific duration and amount of the credits established by local jurisdictions. There are approximately 2,300 properties in the state currently classified as retail service stations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly states that the tax credit may not be granted unless underground storage tanks have been permanently closed in accordance with regulations of the Department of the Environment. The agency is also the primary regulator for contamination remediation mentioned in the legislative intent.

As an independent agency providing review for property tax assessment disputes, the PTAAB would be responsible for hearing appeals related to the eligibility or valuation of this specific property tax credit if denied or contested at the local level.

The bill defines excluded 'retail uses' by referencing licenses for cigarettes, tobacco, and alcohol, all of which are industries regulated by the Comptroller. Additionally, the Comptroller oversees motor fuel industry regulations, which include the retail service stations being converted.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, including those involving property tax credits and assessments. Decisions from the local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding this credit could be appealed here.

The bill encourages the conversion of retail service stations into residential or mixed-use properties. This aligns with the agency's mission to ensure access to affordable housing and support community revitalization projects.

The agency promotes sustainable growth and land use planning. The conversion of service stations (often brownfields) into retail or residential uses falls under land use management and regional revitalization strategies coordinated by this department.

The department is responsible for stimulating the economy and attracting businesses. This tax credit serves as an economic development tool to incentivize the reuse of properties and the expansion of retail or residential infrastructure.

The bill references 'Division II of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article' to define exclusions for alcoholic beverage license holders. While its primary mission is cannabis regulation, the bill's definitions are tied to the administrative article the MCA operates under.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and signs the bill into law. The bill's focus on environmental remediation and economic mobility aligns with executive policy priorities often managed by the Governor's office.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county board of education to consider the provision of educator workforce housing as a school purpose under certain provisions of law; altering the eligible recipients of certain financial assistance and the housing innovation projects the Department of Housing and Community Development shall prioritize for certain financial assistance under the Housing Innovation Pilot Program; etc.
Title: Housing and Community Development - Affordable Housing - Educator Workforce Housing and Municipal Corporations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes local county boards of education to consider the provision of educator workforce housing as a school purpose, allowing them to utilize land or buildings for this purpose rather than declaring them surplus. It defines educator workforce housing as affordable housing reserved for teachers and school employees who are not top-level administrators. Furthermore, the bill expands eligibility for the Department of Housing and Community Development's Housing Innovation Fund, Housing Innovation Pilot Program, and Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program to include educator workforce housing and adds municipal corporations and county boards of education as eligible recipients of this financial assistance.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
stakeholders: Teachers and local school system employees (excluding strategic administrators), local boards of education, municipal corporations, and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Department of Housing and Community Development can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, and state revenues are not affected. Local school boards and municipal corporations become eligible for state financial assistance to develop educator workforce housing. The bill modifies existing programs like the Housing Innovation Fund and the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program; the latter remains subject to an existing $3,500,000 annual tax credit cap.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with administering the Housing Innovation Fund, the Housing Innovation Pilot Program, and the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program, all of which are expanded to include educator workforce housing.

The bill alters the definition of 'school purpose' to include educator workforce housing, which directly impacts local school boards and property management overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education and the State Superintendent.

As the agency responsible for overseeing public school facility needs and capital improvements, the IAC is impacted by changes in how school property is categorized as 'surplus' versus being retained for 'school purposes' like teacher housing.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Housing Innovation Fund and managing the tax credit certifications and state revenue implications for the expanded programs.
The Treasurer is specifically tasked with holding and investing the Housing Innovation Fund separately, as established by the bill.
The agency provides guidance to local governments on land use and sustainable community designations, which are integral to the housing programs expanded by this bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like DHCD and MSDE regarding the implementation of new definitions for school property and housing program regulations.
DBM oversees the fiscal execution and budgetary appropriations for the Housing Innovation Fund and other DHCD-managed grant programs.
The BPW oversees and approves significant state expenditures and the transfer or lease of state-funded property, which may occur as school boards develop educator housing.
The OLA will likely conduct future performance and compliance audits of the newly expanded programs within DHCD and MSDE.
The Governor's Office coordinates executive policy initiatives and is responsible for signing the bill into law and overseeing the general direction of affordable housing policy.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual who is the sole owner of a marine vessel or multiple individuals who jointly co-own a marine vessel to apply to the Department of Natural Resources to designate a beneficiary to take ownership of the marine vessel on the death of the owner or each co-owner; and altering certain provisions of law governing the transfer-on-death designation for motor vehicles to allow multiple individuals who jointly co-own a motor vehicle to designate a transfer-on-death beneficiary.
Title: Motor Vehicles and Marine Vessels - Transfer-on-Death Designations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: This bill allows individuals who solely own or co-own marine vessels and motor vehicles to designate a beneficiary on the certificate of title. Upon the death of the sole owner or the last surviving co-owner, ownership of the vessel or vehicle automatically transfers to the designated beneficiary, bypassing the standard probate and estate administration process.
responsible_party: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources and the Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Owners and co-owners of motor vehicles and marine vessels in Maryland, designated transfer-on-death beneficiaries, and the Maryland Registers of Wills.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Department of Natural Resources (State Boat Act Fund) and the Transportation Trust Fund are expected to increase beginning in FY 2027 as owners apply for new titles to add beneficiary designations. Based on illustrative scenarios in the Fiscal Note, combined revenues could increase by approximately $1,269,540 in FY 2027. Conversely, State general fund revenues may experience a minimal decrease due to a reduction in probate fees and inheritance taxes, as these assets will be transferred outside of the probate estate. There is no impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for marine vessel registration, DNR is the primary implementer of the new transfer-on-death (TOD) designation for vessels, including processing applications and adopting necessary regulations.
The MVA is the primary agency responsible for motor vehicle titling and is mandated by the bill to expand its existing TOD program to include co-owned vehicles.

The bill allows vessels and vehicles to be transferred outside of probate, directly impacting the Register's core mission of estate administration and reducing the collection of probate fees and inheritance taxes.

As the parent agency of the MVA, MDOT is responsible for the fiscal oversight of the Transportation Trust Fund, which will see an increase in revenue from title fees associated with new TOD designations.

The AOC supports the judicial branch, including the Orphans' Courts which handle estate disputes; moving assets out of probate changes the scope of judicial proceedings for these specific property types.

As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for oversight of state revenues, which may see a decrease in inheritance tax and probate fees redirected from the General Fund.

DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and revenue estimation; it must monitor the bill's impact on both the General Fund and special funds like the State Boat Act Fund and the Transportation Trust Fund.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to the DNR and MVA for the drafting of regulations and the implementation of procedures for the new beneficiary designations.

Synopsis: Increasing from $300 to $600 the maximum amount of a credit against the State income tax that an individual may claim for certain expenses incurred for a donation of deer meat to certain organizations; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax Credit - Venison Donation - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Meat, Poultry, Seafood -see also- Clams; Crabs; Food; Oyster

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum state income tax credit that an individual may claim for expenses incurred to butcher and process antlerless deer for donation to a non-profit venison donation program from $300 to $600 per taxable year.
responsible_party: Comptroller’s Office
stakeholders: Hunters who harvest and donate antlerless deer; 501(c)(3) venison donation programs; and food-insecure individuals who receive donated venison.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $125,000 annually from fiscal year 2027 through fiscal year 2029 due to the increase in the maximum tax credit claimed. There is no impact on local government finances. The Comptroller’s Office can implement the bill's changes using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the State income tax credit. The bill requires venison donation programs to report specific information to the Comptroller annually and involves processing tax credits for qualified expenses.

The bill's eligibility for the tax credit is contingent upon compliance with State hunting laws and regulations and 'deer management permits,' which are governed and administered by the Department of Natural Resources. DNR also manages a related grant program for venison donation.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The bill is projected to decrease general fund revenues by $125,000 annually, which directly impacts the state budget managed by DBM.

The Maryland Food Center Authority, which manages regional food industry facilities and distribution, was a consulted stakeholder in the fiscal analysis for this bill, as it relates to the infrastructure of food distribution for charitable organizations.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget; the reduction in general fund revenue from this tax credit alteration must be accounted for in the Governor's fiscal planning.

Synopsis: Altering the procedures for the selection of presidential elector nominees and alternate presidential elector nominees; requiring the State Administrator of Elections to preside and serve as secretary at a certain meeting of certain presidential electors; altering the procedures for the meeting of presidential electors; and establishing procedures for the preparation, delivery, signing, and transmission of an amended certificate of ascertainment after the vote of the State's presidential electors under certain circumstances.
Title: Election Law - Presidential Electors - Selection and Voting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill updates the selection and voting processes for Maryland's presidential electors and alternates. It requires electors to pledge to vote for the candidates who nominated them, establishes procedures for filling vacancies if an elector is absent or violates their pledge, and designates the State Administrator of Elections to preside over the electors' meeting.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Presidential elector nominees, alternate presidential elector nominees, political parties, unaffiliated presidential candidates, and the Governor's Office.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the State Board of Elections can implement its requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the State Administrator of Elections as the official responsible for presiding over the presidential electors' meeting, serving as secretary, preparing certificates of ascertainment, and verifying the consistency of ballots with electors' pledges.
The Governor is responsible for certifying the state's presidential electors and signing both the original and any amended certificates of ascertainment as required by the revised procedures.

The bill requires the Clerk of the Supreme Court of Maryland, whose operations are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, to administer the constitutional oath to the presidential electors before they cast their votes.

As the state's primary legal representative, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and the Governor regarding the implementation of and compliance with these new election procedures.
The Secretary of State acts as the custodian of the Great Seal and official state records, which include the certifications and commissions of the presidential electors.
The bill mandates that presidential electors meet in the State House in Annapolis, a facility whose public areas and use are overseen by the State House Trust.
The Department of General Services is responsible for the maintenance and management of the State House facility and provides security through the Maryland Capitol Police for the meeting of electors.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to file a petition for expungement of a disposition under a certain provision of law if the disposition was included in a case that was disposed of by the court with a no finding designation or designated by the court as having been terminated without finding.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Expungement - No Finding and Case Terminated Without Finding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the expungement of criminal records to include charges for specific offenses when the court disposition is recorded as 'no finding' or the case is designated as 'terminated without finding.'
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals with criminal records containing 'no finding' or 'terminated without finding' court designations, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $11,700 in fiscal 2027 for the Judiciary to update brochures, forms, and instructional videos. There may be an indeterminate operational impact on the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to a potential increase in expungement petitions. Local government finances and operations are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's changes within the Judiciary. It must update case management systems to accommodate 'no finding' and 'terminated without finding' designations and incurs a specific fiscal impact for revising expungement-related brochures, forms, and instructional materials.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) is responsible for processing and executing expungement orders for criminal records across the state. The bill's expansion of eligibility directly impacts the Department's operational workload for record removal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in criminal and expungement proceedings. Its attorneys and staff will be responsible for filing the expanded petitions for expungement authorized under this bill.

The Maryland State Police is a primary custodian of police records subject to expungement orders. The agency must comply with court orders to remove or restrict access to records for eligible dispositions.

The Motor Vehicle Administration maintains driving and vehicle records. Because the bill includes offenses from the Transportation Article as eligible for expungement, the MVA is a key custodian responsible for implementing expungement orders related to those records.

The Maryland State Archives serves as the central depository for permanent judicial and executive records. Expungement orders require the Archives to remove or restrict access to historical records related to the affected cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for criminal justice policy and advises the Governor on public safety strategies. The expansion of expungement eligibility is a significant policy shift within their purview.

As the parent agency for the Motor Vehicle Administration and other modal administrations, the Department of Transportation oversees the records and law enforcement activities impacted by the expungement of transportation-related offenses.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and will likely provide guidance on the legal interpretation of 'no finding' and 'terminated without finding' as used in the bill.

The bill includes offenses related to the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, such as possession with intent to distribute cannabis, as eligible for expungement. The Administration is relevant as the primary regulator for this industry.

The bill explicitly includes various offenses from the Natural Resources Article (related to hunting, boating, and speed limits) as eligible for expungement, impacting the records maintained by the Department and the Natural Resources Police.

The bill allows for the expungement of offenses related to business regulation and occupational licensing. As the agency overseeing these boards and commissions, the Department's background check and regulatory processes are impacted by the removal of these records.

The bill includes specific Election Law Article violations as eligible for expungement. The Board of Elections is the state's oversight body for the integrity of the electoral process and related records.

The State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes offenses related to election integrity and public ethics. Several offenses within the State Prosecutor's jurisdiction are listed as eligible for expungement under the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state agency expenditures and personnel. It is relevant due to the general fund expenditure noted in the fiscal analysis for implementing the bill's requirements.

The Governor is responsible for overseeing the executive branch agencies implementing the bill and for the final approval of the annual state budget, which includes the funds required for the Judiciary's updates.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a merchant, in a certain transaction between the hours of 6 a.m. and 10 p.m., from prohibiting a person from making a cash payment to purchase an essential consumer good, requiring a person to purchase an essential consumer good by using a credit or debit card, or charging or collecting from a person a higher price than for an equivalent cashless transaction for making a cash payment for the purchase of an essential consumer good; establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice; etc.
Title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions for Essential Consumer Goods - Cash Payments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland retailers to accept cash for in-person purchases of essential items like food, water, hygiene products, medicine, and fuel if the total is under $300 and occurs between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Retailers cannot charge higher prices for cash transactions. The law, enforced by the Attorney General, includes specific exceptions for online sales, vending machines, and certain specialty stores, and allows merchants to provide cash-to-card conversion machines instead of accepting physical cash.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Division of Consumer Protection
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, retail merchants selling essential goods, and small businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's penalty provisions are not expected to have a material impact on state or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources. Small businesses may experience a meaningful operational impact if they are required to transition from electronic-only to cash-accepting transaction models.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Division of Consumer Protection within the Office of the Attorney General with enforcing the new cash payment requirements, including a mandated process of providing two opportunities to comply before assessing civil penalties.

The Governor oversaw the development of this policy initiative and signed the bill into law; the Governor's Office also oversees the executive branch departments responsible for consumer protection and economic regulation.

The bill designates 'fuel' as an essential consumer good subject to the cash payment mandate. The Comptroller is the primary regulator of the motor fuel industry in Maryland and ensures compliance among fuel merchants.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by new regulations on retail transactions that affect business operations and the state's commercial climate.

The bill defines 'essential consumer goods' to include health products, medicine, and medical supplies. The Department of Health regulates pharmacies and health care facilities that function as retail merchants and will be subject to these payment rules.

The Department of Labor regulates various retail industries and protects consumers and the public; it is relevant because the bill alters the legal requirements for businesses when conducting transactions with the public.

The bill establishes civil penalties for merchants who fail to comply with cash payment requirements. If merchants contest these fines or enforcement actions by the OAG, the Office of Administrative Hearings would provide the impartial adjudication process.

Synopsis: Requiring a unit of State government to provide a certain debriefing of a contract award to certain persons on request; adding an exemption to the prohibition on an individual who assists in the drafting of specifications, an invitation for bids, or a request for proposals from submitting a bid or proposal or assisting in the submission of a bid or proposal; requiring a procurement contract to include a certain clause pertaining to certain contract modifications related to changes in State law; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Transparency and Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland state procurement laws by requiring government units to provide debriefings to unsuccessful bidders before contract approval. It also establishes new requirements for contract modifications related to changes in state law, alters the timeframes and procedures for filing contract claims and protests, and provides exemptions for individuals providing specific information during the solicitation process to avoid ethics violations.
responsible_party: Office of State Procurement within the Department of General Services
stakeholders: State agencies, procurement officers, and businesses or individuals bidding on or performing state government contracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state expenditures are not expected to increase for the implementation of the bill as it can be handled with existing resources. However, changes to procurement ethics requirements may lead to an increase in bid protests, which could result in project delays and indeterminate cost overruns. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the administrative procedures, timelines, and final action definitions for procurement protests and contract claims, which are the primary matters adjudicated by this Board.
The Department houses the Office of State Procurement, which is specifically mandated by the bill to establish guidelines and procedures for debriefings of unsuccessful offerors.
The bill explicitly requires procurement officers to seek the advice of the Office of the Attorney General on legal issues raised during bid protests and contract claims.

The Board oversees significant state contracts; the bill requires debriefings to be provided before awards are presented to the Board and alters the handling of contract modifications and claims that come under its purview.

As a major procurement unit with extensive construction and service contracts, MDOT is significantly impacted by changes to change order procedures, equitable adjustments, and the extension of construction claim rules to other contract types.
As a principal procurement unit and the agency responsible for state fiscal policy, DBM is directly impacted by the revised procedures for managing contract modifications, protests, and claims.
As the primary procurement unit for state IT infrastructure, DoIT is impacted by the transparency requirements for debriefings and revised timelines for contract disputes.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees the approval of the contracts affected by these new transparency and modification procedures.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer is responsible for reviewing and approving procurements impacted by the bill's new debriefing and claim certification requirements.
The Governor chairs the Board of Public Works and oversees the executive units that must implement these new procurement transparency and protest procedures.
The University System is a major state procurement entity that must adapt its internal review processes for protests and contract claims to meet the bill's new statutory timelines.
OLA will be responsible for auditing state agencies to ensure compliance with the bill's new transparency requirements, debriefing guidelines, and contract claim procedures.
As a large department with significant procurement activity, MDH must adjust its procurement officer workflows to accommodate the bill's mandates on debriefings and legal consultations.
DHS manages numerous social service contracts and will be impacted by the changes to procurement ethics exemptions and claim filing procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's operational and facility contracts will be subject to the bill's new requirements for equitable adjustments and certified claims.
DNR's procurement units must follow the new timelines for resolving bid protests and issuing final agency actions as defined in the bill.
MDE manages various infrastructure and service contracts that will be subject to the bill's new procedures for change orders and contract modifications.
The department's procurement activities for economic development initiatives are subject to the bill's transparency and dispute resolution reforms.
The agency's procurement of services and systems must comply with the new debriefing requirements and the altered timelines for contract claim recovery.
MSDE is impacted by the bill's specific provisions regarding the procurement of educational and social services and the use of requests for information.
The agency's procurement operations must adapt to the new requirement that debriefings occur before contract awards are finalized.
MSP's procurement of equipment and services is impacted by the bill's changes to bid protest procedures and final agency action reviews.
DHCD's procurement of community development and infrastructure support services will be subject to the bill's revised contract claim certification requirements.
DJS is affected by the procedural changes for social service contract solicitations and the new impasse notice requirements for claims.
The department's procurement officers must follow the new guidelines for debriefings and the revised timelines for responding to vendor protests.
While independent, the Judiciary's procurement support agency is affected by changes to state procurement laws that govern inter-branch procedures and auditing standards.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to develop, publish, and maintain a real property flood risk disclosure statement form that includes certain information about a property's flood risk and history; and requiring, beginning July, 1, 2027, a vendor of certain residential real property to provide the purchaser with a completed real property flood risk disclosure statement form before entering into a contract for the sale of the property.
Title: Sale of Residential Real Property - Required Flood Risk Disclosure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to develop and maintain a real property flood risk disclosure form for residential real estate transactions. Starting July 1, 2027, sellers of residential properties with four or fewer units are required to provide this form to purchasers before a contract of sale is signed. The form includes information on whether the property is in a 100-year or 500-year floodplain, history of flood damage claims, and the availability of FEMA elevation certificates.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Purchasers and vendors of residential real property with four or fewer single-family units, and the Maryland Department of the Environment
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances, and the small business impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of the Environment (MDE) develop, publish, and maintain the real property flood risk disclosure statement form. MDE is the primary agency responsible for the administrative implementation of this law.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is responsible for enforcing disclosure laws in real estate transactions. Failure to provide the required flood risk disclosure could lead to consumer complaints and enforcement actions handled by this office.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Real Estate Commission, which regulates real estate licensees. Brokers and agents will be responsible for ensuring these new disclosure forms are completed and provided during residential property sales.

The bill creates new statutory requirements for contracts of sale under the Real Property Article. Disputes regarding the failure to disclose flood risks or inaccuracies in the disclosure form could lead to increased litigation within the state court system.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of the Environment and other implementing agencies. The Governor also plays a role in signing the legislation and coordinating the executive branch's response to flood management and climate resilience policies.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Baltimore County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on certain real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Baltimore County – Property Tax Credit – Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing body of Baltimore County to grant a 100% property tax credit for the real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 located at 730 Wampler Road in Middle River, Maryland.
responsible_party: Governing body of Baltimore County
stakeholders: Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 and Baltimore County government
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state fiscal impact. Baltimore County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $9,600 annually starting in fiscal 2027 if the county grants the credit. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for the final approval and signing of the bill into law, and it oversees the executive branch agencies that may be involved in administering property tax policy.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors all legislation that affects revenue and fiscal policy, including local property tax credits that could have long-term implications for the state's fiscal landscape.

The Maryland Tax Court is the state's highest level of administrative review for tax disputes and would hear any final administrative appeals regarding the eligibility or application of this property tax credit.

The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is the independent agency that hears disputes over property tax credits at the local level, such as those that might arise from the implementation of this credit in Baltimore County.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state tax boards and represents the state in court should any legal challenges arise regarding the property tax credit or its statutory interpretation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting, or obtaining an individual for the purpose of appropriating the government benefits of an individual for the benefit of the person or another through deception, coercion, exploitation, or isolation; prohibiting a person from aiding, abetting, or conspiring with one or more persons to violate a certain provision of the Act; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Benefits Exploitation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: This bill creates the crime of benefits exploitation, making it illegal to knowingly recruit, harbor, transport, or obtain an individual through deception, coercion, exploitation, or isolation for the purpose of taking their government benefits. It also prohibits benefiting financially from such acts or conspiring to commit them, establishing criminal penalties ranging from a misdemeanor to a felony based on the total value of the benefits appropriated.
responsible_party: Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals receiving government benefits (such as Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, SNAP, and veterans benefits), the Maryland Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,573 in fiscal 2027 only for one-time computer programming changes within the Judiciary. Beyond this, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal offenses and graduated penalties that will be adjudicated within the state court system. The fiscal note explicitly identifies a requirement for one-time computer programming within the Judiciary to implement these changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As an agency responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants, the creation of new criminal offenses for benefits exploitation will directly impact their workload. The fiscal note mentions the agency's assessment that additional attorneys may be required to handle cases generated by this bill.

The bill specifically defines 'government benefits' to include several programs administered by this agency, including TANF, SNAP, TDAP, and Public Assistance to Adults. The agency is the primary provider for individuals in economic need who are the targets of the exploitation prohibited by this bill.

The OAG is the state's chief legal officer and is responsible for protecting consumers and vulnerable adults. The fiscal note highlights the OAG's existing authority and specialized units, such as the Senior and Vulnerable Adult Asset Recovery Unit, which are relevant to the investigation and civil prosecution of the types of exploitation addressed in this criminal bill.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating criminal violations of state law, including the newly established felonies and misdemeanors related to benefits exploitation.

The bill protects Medicare and Medicaid benefits, both of which are central to the department's public health and healthcare financing responsibilities. MDH also regulates health care facilities where such exploitation of elderly or disabled individuals may occur.

The bill explicitly includes 'veterans benefits' as a protected category under government benefits. This agency is responsible for assisting veterans in securing and protecting these benefits and advocating for their well-being.

The bill provides protections against the exploitation of 'elderly' adults, a primary demographic served by this department. The agency's long-term care advocacy and support services are directly related to preventing the type of financial harm and coercion defined in the bill.

The bill's definition of coercion includes exerting financial control over a 'disabled' adult. The department is the principal agency responsible for coordinating services and protecting the rights of Maryland residents with disabilities, who are frequently targets of benefits exploitation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new felony and misdemeanor charges with substantial prison sentences (up to 20 years). This agency will be responsible for the incarceration and supervision of individuals convicted under these new provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this office is involved in policy development to reduce crime and recidivism. This bill introduces a specific strategy to address financial crimes against vulnerable populations.

The bill lists 'pension benefits' as a protected government benefit. This agency manages the retirement and pension system for hundreds of thousands of members, making the protection of these distributions relevant to their administrative mission.

This agency determines eligibility for Medicaid, which is one of the primary 'government benefits' listed in the bill. Exploitation schemes often involve the improper use of these health coverage enrollments.

This team's mission is specifically focused on identifying novel ways to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility. Benefits exploitation (such as SNAP and TANF) directly undermines the effectiveness of state programs aimed at these goals.

This independent agency investigates and prosecutes offenses related to the integrity of state institutions. If benefits exploitation involved state employees or systemic corruption within state-administered benefit programs, the State Prosecutor would have jurisdiction.
The office focuses on child well-being and reducing poverty. Exploitation of benefits like TANF and WIC, which are intended to support children and families, falls within their policy purview.

The bill's definition of coercion includes the confiscation of government identification documents. The MVA is the primary state agency responsible for issuing and regulating these identification documents.

The Register of Wills manages probate records and estate administration. Cases of benefits exploitation often impact the assets and pensions of decedents' estates, which are processed through this agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency manages supplemental pension and retirement plans. Because 'pension benefits' are specifically listed in the bill, the exploitation of participants in these voluntary plans is a relevant concern.

This program provides portable retirement and emergency savings accounts for workers. These accounts function similarly to the pension benefits protected by the bill, making the prevention of their exploitation relevant.

The bill's definition of coercion includes providing a 'controlled dangerous substance' to an individual to compel them to act against their will. This agency is responsible for regulating these substances to ensure they are used only for legitimate purposes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for the welfare of Deaf and hard of hearing residents, many of whom receive disability-related government benefits. The bill's protections against exploitation via 'isolation' or 'deception' are particularly relevant to this community.

Synopsis: Altering the date, from November 30 to October 1 each year, by which the Office of the Attorney General must report on certain activities of the Office's Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit and certain activities taken by the Department of the Environment and the Department of Natural Resources in response to findings of the Unit.
Title: Office of the Attorney General - Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit - Reporting Requirement

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: This bill changes the annual deadline for the Office of the Attorney General to submit a report on the activities of the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit from November 30 to October 1. It also requires the report to cover activities from the previous fiscal year and include any actions taken by the Maryland Department of the Environment or the Department of Natural Resources based on the unit's findings.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland Department of the Environment, Department of Natural Resources, the Governor, and the Maryland General Assembly
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State operations or finances. According to the Fiscal Note, there is no impact on local governments or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is a direct recipient of the annual report mandated by this bill.

The Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit is located within the Office of the Attorney General. The Attorney General is responsible for submitting the annual report affected by this legislation.
The bill requires the annual report to include specific actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to findings and recommendations made by the Attorney General's unit.

The bill requires the annual report to include specific actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations made by the Attorney General's unit. Additionally, the reporting date is specifically altered to align with this department's existing reporting schedule.

Synopsis: Authorizing the installation of individual water submeters, used to determine the actual use of water, for each residential unit in an apartment house and mobile home parks; prohibiting the owner, operator, or manager of an apartment house, or mobile home park, or a contractor hired by the owner, operator, or manager, from imposing certain costs on a unit; authorizing the owner, operator, or manager of an apartment house or mobile home park to bill an occupant a certain amount under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Environment - Water - Individual Submeters

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Water -see also- Coastal Bays; Riv,Str,Lks; Wastewater; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the installation of individual water submeters in apartment houses and mobile home parks to fairly allocate water consumption costs based on actual usage. It restricts owners or managers from charging occupants more than the actual utility costs plus a $1 monthly administrative fee, prohibits charging for common area usage or maintenance leaks, and mandates specific record-keeping and disclosure requirements for landlords.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners, operators, and managers of apartment houses and mobile home parks; residential tenants; local housing authorities; and water service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates that the bill's requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues and expenditures are not anticipated to be materially affected. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, as it is tasked with adopting regulations and standards for the accuracy, testing, and record-keeping of individual water submeters.
DHCD must be consulted by MDE during the regulatory process and is also granted authority to approve the installation of submeters by local housing authorities.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division is explicitly named as a state-level body responsible for handling complaints from occupants regarding water submeter billing and violations if local agencies lack jurisdiction.
The Board of Public Works is given specific authority in the bill to approve the installation of individual submeters by local housing authorities.

The bill creates a private cause of action for residents and establishes new requirements for written leases and billing disclosures, which will impact the adjudication of landlord-tenant disputes in the court system.
The Governor, as a member of the Board of Public Works, is responsible for the oversight and approval of submeter installations by local housing authorities as specified in the bill.
The State Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works, which is tasked with approving submetering initiatives for local housing authorities.
The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works, which must approve the installation of individual submeters by local housing authorities.
The bill defines 'water service providers' to include water companies regulated by the PSC, and the legislation parallels existing PSC authority over electricity and gas submetering.

Synopsis: Continuing the Maryland Horse Industry Board in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2036, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: Maryland Horse Industry Board - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Maryland Horse Industry Board by 10 years, from July 1, 2026, to July 1, 2036, allowing the board to continue its regulatory, licensing, and promotional activities for the state's equine industry.
responsible_party: Maryland Horse Industry Board within the Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Owners and operators of more than 800 licensed horse stables, equine industry participants, and researchers in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the board from fiscal 2027 through 2036. The fiscal 2027 budget as introduced includes $435,471 in special funds and $12,298 in federal funds for the board's operation. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board (MHIB) is a unit within the Department of Agriculture. As the primary implementing agency, the Department is responsible for the board's operations, licensing, and inspections of horse stables, and it requested this departmental bill to extend the board's authority.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board is an ongoing regulatory and advisory body within the executive branch. This bill directly concerns the extension of its statutory and regulatory authority.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budget and personnel for state boards. This bill maintains special and federal fund expenditures of approximately $447,000 for the operation of the MHIB through 2036.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Agriculture. The Governor also signed this bill into law and is responsible for appointing members to various state boards such as the MHIB.
The OAG provides legal counsel and representation to all state agencies, boards, and commissions, including the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Horse Industry Board.

The Comptroller acts as the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector. The agency is responsible for processing the revenues and expenditures of the Maryland Horse Industry Fund maintained by this bill.
The Treasurer's Office is the custodian of state funds, including special funds like the Maryland Horse Industry Fund, and manages the receipt and investment of these revenues.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Disabilities to establish affordable and accessible housing programs; authorizing the Department to establish one or more affiliated foundations to work with certain programs and units of the Department to solicit and accept funds, partner with individuals and entities, and promote certain activities that support certain projects; prohibiting an affiliated foundation from influencing determinations regarding eligibility for any program, benefit, or services administered by the Department; etc.
Title: Department of Disabilities - Housing Programs and Affiliated Foundations - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Disabilities to establish and oversee affordable and accessible housing programs. It also authorizes the department to create affiliated foundations to solicit and accept private or public funds and partner with entities to support innovative projects in assistive technology, disability employment policy, and accessible housing.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities, the Maryland Department of Disabilities, and collaborating businesses, governmental entities, and nonprofit organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's requirements can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources. However, if an affiliated foundation is established and provides contributions, Maryland Department of Disabilities special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount. Additionally, the department must hire an independent certified public accountant to audit established foundations, which may result in a minimal, indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures. The bill does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Disabilities to submit an annual report to the Governor regarding the implementation of the new housing programs and the activities of any affiliated foundations, including the service of State employees on their boards.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for budget execution and personnel management. The fiscal note indicates that MDOD may require general fund expenditures for the annual audits of affiliated foundations, which falls under DBM's oversight of state spending and agency resources.

This bill directly mandates the Department of Disabilities to establish and oversee affordable and accessible housing programs and authorizes it to create affiliated foundations to support its various offices and programs. The department is responsible for developing operating policies, hiring auditors, and reporting on these new entities.

The bill's focus on establishing affordable and accessible housing programs for individuals with disabilities overlaps with the mission of the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), which is responsible for ensuring residents have access to safe and affordable housing.

The bill requires the Secretary of Disabilities to receive and deposit funds from affiliated foundations into a separate special fund. The State Treasurer's Office, as the chief financial agency responsible for receiving and depositing state funds, will be involved in the management of these new accounts.
The Office of the Attorney General is explicitly required by the bill to review and approve the operating policies for any newly established affiliated foundations for form and legal sufficiency.

The bill grants the State Ethics Commission a direct regulatory role, requiring it to review and approve conflict-of-interest policies for the foundations and oversee the service of State employees as directors of these foundations. It also receives an annual report on these matters.

Synopsis: Expanding the authority of the Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service to delegate certain functions to the Deputy Treasurer of the Service; increasing the threshold amount from $25,000 to $50,000 or less for estimated contract costs under which the Service may use the small procurement process; and altering the process for providing notice of the establishment or adjustment of certain rates charged for Service projects, products, or services.
Title: Maryland Environmental Service - Authorizations and Requirements - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: The bill expands the authority of the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) Treasurer to delegate financial duties to the Deputy Treasurer, increases the threshold for MES small procurement contracts from $25,000 to $50,000, and updates the public notification requirements for rate changes within service districts to include digital and direct mail options.
responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Service (MES)
stakeholders: Residents and ratepayers in Maryland Environmental Service districts, MES administrative staff, and vendors or contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no material effect on state or local finances. The Maryland Environmental Service may experience administrative efficiencies as the higher small procurement threshold allows it to more quickly acquire goods and services for approximately 26 percent of its contracts that fall within the $25,000 to $50,000 range.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill for the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) that directly alters its internal governance, increases its small procurement threshold, and modernizes its public notice requirements for rate adjustments.

The bill explicitly requires the MES Treasurer to be covered by a surety bond or insurance in an amount determined by the State Treasurer and mandates that MES funds be deposited in financial institutions authorized by the State Treasurer.
The Board of Public Works oversees state procurement and financial integrity; this bill alters the small procurement threshold for MES, which is an independent state instrumentality.

MES provides environmental services such as water and wastewater management that are regulated by the Department of the Environment, which was also consulted as an information source for this legislation.
The Department of Transportation is a primary user of MES services and was consulted for the fiscal analysis regarding potential administrative and procurement efficiencies.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from slaughtering or causing the slaughter of a racehorse in the State for certain commercial purposes; prohibiting a person from purchasing, selling, transferring, offering for sale, importing into the State, or transporting a racehorse if the person knows or reasonably should know that the racehorse will be slaughtered for certain commercial purposes; requiring certain fines collected by the State Racing Commission to be distributed to the racing Special Fund; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the slaughter of racehorses for commercial purposes, such as human or animal consumption, and bans the sale, purchase, or transport of racehorses intended for slaughter. It establishes criminal penalties for violations, including fines and imprisonment, and authorizes the State Racing Commission and the Department of Agriculture to suspend or revoke licenses of those who violate the act.
responsible_party: State Racing Commission and Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Racehorse owners, breeders, trainers, licensed veterinarians, horse transport businesses, and the Maryland racing industry.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the horse racing special fund may increase starting in fiscal 2027 based on collected fines. Individual fines range from $1,000 to $2,000, while corporate or entity fines range from $2,500 to $5,000 per offense. State expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Racing Commission, which is the primary body responsible for adopting regulations, collecting fines, and suspending or revoking licenses for violations of the racehorse slaughter prohibition.

The Department of Agriculture is explicitly authorized to revoke or suspend licenses of persons who violate the prohibition and must be consulted by the Racing Commission in the adoption of implementing regulations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and Department of Agriculture, and would be involved in drafting regulations and advising on the enforcement of the new criminal and administrative penalties.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including the new misdemeanor offenses related to the illegal slaughter, transport, or sale of racehorses.
The judicial branch will be responsible for adjudicating the misdemeanor criminal cases and managing the collection of court-imposed fines established by the bill.

The Office of Administrative Hearings would conduct hearings for individuals or entities that contest the revocation or suspension of their licenses by the Racing Commission or Department of Agriculture.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller's office manages the collection and distribution of state revenues, including the fines directed to the racing Special Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department would be responsible for the supervision of individuals convicted of the misdemeanor offense if a sentence of imprisonment is imposed.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for overseeing the fiscal impact of the bill on the state budget, including the potential increase in special fund revenues from fines.

Synopsis: Increasing, from $4,000,000,000 to $5,000,000,000, the limit on the amount of certain revenue bonds that the Maryland Transportation Authority may have outstanding and unpaid on June 30 each year; etc.
Title: Maryland Transportation Authority - Revenue Bond Limit - Increase

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Public Debt -see also- County & Balt City Bonds; State Bonds
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill increases the statutory limit on the amount of outstanding revenue bonds the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) may carry from $4 billion to $5 billion. The increase is intended to provide MDTA with the necessary financial flexibility to fund capital projects, including the reconstruction of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, while awaiting federal reimbursements.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA)
stakeholders: Maryland Transportation Authority, the Maryland Department of Transportation, toll facility users, and construction contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases MDTA's debt capacity by $1,000,000,000. Consequently, MDTA nonbudgeted revenues will increase as bonds are issued, with current projections suggesting this will occur starting in fiscal 2029. Nonbudgeted expenditures will also increase to pay the debt service on these additional bonds. This measure may also prevent or delay the need for toll increases that would otherwise be required to fund MDTA's capital program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary subject of the bill, which directly increases its revenue bond debt capacity from $4 billion to $5 billion to fund capital projects and bridge reconstruction.
As the parent department of the Maryland Transportation Authority, MDOT requested this departmental bill to manage its long-term capital program and respond to federal reimbursement uncertainties.

The Treasurer's Office is the state's chief financial agency, responsible for the management of state funds and bond sale revenue; the agency was also a primary information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state and is responsible for long-term fiscal planning and supervising budget execution, both of which are impacted by changes to state debt capacity.
The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and is a member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees the state's fiscal integrity and major financial transactions.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and protects the state's fiscal integrity, including the landscape of state bond issuances.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and departments like MDOT, proposed the legislation as a departmental request, and ultimately approved the bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies, including MDOT and MDTA, regarding the legal sufficiency and implementation of debt capacity changes.

Synopsis: Delaying the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029-2030 financial aid award year.
Title: Higher Education - Guaranteed Access Grant Program - Applicability

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill delays the transfer of administrative responsibilities for the Guaranteed Access Grant Program—specifically award notification and issuance—from the Maryland Higher Education Commission to institutions of higher education until the 2029–2030 financial aid award year.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Low-income undergraduate students eligible for Guaranteed Access Grants and Maryland institutions of higher education, including public universities, community colleges, and nonpublic institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures and revenues associated with the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program are delayed until fiscal 2029. This includes the postponement of programming costs for the Maryland College Aid Processing System and administrative staffing costs at institutions of higher education. While the transfer is delayed, the Maryland Higher Education Commission continues to incur costs for the centralized administration of the program. Specific dollar estimates were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for state financial aid, MHEC is directly responsible for the Guaranteed Access Grant Program. The bill delays the decentralization of this program, requiring MHEC to continue central administration, award notification, and issuance through the 2029-2030 award year.
USM institutions are the primary entities slated to take over the administration of GA Grants. The bill delays this administrative transfer and the associated funding until FY 2029.

As an independent public university, Morgan State is directly impacted by the delay in taking over GA Grant award notification and issuance responsibilities, as well as the delay in receiving state funds to support this administrative function.

As an independent public honors college, the institution is impacted by the delay in the decentralization of the GA Grant program, which defers its role in award notification and the receipt of related administrative funding.

DBM is responsible for state budget development. The bill results in a delay of planned general fund expenditures that were intended to support the administrative costs of grant decentralization at public institutions.

MSDE works with MHEC on the prequalification process for GA Grants, particularly identifying eligible students in middle and high school. The administrative timeline of the overall program is relevant to their coordination efforts.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MHEC and would be responsible for reviewing the regulations MHEC is required to adopt to implement the bill's provisions.

The MLDS Center tracks student financial aid data from MHEC to analyze educational and workforce outcomes. A multi-year delay in the decentralization of a major grant program affects their data collection and longitudinal studies.

As a departmental bill requested by an executive agency (MHEC) and signed by the Governor, the office oversees the executive branch's policy initiatives and the annual budget process, which are impacted by this administrative delay.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland National Guard's tuition assistance program by including 'training assistance' for expenses such as industry-required tools, technology, professional equipment, and certification costs. It also broadens the definition of eligible institutions to include any trade or career school recognized by the Maryland Higher Education Commission or the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council, removing the requirement that private institutions must provide a tuition waiver of at least 50% to participate.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department
stakeholders: Active members of the Maryland National Guard and Maryland-recognized private career, trade, and vocational schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances because assistance is authorized only to the extent that funds are provided in the State budget. According to the fiscal note, the fiscal 2025, 2026, and 2027 budgets include 600000 for tuition assistance to members of the Maryland National Guard.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is the primary authority responsible for certifying eligibility for National Guard members and administering the expanded tuition and training assistance program created by this bill.

The bill directly affects the service members of the Maryland National Guard by expanding the types of institutions they can attend and the specific expenses (training assistance for equipment and certifications) that the state will reimburse.
The bill expands the program to include private career schools recognized by the Commission and relies on its regulatory oversight to define eligible institutions.

The bill extends eligibility to institutions recognized by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC), which is housed within the Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.

This agency is responsible for advocating for and assisting active-duty service members and their families in securing benefits; the bill represents a significant expansion of those educational and professional benefits.
USM institutions are specifically named as eligible participants in the tuition assistance program and will be responsible for processing these benefits for enrolled Guard members.
Morgan State University is explicitly named as an eligible institution for the National Guard tuition and training assistance program.
St. Mary's College is explicitly named as an eligible institution for the National Guard tuition and training assistance program.
The department oversees the budget execution for the tuition assistance program, which is funded based on state budget allocations ($600,000 annually).

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that a certain police employee or deputy State fire marshal is entitled to a certain pay rate on promotion to a higher rank if a certain other police employee or deputy State fire marshal in the same rank is at a lower pay rate.
Title: Public Safety - Police Employees and Deputy State Fire Marshals - Repeal of Pay Rate Restriction on Promotion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
