Synopsis: Providing for command and control of State active duty personnel during mobilizations of the Maryland National Guard.
Title: Maryland Military Department – Supervision of State Active Duty Personnel

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill clarifies and codifies the chain of command for the Maryland Military Department during State active duty. It specifies that all units, including the National Guard and the Maryland Defense Force, are under the operational command and control of the Adjutant General or a designated officer, even if the Adjutant General is in a federal status where the Governor remains the Commander in Chief.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard, the Maryland Defense Force, State Operations personnel, the Adjutant General, and local law enforcement authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact because it codifies existing practice within the Maryland Military Department to ensure operational effectiveness during emergency mobilizations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is the primary official whose command and control authority is defined and clarified by this bill, specifically regarding the supervision of personnel during State active duty while in a federal status.
The bill directly governs the operational command structure and supervision of Maryland National Guard members when they are ordered into State active duty.

The Governor serves as the commander-in-chief of Maryland's military forces and holds the authority to order the militia into State active duty; this bill establishes the subordinate command structure for those operations.

The bill maintains provisions that allow ranking military officers on State active duty to direct and control the Maryland State Police under specific emergency exigencies and subject to the Governor's order.

Synopsis: Providing that a manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch may not take an adverse action against a dealer for disclosing on its website that the advertised price of a vehicle is the manufacturer's minimum allowable advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price for the vehicle.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Prices Listed on Dealer Websites (Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: The Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act prohibits vehicle manufacturers, distributors, or factory branches from taking adverse action against a motor vehicle dealer for disclosing on its website that an advertised price is the manufacturer's minimum allowable price and that the dealer may offer a lower price. This protection is contingent on the dealer not violating laws regarding false, deceptive, or misleading advertising.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, licensed vehicle dealers, and consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The impact on small business is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary regulator for vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and dealers in Maryland. This bill directly amends the sections of the Transportation Article that the MVA is responsible for enforcing, specifically regarding the conduct and licensing standards between manufacturers and dealers.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT oversees the state's vehicle laws and regulatory framework. The agency is responsible for the overall policy direction in this sector and was identified as a primary information source for the legislation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and MVA. Additionally, the agency's Consumer Protection Division is concerned with advertising transparency and business practices, which are directly impacted by the bill's requirements for price disclosure on dealer websites.

OAH is responsible for adjudicating contested administrative cases involving state agencies like the MVA. Disputes arising from regulatory enforcement or licensing challenges related to the new prohibitions in this bill would be heard by an Administrative Law Judge at OAH.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs legislation into law. As the bill regulates business practices within a significant state industry, it aligns with the office's role in coordinating policy initiatives and executive branch oversight.

Synopsis: Authorizing an address in this State supplied by a commercial mail receiving agency to be designated as the principal office of a Maryland corporation, limited liability company, limited liability partnership, or limited partnership; and defining "commercial mail receiving agency" as a person that is authorized by the U.S. Postal Service to accept delivery of mail on behalf of another person as a business service.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Principal Offices - Private Mailboxes

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill allows Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, and limited partnerships to use an address provided by a commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) as their principal office, provided they have a valid agreement with the CMRA in compliance with U.S. Postal Service regulations.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, limited partnerships, and commercial mail receiving agencies (CMRAs).
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues are expected to increase minimally in fiscal 2027 due to business entities paying a $25 filing fee to update their principal office address. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill without a material impact on expenditures. There is no fiscal impact on local governments. Small businesses operating as CMRAs may see a potential increase in business.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and signing legislation into law. This bill was approved by the Governor on April 28, 2026, and affects the regulatory framework for Maryland business entities.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is concerned with the ease of doing business in Maryland. Authorizing private mailboxes as principal offices affects business formation and administrative requirements for corporations and partnerships.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a potential meaningful impact on small businesses, particularly Commercial Mail Receiving Agencies (CMRAs), which will benefit from additional business generated by this change.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), which must implement this change in the legal definition of a principal office for business filings.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and tax collector. While the fiscal impact is minimal, the agency relies on accurate corporate records and principal office addresses for tax compliance and revenue collection.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency for Maryland. The bill has a minimal impact on special fund revenues from business filing fees, which DBM monitors as part of the state's long-term fiscal planning.

Synopsis: Requiring each local school system to identify, in its regular safety evaluation, issues of accessibility for individuals with disabilities; and requiring local school systems to include in a certain annual report instances in which a public school facility became inaccessible for a student with a disability in a manner that could impede evacuations or emergency response.
Title: Public Schools - Individuals With Disabilities - Accessibility and Emergency Planning

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland local school systems to identify accessibility issues for individuals with disabilities as part of their regular school safety evaluations and to report specific instances where facilities became inaccessible for students with disabilities in ways that could impede emergency responses or evacuations.
responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety and local school systems
stakeholders: Students with disabilities, school staff and visitors with disabilities, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) can implement the bill's requirements with existing resources. Local school systems are not expected to see a material financial impact because the bill does not change existing federal or state accessibility laws, only evaluation and reporting protocols.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local school systems to submit safety evaluations and annual reports concerning accessibility and emergency planning to the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS). MCSS is also tasked with consulting on updates to school emergency plans to correct identified weaknesses.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the public school system and the local school systems mentioned in the bill. Additionally, the Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within MSDE, and MSDE previously established the emergency planning guidelines referenced in the bill's implementation history.

The bill mandates that local school system safety coordinators coordinate with the Interagency Commission on School Construction's (IAC) facility assessment process when identifying issues with public school facilities that could impact safety and accessibility.

The bill is specifically focused on accessibility and emergency planning for individuals with disabilities. The Department of Disabilities is the principal agency for ensuring inclusive policies and accessibility across all state programs and services.

As the agency responsible for coordinating the state's preparedness and response for emergencies, the department has an interest in the updates to school emergency plans and evacuation protocols for vulnerable populations.

The bill includes provisions regarding the confidentiality of reports and exemptions from the Maryland Public Information Act, which may require legal interpretation and guidance from the Office of the Attorney General.
The Governor oversees the executive branch departments involved (MSDE, Disabilities, Emergency Management) and coordinates broad policy initiatives related to safety and accessibility.

The department oversees the state budget; while the fiscal note indicates the bill can be implemented with existing resources, any future capital or operational adjustments identified through the safety evaluations would involve DBM oversight.

Synopsis: Providing that a certain landlord may not refuse to rent to a prospective tenant who pays rent with the assistance of an income-based housing subsidy under certain circumstances, subject to a certain exception; establishing that a violation of the Act is a discriminatory housing practice and is subject to enforcement by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; and requiring that a certain landlord offer a certain tenant the option of having positive rental payment history reported to a certain consumer reporting agency.
Title: Landlord and Tenant - Discrimination in Housing for Income-Based Housing Subsidies and Positive Rental History Reporting

Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill prohibits landlords from refusing to rent to prospective tenants who use income-based housing subsidies based on their income, credit score, or certain credit history. Additionally, it requires landlords owning six or more residential rental units to offer tenants the option to have their positive rental payment history reported to a consumer reporting agency, for which the landlord may charge a monthly fee of up to $10 or the actual cost.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residential tenants, prospective tenants with income-based housing subsidies (such as Section 8 vouchers), and landlords owning six or more residential rental units.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) and the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations, including the workloads of the Judiciary and the Office of Administrative Hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Commission on Civil Rights to enforce the new prohibitions against housing discrimination based on the use of income-based housing subsidies.

The bill requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations governing positive rental payment history reporting and to specify the required form of the offer landlords must provide to tenants.
The bill and fiscal note indicate that the Judiciary may see impacts related to civil actions filed in circuit court for alleged discriminatory housing practices.

The fiscal note specifies that the Office of Administrative Hearings is responsible for conducting administrative hearings for housing discrimination complaints referred by the Commission on Civil Rights.
The bill is relevant to this department as it protects individuals using housing subsidies, which includes many Marylanders with disabilities who rely on federal or state vouchers.
The bill’s provisions protecting low-income tenants align with the office's mission to address child poverty and improve economic mobility for vulnerable families.
The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the implementing agencies (MCCR and DHCD) and handles legal challenges or enforcement actions related to state law.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the sunset provision for laws that allow county boards of education to transport certain students—such as those with disabilities, homeless youth, or foster children—using vehicles other than traditional Type I or Type II yellow school buses. It also requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to review and report on safety regulations for these alternative vehicles by January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), county boards of education, and the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA)
stakeholders: Public school students (including those with disabilities, preschool-age, homeless youth, and children in foster care), county boards of education, and private transportation companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education and the Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local school system expenditures may decrease because boards can continue using cost-effective alternative transportation instead of returning to more expensive Type I and Type II school vehicles for certain routes. No specific dollar estimates for these savings were provided in the Fiscal Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) as the primary agency responsible for reviewing regulations regarding alternative student transportation, conducting a study on vehicle and driver requirements, and reporting findings to the General Assembly.
The bill explicitly requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to consult with MSDE during the review of regulations and the development of safety standards for vehicles and drivers.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT is involved in the consultation process and the oversight of vehicle and driver safety standards relevant to state transportation policy.

The bill specifically requires MSDE to examine the regulations adopted by the Public Service Commission (PSC) for transportation network operators and determine if student transportation regulations can be aligned with them.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to MSDE and MVA regarding the development and revision of state regulations, ensuring that any changes to student transportation safety standards are legally sufficient.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved (MSDE and MDOT) and is responsible for signing the bill into law and ensuring policy initiatives are coordinated across departments.

The Department of Budget and Management is the principal fiscal agency that oversees the budget and personnel for the departments tasked with conducting the study, though the fiscal note indicates requirements can be met with existing resources.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to grant a property tax credit for real property located in a Rural Legacy Area if the property owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program.
responsible_party: The governing body of Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Property owners in Anne Arundel County located in Rural Legacy Areas who have sold their development rights.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and county expenditures are not affected. Anne Arundel County property tax revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $27,825 annually beginning in fiscal 2027, assuming the county governing body grants the credit. The estimate is based on 21 current eligible properties and the fiscal 2026 county real property tax rate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the Rural Legacy Program, which is established under the Natural Resources Article and administered by the Department of Natural Resources to protect farm and forest lands.

The fiscal note identifies that the Board of Public Works has approved over $12 million in grants under the Rural Legacy Program to Anne Arundel County for the purchase of conservation easements, which is the prerequisite for the tax credit.
This agency provides administrative review for property tax assessment disputes, including those involving valuations and property tax credits of the type authorized by this bill.
The agency promotes sustainable growth and resource management; Rural Legacy Areas are a key component of state land use planning and preservation strategy.
The bill authorizes a tax credit for properties in Rural Legacy Areas, similar to existing credits for agricultural land preservation programs managed or supported by this department.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees state expenditures and fiscal policies related to tax law enforcement and revenue collection.
The Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works, which approves the grants for the Rural Legacy Program easements that qualify property owners for the tax credit.
The council advocates for rural interests and natural resource stewardship in Maryland's counties, including the preservation of rural lands through programs like the Rural Legacy Program.
This multi-agency initiative coordinates efforts to protect the Chesapeake Bay and preserve farmland through programs like the Rural Legacy Program.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including environmental conservation and rural preservation programs cited in the bill.

bill_summary: This bill extends the deadline for the Maryland Department of the Environment to submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the synthetic turf industry, existing turf fields, and disposal and recycling practices from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: The Maryland Department of the Environment, the Synthetic Turf Council, synthetic turf producers, retailers, and users (including local governments, county school systems, higher education facilities, and professional sports organizations), and local environmental and community stakeholders.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, extending the deadline for the Maryland Department of the Environment to submit the required report does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business impact is considered minimal or none.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment is the primary agency tasked with conducting the study on synthetic turf and submitting the final report to the General Assembly. This bill specifically extends their deadline for this mandate.
The bill explicitly lists 'county school systems' as key users and stakeholders that the Department of the Environment must consult for the study. MSDE oversees these local school systems.

The bill identifies 'higher education facilities' as users of synthetic turf and required consultees. The University System of Maryland was also specifically listed as a source of information in the fiscal note.

As one of Maryland's public higher education institutions, Morgan State University is a 'higher education facility' and user of synthetic turf that falls under the required consultation group for the study.
The college is a public higher education facility and user of synthetic turf. It was specifically listed as a source of information in the fiscal note regarding the study.
The bill requires consultation with 'professional sports organizations' and synthetic turf users. The Stadium Authority manages professional venues that utilize these surfaces.

The IAC oversees the planning and funding of public school capital projects. Because synthetic turf fields are significant components of school facility construction and maintenance, the results of the study may impact their long-term facility sufficiency standards.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the primary implementing agency (MDE), and the Governor signed the bill into law.
The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment as it fulfills its statutory study and reporting requirements.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Health Care Commission by reducing from nine to eight the number of members who are individuals who do not have any connection with the management or policy of a health care provider or payor and including an administrator of a hospital; and altering from five to four the number of Commission members who must be residents of different counties with a population of 300,000 or more.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the membership structure of the 15-member Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC). Additionally, it adjusts residency requirements by reducing the minimum number of members who must reside in counties with populations of 300,000 or more from five to four.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Hospital administrators, physicians, health care payors, nursing home administrators, nonphysician health care practitioners, and residents of Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. Altering the membership of the Maryland Health Care Commission does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership composition of the Maryland Health Care Commission by altering the ratio of consumer members to industry representatives, specifically adding a hospital administrator and changing geographic residency requirements for appointees.

This office is responsible for vetting and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. The bill changes the specific legal requirements and demographics they must use when identifying and screening candidates for the Maryland Health Care Commission.

The Governor is the appointing authority for the members of the Maryland Health Care Commission. This bill changes the Governor's statutory mandate regarding the qualifications and geographic distribution of these appointees.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent regulatory agency located within the Maryland Department of Health. Changes to the commission's membership impact the administrative and regulatory oversight structure within the Department's health planning domain.

responsible_party: Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board; Governor of Maryland

fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no operational or fiscal impact on the State or local governments, and revenues are not affected.

The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing officials to various boards and commissions. This bill specifically requires the Governor to appoint the members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board based on the updated composition and provides the Governor with the authority to remove members.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards. This bill changes the required qualifications and nominating organizations for seats on the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, directly impacting the office's recruitment and vetting processes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board is a permanent executive body described in the summary for this collective entity. bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system for school or student safety concerns. It mandates local school systems to participate in the system by July 1, 2027, unless they already operate a substantially similar reporting system, and ensures the confidentiality of reports by requiring custodians to deny public records inspection of related materials.
responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS)
stakeholders: Students, teachers, school staff, parents, local school systems, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, there is no state or local fiscal impact as the bill codifies existing practices. The Maryland Center for School Safety already operates the 'Safe Schools Maryland' anonymous reporting system, and local school systems are already in compliance with the bill's requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary entity mandated by the bill to develop and administer the anonymous reporting system, establish operational guidelines, and provide training for school personnel.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within MSDE. Furthermore, MSDE oversees the local school systems that are required by this bill to participate in the anonymous reporting system.

The bill establishes a new exemption to the Maryland Public Information Act regarding the anonymous reporting system. The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on the implementation of such laws and publishes the state's Public Information Act Manual.
The bill requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to submit reports and summaries regarding school safety and incident data to the Governor.

The bill requires the anonymous reporting system to facilitate the forwarding of safety concerns to appropriate response personnel, which includes law enforcement. Additionally, the Center is required to maintain relationships with law enforcement to ensure emergency preparedness and response.

bill_summary: This bill reduces the membership of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County from 15 to 11 members. It reconfigures the board to include two at-large members and nine members representing each of the nine Baltimore County councilmanic districts, aligning with the county's updated redistricting structure. responsible_party: The Governor of Maryland and the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County
stakeholders: Current and prospective members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, the Community College of Baltimore County, and the residents of Baltimore County.

Locally, there will be a minimal decrease in reimbursement expenditures for board members starting in fiscal year 2027 as a result of the board size being reduced from 15 to 11 members. Local revenues are not affected. Specific dollar estimates were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the official appointing authority for the members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County. This bill directly modifies the composition of the board that the Governor must appoint.
As the state's regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission has a general interest in the governance and administrative structure of Maryland's community colleges.

This office is responsible for recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. It will be the primary agency managing the transitions and new appointments required by the board's restructuring.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions and typically reviews such legislation for constitutional and legal sufficiency regarding board member transitions and term expirations.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the State Ethics Commission, and the Governor is responsible for the overall policy and integrity of public ethics laws and the coordination of state and local government accountability.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the State Ethics Commission and other executive boards, likely providing legal guidance on the implementation and interpretation of the updated financial disclosure procedures.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits law enforcement officers who are assigned as school resource officers from engaging in sexual contact, vaginal intercourse, or other sexual acts with students enrolled at the school where the officer is assigned. Violations are classified as a misdemeanor punishable by up to three years in prison and/or a maximum fine of $3,000.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Students enrolled in Maryland schools and law enforcement officers serving as school resource officers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is an independent unit within the Department of Education specifically responsible for coordinating school safety, overseeing the certification of school safety personnel, and providing training for school resource officers, who are the primary subjects of the bill's regulations.

As the oversight body for Maryland's public schools, the department is directly involved because the bill regulates the conduct of law enforcement officers assigned to its schools as school resource officers and affects the safety of students under its care.

The Maryland State Police is the primary state law enforcement agency, and its officers often serve as school resource officers. This bill creates a specific criminal prohibition and misdemeanor offense that directly impacts the conduct and regulation of these officers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for representing indigent defendants in criminal proceedings. This bill creates a new misdemeanor offense, potentially increasing the caseload and legal defense requirements for the agency.

The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the judicial branch, which will be responsible for adjudicating criminal cases and sentencing individuals charged under this new misdemeanor provision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency oversees state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation; it would be responsible for the supervision or incarceration of individuals convicted of violating the bill's prohibitions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The GOCPP coordinates Maryland's public safety and criminal justice strategies. This bill amends the Criminal Law Article regarding law enforcement conduct, which falls under their policy coordination scope.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland State Police and the Department of Education, regarding the implementation and enforcement of this criminal law.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Governor's approval and involves multi-agency coordination between education and law enforcement sectors.

responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation
stakeholders: Maryland Legal Services Corporation, the Governor of Maryland, the Maryland State Senate, and lawyers admitted to the Bar in Maryland.

The Maryland Legal Services Corporation provides grants for civil legal assistance to low-income residents, which directly impacts the state's judicial system; additionally, the Administrative Office of the Courts was a primary source of information for the bill's fiscal note.

responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: Maryland Capitol Police officers, state employees, local law enforcement agencies, and the general public on or near State-owned or leased properties.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, altering and expanding the jurisdiction of the Maryland Capitol Police is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. The expansion of duties is expected to be managed using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Capitol Police is a unit within the Department of General Services. The bill directly alters and expands its jurisdictional authority and enforcement powers.

The bill requires the Maryland Capitol Police to notify the Secretary of State Police (head of MSP) in advance of investigations or enforcement actions and establishes coordination protocols between the two agencies.
The bill explicitly requires that notification of enforcement actions be provided to the Chief of Police of the Maryland Department of Health Secured Transport and Investigation Unit.
The bill explicitly requires that notification of enforcement actions be provided to the Superintendent of the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Police.
The bill explicitly requires that notification of enforcement actions be provided to the Chief of Police of the Maryland Transit Administration Police Force, which is a modal administration of MDOT.
The Board of Public Works is authorized by the bill to designate public improvements or grounds to be under the jurisdiction and police authority of the Maryland Capitol Police.

The bill repeals a specific statutory provision regarding jurisdiction over buildings administered by the Department of Labor in favor of a new statewide jurisdictional standard for State-owned property.

The Governor's Office oversees the Department of General Services and the implementation of state law enforcement policy; the Governor also appoints the Secretary of General Services who manages the Capitol Police.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is empowered by the bill to designate grounds for Maryland Capitol Police jurisdiction.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is empowered by the bill to designate grounds for Maryland Capitol Police jurisdiction.
The OAG serves as legal counsel to the Department of General Services and would provide guidance on the expanded statewide police authority and inter-agency notification requirements.
As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM oversees the administrative and personnel structures of executive agencies like the Department of General Services.

bill_summary: This bill enters Maryland into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact, which allows licensed school psychologists to practice across state lines in member states. The compact establishes a streamlined pathway for psychologists to obtain equivalent licenses in other member states, helping to address workforce shortages and ensure student access to qualified professionals. It creates the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission to govern the compact, manage a shared database of licensure and disciplinary information, and coordinate interstate rules and enforcement.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Licensed school psychologists, students and the public receiving school psychological services, local school systems, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) general fund expenditures increase by $37,000 in fiscal 2027, which includes a one-time cost of $30,000 to enhance the state licensure system and a $7,000 annual participation fee. Ongoing annual expenditures for the participation fee are estimated at $7,000 thereafter. There may be a minimal increase in MSDE fee revenue from equivalent licenses, though these fees are limited to $10 each by state law. Criminal background check fees are anticipated to be offset by the costs of conducting the checks. There is no direct local fiscal impact, although the bill may facilitate the recruitment of school psychologists to fill local vacancies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator for school psychologists in Maryland, the Department of Education is the lead agency for implementing the compact, managing multistate license applications, and overseeing the related fiscal expenditures and system upgrades.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the Department of Education and will be responsible for providing legal guidance on compact compliance, rulemaking, and representing the state in potential litigation or dispute resolution.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates intergovernmental relations, which are central to the implementation and maintenance of interstate compacts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) is responsible for conducting the mandatory state and national criminal history records checks required for compact licensure and renewal.
The department oversees state expenditures and fiscal planning; the bill requires new general fund expenditures for licensure system enhancements and annual compact participation fees.
The bill contains specific provisions to facilitate the licensure and mobility of active military members and their spouses, aligning with the department's mission to support military families.
The bill explicitly states that the judicial branches of member states are responsible for enforcing the compact and identifies specific jurisdictions for legal proceedings involving the Commission.
The compact's provisions for active military members specifically include members of the National Guard, which falls under the leadership and oversight of the Adjutant General.

The implementation of the compact requires one-time enhancements to the state's educator licensure system, which falls under the department's responsibility for statewide information technology strategy and infrastructure.

While school psychologists are licensed via the Department of Education, the Department of Health oversees broader behavioral and mental health policies that may overlap with the professional services governed by the compact.
The compact aims to improve the availability of school psychological services, which are critical for students with disabilities whom the department is tasked with supporting.
The office's mission to improve access to health services and child well-being is directly supported by the compact's goal of increasing the availability of qualified school psychologists.

The agency provides support for criminal investigations and manages specialized services that may interact with the exchange of investigative records for law enforcement purposes mentioned in the compact.

stakeholders: Paid firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, and state and local government employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government expenditures are expected to increase minimally starting in fiscal year 2027 due to the expanded occupational disease presumption. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company may see a minimal increase in benefit expenditures and potential revenue increases from adjusted premiums. While the fiscal note identifies these potential increases, it notes that the overall financial impact is anticipated to be minimal because many hypertension-related claims are already compensable or refiled under current law.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and represents the state in workers' compensation appeals and litigation involving state employees.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is the state agency responsible for the planning, financing, and construction of major sports and entertainment facilities in Maryland, including the large-scale renovation project at Pimlico mentioned in the fiscal note.

bill_summary: HB 351, known as the No Kings Act, authorizes an aggrieved party or the Maryland Office of the Attorney General to bring a civil action against a 'covered officer' (an officer authorized to make arrests for federal violations and carry firearms) who deprives an individual of constitutional or legal rights under color of law. The bill allows plaintiffs to seek damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief, and permits the court to award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to a prevailing plaintiff. It establishes a five-year statute of limitations for such actions.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Aggrieved individuals whose constitutional rights are violated, federal or 'covered' officers with arrest and firearm authority, the Office of the Attorney General, and small business law firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to affect State liability or expenditures as it is interpreted to apply to federal law enforcement officers rather than State employees. State general fund revenues may increase if the Office of the Attorney General is awarded damages or recovers legal fees. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected. There is a potential meaningful impact on small business law firms that litigate constitutional rights claims.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to bring civil actions against covered officers for constitutional violations and to seek damages and injunctive relief.
The bill text specifically identifies a 'State Prosecutor' as an authorized party to bring civil actions for the deprivation of constitutional rights.

The Treasurer manages the State Insurance Trust Fund and handles tort claims. The fiscal note indicates the office anticipates a high volume of claims and may require additional adjusters due to the bill.
The bill establishes a new civil cause of action, requiring the judicial system to manage increased litigation and procedural support for these cases.

As the primary law enforcement agency, MSP is impacted by legislation regarding the civil liability of officers and is mentioned as an information source in the fiscal note regarding the definition of 'covered officers'.
DNR employs law enforcement officers (Natural Resources Police) who carry firearms and make arrests; they are mentioned in the fiscal note as being involved in the assessment of the bill's scope.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

DBM is the principal fiscal agency that would be responsible for authorizing additional personnel or budget resources if the State Treasurer or Attorney General experiences a significant increase in workload.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and coordinated the approval of this emergency measure, which impacts multiple state executive agencies.

fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. Both the State Board of Elections and local municipalities are expected to handle the reporting and website display requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for election administration and oversight in Maryland, the State Board of Elections is directly responsible for receiving reporting data from municipalities, displaying lists of upcoming municipal elections and offices on its website, and identifying municipalities that fail to report required information.

The Office of the Attorney General provides essential legal counsel to the State Board of Elections regarding the implementation of new statutory mandates and ensures that the proposed reporting and website display requirements comply with state law.

The creation of new misdemeanors and felonies related to the unauthorized employment of acupuncturists will require adjudication through the Maryland judicial system.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD would be responsible for providing legal representation to indigent individuals charged with the new criminal offenses created by this bill.
The bill requires that penalties collected by the Board be remitted to the General Fund. The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and revenue manager for the General Fund.
The Treasurer acts as the custodian of state funds, including the General Fund where any penalties collected under the bill's enforcement provisions will be deposited.
The bill moves the board away from physical renewal certificates to 'making available proof of renewal,' which typically requires IT infrastructure and digital licensing support.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, this office is relevant because the bill establishes new criminal classifications and penalties.
DBM oversees state revenue estimates and fiscal planning; while the fiscal impact is noted as not material, the bill creates new revenue streams for the General Fund via civil and criminal fines.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions of law to include physician assistants in the health care practitioners who may take certain actions, including actions related to the guardianship of disabled persons, admission of individuals to mental health facilities, and the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program; altering the health care practitioners that may order that a pregnant incarcerated individual be admitted to the infirmary; requiring the  Maryland Department of Health to cover certain charges for certain emergency evaluees; etc.
Title: Physician Assistants and Midwives - Parity With Other Health Care Practitioners

bill_summary: This bill expands the scope of practice for physician assistants (PAs), certified nurse-midwives, and licensed certified midwives to grant them parity with other health care practitioners in various clinical and administrative roles. It authorizes PAs to certify competency for guardianships, perform evaluations and certifications for voluntary and involuntary mental health admissions, prescribe emergency epinephrine in youth camps, and certify sick leave for state employees. Additionally, health maintenance organizations (HMOs) must allow members to select these practitioners as primary care providers, and the Maryland Health Care Commission is required to study and report on emergency department wait times for individuals awaiting involuntary mental health admission.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Physician assistants, certified nurse-midwives, licensed certified midwives, patients requiring mental health services, state employees, and health maintenance organization (HMO) members.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note states that the Maryland Health Care Commission can fulfill the bill's review and reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on state or local revenues. Although the bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to cover charges for examinations performed by physician assistants for certain emergency evaluees, the fiscal note does not provide a specific dollar estimate for these expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to review data on emergency department stays for individuals subject to involuntary admission and submit a report with findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by November 1, 2026.

The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for the Health-General provisions amended by the bill, including mental health admissions, emergency evaluations, the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program, and the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters medical protocols within the state's correctional system by authorizing physician assistants and midwives to order the admission of pregnant incarcerated individuals to the infirmary.

The bill impacts the Attendant Care Program by allowing physician assistants to certify eligible individuals as being at risk of institutionalization, a key function in providing supports for Marylanders with disabilities.
The bill amends the Human Services Article regarding the Attendant Care Program, which provides assistance to residents in need, directly affecting the certification process for program eligibility.

The bill modifies procedural requirements for guardianship petitions for disabled persons by allowing physician assistants to sign required certificates of competency, which impacts judicial filings and court operations.
As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is impacted by the provision allowing physician assistants to sign sick leave certificates for state employees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the membership and alters the duties of the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations to include a representative from the Maryland Academy of Physician Assistants.
The bill specifies that hospitals shall be paid at rates approved by this commission for initial consultant examinations of emergency evaluees when performed by physician assistants.

State Police officers serve as peace officers who are authorized to receive emergency evaluation petitions and transport evaluees; the bill expands the list of practitioners who can submit these petitions to include physician assistants.

The bill introduces new quality of care standards for health maintenance organizations (HMOs) regarding a member's choice of primary care providers, which falls under the regulatory scope of the insurance administration.
The bill's changes to the Attendant Care Program and guardianship requirements for disabled persons directly impact the department's core mission of supporting older adults and their caregivers.

The OAG will provide legal counsel to the various state health boards and executive agencies as they implement the expanded scope of practice and regulatory changes for physician assistants and midwives.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies implementing the bill and holds the authority to appoint members to the state commissions affected by these changes.

Synopsis: Clarifying that applicants for licensure as an optometrist and certain applicants for reinstatement are required to pass all sections of each part of a licensure examination; repealing the requirement that the State Board of Examiners in Optometry give examinations to licensure applicants; prohibiting the Board from placing a licensee on inactive status for more than 6 consecutive years; etc.
Title: State Board of Examiners in Optometry - Examination Requirements and Time Period for Inactive Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill clarifies that applicants for licensure or reinstatement as an optometrist must pass all sections of each part of a licensure examination and limits the duration of inactive status for licensees to a maximum of six consecutive years. It also removes the requirement for the State Board of Examiners in Optometry to directly administer examinations and collect reexamination fees, aligning the law with the current practice of using national testing services.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners in Optometry
stakeholders: Applicants for optometry licensure, current licensed optometrists, and the State Board of Examiners in Optometry.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not substantively change board activities or operations, and board special fund expenditures are not affected. While the bill repeals a reexamination fee, it primarily aligns statute with current practice where examinations are administered by the National Board of Examiners in Optometry (NBEO) rather than the State Board, resulting in no significant fiscal impact on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners in Optometry is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Health. This bill directly amends the Health Occupations Article concerning the Board's licensing requirements, examination standards, and inactive status policies.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health and its professional licensing boards, including the State Board of Examiners in Optometry, to ensure compliance with the new statutory requirements.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and is responsible for signing the bill into law and appointing members to the State Board of Examiners in Optometry.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the fiscal operations and personnel policies of state agencies, including the special-funded health boards, although the fiscal note indicates no substantive impact on board expenditures.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including appeals from individuals who may be denied licensure or reinstatement by the State Board of Examiners in Optometry under the new examination criteria.

Synopsis: Authorizing supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library to form, join, and participate in an employee organization and engage in certain other activities related to collective bargaining; authorizing certain bargaining units for the employees of the Baltimore County Public Library; and altering certain provisions to provide that an employee may be deemed a certain management employee, rather than a supervisory employee, under certain circumstances.
Title: Baltimore County Public Library - Collective Bargaining - Supervisory Employees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill grants collective bargaining rights to supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library and authorizes the creation of two distinct bargaining units: one for supervisory employees and one for non-supervisory employees. It also adjusts the definition of management and supervisory employees to clarify eligibility for collective bargaining.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Public Library Board of Trustees
stakeholders: Supervisory and non-supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library, the library's Board of Trustees, and the Baltimore County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on State finances. At the local level, Baltimore County Public Library expenditures may increase minimally due to the potential for higher employee salaries and the cost of hiring outside mediators, depending on the outcome of future collective bargaining negotiations. The library is expected to handle administrative tasks like payroll deductions for union fees using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is the central state agency responsible for administering and overseeing collective bargaining for public sector employees. Since this bill establishes new collective bargaining units and expands rights for supervisory employees within a public library system, PERB would be responsible for certifying the bargaining units and resolving any labor disputes.

The Maryland State Library Agency (MSLA) provides strategic leadership and coordination for the state's 24 public library systems. As this legislation directly impacts the governance and labor relations of the Baltimore County Public Library system, it falls under the MSLA's scope of policy oversight for libraries.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland State Library and the Public Employee Relations Board. They would be involved in advising these agencies on the implementation of the new collective bargaining law and representing the state in any associated legal challenges.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives. This bill requires the Governor's approval and aligns with broader state labor and collective bargaining policy coordination.

Synopsis: Requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations that provide coverage for chemotherapy to treat cancer to provide coverage for scalp cooling systems used for the preservation of hair in connection with chemotherapy treatment; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed in the State on or after January 1, 2027.
Title: Health Insurance - Scalp Cooling Systems - Required Coverage

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers, including insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations that cover chemotherapy for cancer, to also provide coverage for scalp cooling systems used to prevent or reduce hair loss associated with the treatment.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Cancer patients receiving chemotherapy, health insurance carriers, and state and local government health benefit programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in special fund revenues in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. State expenditures for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program are expected to increase by an estimated range of $11,600 to $302,800 annually beginning in FY 2027. Local governments may experience increased health care costs for fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing the insurance market. This bill creates a new health insurance mandate, requiring the MIA to review rate and form filings from carriers to ensure compliance and handle potential consumer complaints. The fiscal note also identifies a direct increase in special fund revenues for the MIA from filing fees.

DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note explicitly states that the program's expenditures will increase because it generally provides coverage for mandated benefits, and the program does not currently cover scalp cooling systems.

MDH oversees health policy and the administration of Medicaid and Managed Care Organizations (MCOs). The bill's preamble specifically mentions MCOs as entities required to provide this coverage, and the mandate directly impacts the scope of health services provided in the state for cancer treatment.

The MHBE administers the state's health insurance marketplace. While the fiscal note suggests the mandate currently excludes the individual and small group ACA markets to avoid state defrayal costs, the agency is relevant as any changes to mandated benefits impact the broader health insurance landscape and benchmark plans they oversee.

The MHCC is responsible for planning health system needs and improving access to care. New mandates for medical devices like scalp cooling systems fall under their purview of monitoring health service availability and quality.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health, regarding the implementation and enforcement of new insurance mandates and regulatory compliance.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies implementing this mandate and approved the legislation. The office also manages the overall state budget, which is impacted by the fiscal requirements for the state employee health plan.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. Disputes between the Maryland Insurance Administration and carriers, or between consumers and state-regulated health plans regarding coverage denials for this new mandate, may be referred to the OAH.

Synopsis: Repealing certain provisions of law requiring a person to hold a concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) general discharge permit issued by the Department of the Environment before the person may begin construction on any part of a new CAFO; and authorizing the Department, under certain circumstances, to authorize a person to begin construction on any part of a new animal feeding operation under a certain approval process established by the Department.
Title: Water Pollution Control - Discharge Permits - Animal Feeding Operations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that a person must obtain a concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) discharge permit before beginning construction on a new CAFO. It authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to establish an approval process allowing construction to start on new animal feeding operations (AFOs) if the general discharge permit has been administratively extended, provided the applicant demonstrates compliance with specific regulatory requirements and construction permits.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE)
stakeholders: Animal feeding operation (AFO) and concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) owners and operators, agricultural businesses, and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations, and there is no impact on local government finances. There may be a minimal overall impact on small businesses, though specific AFOs could benefit from starting construction sooner while updated general discharge permits are being finalized.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Environment Article and names the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) as the primary agency responsible for issuing discharge permits and establishing the new approval process for animal feeding operation construction.

The bill impacts animal feeding operations (AFOs), which are central to Maryland's agricultural community. The agency's mission includes promoting the economic viability of farming and agribusiness, and they were consulted as a source for the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council is responsible for coordinating interagency efforts (MDE, MDA, DNR) to restore the Chesapeake Bay. Since CAFO discharge permits are critical for water quality and nutrient management in the Bay watershed, this policy change is highly relevant to their advisory and coordination role.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MDE and MDA) responsible for implementing this law. Additionally, as an emergency measure, the Governor's immediate signature and executive oversight of environmental policy initiatives are required.

DNR is responsible for managing the state's natural resources and waterways. Changes in water pollution control regulations for AFOs directly affect the health of the fisheries and aquatic ecosystems that DNR manages.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services to rural businesses to help them acquire and develop facilities. This bill's impact on the timing of AFO construction permits may affect the financing and operational timelines for the agricultural clients they support.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates efforts across MDE, MDA, and Planning to protect the Chesapeake Bay and manage sustainable growth. The regulation of agricultural pollutants is a core component of its cross-departmental strategy.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE and the General Assembly. They may be required to assist in drafting the new approval process or defending the state in the event of legal challenges to administratively extended permits.

The Council advocates for the interests of rural counties, where animal feeding operations are predominantly located. Changes to construction requirements for these operations affect the economic development of rural communities.

Synopsis: Repealing the maximum age for children in certain residential child care programs who receive educational support; requiring operators of certain residential child care programs to provide certain educational opportunities to the children for whom they have legal custody or care and control; requiring that applicants to be child and youth care practitioners undergo certain training; prohibiting an individual who holds a certificate as a residential child and youth care practitioner from being required to complete certain training; etc.
