bill_summary: This bill removes the maximum age limit for children in residential child care programs to receive educational support and mandates that program operators provide specific educational opportunities, including ensuring school stability, meeting with teachers, providing study time and homework assistance, and offering access to computers. It also establishes comprehensive training requirements for residential child and youth care practitioners, covering topics such as child development, suicide prevention, and behavioral management, while allowing existing practitioners to complete new training upon certificate renewal.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services, Maryland Department of Health, Department of Juvenile Services, and the State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals
stakeholders: Children residing in licensed residential child care programs (group homes, alternative living units, and emergency shelters), licensed operators of these programs, and certified residential child and youth care practitioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in fiscal 2027 for the Department of Human Services to conduct staff training, update regulations, and modify contracts. Future year monitoring costs are indeterminate but expected to be minimal. The Maryland Department of Health, Department of Juvenile Services, and the State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no direct impact on local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a primary licensing agency for residential child care programs and the entity responsible for 'best interest' determinations regarding school enrollment, DHS is heavily impacted. The fiscal note also specifies a $25,000 expenditure for DHS to update regulations and provide training.

DJS is one of the three principal licensing agencies for residential child care programs covered by the bill. It must ensure that its licensed operators comply with the new educational and practitioner training standards.

MDH is a licensing agency for these programs. Furthermore, the bill amends the Health Occupations Article regarding the certification of residential child and youth care practitioners, a regulatory function managed within MDH.

The bill amends the Education Article and establishes new requirements for school enrollment, IEP support, and 504 plans for children in residential care, directly impacting MSDE's oversight of the public education system.

The GOC coordinates policy and well-being for Maryland's vulnerable children. This legislation specifically targets the educational outcomes and professional care of children in state-funded residential programs, which falls under its core mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent children and youth in the juvenile justice and child welfare systems. The new educational rights and training standards for practitioners directly impact the advocacy and protection of their clients' rights.
DBM is responsible for the state's personnel and fiscal management. It will oversee the general fund expenditures required by DHS for staff training and contract modifications.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE, MDH, DHS, and DJS. It will be involved in drafting and reviewing the regulatory updates and contract modifications necessitated by this bill.

The bill includes specific requirements for supporting children with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and 504 plans, which are central to the Department of Disabilities' mission to ensure inclusive services for youth.

The bill specifically mentions children who are dually enrolled in high school and institutions of higher education, requiring operators to provide them with computer and internet access for their studies.

The MLDS Center tracks student and workforce outcomes. Changes to the educational support and age requirements for children in residential child care programs are relevant to their data collection on vulnerable student populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the coordinating body for public safety and juvenile delinquency strategies, GOCPP is impacted by changes to the standards of care and rehabilitation for youth in residential placements.

The AOC supports the judiciary which oversees cases involving children in the legal custody of the state; changes to educational requirements and practitioner training may be relevant to court-ordered care plans.

Synopsis: Extending the reporting date and the termination date for a workgroup convened by the State Retirement Agency to study transfers of member service between State and local retirement and pension systems; and requiring the State Retirement Agency to report to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, the House Appropriations Committee, and the Joint Committee on Pensions and not the entire General Assembly.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Transfers Between Systems - Workgroup - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the reporting deadline for a workgroup convened by the State Retirement Agency to study the transfer of member service between State and local retirement and pension systems. The reporting date is changed from December 1, 2025, to October 1, 2026, and the workgroup's termination date is extended by one year to June 30, 2027. It also mandates that the report be submitted to specific legislative committees.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members of State and local retirement and pension systems and the State Retirement Agency
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State or local fiscal impact. According to the fiscal note, extending the reporting date and termination date for the workgroup does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the State Retirement and Pension System, the SRA is mandated by this bill to convene the workgroup, conduct the study, and submit the resulting report by the revised deadline.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically extends the operational lifespan and reporting requirements for a workgroup (a temporary advisory body) tasked with studying pension service transfers.
The Governor is a mandated recipient of the findings and recommendations report submitted by the State Retirement Agency.
As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM is a key stakeholder in the management of state employee benefits and retirement policies, which are the subject of the workgroup's study.

Synopsis: Altering certain terminology relating to State parks that preserve and interpret the history of certain populations.
Title: Natural Resources - State Parks - Terminology

NarrowSubjects.Name: Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.
Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill updates the terminology used for State parks that preserve and interpret the history of underrepresented populations, specifically removing the word "historical" from the titles of "State historical parks," "Freedman’s State Historical Park," and "Port of Deposit State Historical Park" while maintaining their original historical purposes and missions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Underrepresented communities (including African American, Asian, Indigenous or Native American, and Hispanic or Latino populations), local governments in Montgomery County, Baltimore City, and Cecil County, and the Maryland Park Service.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances. According to the fiscal note, signs and publications have not yet been produced for the renamed parks, so there are no associated replacement costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for managing the State park system and implementing the terminology changes and park establishments mandated by the bill.

The Secretary of Planning and the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is housed within this department, are designated members of the stakeholder advisory committee for Port Deposit State Park.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee for the newly established Port Deposit State Park.

The Secretary of the Environment serves on the stakeholder advisory committee for Port Deposit State Park, and the Commission on Environmental Justice and Sustainable Communities provides input on the establishment of State parks.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration, a modal agency of MDOT, is designated as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee for Port Deposit State Park.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration is specifically named as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee for the Port Deposit State Park.

The agency oversees several ethnic and cultural commissions, such as the Commission on Indian Affairs and the Commission on Asian Pacific American Affairs, which are required to provide input on the establishment of specific State parks.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates input from several existing commissions and establishes new stakeholder advisory committees to oversee the management and scope of Freedman's State Park and Port Deposit State Park.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments and commissions involved in park establishment and is responsible for policy coordination related to the state's natural and historical resources.

Synopsis: Prohibiting provisions of the governing documents of a condominium or homeowners association from unreasonably restricting the governing body from installing or authorizing the installation of electric vehicle recharging equipment; establishing that the installation or authorization of electric vehicle recharging equipment by a governing body is subject to certain budget processes of the condominium or homeowners association for a common area renovation or alteration similar in cost or magnitude; applying the Act retroactively; etc.
Title: Condominiums and Homeowners Associations - Governing Documents - Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill prohibits condominium and homeowners association (HOA) governing documents from unreasonably restricting the association's governing body from installing or authorizing electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment in common or limited common use parking areas. It mandates that such installations follow the association's standard budget process for similar common area renovations and requires the governing body to consider the community's parking needs. Additionally, it allows governing bodies to grant three-year renewable licenses for the equipment and electricity supply, and the provisions apply retroactively to existing governing documents.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of condominiums and homeowners associations
stakeholders: Residents, unit owners, and lot owners in condominiums and homeowners associations; governing boards of common ownership communities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. The fiscal note indicates that small business impacts are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is responsible for enforcing laws related to consumer rights and often provides guidance on homeowners association (HOA) and condominium disputes. This bill directly alters the enforcement of covenants and restrictions within these communities.

The Maryland Energy Administration is tasked with promoting renewable energy and energy efficiency. This bill aligns with their mission by facilitating the expansion of electric vehicle (EV) recharging infrastructure within residential common ownership communities.

The Secretary of State's office is responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums. Since the bill mandates changes to how condominium governing documents address EV equipment, it falls within their regulatory and records oversight purview.
The bill establishes new legal standards for governing documents and applies them retroactively, which may lead to litigation or requests for judicial interpretation within the court system.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and signs legislation into law. This bill touches on environmental policy and housing regulation, which are key areas of executive policy coordination.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and provides land use guidance. The integration of EV charging in community parking structures is a component of modern sustainable residential planning.

Synopsis: Adding Class B (on-sale) beer and wine and Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses to the list of alcoholic beverages licenses for which the prohibition against issuing multiple licenses for the same person or premises in Prince George's County does not apply.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Multiple Licenses Prohibition - Exceptions PG 313-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill creates an exception to the general rule in Prince George's County that a person or entity may only hold one alcoholic beverages license. Specifically, it allows for multiple Class B (on-sale) beer and wine licenses or Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses to be held by the same person or for the same premises.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Business owners and alcoholic beverage license applicants in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George’s County revenues increase to the extent that the Board of License Commissioners issues additional Class B licenses. The annual license fee is $365 for a Class B beer and wine license and $2,305 for a Class B beer, wine, and liquor license. The State has no fiscal impact, and the county can manage enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the principal state-level official responsible for regulating the alcoholic beverages industry. As the bill amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article to modify licensing rules, it directly falls under the Comptroller's broad regulatory and tax collection oversight of the industry.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor, General Assembly, and state agencies on the legality and enforcement of amendments to the Annotated Code of Maryland, including changes to alcoholic beverages licensing statutes.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly. This bill was approved by the Governor on May 26, 2026.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission and extending the termination of the Commission.
Title: Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission - Membership and Termination - Altered and Extended

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the composition of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission by reducing the number of members from the Senate of Maryland and the House of Delegates from two each to one each, while adding two members from the private sector to be appointed by the Governor. It also extends the termination date of the Commission from September 30, 2026, to September 30, 2028, and mandates annual reports on findings and recommendations for promoting trade between Maryland and Ireland.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Private sector businesses, the Irish-American community, public institutions of higher education, the Maryland Chamber of Commerce, and the Maryland General Assembly.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Commerce can continue to support the commission using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances. Commission members do not receive compensation but are entitled to reimbursement for travel expenses under Standard State Travel Regulations as provided in the State budget.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission is established within the Department of Commerce. The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a member, and the department is responsible for supporting the commission's activities with its resources.

The Secretary of State (or designee) is a statutory member of the commission. The agency is also responsible for managing the state's international affairs and diplomatic relations, which aligns with the commission's mission.

As the primary diplomatic liaison for Maryland, this division within the Secretary of State's office coordinates international engagement and would be functionally involved in the commission's efforts to promote trade and academic exchanges with Ireland.

The bill alters the commission's membership by adding private sector members and Irish-American community representatives appointed by the Governor. This office recruits and vets candidates for such positions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership, reporting requirements, and termination date of the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission, which falls under this collective category of state-authorized bodies.
The Governor is responsible for appointing several members of the commission and receiving its annual report on trade and academic recommendations.

The commission is tasked with promoting academic exchanges between Maryland and Ireland and must include a representative from a public institution of higher education, areas overseen by the commission.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions and would provide advice regarding the commission's statutory duties and regulations.

As a major provider of public higher education in the state, the University System is a primary stakeholder in the commission's mandate to promote academic exchanges and may provide the representative for higher education.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State is a stakeholder in the commission's mission to promote academic exchanges between Maryland and Ireland.
As a public institution of higher education, the college is a stakeholder in the commission's efforts regarding academic exchanges.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, it oversees the budget for the Department of Commerce, which must support the commission's activities and expense reimbursements.

Synopsis: Adding bacterial vaginosis to the list of diagnoses for which certain health care practitioners may prescribe, dispense, or otherwise provide antibiotic therapy to a sexual partner of a diagnosed patient without making a personal physical assessment of the sexual partner; and adding licensed certified midwives to the list of health care practitioners who may prescribe, dispense, or otherwise provide antibiotic therapy to a sexual partner of a diagnosed patient without making a certain assessment of the sexual partner.
Title: Public Health - Expedited Partner Therapy - Bacterial Vaginosis and Licensed Certified Midwives

bill_summary: This bill expands Maryland's expedited partner therapy program by adding bacterial vaginosis to the list of infections for which a healthcare practitioner can prescribe antibiotics to a patient's sexual partner without a physical examination. It also authorizes licensed certified midwives to provide such therapy and updates program terminology from 'sexually transmitted infection' to 'an infection transmitted through sexual activity'.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Patients diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis or other STIs, their sexual partners, and health care practitioners including physicians, advanced practice registered nurses, physician assistants, and licensed certified midwives.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues, local government finances, or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency impacted. The bill specifically tasks the Secretary of Health with adopting regulations to implement the expedited partner therapy (EPT) changes. MDH is responsible for updating EPT protocols, provider materials, and overseeing the inclusion of bacterial vaginosis and licensed certified midwives in the program.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health. They would likely be involved in reviewing and drafting the updated regulations required by the bill to ensure they comply with existing state and federal health laws.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for planning the state's health system needs and improving access to health care. Expanding EPT to include bacterial vaginosis and allowing midwives to provide this therapy is a public health initiative aimed at improving access and reducing reinfection rates.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives. The Governor will also be responsible for signing this bill into law and oversees the Department of Health's implementation of the program.

The Department of Budget and Management is the state's principal fiscal agency. While the fiscal note indicates the bill can be implemented with existing resources, DBM monitors any changes to agency mandates and regulatory responsibilities for long-term fiscal planning.

Synopsis: Requiring, subject to certain conditions, the Prince George's County Board of Education to provide, at no charge, drink spiking detection products and drug detection strips to public high school students in the county through school-based health clinics or school libraries beginning in the 2026-2027 school year; and requiring each public high school in the county to submit a certain report to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response on or before October 1 each year.

bill_summary: Beginning in the 2026–2027 school year, this bill requires Prince George’s County public high schools to provide students with drink spiking detection products and drug detection strips (for fentanyl) at no charge. However, schools are only required to provide these items if they are supplied to the schools at no cost. Additionally, each high school must submit an annual report to Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response detailing the quantity of products distributed.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of Education
stakeholders: Prince George’s County public high school students and the Prince George’s County Public Schools system
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not impacted as the Office of Overdose Response can handle reporting with existing resources. Local expenditures for Prince George’s County Public Schools may increase minimally for the installation of dispensers, though the products themselves are only required to be distributed if obtained at no cost to the school system. Prince George's County may use Opioid Restitution Fund awards to supply the drug detection strips.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland's Office of Overdose Response (MOOR) is an entity within the Executive Department (Governor's Office). The bill specifically requires public high schools to submit annual reports on the distribution of drug detection products directly to MOOR.

The bill amends the Education Article and mandates the Prince George’s County Board of Education to require high schools to provide drug detection products. The requirement for drug detection strips is also triggered by reports of naloxone use previously submitted to the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) manages the Overdose Response Program (ORP), which the fiscal note identifies as the source for drug detection strips provided at no cost to authorized entities, including schools.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education focused on school safety, the Center is relevant to initiatives addressing drug-related safety concerns and providing technical assistance to schools regarding safety products.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and manages funding related to crime and recidivism. It is broadly relevant to the policy coordination of overdose prevention and drug detection initiatives.

Synopsis: Authorizing a party to the guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person to request a stay of certain civil actions or proceedings on the filing of a petition for guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person; requiring a certain party to the guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person to provide certain notice to a court granting a stay and to parties to a civil action or proceeding; establishing that a stay may be in effect  for not more than 90 days, unless extended for good cause; etc.
Title: Petition for Guardianship of the Property of Alleged Disabled Person - Stay of Civil Actions and Proceedings
bill_summary: This bill allows a party involved in a guardianship proceeding for an alleged disabled person to request a temporary stay of certain civil actions, such as evictions, foreclosures, or debt collection efforts, against that person. The stay generally lasts up to 90 days, requires notice to all parties, and mandates that legal service for the stayed actions be directed to the appointed guardian once the stay is lifted.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Alleged disabled persons, legal guardians, landlords, mortgage lenders, creditors, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates the bill can be implemented using existing State resources without materially affecting revenues. Although the Judiciary estimated a one-time programming cost of $142,238, the fiscal note suggests these requirements can be absorbed within current budgets. There is no impact on local government finances. Small businesses acting as plaintiffs in civil actions, such as landlords or lenders, may experience delayed revenue due to the authorized stays.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch by establishing new procedures for the stay of specific civil actions (such as rent cases, foreclosures, and sheriff's sales) upon the filing of a petition for guardianship of property. The Judiciary is the primary entity responsible for implementing these stays, managing notices, and potentially updating court programming.

The Register of Wills serves as the Clerk to the Orphans' Court, which has jurisdiction over certain guardianship and estate matters under the Estates and Trusts Article. The bill specifically amends this Article, and the Register of Wills was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

The Department of Human Services oversees Adult Protective Services (APS), which is responsible for protecting vulnerable adults from abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation. APS frequently initiates or is involved in guardianship petitions for disabled adults.

The bill concerns legal protections and property management for 'alleged disabled persons.' This department is the principal agency for coordinating services and improving policy outcomes for Maryland residents with disabilities.

The Department of Aging is dedicated to protecting the rights and quality of life for older adults and people with disabilities. Many individuals who are subjects of property guardianship petitions fall within this agency's primary demographic.

The Department of Health manages services for individuals with developmental and behavioral disabilities. These populations may require guardians of property, and the bill's provisions regarding stays of civil actions would affect their financial and housing stability.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the state and its agencies. It would provide legal counsel to departments like DHS and MDH that are involved in guardianship proceedings or affected by the bill's procedural changes.

The bill allows for stays of evictions (failure to pay rent, wrongful detainer) and foreclosures. These actions are directly relevant to the department's mission of ensuring housing stability and providing solutions for homelessness.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies responsible for vulnerable adult protection and will be responsible for signing the bill into law.

Synopsis: Extending to December 31, 2027, the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances to study and make recommendations related to the use of natural psychedelic substances; adding a representative of a historically Black college or university in the State to the Task Force; and requiring the Task Force to submit an updated report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before October 31, 2026.
Title: Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances - Extension and Membership

bill_summary: This bill extends the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances for an additional year, through December 31, 2027. It also adds a representative from a Maryland historically Black college or university (HBCU) to the task force membership and requires an updated report of findings and recommendations to be submitted by October 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: Maryland Cannabis Administration, Maryland historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs), healthcare and behavioral health professionals, law enforcement, and patients with conditions treatable by psychedelic substances.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration can continue providing staff support for the task force using existing resources. Any expense reimbursements for task force members are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. There is no fiscal impact on local governments or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration is the primary agency responsible for providing staff for the Task Force and its Director (or designee) serves as a member. The fiscal note specifies that MCA can provide support with existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly concerns the extension and membership of the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances, which falls under this category of state entities.

The Governor appoints the majority of the Task Force members, including the new representative from a historically Black college or university, designates the chair, and receives the mandated reports.

The Secretary of Health (or designee) is a statutory member of the Task Force. The bill involves studying substances with health applications, behavioral health treatment, and substance use disorders.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is a statutory member of the Task Force, reflecting the potential relevance of psychedelic substances to the community of people with disabilities.

The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now the Department of Veterans and Military Families) is a statutory member of the Task Force, likely due to research into the use of psychedelics for veteran-specific health issues like PTSD.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Task Force is specifically charged with making recommendations regarding the transition from criminalizing psychedelic substances, including the release of incarcerated individuals and expungement of records, which directly impacts the correctional system.

As one of Maryland's prominent historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) and a state agency, Morgan State University is a primary candidate for the new representative seat added to the Task Force by this bill.
The University System of Maryland is explicitly listed as a source for one Task Force member. Additionally, USM includes several HBCUs that could provide the new representative required by the bill.
The Task Force includes a member of law enforcement and is tasked with recommending drug policy reforms and transitions from criminalization, which are relevant to state law enforcement operations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state task forces, including the new HBCU seat created by this legislation.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and task forces. They would likely advise the Task Force on legal matters related to drug policy reform and the creation of a state access program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Task Force's mandate to recommend decriminalization and expungement strategies is highly relevant to the Office of the Public Defender's role in protecting the rights of indigent defendants and those with criminal records.
As the central fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budget execution for the agencies involved, and the fiscal note mentions that task force expenses are absorbable within existing budgets.

Synopsis: Establishing, beginning July 1, 2028, the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program in the Department of Agriculture to award grants to eligible entities to develop and implement on-farm organics recycling, compost use, wasted food prevention, and food rescue; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $250,000 for the program; and requiring the Department, beginning December 31, 2028, to annually report to the General Assembly on the impact of the grant program.
Title: On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program - Established

bill_summary: The bill establishes the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. The program provides grants to farmers, nonprofits, and other eligible entities to support projects involving on-farm organics recycling, composting, food waste prevention, and food rescue efforts.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA)
stakeholders: Farmers, urban farmers, urban agricultural producers, soil conservation districts, nonprofit organizations, institutions of higher education, and Maryland businesses in partnership with agricultural producers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $250,000 starting in fiscal year 2028. According to the Fiscal Note, total state expenditures will increase from $250,000 in FY 2028 (covering initial administrative costs) to approximately $380,300 by FY 2031 to account for both the $250,000 in grant awards and ongoing personnel and software expenses. Local soil conservation districts and public institutions of higher education may experience a positive fiscal impact as grant recipients.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is mandated by the bill to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 in the state budget bill for the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program starting in fiscal year 2028.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the distribution of grant funds, processing state payments, and ensuring the fiscal integrity of the new grant program's expenditures.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and deposits, including the mandated appropriations for the new grant program, and oversees the state's fiscal planning.

The OAG will provide legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Maryland Department of the Environment regarding the development of regulations and the administration of the new grant program.
The Department of Agriculture is the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and reporting on the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program.
DBM is responsible for implementing the mandated $250,000 budget appropriation and overseeing the creation of the new administrative position required to manage the grant program.
The Department of the Environment is specifically named as the consulting agency to assist the Department of Agriculture in administering the program and identifying funding sources.
Institutions of higher education are designated as eligible entities to receive grants under the new program, making the commission relevant as the coordinating body for these institutions.

The bill requires the administering agencies to identify and apply for additional funding for the grant program, a task that aligns with the GGO's mission to assist state agencies in acquiring and managing grants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The grant program prioritizes projects that serve underserved and overburdened communities and includes partnerships with businesses, which falls under this office's mission to connect small businesses to economic opportunities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO’s mission to support the sustainability and profitability of Maryland's agricultural and rural industries is directly aligned with the goals of the on-farm organics and composting grant program.
MES provides technical and operational environmental services, including composting management, and was identified as an information source for the fiscal analysis of the bill.
As an operator of regional food distribution facilities, the Authority is relevant to the bill's objectives regarding wasted food prevention and food rescue.
As a state institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to apply for and receive grants under the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program.
The Council advocates for rural counties and agricultural interests, which are the primary beneficiaries of the on-farm composting and organics diversion grants.
As a public institution of higher education, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible entity for grant funding under the provisions of the bill.
The bill's focus on sustainable agricultural practices, composting, and food waste reduction aligns with this multi-agency initiative to promote environmental protection and sustainable development.
The University System of Maryland and its member institutions are eligible grant recipients under the definition of higher education institutions provided in the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a family child care provider who is a member of a reserve component to designate a substitute to provide family child care for not more than 45 working days in any 12-month period while the family child care provider is absent for required training and active service.
Title: Family Child Care Providers - Reserve Component Members - Substitute Provider
bill_summary: This bill requires a family child care provider who is a member of a military reserve component to designate a substitute to provide care during the provider's absence for required training and active service for up to 45 working days in any 12-month period.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)
stakeholders: Family child care providers who are members of a military reserve component, substitute child care providers, and families whose children are enrolled in these child care programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill's changes with existing resources, and there is no impact on State revenues or local finances. Small business family child care providers who are members of a reserve component may experience a meaningful benefit from the extended time authorized for using substitute providers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is responsible for the oversight and registration of family child care homes. The bill amends the Education Article and directly impacts MSDE's regulatory authority regarding the designation and time limits of substitute providers for child care homes operated by military personnel.

The Adjutant General oversees the Maryland National Guard. This bill specifically targets National Guard members who are child care providers, enabling them to fulfill training and service requirements without jeopardizing their civilian business operations.

The bill directly applies to members of the Maryland National Guard, providing them with legal provisions to use substitutes in their child care businesses for an extended period (45 days) during their absence for training or active service.

This agency is tasked with assisting active-duty service members and their families in securing benefits and support. This legislation provides economic stability for military families where a member is a small business owner (child care provider) called to service.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MSDE and the Military Department) involved in this bill, coordinates policy initiatives, and the Governor is responsible for signing the act into law.

Synopsis: Renaming the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to be the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; renaming the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to be the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; and altering the membership of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

bill_summary: This bill renames the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to be the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, and similarly renames the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing. It expands the membership of the council to 19 members by adding the Secretary of Disabilities or a designee. The bill also requires that existing printed materials, such as letterhead and business cards, be used up before new ones with the updated name are printed.
responsible_party: Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland, and the Maryland Department of Disabilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's state fiscal impact is minimal. Costs related to renaming the office and advisory council can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, as the bill mandates the use of current printed supplies until they are exhausted. The Maryland Department of Disabilities can also fulfill its new seat on the advisory council with existing resources. There is no impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary purpose is to rename this office to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing and restructure its associated Advisory Council.
The Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is a unit within the Governor's Office, and the Behavioral Health Advisory Council mentioned in the bill is also located within the Office of the Governor.
The bill expands the membership of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to include the Secretary of Disabilities or their designee.
The Superintendent of the Maryland School for the Deaf serves as a mandatory member of the renamed and expanded Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

The bill amends the Education Article regarding the Deaf Culture Digital Library, which is overseen by the Maryland State Library Agency, requiring coordination for sensitivity training and advisory board participation.
The Secretary of Aging or their designee is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to clarify immediate vesting rights for the Director of the newly renamed Office, which falls under DBM's purview as the central personnel agency.
The State Superintendent of Schools is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
The Secretary of Health is a mandated member of the Advisory Council and the department must cooperate with the Office on specific programs related to individuals who are deafblind.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
The Secretary of Human Services is a mandated member of the Advisory Council and the department must cooperate with the Office on specific programs for individuals who are deafblind.
The Secretary of Labor is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

The Secretary of Transportation is a mandated member of the Advisory Council, and the Office Director serves on the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation within MDOT.
The bill specifies vesting rights for the Director of the renamed Office within the state retirement system managed by this agency.
This office is responsible for the recruitment and vetting of the members appointed by the Governor to the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
A representative from the Commission on Civil Rights is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

Synopsis: Requiring nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives to notify each resident and prospective resident in writing or by written electronic communication if the nursing home, assisted living program, nurse midwife, or licensed certified midwife either does not maintain professional liability insurance or professional liability insurance coverage has lapsed; and requiring conspicuous posting of the information that the professional liability coverage has not been maintained.
Title: Professional Liability Insurance Coverage - Nursing Homes, Assisted Living Facilities, Nurse Midwives, and Licensed Certified Midwives - Disclosure (Nyeli Rose Lewis Act of 2026)

bill_summary: This bill, known as the Nyeli Rose Lewis Act of 2026, requires nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives to provide written or electronic notification to residents, prospective residents, or patients if the provider does not maintain professional liability insurance or if such coverage has lapsed and has not been renewed. It also requires these providers to post a notice regarding the lack of insurance in a conspicuous location within their facility or place of practice.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Residents and prospective residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities, patients of nurse midwives and licensed certified midwives, and the healthcare providers and facilities themselves.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of nursing homes, assisted living programs, and health occupations via the Board of Nursing, the Maryland Department of Health is responsible for the implementation and enforcement of the bill's professional liability insurance disclosure requirements.

The agency regulates the professional liability insurance market in Maryland and investigates consumer complaints; it is a critical stakeholder regarding the insurance lapses and renewals mentioned in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office administers the mandatory arbitration system for medical malpractice claims; the availability of professional liability insurance directly impacts the legal proceedings and potential recovery for patients under their jurisdiction.

The agency is dedicated to protecting the rights of older adults in long-term care settings; these disclosure requirements directly impact the transparency and consumer protections for the residents they serve.

The OAG provides primary legal counsel to the Department of Health and its various boards, assisting in the enforcement of the new disclosure mandates and representing the state in related litigation.
The commission's mission involves increasing healthcare accountability and informing consumer decision-making, which are the primary objectives of requiring insurance disclosures from providers.

OAH is responsible for adjudicating contested regulatory cases; it would hear any appeals from nursing homes, assisted living facilities, or midwives facing penalties for non-compliance with the bill.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Class B-SEC (small event center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George's County. The license is designed for venues operating on a per-event basis with a capacity between 75 and 110 individuals and requires a minimum capital investment of $350,000 in dining and kitchen facilities. It limits the number of such licenses to 24 per year and 3 per legislative district.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Owners and operators of small event centers in Prince George's County, and individuals attending events at these centers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Prince George’s County license fee revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $10,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2027, based on an expected three applications for the new license at $3,500 each. There is no impact on State finances or local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector and regulator of the alcohol industry, the Comptroller oversees the framework for alcohol licensing and collects the state taxes associated with the increased alcohol sales authorized by this new license.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, including local liquor boards, and reviews such legislation for constitutional and legal sufficiency.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, signs alcoholic beverage legislation into law, and holds the authority to appoint the members of the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners, which is the primary body tasked with issuing and regulating the licenses established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates that the bill has a potentially meaningful impact on small businesses, as it creates a new licensing category that allows small event center owners to generate additional revenue through alcohol sales.

The Department of Commerce is responsible for stimulating the economy and supporting business retention; the establishment of a new event-based liquor license supports the commercial and hospitality sectors in Prince George's County.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland State and local government entities, including county sheriffs, from entering into immigration enforcement agreements with the federal government to enforce civil immigration law. It also mandates the immediate termination of any such existing agreements, such as 287(g) agreements, upon the bill's enactment as an emergency measure.
responsible_party: The State of Maryland, local government units, and county sheriffs
stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies, county sheriffs, and individuals subject to civil immigration enforcement within Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While specific jurisdictions including Allegany, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, St. Mary’s, and Washington counties are required to terminate existing 287(g) agreements, no specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditure changes are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are directly prohibited by the bill from entering into or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements with the federal government.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities and parole/probation functions; the bill directly prohibits its agencies and employees from participating in civil immigration enforcement agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, directly advising the Governor on policy impacts like those mandated by this bill.

This office serves as the primary liaison to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which is the federal entity that enters into the immigration enforcement agreements (such as 287(g)) that this bill prohibits.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and has previously issued guidance to law enforcement regarding interactions with federal immigration authorities; it would likely oversee the legal termination of existing agreements.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing the state's mandate to terminate existing immigration enforcement agreements across all state agencies and units.
The MDTA maintains its own nationally accredited police force, which is subject to the bill's prohibition on state agencies entering or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements.
MDOT oversees several modal administrations with law enforcement functions (such as the Maryland Transit Administration police) that are subject to the bill's prohibitions.
The department oversees the Natural Resources Police, who are state officers prohibited by the bill from entering into immigration enforcement agreements.
As an agency that manages youth in detention and community supervision, DJS and its employees are prohibited from engaging in civil immigration enforcement under the bill.
As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM monitors the operational and budget execution impacts for agencies required to terminate existing federal agreements.

Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Orthoses and Prostheses (So Every Body Can Move Act)

bill_summary: The So Every Body Can Move Act requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and private health insurers to provide coverage for orthoses (devices that support or improve function of body parts) and clarifies existing coverage for prostheses. It establishes that medical necessity for these devices includes activities of daily living and physical activities like running or biking. The bill also sets limits on cost-sharing and requires insurance carriers and managed care organizations to submit compliance reports detailing claims and payments by 2032.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Individuals requiring orthoses or prostheses, healthcare providers, private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill essentially codifies current Medicaid coverage, resulting in no direct fiscal impact on the state program. For commercial insurance payers, the estimated annual cost to expand coverage for orthoses is approximately 1,450,000 (roughly 0.11 dollars per member per month). The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal special fund revenue increase from 125 dollar filing fees in FY 2027. Local governments may experience increased health care expenditures if they offer fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central personnel agency, DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note indicates the bill has a negligible impact on the program as it already provides some coverage for orthoses.

The department coordinates services and policy for residents with disabilities. The bill's expansion of coverage for orthoses and prostheses directly impacts the accessibility of essential equipment for this population.

MDH administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is required by the bill to provide coverage for orthoses starting in 2027. Additionally, MDH is responsible for jointly prescribing and submitting compliance reports on insurance claims.

The MHBE manages the marketplace for individual and small group health plans. These plans must include Essential Health Benefits (EHBs), which are directly affected by state mandates for coverage of medical devices like orthoses and prostheses.
MHCC is a regulatory agency within MDH that plans for health system needs and previously evaluated the cost impact and utilization of orthoses codes to inform this legislation.

MIA is the primary regulator for private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs. The bill requires MIA to oversee carrier compliance, jointly prescribe reporting forms, and aggregate claims data.

Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council to include an examination of the capacity of health care providers to deliver care to certain individuals and to identify methods by which the State can assist health care providers in delivering care to certain individuals; establishing the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program in the Maryland Department of Health to lead the State's public health efforts relating to brain health and dementia; etc.
Title: Health - Dementia Services and Brain Health Program and Provider Resource Toolkit

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to lead state public health efforts regarding brain health and dementia. It tasks the program with implementing the State Plan on Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias and requires MDH, in collaboration with the Department of Aging and other stakeholders, to develop and maintain a provider resource toolkit for health care providers by October 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Health care providers, individuals with or at risk for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, and their caregivers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland Department of Health (MDH) general fund expenditures increase by $77,700 in FY 2027 to hire one program administrator to manage the new program and toolkit. This expenditure is projected to increase annually, reaching $103,500 by FY 2031. The Maryland Department of Aging can participate using existing budgeted resources. There is no reported impact on local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Aging is explicitly required to provide staff support for the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council and is a named partner in developing the provider resource toolkit for dementia care.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the state's personnel and budget; the bill establishes a new permanent Director position and a dedicated program with specific general fund expenditure increases identified in the fiscal note.

The bill focuses on improving services and care for individuals with dementia, a population that often qualifies for disability services; the department coordinates services and policy for inclusive settings for this demographic.

The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency, responsible for establishing the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program, hiring the Director, and creating the provider resource toolkit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the duties and staffing structure of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council, which is an executive advisory body.
The Governor's Office receives reports on the program's activities, manages appointments to the council, and must include specific funding for the Director and Council in the annual budget.

The program is required to collaborate with State-led care transformation initiatives to incorporate dementia-capable care practices into health care models, which relates to the HSCRC's role in hospital quality and health outcomes.

The commission is responsible for planning health system needs and access; the bill requires the program to collaborate with care transformation initiatives and promote the toolkit across health sectors.

The program must coordinate with academic institutions and continuing education providers to promote dementia-specific education and training, which falls under the commission's regulatory and coordinating authority.
As a public research university, Morgan State may coordinate with the program regarding dementia-specific education, training, and academic partnerships for health care professionals.
The Office of Appointments is responsible for vetting and recommending candidates for the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council.
As a public institution of higher education, the college may be involved in the coordination of dementia-specific education or training initiatives specified in the bill.

The bill requires coordination with academic institutions for dementia-specific training and certification; the University System is the state's primary network for these public educational resources.

bill_summary: This bill makes the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council (ZEEVIC) a permanent entity by repealing its sunset date. It also modifies the Council's membership to include the Secretary of Agriculture and representatives of fuel cell vehicle manufacturers, alters its specific duties to focus on identifying barriers and recommending policies for electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and establishes a permanent annual reporting requirement.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local governments, electric vehicle advocacy organizations, electric utility companies, vehicle and charging station manufacturers, fleet operators, electrical workers, and environmental organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements for reporting and staffing the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council can be managed with existing resources. There is no anticipated impact on State or local revenues, and no additional expenditures are mandated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department is statutorily required to provide primary staff support to the Council, and the Secretary of Transportation serves as a member of the Council.
The agency is statutorily required to assist the Department of Transportation with staff support for the Council, and the Director is a member.
The Commission is statutorily required to assist with staff support for the Council, and the Executive Director of the Technical Staff is a member.
The bill adds the Secretary of Agriculture as a new permanent member of the Council.
The Secretary of the Environment is a member of the Council, which coordinates policies related to zero-emission vehicles and charging infrastructure.
The Secretary of Planning is a member of the Council; the Council's duties include recommending policies for integrating infrastructure into residential and commercial areas.
The Secretary of Commerce is a member of the Council, which focuses on economic and infrastructure development related to electric vehicles.
The Secretary of General Services is a member of the Council; the Council's focus on fleet purchases and charging infrastructure impacts the agency's management of state facilities and vehicles.
The People's Counsel is a member of the Council representing the interests of residential utility consumers in the development of electric vehicle infrastructure.
The Governor appoints several members of the Council, designates its leadership, and receives its annual reports. This bill makes these responsibilities permanent by repealing the sunset provision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines the permanent status, membership, and duties of the Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council, which falls under this administrative category.
The office is responsible for recruiting and vetting the various representatives the Governor must appoint to the Council under the revised membership structure.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from suspending or revoking a license to practice veterinary medicine in the State, reprimanding or censuring a licensee, or placing a licensee on probation solely on the basis of the licensee discussing or recommending the use of cannabis or a product that contains cannabidiol on an animal for potential therapeutic effect or health supplementation purposes.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from taking disciplinary action against a veterinarian, such as suspending or revoking a license, solely because the licensee discussed or recommended the use of cannabis or products containing cannabidiol (CBD) for an animal for therapeutic or health supplementation purposes.
responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed veterinarians, veterinary practitioners, and the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners has not historically taken disciplinary actions that would be prohibited by this bill, and the impact on small veterinary businesses is expected to be minimal or none.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is a unit within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. The bill directly amends the Agriculture Article to restrict the Board's disciplinary authority over licensed veterinarians regarding the discussion or recommendation of cannabis for animals.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative and counsel for state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners, and would provide legal guidance on the implementation of these new disciplinary restrictions.

The bill defines 'cannabis' by referencing the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which is overseen by this administration. While the bill regulates veterinary practice rather than the cannabis industry directly, it concerns the therapeutic discussion of products regulated by this agency.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including disciplinary hearings for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners. This bill establishes a legal defense or restriction that would be applied in such hearings.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Agriculture, and the Governor signed the bill into law.

Synopsis: Establishing, in Howard County, a gift basket permit that authorizes a permit holder to sell and deliver gift baskets containing beer, wine, or liquor to certain individuals under certain circumstances; providing that certain distance requirements do not apply to the issuance of the permit; and providing a gift basket permit fee of $100.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a gift basket permit in Howard County for businesses primarily engaged in the sale and delivery of flowers or gift baskets, authorizing them to sell and deliver baskets containing beer, wine, or liquor to legal-age consumers. The permit costs $100 annually, excludes chain stores and supermarkets, and requires that alcohol be purchased from local retail licensees and not exceed 10% of the holder's total annual gross sales.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Florists and gift basket businesses in Howard County, and consumers of legal drinking age in the county.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal impact. Local revenues for Howard County increase by $100 annually for each permit issued. Based on an illustrative estimate of 15 potential florist applicants, Howard County revenues are projected to increase by approximately $1,500 annually. Monitoring and enforcement activities are expected to be handled within existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the state's chief executive responsible for signing House Bill 456 into law. The office oversees the executive branch and the enforcement of state laws, including those modified by this legislation in the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

As the state's principal financial officer and regulator of the alcohol industry, the Comptroller is responsible for broad oversight of alcohol-related laws and tax collection. This bill establishes a new permit type for the sale and delivery of alcohol, which falls within the industry regulated by this agency.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal representative for the state. It is relevant to this bill as it provides legal counsel to the Governor and General Assembly on the constitutional and statutory implications of creating new permit types and amending the state's alcoholic beverages laws.

The bill amends existing law regarding the proximity of alcohol-licensed establishments to public school buildings. As the state agency overseeing public education and local school systems, the Department of Education is relevant to legislative changes that affect the zoning and licensing of businesses near school facilities.

bill_summary: This bill requires each institution of higher education in Maryland that provides on-campus housing to provide free menstrual hygiene products, such as size-appropriate tampons and sanitary napkins, in all student health centers by August 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Institutions of higher education that provide on-campus housing
stakeholders: Students at Maryland institutions of higher education with on-campus housing, the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and community colleges with on-campus housing.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local higher education expenditures are expected to increase, likely minimally, starting in fiscal 2029 (with some costs potentially incurred earlier) to cover the procurement of products, installation of dispensers, and ongoing maintenance. No specific dollar estimates are provided in the fiscal note. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, this agency is responsible for overseeing policies that affect the public and private institutions of higher education mandated by this bill.

As the governing body for 12 public institutions, the University System of Maryland will be directly responsible for the implementation and funding of the requirement to provide free menstrual hygiene products at its various campuses.

As an independent state agency and public university that provides on-campus housing, Morgan State is directly impacted by the bill's requirement to provide free menstrual hygiene products in its student health centers.
As a public honors college and independent unit of state government, the college is directly impacted by the bill and must implement the requirement in its student health center.

The bill mandates the provision of menstrual hygiene products specifically in student health centers; the Department of Health regulates health care facilities and oversees public health policy in the state.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budgets of public higher education institutions and will be involved in any fiscal adjustments required to meet the bill's mandates.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and institutions of higher education and may be required to advise on compliance with the new statutory requirements.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including public institutions of higher education, and is responsible for the final approval and signing of the bill into law.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Rural Readiness Program and the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to support rural communities in Maryland. Administered by the Rural Maryland Council, the program helps local entities build capacity for economic development and grant applications, while the fund provides grants of up to $50,000 for planning and community initiatives to those who complete the program.
responsible_party: Rural Maryland Council
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, State-recognized tribes, higher education institutions, regional planning agencies, and economic or workforce development organizations in 18 specified rural Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually starting in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund. Correspondingly, special fund revenues and expenditures increase as grants are awarded. Local governments in rural areas benefit from access to technical support and grants, though they are required to provide a 20% match for awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Rural Readiness Program and the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund, both of which are to be administered by the Rural Maryland Council. This is the primary implementing agency for the bill's core provisions.
The Rural Maryland Council is administratively housed within the Department of Agriculture. As the parent agency, the Department will oversee the Council's expanded responsibilities and budget.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the new Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund, a special nonlapsing fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State money.

The bill creates a new special fund requiring an estimated annual general fund expenditure of at least $100,000 for capitalization, necessitating coordination with DBM for budget planning and execution.
As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will provide legal counsel to the Rural Maryland Council regarding the establishment of the new program, fund regulations, and grant agreements.
The Council is required to submit an annual report on the grant program to the Governor. The Governor also oversees the executive branch and proposed the budget containing the fund's appropriations.

The bill focuses on rural economic development, which overlaps with the mission of the Department of Commerce. Furthermore, economic development organizations are identified as eligible applicants for the program.

Institutions of higher education are designated as eligible applicants for the Rural Readiness Program and associated grants, making the bill relevant to the Commission's oversight of these institutions.
As an institution of higher education in the State, Morgan State University is an eligible applicant for the Rural Readiness Program and the new capacity building grants.
Institutions within the University System of Maryland are eligible applicants for the program and funding established by the bill.
As an institution of higher education in the State, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible applicant for the program and grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Board (MAERDAB) is responsible for reviewing and approving grant applications and recipients for the new fund.
