bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to annually proclaim January as Muslim American Heritage Month and May as Jewish American Heritage Month in recognition of the contributions made by these communities to the State. The proclamations urge educational and cultural organizations to observe these months with appropriate programs, ceremonies, and activities.
responsible_party: The Governor
stakeholders: Muslim Marylanders, Jewish Marylanders, and educational and cultural organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, this bill has no financial impact on State or local governments. Commemorating Muslim American Heritage Month and Jewish American Heritage Month does not affect State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Governor to annually issue proclamations for Muslim American Heritage Month and Jewish American Heritage Month.

This office oversees cultural and faith-based commissions and is responsible for community engagement. It would likely play a role in coordinating the observances and activities associated with these heritage months.
The Secretary of State is the custodian of the state's official records, including the proclamations issued by the Governor as required by this bill.

The bill requires the Governor's proclamation to urge educational organizations to observe these heritage months. As the oversight body for the state's public education system, MSDE is relevant to this directive.
The bill requires the Governor's proclamation to urge cultural organizations to observe these heritage months. The Department of Commerce oversees the state's cultural and arts initiatives.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning on or before July 1, 2026, and every 6 months thereafter, the Department of the Environment to report to the General Assembly on any changes in federal environmental policy that have been deemed legally valid by a final decision of a federal court and, if there has been a change in federal environmental policy, on the steps the State is taking to respond to that change.
Title: Department of the Environment - Federal Environmental Policy - Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to report to the General Assembly every six months regarding legally valid changes in federal environmental policy. These reports must specifically address changes in greenhouse gas emissions standards for motor vehicles and stationary sources, impacts on the State's federally delegated authority, and policies related to nuclear power, while also detailing any steps the State is taking in response to these federal changes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Maryland Department of the Environment, the Maryland General Assembly, motor vehicle manufacturers, operators of stationary emission sources, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can fulfill the bill's reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Department of the Environment to report on state responses to federal policy shifts, which directly involves executive policy strategy and intergovernmental relations.

The Comptroller serves as a member of the Board of Public Works and regulates various industries. While not the primary reporter, shifts in federal environmental policy can impact state revenues and industrial regulations overseen by the agency.

The bill requires reporting on changes in federal environmental policy deemed 'legally valid by a final decision of a federal court.' The OAG is the chief legal officer for the state and would be responsible for interpreting these legal decisions and providing counsel on the state's legal responses.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and personnel. While the fiscal note states the bill's requirements can be met with existing resources, DBM manages the long-term fiscal planning and efficiency of the agency responsible for the reporting.

The bill's reporting requirements include federal policy changes regarding stationary source emissions, which can significantly impact business attraction, retention, and the economic competitiveness of Maryland's industrial sectors.

The Department of the Environment is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, responsible for monitoring federal policy, analyzing court decisions, and producing the required semi-annual reports.

The bill specifically references federal findings on whether greenhouse gas emissions cause air pollution that may endanger public health or welfare. The Department of Health is the state's lead agency for protecting public health and monitoring related environmental health risks.
DHCD administers energy efficiency programs and revitalization efforts that may be affected by changes in federal environmental policy and greenhouse gas emissions standards.

DNR is responsible for conserving natural resources and managing state lands. Changes in federal greenhouse gas policies and environmental standards impact the agency's restoration and conservation goals, particularly those related to climate change.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and manages environmental preservation through land use planning. It plays a role in the state's broader response to environmental policy changes through its coordination of the Smart, Green & Growing initiative.

The bill focuses heavily on greenhouse gas emissions from motor vehicles and engines. MDOT oversees the state's transportation network and is directly impacted by shifts in federal vehicle emissions standards and delegated Clean Air Act authority.
As a modal administration of MDOT, the MAA's operations at BWI and Martin State Airport are subject to federal environmental policies and emissions standards for engines and stationary sources.

The MCEC advances clean energy adoption and manages clean energy financing. Changes in federal environmental policy and greenhouse gas regulations directly influence the center's mission and the economic viability of the projects it finances.

The MEA coordinates state energy policy and manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. The bill's focus on greenhouse gas standards, stationary sources, and nuclear power directly overlaps with the MEA's core policy and planning responsibilities.
The MPA manages state-owned port facilities, which include stationary sources and heavy equipment impacted by federal greenhouse gas emissions standards and environmental regulations.

The MTA operates large multi-modal public transit systems. Federal policy changes regarding motor vehicle and engine emissions standards directly affect the MTA's fleet procurement and sustainability goals.
The MDTA maintains toll facilities and is responsible for the environmental impact and management of traffic flow on its roadways, which are affected by federal vehicle emissions standards.

The MVA is responsible for the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP) and oversees vehicle-related regulations. The bill's emphasis on motor vehicle greenhouse gas standards and federal findings on mobile source pollution is highly relevant to MVA's regulatory functions.
The OLA is responsible for ensuring fiscal compliance and evaluating the performance of state programs. They may audit MDE's adherence to the new reporting mandates established by the bill.

The OPC advocates for utility consumers. Federal policy changes related to stationary source emissions and nuclear power can impact utility rates and the transition to cleaner energy sources, areas where the OPC represents consumer interests.

The PSC regulates public utilities, including power plants (stationary sources) and nuclear energy providers. The bill's specific inclusion of nuclear power and stationary source emissions standards makes it highly relevant to the PSC's regulatory oversight.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates sustainable development and environmental protection. The reporting on federal policy changes and the state's subsequent response is central to the initiative's goal of aligning agency activities with sustainability visions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Various climate and environmental task forces and advisory boards appointed by the Governor may be involved in reviewing the required reports or formulating the state's response to federal policy changes.

The Trust supports environmental restoration. While not a primary policy agency, the reporting on federal policy shifts can inform the Trust's grant-making priorities for water quality and environmental education.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council advises the Governor on the management and restoration of the Bay. Federal environmental policy shifts, especially those affecting delegated authority under the Clean Water Act, are critical to the Council's advisory mission.

Maryland participates in several environmental and transportation interstate compacts. Changes in federal policy on greenhouse gases often require coordinated responses through these interstate bodies.

SHA manages the state's non-toll highways. Federal policy changes affecting vehicle emissions standards and air quality findings influence SHA's planning, environmental mitigation, and traffic management strategies.

Synopsis: Altering the quota on the number of alcoholic beverages licenses that the Board of License Commissioners for Cecil County may issue to apply only to Class A licenses based on a certain ratio.
Title: Cecil County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
bill_summary: This bill alters the quota for Class A alcoholic beverages licenses in Cecil County, limiting the number of licenses to one for every 2,000 registered voters. It requires at least two Class A licenses in each election district and specifies that other license classes are excluded from the quota calculation.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Cecil County
stakeholders: Potential Class A alcoholic beverages license applicants and registered voters in Cecil County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or Cecil County finances or operations. According to the fiscal note, there is no State effect and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing legislation into law and overseeing the executive branch, which includes the administration of state-mandated local boards like the Cecil County Board of License Commissioners.
As the state's chief regulator of the alcohol industry, the Comptroller oversees the licensing and tax collection framework that this bill's alteration of Cecil County license quotas affects.

The bill defines alcoholic beverage license quotas based on the number of registered voters in the county. The State Board of Elections manages the statewide voter registration system which serves as the source of this data.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, including local boards of license commissioners, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of alcoholic beverages laws.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person in St. Mary's County from standing in a roadway, a shoulder, a median divide, or an intersection determined by the county or a municipal corporation in the county, in consultation with the State Highway Administration, to be inherently dangerous; and prohibiting a police officer from issuing a citation for a violation of the Act unless appropriate signs have been installed.
Title: St. Mary's County - Prohibition on Standing in Inherently Dangerous Highway

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits individuals in St. Mary's County from standing in roadways, shoulders, median dividers, or intersections that have been designated as inherently dangerous by the county or a municipal corporation in consultation with the State Highway Administration. It mandates that law enforcement may only issue citations for violations if appropriate warning signs have been installed in accordance with state standards, and any signs placed on State highways must be approved by the State Highway Administration.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County, municipal corporations within St. Mary's County, and the Maryland State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Pedestrians and motorists in St. Mary's County, local law enforcement agencies, and local government officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances. The State Highway Administration and St. Mary's County can handle the bill's consultation and signage requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the parent department of the State Highway Administration (SHA), MDOT is responsible for the state's transportation network and the implementation of the Transportation Article, which this bill amends.

The bill explicitly requires St. Mary's County to consult with SHA when determining if a state roadway is 'inherently dangerous' and mandates that any signage installed on state highways must be approved by SHA and comply with its manual and specifications.

The Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing motor vehicle laws on state highways. The bill establishes a new prohibition for which their officers would be responsible for issuing citations, subject to the signage requirements outlined in the legislation.
The bill creates a new traffic-related offense, which will lead to citations that must be processed and adjudicated through the state's judicial system.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill, for fiscal year 2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, a minimum appropriation for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman from certain money remitted by managed care organizations and, under certain circumstances, general funds.
Title: Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman - Mandatory Appropriation

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to provide a mandatory annual appropriation of at least $2,000,000 for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman within the Maryland Department of Aging. The funding is sourced from remittances paid by Medicaid managed care organizations that fail to meet medical loss ratio standards; if these remittances are insufficient, the state must provide general funds to cover the difference. This funding is intended to supplement and not supplant existing funding for the office.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities, the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, and Medicaid managed care organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill establishes a mandated appropriation beginning in fiscal 2028. State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $2,000,000 annually starting in fiscal 2028 to satisfy the mandate or backfill Medicaid funding. While up to $2,000,000 in special funds from managed care organization remittances will be redirected to the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, this reduces the special funds available for Medicaid, necessitating a general fund increase. Local area agencies on aging may also see an increase in revenues and expenditures to support local ombudsman staff.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific minimum appropriation for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman in the annual budget bill, directly impacting the Governor's executive budget-proposing authority.
The Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman is located within the Department of Aging. The bill provides a mandatory funding source for this office and expands its operational resources.

The bill's primary funding source involves money remitted by Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), which are regulated and managed by the Maryland Department of Health. The fiscal note indicates a corresponding decrease in MDH special fund expenditures.

As the principal fiscal agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM must manage the implementation of this new mandatory appropriation and the potential use of general funds to fill funding gaps.
The Comptroller is responsible for collecting the nursing facility quality assessments and other state revenues mentioned in the bill, and for distributing those funds as directed by law.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Governor and state agencies regarding the implementation of new laws and mandatory budget requirements.
OLA is responsible for auditing executive branch agencies and ensuring that mandatory appropriations are used in accordance with the law and that financial reporting is accurate.

Synopsis: Altering which entities are eligible to receive grants from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund to exclude certain physicians, laboratories, and persons, and include certain nonprofit institutions.
Title: Public Health - Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund - Entities Eligible for Grants

Physicians -see also- MedExmnrs; Pediatr; Psychiatrists etc.

bill_summary: This emergency bill narrows the list of entities eligible to receive grants from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund. It restricts eligibility to nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations, effectively removing laboratories and individual persons from the list of eligible grant recipients.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations involved in pediatric cancer research, as well as laboratories and individual researchers who will no longer be eligible for grants.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, this bill has no state or local fiscal impact because the changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances. While the fiscal 2027 budget includes $2,481,141 in special fund expenditures for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, this bill does not change that appropriation amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Health is explicitly responsible for administering the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, adopting regulations for the grant program, and submitting annual reports to the General Assembly regarding the fund's use.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill and fiscal note reference the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission (established under § 20–121), which is tasked with overseeing the award of competitive grants and developing criteria for grant applications.
The Governor is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which includes mandated appropriations for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, and oversees the Department of Health.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the development and execution of the state budget, which includes the special fund expenditures for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission, and would likely be involved in reviewing the regulations and grant eligibility criteria altered by this bill.
Educational institutions are specifically listed as eligible entities to receive grants from the fund; the Commission oversees policies related to these institutions.
Member institutions of the University System of Maryland are educational institutions eligible to apply for and receive research grants from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
As a public educational institution and research university, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to receive research grants from the fund.
As a public educational institution, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible entity to receive research grants from the fund.

Synopsis: Providing that a registered reduction operator is not civilly liable for transferring and a veterans service organization is not civilly liable for receiving unclaimed hydrolyzed or soil remains of a veteran or an eligible dependent of a veteran for the purposes of disposition if acting in good faith.
Title: Reduction Facilities and Veterans Service Organizations - Hydrolyzed and Soil Remains - Immunity

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: The bill provides civil immunity to registered reduction operators, funeral establishments, and crematories when they transfer unclaimed hydrolyzed or soil remains of veterans or their eligible dependents to a veterans service organization in good faith. It also grants civil immunity to veterans service organizations that receive such remains for the purposes of final disposition.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Office of Cemetery Oversight) and Maryland Department of Health (State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors)
stakeholders: Veterans and their eligible dependents, registered reduction operators, licensed funeral establishments, crematory permit holders, and veterans service organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State operations and finances are not materially affected by the bill. There is no local fiscal impact, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a statutory civil immunity defense for certain entities, which directly impacts civil litigation and the adjudication of claims within the state court system managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which regulates licensed funeral establishments and certain crematories and reduction facilities. These entities are directly granted civil immunity under the bill.

The Office of Cemetery Oversight within the Department of Labor regulates crematories and natural organic reduction facilities. The bill provides civil immunity to the registered reduction operators and permit holders regulated by this department.

The bill focuses on the disposition of remains for veterans and their dependents. The Department of Veterans and Military Families is the principal agency for veteran affairs and, according to the fiscal note, acts as the designated entity for final disposition if a veterans service organization does not take possession.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state agencies involved (Health, Labor, and DVMF) and is responsible for representing the state's interests in matters involving changes to civil liability and the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article.

Synopsis: Clarifying the membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain employees of certain Maryland Department of Health facilities; and clarifying that certain participating employees who are appointed, promoted, or transferred are members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System as a condition of employment.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Membership - Clarifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The bill expands the membership of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System to include CAMH Specialist I and II employees at seven specific Maryland Department of Health facilities. It establishes that these employees are members as a condition of employment beginning July 1, 2026, and provides a mechanism for transferring service credit from the Employees' Pension System or Employees' Retirement System.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: CAMH Specialist I and II employees at specific Maryland Department of Health facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the bill affects only approximately 12 positions. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Health (MDH) by expanding the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System (CORS) to include specific job classifications (CAMH Specialist I and II) at several MDH facilities, such as the Eastern Shore Hospital Center and Springfield Hospital Center.

As the agency responsible for managing the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), it is the primary entity tasked with implementing the bill's requirements, including the transfer of service credits and the administration of benefits for the newly included members.

The department serves as the state's central personnel agency, managing employee benefits and policies. The bill modifies retirement system eligibility and membership conditions for state employees, which falls under its oversight of personnel resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill clarifies and amends the eligibility criteria for membership in the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System, which is the principal retirement plan for various law enforcement and specialized roles within this department.

The bill's statutory amendments clarify the inclusion of several Department of Juvenile Services positions, such as community detention officers and case management specialists, within the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state agencies and the retirement system regarding the interpretation and implementation of the statutory changes to the pension laws and membership conditions.

Synopsis: Renaming the Children's Cabinet Fund to be the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund; requiring the Governor, for fiscal years 2028 through 2030, to include an appropriation in the annual budget bill to the Fund of an amount at least equal to the appropriation to the Fund in fiscal year 2027; and requiring, in fiscal year 2031, the Governor to provide an appropriation to the Fund of $500,000 above the appropriation for fiscal year 2030, to be used for grants to the local management boards.
Title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards

NarrowSubjects.Name: Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.

bill_summary: This bill renames the Children’s Cabinet Fund to the Children’s Cabinet Interagency Fund and establishes mandated appropriation levels for the fund between fiscal 2028 and 2031. The funds are designated for grants to local management boards to support interagency service delivery systems for children, youth, and families.
responsible_party: Governor’s Office for Children
stakeholders: Maryland children, youth, and families, and local management boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in fiscal 2031 to meet the mandated appropriation requirement. For fiscal 2028 through 2030, the Governor is required to appropriate an amount at least equal to the fiscal 2027 appropriation (estimated at $22,300,000). Local management boards will see a corresponding $500,000 increase in revenues and expenditures in fiscal 2031 due to the additional grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution. It must ensure the bill's mandated appropriations for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund are included and managed starting in fiscal 2028.

The bill amends the Education Article to require the department to collaborate with the fund's fiscal agent on a redesigned rate-setting process for nonpublic schools and child care programs. MSDE is also a member of the Children's Cabinet that oversees the fund.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to update the name of the fund used to provide services to children with disabilities. As a member of the Children's Cabinet, the department is involved in setting the priorities for the fund's expenditures.

The bill substantively renames the fund within the Human Services Article and mandates its funding levels. DHS is a primary member of the Children's Cabinet and is involved in programs related to out-of-home care and child well-being covered by the fund.

As a member of the Children's Cabinet, the Department of Juvenile Services participates in determining the allocation of the fund, particularly regarding prevention of out-of-home placements and services for at-risk youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This entity encompasses the Children's Cabinet, which is the body responsible for adopting the priorities, policies, and procedures for the fund and overseeing the distribution of grants to local management boards.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include specific minimum appropriations for the fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2031.

The Governor's Office for Children is explicitly named as the fiscal agent for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund. The agency staffs the Children's Cabinet and provides technical assistance to the local management boards that receive the grants mandated by the bill.

Synopsis: Removing the maximum amount that Baltimore City is authorized to establish for civil and criminal fines and penalties for violating certain ordinances, rules, or regulations.
Title: Baltimore City - Ordinance Enforcement - Fines and Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum civil and criminal fines and penalties that the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore may establish for the violation of any city ordinance, rule, or regulation from $1,000 to $5,000.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
stakeholders: Residents, businesses, and entities in Baltimore City subject to local ordinances, rules, and regulations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 as the city imposes and collects higher fines for ordinance violations. For context, in fiscal 2024, the Baltimore City Environmental Control Board issued citations totaling approximately $7.8 million and collected $5.9 million under the previous $1,000 cap. The city indicates that significantly higher fines might initially reduce collection rates, though unpaid fines can result in property liens or tax sales.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the Administrative Office of the Courts is relevant because the bill increases the maximum civil and criminal fines for ordinance violations. These violations are adjudicated within the state court system, specifically the District Court of Maryland, which the AOC manages and supports.

The Governor's Office is relevant as the Governor must sign or veto the legislation. Additionally, the office oversees the execution of state laws, including those that grant or expand the general powers of local jurisdictions like Baltimore City.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and the Governor. They review legislation for legal and constitutional sufficiency, and they would represent the state in any legal challenges regarding the delegation of authority to Baltimore City to increase these penalties.

Synopsis: Establishing in Anne Arundel County a Class GC (golf course) license that authorizes the holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption at a golf course with at least nine holes; and establishing in Anne Arundel County sports activity venue licenses that authorize the holder to sell beer and wine or beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption at a certain sports activity venue.
Title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages – Golf Course License and Sports Activity Venue Licenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: This bill establishes new alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County, specifically a Class GC (golf course) license for courses with at least nine holes and sports activity venue licenses for commercial recreational facilities offering activities like bowling, golf simulators, and pickleball. It defines the scope of the licenses, sets operating hours from 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. daily, eliminates the need for separate Sunday permits, and establishes annual fees and training requirements for license holders.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Owners and operators of golf courses and commercial recreational facilities in Anne Arundel County, and patrons of these establishments.
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues will increase starting in fiscal 2027 by an indeterminate amount depending on the number of licenses issued. The annual fees are $1,200 for a Class GC license or a sports activity venue beer, wine, and liquor license, and $740 for a sports activity venue beer and wine license. The bill has no effect on State revenues or expenditures and no impact on local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief executive, the Governor signed this bill into law (Chapter 850) and oversees the executive branch departments that may provide peripheral support or oversight to local licensing boards.

The Comptroller is the primary state official responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting related state revenues, although this bill specifically addresses local licenses in Anne Arundel County.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies regarding the interpretation and enforcement of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.
The Secretary of State is the custodian of the state's official records and is responsible for processing and recording the laws passed by the General Assembly and signed by the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring certain health systems to comply with certain insurance provisions regarding notice of termination of contracts; altering the notification requirements a carrier is required to provide an enrollee regarding changes to the carrier's provider panel; altering the notice requirements a carrier is required to provide to the Insurance Commissioner for certain material changes to the carrier's provider panel; requiring certain notice if a carrier and health system intend to terminate certain contracts; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands requirements for health insurance carriers regarding notifications to enrollees when providers, specifically including behavioral health providers, are terminated from a network. It mandates that carriers and health systems provide 90 days' notice before contract terminations and continue to adhere to contract terms, including reimbursement rates and billing protections, for a 90-day transitional period. The bill also establishes a 90-day special enrollment period for individuals whose regular healthcare providers are removed from their plan's provider panel.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance enrollees, primary care providers, behavioral health providers, health systems, hospitals, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange can manage the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. While the Insurance Commissioner is authorized to impose a $5,000 per day fine on carriers that fail to file required access plan updates, this penalty is not expected to significantly affect State revenues. There is no anticipated fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for managing state employee benefits, including health insurance policies, the Department of Budget and Management is impacted by regulations affecting carrier provider networks and the continuity of care for state employees and their dependents.

The bill adds provisions to the Health - General Article specifically governing health systems (hospitals and their affiliates). MDH regulates these entities and also oversees behavioral health services, which are subject to new notification requirements under the bill.

The bill requires carriers and health systems to adhere to contract reimbursement terms for 90 days after termination or nonrenewal. This directly impacts the regulation of hospital revenues and the all-payer system overseen by the HSCRC.

The bill mandates a new special enrollment period for individuals on the Individual Exchange whose providers are terminated from a network. MHBE is responsible for administering this marketplace and implementing these enrollment changes.

The MHCC is responsible for planning for health system needs and improving access to care. The bill's requirements for network access plans and notifications regarding material changes to provider panels fall within the commission's scope of monitoring health services.

MIA is the primary regulator for this bill. The Insurance Commissioner is responsible for reviewing network access plans, developing uniform forms for transitional care, receiving termination notices, and imposing fines for non-compliance.

The OAG serves as the legal representative for the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health. It would provide legal counsel and enforcement support regarding the consumer protection and regulatory requirements established by the bill.

Synopsis: Transferring the authority to regulate certain crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors; altering the circumstances under which the Governor may remove an appointed member of the Board; altering the quorum of the Board; and specifying that the Board may take action with a simple majority vote of the quorum.
Title: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors – Board Operations and Regulation of Crematories and Reduction Facilities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds

Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill transfers the authority to regulate crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors. It updates board operations by altering quorum requirements and the process for removing appointed members, mandates the hiring of an additional full-time inspector by fiscal 2028, and requires the board to establish a stakeholder workgroup to review relevant regulations.
responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors
stakeholders: Crematory operators, reduction facility operators, licensed morticians, funeral directors, and consumers of death care services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by an estimated $101,200 in fiscal 2027 to support the hiring of an additional inspector, as required by the bill's mandate for the board to maintain at least two inspectors. These costs are projected to grow to $103,500 by fiscal 2031. Office of Cemetery Oversight special fund revenues decrease by approximately $6,000 biannually starting in fiscal 2027 due to the transfer of registration and permit authority. The Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors will see an indeterminate increase in special fund revenue from newly collected crematory and reduction facility fees. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primarily impacts the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which is a regulatory body situated within the Maryland Department of Health. The department will gain regulatory oversight and revenue from crematories and reduction facilities, and the bill mandates the creation of a new inspector position within this board.

The bill transfers regulatory authority and oversight of crematories and reduction facilities away from the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which is an agency within the Department of Labor. This results in a direct loss of jurisdiction and special fund revenue for the department.

The bill alters the Governor's statutory authority to remove appointed members of the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, changing the criteria for removal to include repeated unexplained absences or just cause.

The bill explicitly requires the creation of a new Position Identification Number (PIN) for a full-time inspector starting in fiscal year 2028, which falls under DBM's responsibility for managing state personnel resources and the annual budget.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the OAG provides counsel to the Board. Additionally, the bill specifically allows for the referral of consumer complaints to the OAG for binding arbitration.
The bill identifies the OAH as a potential venue for binding arbitration of consumer complaints and provides for contested case hearings for individuals aggrieved by Board decisions.

The bill involves the transfer of records and processes related to identifying unclaimed remains of veterans and their eligible dependents for proper disposition, which is a core interest of this department.
The Board is required to pay all collected fees and funds to the Comptroller for distribution into the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors Fund.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding civil liability protections for funeral establishments and establishes procedures for judicial review of Board decisions in circuit courts.

The bill establishes scientific and safety standards for 'natural organic reduction' (composting), including heavy metal and pathogen testing, which relates to the environmental protection standards overseen by MDE.

Because the bill modifies the composition and removal rules for the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, this office will be involved in the administrative process of vetting and managing these gubernatorial appointments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a certain controller from knowingly selling the personal data of a consumer to a certain governmental unit that has engaged in or supported civil immigration enforcement under certain circumstances; requiring a custodian of a public record to take reasonable steps to determine whether a public record is accessed for enforcing immigration law; requiring an entity that operates a certain message switching system to take certain actions regarding system access; etc.
Title: Data Privacy - Consumer Data, Public Records, and Message Switching System (Data Privacy Act)
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 874

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill enhances privacy protections for Maryland residents by prohibiting data controllers from selling personal data to government units involved in civil immigration enforcement. It requires custodians of public records to take reasonable steps to ensure records are not accessed for immigration enforcement purposes without a warrant and extends these protections to law enforcement message switching systems. Additionally, it expands the definition of sensitive data and requires state and local government entities to update their data protection and disclosure procedures.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Motor Vehicle Administration, Department of State Police, and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents, data controllers and processors, state and local government agencies, law enforcement agencies, and individuals or entities requesting public records.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary may increase significantly to implement new procedures for determining the intent of every data request. While most other state and local agencies are expected to manage the requirements within existing resources, some local governments may experience significant operational impacts due to the increased scrutiny required for public record requests. The bill has no direct impact on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies that the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts will experience a significant operational impact and increased general fund expenditures to implement new procedures for determining the purpose of data requests across all courthouse kiosks and records.

As a major collector of sensitive personal and financial data, the Comptroller is subject to the bill's expanded Public Information Act restrictions and the requirement to develop procedures to prevent the sale or redisclosure of sensitive data.

DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and personnel oversight; it will need to manage the budgetary impact of the bill, including potential staffing or programming costs for agencies like the Judiciary and DPSCS.

Mentioned in the fiscal note as being affected, MSDE will need to ensure its data management and public record disclosure policies comply with the bill's new sensitive data protections and immigration enforcement inquiries.

As an agency handling sensitive health and personal data, MDH is impacted by the bill's new restrictions on data disclosure for immigration enforcement and the requirement to develop privacy procedures in consultation with DoIT.
The bill explicitly requires every Maryland governmental entity to consult with DoIT to develop and publish procedures that prevent the sale and redisclosure of sensitive data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically names DPSCS to adopt regulations regarding message switching systems and reporting requirements for immigration-related data requests. It is a primary implementing agency for the public safety provisions.

The bill specifically tasks the Motor Vehicle Administration (a unit of MDOT) with adopting regulations to ensure compliance with data disclosure restrictions and mandates annual reporting on immigration enforcement data requests.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to adopt regulations to enforce data privacy compliance and to report annually on requests for personal information or facial recognition searches for immigration purposes.

The OAG oversees the Public Information Act Manual and website and will provide legal guidance to all state agencies on implementing the bill's new restrictions on data sharing and immigration enforcement inquiries.

Synopsis: Authorizing specified organizations that are affiliated with a professional National Football League team that plays its home games in Baltimore City to conduct raffles, subject to certain limitations; and extending for a period of 4 years and one month to June 30, 2029 the termination date of certain provisions of law authorizing certain organizations that are affiliated with a professional Major League Baseball team that plays its home games in Baltimore City to conduct certain raffles.
Title: Baltimore City - Raffles - Organizations Affiliated With Professional Baseball and Football Teams

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes charitable organizations affiliated with professional National Football League (NFL) teams that play home games in Baltimore City to conduct raffles during games, subject to specific geographical and time-based limitations. It also extends the existing authorization for organizations affiliated with Major League Baseball (MLB) teams to conduct similar raffles through May 31, 2031.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Police Commissioner and designated Baltimore City agencies
stakeholders: Charitable organizations affiliated with professional NFL and MLB teams in Baltimore City, and individuals attending home games of these teams.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no material impact on State or local finances. The Fiscal Note indicates that while there might be a potential decrease in State lottery revenues due to substitution effects, the impact is small enough that State finances are not affected. The Baltimore City Police Department can manage the issuance of raffle permits using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the regulatory body for all commercial gaming and lottery operations in the state, this agency is responsible for overseeing the integrity of gaming. The fiscal note explicitly mentions a potential, though minor, impact on state lottery revenues due to substitution effects from these authorized raffles.

The Maryland Stadium Authority plans, builds, and manages the Camden Yards Sports Complex, which includes Oriole Park and M&T Bank Stadium. The bill's provisions regarding raffle geofencing and timing are directly tied to these physical locations and the professional teams (Orioles and Ravens) that use them.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector. The agency was consulted for the fiscal note and has an interest in the tracking of state revenues, including potential impacts on lottery funds or tax implications from gaming proceeds.

While local city agencies handle the permitting, the Maryland State Police is the primary law enforcement agency for the state and often coordinates on gaming enforcement and criminal law issues. They were also consulted during the fiscal analysis of the bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They may be involved in interpreting the interaction between this local authorization and broader state criminal laws regarding gaming.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Governor's signature to become law and impacts gaming policy in the state's largest city.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law governing information technology plans apply to certain public institutions of higher education; establishing a policy of the State that State and higher education employee e-mail systems and resources are intended to support State business and may not serve as a public forum; requiring certain policies, plans, and standards to include provisions to implement systems that automatically filter spam e-mail from certain email accounts; etc.
Title: Information Technology – State and Higher Education E–Mail – Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that email systems for State and public higher education employees are intended to support State business and are not public forums. It requires State IT policies and standards to include protections against spam and other unauthorized uses, such as automated filtering, while permitting incidental personal use that has a minimal impact on resources and follows professional norms.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Information Technology and the governing boards of public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: State and higher education employees, State agencies, and public institutions of higher education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances as it generally codifies existing practices regarding email usage and security. There is no direct impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for state information technology strategy and policy, the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) is responsible for overseeing the IT plans and standards that this bill modifies, including the new email and spam filtering requirements.

The bill explicitly requires the governing boards of public institutions of higher education, such as USM, to develop and submit IT policies and plans that comply with the new email security and usage standards.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State's governing board is specifically required by the bill to submit IT policies and plans regarding employee email systems and anti-spam measures.

The bill mandates that governing boards of public institutions of higher education, including St. Mary's College, develop IT policies and plans that incorporate the specified email usage and security requirements.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the implementation of policies. This bill involves legal definitions of 'State Business' and 'public forums,' which may require legal interpretation and defense of state personnel communication policies.
As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is affected by policies regarding state employee resources and the regulation of 'incidental personal use' of information technology by employees.

The bill's definition of 'spam email' specifically excludes bulk communications from 'exclusive representatives' (unions), which falls under the jurisdiction of PERB regarding collective bargaining and labor-management communication.

MHEC serves as the coordinating board for the state's higher education institutions, which are directly impacted by the bill's requirements for higher education employee email systems and IT planning.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch units that must comply with these new IT policies and receives the final approved plans through the Secretary of Information Technology.

OLA conducts fiscal and compliance audits of state agencies and will be responsible for ensuring that agencies have correctly implemented and documented the mandated IT email policies and spam filters.
As the oversight body for the state's public education system, MSDE is identified in the fiscal note as a relevant stakeholder and must ensure its own IT plans align with the bill's requirements.
MDOT is a major executive department with a large employee base that will be subject to the new email usage policies and anti-spam technical standards required by the bill.
The Comptroller's Office is a significant executive unit that must update its IT policies and standards to comply with the bill's provisions regarding state business email use.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on awarding the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship after June 30, 2030; and repealing the limitation on renewing the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship if the scholarship recipient received an initial scholarship before June 30, 2030.
Title: Higher Education - Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship - Repeal of Termination Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the June 30, 2030, termination date for awarding initial scholarships under the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship program and removes the limitation on renewing scholarships for recipients after that date, effectively making the program permanent.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Maryland residents who are veterans, active service members, or activated reservists who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, as well as their spouses and children.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures will increase by an estimated $750,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2031 to maintain the scholarship program beyond its previous sunset date. There is no fiscal impact through fiscal 2030 as the program is already funded at approximately $750,000 annually. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for administering state financial aid programs, the Maryland Higher Education Commission (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is responsible for awarding the scholarships, managing the program's special fund, and submitting annual reports to the General Assembly.

The scholarship specifically benefits Maryland veterans and active-duty service members who served in the Afghanistan and Iraq conflicts, as well as their families. This aligns with the agency's mission to assist these groups in securing benefits and services.

The Governor's Office is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which includes the $750,000 appropriation for this scholarship program. Additionally, the Governor appoints members to various boards and oversees the executive departments involved.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for developing the state's budget and long-term fiscal planning. The bill has a notable fiscal impact by maintaining $750,000 in general fund expenditures indefinitely beyond FY 2030.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund separately.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Comptroller shall account for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.

The scholarship is available to active service members and members of reserve components who were activated for the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, all of whom fall under the senior military advisory and readiness purview of the Adjutant General.
The scholarship is specifically available to active service members and reserve members who served in the specified conflicts, many of whom are members of the Maryland Army or Air National Guard.

The scholarship amount is capped based on the average tuition, fees, and room and board at institutions within the University System of Maryland, and these institutions serve as eligible locations for scholarship recipients to use their awards.
As a state public university and eligible institution, Morgan State University is a site where scholarship recipients may enroll and apply their awards.
As a state public college and eligible institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is a site where scholarship recipients may enroll and apply their awards.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law regarding priority registration at public institutions of higher education, resources and support at community colleges, senatorial and Delegate scholarships, and preferences in hiring by the Public Service Commission to the spouses of active service members and veterans; etc.
Title: Uniformed Services Spouses Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: The Uniformed Services Spouses Act extends various state-level benefits to the spouses of active-duty service members and veterans. These benefits include priority course registration and dedicated resource centers at public colleges and universities. The bill also makes spouses of active service members eligible for certain state scholarships for out-of-state study if they are Maryland residents. Additionally, it expands state and local government hiring and promotion preferences to include spouses and broaden the pool of eligible veterans to include those with any discharge that is not dishonorable.
responsible_party: Maryland public institutions of higher education, community colleges, the Maryland General Assembly, the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, and the Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Active-duty service members and their spouses, veterans with an other than dishonorable discharge and their spouses, surviving spouses of veterans, and applicants for state and local government employment
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill's requirements can be managed using existing budgeted resources, and there is no effect on state revenues. Local government finances are not materially affected. Administrative costs, such as updating the state's job application system, are considered minimal and absorbable. The bill does not increase the total funding for senatorial or delegate scholarships but expands the pool of eligible applicants for existing funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office is responsible for the overall oversight of state agencies implementing these changes and signed the bill into law.
The Comptroller is an 'appointing authority' and a major state employer whose hiring selection tests will be impacted by the expanded veteran and spouse credit definitions.
The Treasurer's Office is an 'appointing authority' whose hiring selection tests will be impacted by the expanded credit definitions for veterans and spouses.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and institutions of higher education regarding the implementation and interpretation of the new eligibility definitions and hiring preferences.
DBM is the principal personnel agency for the state and must update the JobAps system and personnel policies to accommodate the expanded definitions for veteran and spouse hiring credits.
The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article regarding hiring and promotion preferences granted by private and local government employers to veterans and spouses.
The bill directly concerns the benefits, support services, and resource centers for veterans and their families, which is the core mission of this department.
MHEC is responsible for statewide policies for colleges and universities and oversees the Senatorial and Delegate scholarship programs, both of which are significantly altered by the bill.
The bill's synopsis explicitly mentions expanding preferences in hiring by the Public Service Commission to include spouses of active service members and veterans.
USM institutions are public institutions of higher education required by the bill to grant priority registration for courses to eligible spouses of service members.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University must implement the bill's requirement to grant priority registration to eligible spouses of service members.
As a public institution of higher education, the college must implement the bill's requirement to grant priority registration to eligible spouses of service members.

Synopsis: Altering membership criteria for a Class C (veterans' organization) alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County by including certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service, and repealing a requirement that members of the veterans' organization served in a war; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class C (Veterans' Organization) Licenses - Membership
bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility criteria for Class C (veterans' organization) alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County by replacing the requirement that members must have served in the 'armed forces of the United States in a war' with a requirement for service in the 'uniformed services.' This change allows organizations with members who served in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the Public Health Service (PHS) to qualify and removes the requirement that service must have occurred specifically during a period of war.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Veterans' organizations in Anne Arundel County and individuals who served in the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County's finances or operations. While the annual fee for a Class C (veterans' organization) license is $300, the bill's changes to membership criteria are not anticipated to significantly alter the number of licenses issued or the revenue generated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership criteria for veterans' organization alcoholic beverages licenses by replacing 'armed forces' with 'uniformed services' and removing the requirement for wartime service. This directly affects the definition and recognition of veterans and their organizations, which is central to the agency's mission of advocating for and assisting Maryland's veterans and military families.

The Comptroller is the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry. While local boards of license commissioners in Anne Arundel County handle the specific issuance and enforcement of these licenses, the bill amends the statewide Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which falls under the Comptroller's general regulatory and oversight authority.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time within which the Securities Commissioner in the Office of the Attorney General may exercise a power under certain provisions of law governing the sale of franchises; altering the period of time within which an action for liability under a certain provision of law pertaining to franchise offers for sale must be brought; prohibiting a franchisor and certain others from inhibiting the right of franchisees to associate for certain purposes;  etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law - Alterations (Franchise Reform Act)

bill_summary: The Franchise Reform Act alters the Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law by extending the statute of limitations for enforcement and civil liability actions, protecting the rights of franchisees to join and participate in trade associations, and establishing a pilot program for the expedited review of franchise registration renewal applications.
responsible_party: Securities Commissioner in the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Franchisors, franchisees, and the Office of the Attorney General
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least $305,500 in FY 2027 to hire one Assistant Attorney General, one administrator, and one examiner to manage the pilot program and extended enforcement duties. Costs are projected to increase annually to approximately $413,400 by FY 2031. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no significant impact on local government operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Securities Commissioner within the Office of the Attorney General with administering and enforcing the Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law, including managing the new Fast-Track Review Pilot Program and submitting a related report to the General Assembly.

The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in general fund expenditures for the creation of new staff positions (Assistant Attorney General, administrator, and examiner) to handle the expanded enforcement window and reporting requirements, necessitating coordination with DBM's budget and personnel functions.

The bill alters the statute of limitations for civil liability and creates a new cause of action in circuit court regarding the right of franchisees to associate, which impacts the operations and volume of the judicial system.

The bill pertains to business regulation and the economic role of franchising in Maryland. As the state's primary economic development agency, the alterations to franchise disclosure and transparency impact the business climate Commerce is tasked with supporting.

Synopsis: Legalizing the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement to the extent to which that code or supplement contains laws enacted by the General Assembly.
Title: Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws - 2025 Edition - Legalization

bill_summary: This bill legalizes the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement containing laws enacted by the General Assembly, establishing the code as official evidence of law in Maryland courts and for use by public officials.
responsible_party: Baltimore County
stakeholders: Baltimore County residents, public officials, and the Maryland judicial system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state fiscal impact. Baltimore County is expected to manage publication costs for the new edition within existing budgeted resources, and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws shall be recognized by all courts of the State as evidence of the law enacted by the General Assembly, which directly impacts judicial proceedings and the administration of the courts.

As the chief legal officer for Maryland, the OAG will utilize the legalized code in court proceedings, criminal and civil appeals, and when providing legal counsel to state agencies regarding matters involving Baltimore County's local laws.
The Archives is the central depository for permanent government records and is responsible for preserving and making accessible judicial and legislative records, such as legalized county codes.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing state laws; the bill requires all state public officials to recognize the legalized code as evidence of law.

Synopsis: Altering the date from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030, by which certain community solar energy generating systems must be approved by the Public Service Commission in order for land that is used by the community solar energy generating systems to qualify for the agricultural use assessment; requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to issue a preconstruction determination under certain circumstances; authorizing the Department to rescind a preconstruction determination under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Property Tax - Agricultural Use Assessment - Community Solar Energy Generating Systems

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the deadline for community solar energy generating systems to be approved by the Public Service Commission to qualify for agricultural use property tax assessments from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030. It also establishes a process for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to issue preconstruction determinations for proposed agrivoltaics projects and authorizes the department to charge application fees to cover associated administrative costs.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Agricultural landowners, community solar energy system developers and operators, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027, depending on the number of additional community solar systems that qualify for agricultural assessments between 2025 and 2030. Administrative expenditures for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation are expected to be offset by newly authorized application fees. Specific dollar estimates for revenue changes are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires that community solar energy generating systems be approved by the Public Service Commission under § 7–306.2 of the Public Utilities Article to qualify for the agricultural use assessment. The bill also extends the deadline for this commission's approval from 2025 to 2030.

The board is responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments and disputes over property tax credits and exemptions. This bill alters the criteria and adds a preconstruction determination process for agricultural use assessments, which would likely lead to appeals handled by this agency.

The bill concerns the 'agricultural use assessment' and defines criteria for 'agrivoltaics,' which involves the dual use of land for both solar energy and farming. The agency's mission is to promote the economic viability of farming and agricultural products.

The agency promotes renewable energy and energy efficiency. This bill provides tax incentives for community solar energy generating systems, which falls under the agency's policy scope of advancing clean energy adoption.

The Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, including property tax assessments and exemptions. It would adjudicate cases resulting from contested decisions regarding the new agricultural use criteria and preconstruction determinations.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is relevant due to the bill's impact on state property tax revenues which flow into the Annuity Bond Fund, as noted in the fiscal note.

The Treasurer manages the state's financial assets and serves on the Board of Public Works. The fiscal note indicates a potential decrease in Annuity Bond Fund revenues, which are used to service state debt overseen by the Treasurer.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Public Service Commission and assessment authorities, and may be required to represent them in legal challenges or appeals related to the new tax assessment process.

The agency oversees land use planning and sustainable growth. This bill deals with the siting of solar energy systems on land traditionally zoned or assessed for agricultural use, involving the intersection of renewable energy and land preservation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is tasked with supporting the sustainability and profitability of Maryland's agricultural industry. The bill's promotion of agrivoltaics provides a potential new revenue stream (solar) for agricultural land while maintaining farm status.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable development and protecting the environment while supporting economic growth. This bill aligns with these goals by balancing renewable energy production with agricultural land preservation.
The Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives and the executive branch agencies implementing this law, such as the Public Service Commission.

Synopsis: Delaying the implementation of the Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program until taxable year 2030; requiring the Comptroller's Office, on or before December 1, 2026, to study and make recommendations regarding outreach efforts to encourage eligible taxpayers to claim the State earned income tax credit; and requiring the Department of Service and Civic Innovation to make certain recommendations concerning methods to assist low-income Marylanders with claiming certain credits and obtaining certain assistance.
Title: Earned Income Tax Credit - Assistance Program Implementation Delay and Study
