Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill delays the implementation of the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program for Low-Income Families until tax year 2030. It also mandates that the Comptroller’s Office and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation conduct studies and make recommendations regarding outreach and assistance strategies to help eligible low-income taxpayers claim the credit.
responsible_party: Maryland Comptroller’s Office and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation
stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit
fiscal_impact_summary: The Comptroller’s Office and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation can conduct the required studies and prepare the related reports with existing budgeted resources. The bill's primary fiscal impact is a five-year delay in State general fund and local income tax revenue reductions that would result from increased claims under the program. Specific dollar estimates for the revenue impact are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program and is specifically tasked by the bill to conduct a study and make recommendations regarding outreach efforts to encourage eligible taxpayers to claim the credit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Service and Civic Innovation study and make recommendations on how Maryland Corps participants can assist low-income residents with claiming the earned income tax credit and other assistance.

The bill specifically requires the Comptroller to analyze opportunities for partnership with state social service agencies for data sharing and outreach; as the primary social service provider for low-income residents, this agency is directly impacted by potential coordination.
The Governor's Office receives formal reports from the Comptroller regarding the program's effectiveness and the results of the mandated outreach studies.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved because the bill delays the implementation of a program that has significant impacts on state general fund revenues.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Comptroller and other agencies regarding the implementation of the program, including potential data-sharing agreements and privacy risks analyzed in the bill's study.
The EITC is a core tool for reducing child poverty, which is the primary mission of this office; the delay and outreach strategies directly affect their policy priorities.

The team is tasked with identifying and testing novel initiatives to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility, aligning with the bill's focus on researching and developing new outreach strategies for the EITC.

Synopsis: Altering the Maryland Uniform Disclaimer of Property Interests Act to provide for the disclaimer of nonprobate transfers at death; providing for the creation, revocation, recordation, and effects of a transfer-on-death deed for real property; providing example forms for the creation and revocation of a transfer-on-death deed; providing for the retroactive application of the Act to transfer-on-death deeds executed prior to the effective date of the Act for a transferor who dies on or after October 1, 2026; etc.
Title: Real Property - Transfer-on-Death Deed - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Transfer-on-Death Deed Act, which allows real property owners to transfer their property to beneficiaries upon death without the property going through the probate process. It details the procedures for creating, recording, and revoking transfer-on-death deeds and provides standard forms for public use.
responsible_party: Judiciary, Clerks of the Circuit Court, and the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland real property owners, designated beneficiaries of real estate, and legal professionals specializing in estate planning.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $15,696 in FY 2027 for one-time Judiciary programming costs. General fund revenues from probate fees and inheritance taxes may experience a minimal, indeterminate decrease as more properties bypass probate. Special fund revenues for the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund may increase from recordation surcharges. Transfer-on-death deeds for primary or secondary residences are exempted from state and local transfer and recordation taxes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary is the primary implementing agency for the bill's recordation requirements through the Clerks of the Circuit Court; the fiscal note identifies a $15,700 expenditure for necessary programming changes to accommodate the new deed and intake sheet protocols.

This agency is directly impacted by the creation of a nonprobate method for transferring real property, which bypasses the standard probate process and is projected to decrease revenue from probate fees and inheritance taxes administered by the Register.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller is relevant because the bill establishes specific exemptions from recordation and transfer taxes and impacts state general fund revenue collections.

The OAG is responsible for providing legal counsel to the Judiciary and executive agencies regarding the implementation of this new real property transfer framework and its interaction with existing probate, trust, and tax statutes.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency responsible for budget development and supervision; the bill has a notable fiscal impact on general fund expenditures and revenues as detailed in the fiscal note.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates the policy initiatives and intergovernmental relations necessary for the implementation of the new Transfer-on-Death Deed Act.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include an appropriation of $450,000 in the annual budget bill for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
Title: Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 in the State budget for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program for fiscal years 2028 through 2030. The program provides grants to local jurisdictions and child care resource centers to help establish and support family child care providers, with a focus on areas with high poverty, unemployment, or child care shortages.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)
stakeholders: Local governments, child care resource centers, and family child care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $450,000 for fiscal years 2028 through 2030. According to the Fiscal Note, while this represents a mandate, general fund expenditures are not anticipated to increase relative to historical funding levels because the program has typically received this amount even without a mandate. Federal funds must be used to satisfy the requirement if available. Local governments benefit from guaranteed grant funding during these years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly places the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). MSDE is responsible for administering the program, partnering with the Maryland Child Care Resource Network, and awarding grants to local programs.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the state's budget development. The bill mandates a specific appropriation of $450,000 for fiscal years 2028 through 2030, which DBM must include in the annual budget bill.

The Governor is required by the bill to include the mandated appropriation in the annual budget bill. Additionally, the Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies (MSDE and DBM) tasked with implementing and funding the program.

The program's focus on expanding childcare access to areas with high poverty rates and improving child well-being aligns directly with the mission of the Governor's Office for Children, which leads statewide efforts to reduce child poverty.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Family child care providers are frequently small, minority, or women-owned businesses. The bill specifically requires grant recipients to establish partnerships with organizations that support these types of businesses, aligning with the office's coordinating role.

The program addresses the Governor's top priorities of reducing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility, which are the primary focus areas for the Maryland State Innovation Team's pilot initiatives.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Education regarding the administration of the program, grant agreement requirements, and compliance with the mandates established by the bill.

The program supports small business development and workforce training for childcare providers, which are facets of the state's broader economic development goals managed by the Department of Commerce.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain local detention center officers of Dorchester County in the event Dorchester County becomes a participating governmental unit in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System; and providing that certain local detention center officers who join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System and receive certain service credit shall no longer be members of the Employees' Pension System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Dorchester County

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires Dorchester County detention center officers to join the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System (CORS) as a condition of employment if the county chooses to participate in the system. It transfers service credit from the Employees’ Pension System to CORS for eligible officers and exempts them from certain credit transfer payment requirements.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Dorchester County detention center officers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. According to the fiscal note, Dorchester County's pension liabilities are estimated to increase by $842,000. Due to a new entrant liability credit of $111,008, the net increase in employer contributions is estimated at $37,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2028. There is no expected impact on other participating governmental units in the retirement system.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 744 specifically mandates membership and service credit transfers within the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System (CORS) and the Employees’ Pension System (EPS), both of which are managed and administered by the State Retirement Agency. The agency is responsible for overseeing the participating governmental unit (PGU) pool and managing the actuarial liabilities and asset transfers described in the bill.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the state, DBM oversees state employee benefits, including pension policies. Since CORS is a state-administered retirement system, any legislative changes to membership eligibility or credit transfers fall under the department's broad purview over personnel policy and fiscal planning.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel to the State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System. They would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation of the new pension provisions and ensuring compliance with the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and all state agencies, including the State Retirement Agency. The Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and has ultimate oversight over the fiscal health of state-administered systems.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Maryland Department of Health from imposing a copay, coinsurance, or deductible for services provided in accordance with the Collaborative Care Model; requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for services provided in accordance with the Collaborative Care Model; requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to study the impact of eliminating cost-sharing for services provided under the Collaborative Care Model; etc.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: The bill prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from imposing cost-sharing requirements, such as copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles, for services provided through the Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) within the Medicaid program. It also mandates that private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations provide coverage for CoCM services. Additionally, the Maryland Health Care Commission is required to conduct a study on the impact of eliminating cost-sharing for CoCM services in the private insurance market and report its findings by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Health Care Commission, and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Medicaid recipients, individuals with private health insurance or HMO plans, health insurance carriers, and primary care providers utilizing the Collaborative Care Model.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is expected to be minimal. The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minor increase in special fund revenues from $125 rate and form filing fees in FY 2027. There is no immediate fiscal impact on Medicaid because the program does not currently impose cost-sharing for Collaborative Care Model services. The Maryland Health Care Commission can conduct the required study within existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from imposing cost-sharing for Collaborative Care Model services within the Medicaid program and requires the department to provide statewide reimbursement for these services.

The bill mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct a formal study on the impact of eliminating cost-sharing for Collaborative Care Model services and report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.

The bill adds new requirements to the Insurance Article for private insurers and HMOs to cover the Collaborative Care Model; the MIA is responsible for regulating these entities, enforcing compliance, and reviewing related rate and form filings.

As the administrator of the state's health insurance marketplace, the Exchange is impacted by legislative changes that mandate specific coverage and alter cost-sharing structures for private health plans available to Maryland residents.

As the agency responsible for managing the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM oversees health plans that are subject to or affected by changes in state insurance mandates and benefit requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health, the Maryland Health Care Commission, and the Maryland Insurance Administration regarding the implementation and enforcement of the bill's new statutory requirements.

bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities. Specifically, it reduces the number of legislative members, removes representatives from the Health Facilities Association of Maryland and Voices for Quality Care, adds a representative from LeadingAge Maryland, and updates the names of certain participating organizations.
responsible_party: Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities
stakeholders: Residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities and their families, the assisted living industry, and healthcare advocacy organizations such as LeadingAge Maryland, AARP, and the Alzheimer's Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The changes are technical in nature, relating solely to the membership composition of the oversight committee, and do not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership of the Oversight Committee, which includes the Secretary of Health, the Director of the Office of Health Care Quality (within MDH), and the Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health. MDH is the primary agency concerned with the oversight of nursing homes and health facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities falls under this collective category of advisory and oversight bodies. The bill's primary purpose is to alter the composition of this specific committee.

The Secretary of Aging is a statutory member of the Oversight Committee. The department is also responsible for the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, who is a member of the committee and selects several consumer representatives.

The Secretary of Disabilities or a designee is a statutory member of the Oversight Committee, reflecting the agency's interest in the quality of care for residents with disabilities in these facilities.
The Secretary of Human Services or a designee is a statutory member of the Oversight Committee, as the department assists vulnerable adults who may reside in these facilities.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the qualification requirements for the early childhood educator career ladder for private prekindergarten providers. It replaces fixed statutory deadlines with relative timeframes for educators to obtain required credentials and introduces new pathways for teaching assistants and lead teachers to meet experiential and educational standards.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Private prekindergarten providers and early childhood educators, including teachers and assistant teachers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no impact on State or local revenues or expenditures, as it does not change funding formulas or require new State resources. There is a potential meaningful impact on small businesses, specifically private prekindergarten providers, by providing additional flexibility in meeting staffing and credentialing requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for establishing, overseeing, and implementing the early childhood educator career ladder for private providers as described in the bill.

The Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center links student and workforce data. This bill directly impacts the pathways and qualification timelines for the early childhood workforce, which is essential data for tracking long-term educational outcomes.
The bill requires educators to obtain Associate and Bachelor's degrees from accredited institutions. The Commission oversees these institutions and statewide postsecondary education policies.
The agency's mission to reduce child poverty and enhance well-being is directly supported by expanding access to high-quality, publicly funded prekindergarten and stabilizing its workforce.
The team is charged with piloting novel initiatives to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility; enhancing the prekindergarten educator pipeline is a core strategy for these priorities.
As the state's public higher education system, USM institutions are responsible for training and certifying many of the educators who will enter this career ladder.
The agency oversees workforce development and adult learning programs, which intersect with the bill's creation of new professional pathways for early childhood educators.
The Board sets the statewide vision for workforce development and coordinates partnerships to ensure residents have access to pathways to prosperity, such as the early childhood career ladder.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Education and the General Assembly regarding the implementation and legality of regulatory changes to the career ladder.
As a state-run university with a focus on urban research and education, MSU provides the teacher training and degrees required by the educators impacted by this bill.
As a public honors college with a Master of Arts in Teaching, the college prepares educators who may participate in the lead teacher or consulting teacher levels of the career ladder.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates major policy initiatives, including the implementation of the state's education reforms and career ladder structures.
While the fiscal note indicates no material fiscal impact, DBM is responsible for the overall fiscal planning and efficiency of state-run educational initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Many private prekindergarten providers are small businesses that may be minority or women-owned; changes to staffing qualification timelines impact their operational flexibility.
The Council advocates for rural interests, including access to education services; adjusting qualification deadlines may help rural private providers remain eligible for public funding.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from using force, threat of force, or physical obstruction to interfere with or physically injure another individual while they are lawfully exercising or attempting to exercise their religious freedom at a place of religious worship. Violators are subject to misdemeanor penalties.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and local State's Attorneys
stakeholders: Individuals practicing religious beliefs at places of worship, religious organizations, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations. Conviction of the new misdemeanor is subject to imprisonment for up to 90 days and/or a maximum fine of $1,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor for obstructing or interfering with religious exercise, which will be adjudicated within the Maryland court system managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense carrying a potential penalty of 90 days in jail. The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with crimes that carry a possibility of incarceration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is responsible for the supervision of justice-involved individuals, including those placed on parole or probation following a conviction for the new misdemeanor created by this bill.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including the new prohibition on force or obstruction at places of religious worship.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel regarding the enforcement and interpretation of state criminal laws.
This office oversees faith-based commissions that engage with religious communities; it would likely be involved in outreach and policy advice regarding protections for religious worshipers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates the state's criminal justice strategies and advises the Governor on public safety policies, including new criminal statutes.

While this is a criminal law matter, the underlying subject involves the protection of the exercise of religious beliefs, which aligns with the Commission's mission to protect civil rights and prevent discrimination.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the enforcement of state laws, and the Governor signed this bill into law.

Synopsis: Providing for the valuation of a gift card for the purpose of determining value for crimes involving theft; prohibiting a person, with the intent to defraud another, from altering or tampering with a gift card or its packaging; and providing that a violation of the Act is a misdemeanor punishable by a term of imprisonment of up to 18 months or a fine not to exceed $500 or both.
Title: Criminal Law - Theft and Fraud Crimes - Valuation and Forgery of Gift Cards

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill makes it a crime to tamper with gift cards or their packaging to defraud others, creating a misdemeanor known as gift card forgery. It also establishes specific rules for determining the value of a gift card for theft prosecutions, setting the value as the greatest of the face value, a default of $100 if no value is listed, the value represented by the defendant, or the actual loss incurred.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Consumers, retail businesses, law enforcement agencies, and individuals involved in criminal proceedings related to gift card theft or fraud.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor of 'gift card forgery' and establishes specific valuation rules for gift cards in theft cases, directly impacting judicial proceedings, evidence assessment, and court administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency representing indigent defendants, the Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for defending individuals charged with the new misdemeanor of gift card forgery and navigating the new statutory valuation rules in theft cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor with a penalty of up to 18 months in prison. This may lead to an increase in individuals under the supervision of the Division of Parole and Probation or housed in correctional facilities.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including the new prohibitions against gift card tampering and fraud.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and enforces laws related to consumer protection; the bill's focus on gift card fraud and consumer product tampering falls within their area of concern for public safety and consumer rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and public safety policy, making the creation of new criminal penalties and theft valuation methods relevant to their mission.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives related to law enforcement and public safety, including the final approval of criminal law changes.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to develop a process to allow a homeowner to designate a family member or another representative of the homeowner to communicate and work with the Ombudsman on the homeowner's behalf; requiring the dwelling of a homeowner to be withheld from tax sale if the homeowner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship; increasing the maximum value of a dwelling that a homeowner may reside in and be eligible for the Homeowner Protection Program to $450,000; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protections - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: This bill expands protections for homeowners against tax sales by requiring local collectors to withhold properties from sale if the owner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship. It increases the eligibility threshold for the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) by raising the maximum allowable dwelling value from $300,000 to $450,000, and it establishes a process for homeowners to designate representatives to work with the State Tax Sale Ombudsman on their behalf.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners facing tax sale, specifically those with terminal illnesses, medical hardships, or properties valued up to $450,000; local government tax collectors; and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures may increase as expanded eligibility allows Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) funds to be more fully utilized, with potential for increased future revenues from homeowner repayments; however, total annual program funding remains $750,000. Local government revenues may see minimal delays or reductions starting in fiscal 2027 due to the new requirements for withholding properties from tax sale.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to define 'terminal illness' and 'medical hardship' by regulation. These definitions are central to determining eligibility for withholding properties from tax sale and priority enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program.

The bill impacts the Governor's oversight of executive branch agencies and programs. Additionally, the fiscal note mentions a statutory requirement for the Governor to annually appropriate $250,000 to the Homeowner Protection Fund, which the bill expands by increasing eligibility thresholds and priorities.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for managing the mandated annual appropriation to the Homeowner Protection Fund and overseeing the budget implications of expanding program eligibility and enrollment priorities.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the executive branch and would be responsible for providing legal review of the new regulations defining medical hardships and the procedural framework for homeowners to designate representatives to communicate with the Ombudsman.

The bill's protections for homeowners with terminal illnesses, medical hardships, or low income significantly impact older adults, who are primary constituents of the Department. The underlying law also specifically protects homeowners at least 65 years old from tax sales.

The bill includes priority enrollment for the Homeowner Protection Program for individuals receiving federal disability benefits and those facing medical hardships, aligning with the Department's mission to support Marylanders with disabilities and improve their access to secure housing.

The bill amends § 14-836 of the Tax - Property Article, which governs the judicial foreclosure of the right of redemption. It introduces a new procedural requirement for plaintiffs to send notice to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman in cases involving owner-occupied property, impacting court-supervised tax sale proceedings.

The Department's mission to prevent homelessness and ensure access to secure, affordable housing is directly supported by the bill's aim to divert vulnerable homeowners from the tax sale process and allow them to remain in their homes.

Synopsis: Altering the hours during which a holder of a Class B beer, wine, and liquor (golf course) license in Wicomico County may sell alcoholic beverages so as to begin at 7 a.m. rather than 10 a.m., Monday through Sunday.
Title: Wicomico County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B (Golf Course) License - Hours of Sale
bill_summary: This bill extends the permitted hours for the sale of alcoholic beverages by holders of a Class B beer, wine, and liquor (golf course) license in Wicomico County. It changes the starting time for sales from 10:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. every day of the week.
responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Owners and operators of public, for-profit 18-hole golf courses in Wicomico County and their patrons.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Locally, Wicomico County can handle any additional enforcement activities with existing resources, and county revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for the final review and signing of all legislation passed by the General Assembly. This bill was approved and signed into law by the Governor.

The Comptroller's office is identified in the agency summary as the entity that regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. This bill directly amends hours of sale for a specific class of alcoholic beverages license.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the state government regarding the enforcement and interpretation of state laws, including those within the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

Synopsis: Establishing a provisional social work license through which an individual issued a provisional social work license may receive a full license; and requiring the Board, beginning in 2027, to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the number of provisional licenses issued, the number of provisional license holders who obtained full licensure, and any recommendations for improving the program and the program's impact on the health care workforce.
Title: State Board of Social Work Examiners - Provisional License to Practice Social Work - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill establishes a provisional social work license for applicants who have completed the education and experience requirements for bachelor or master social work but have not yet passed the required examination. The license allows individuals to practice under the supervision of a board-approved social worker for a period of 12 to 24 months while they prepare for the exam.
responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
stakeholders: Applicants for bachelor and master social work licenses and board-approved social work supervisors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Social Work Examiners special fund expenditures increase by $64,900 in FY 2027 to hire an administrator to manage the new licensing category. Expenditures are expected to increase annually thereafter, reaching $85,400 by FY 2031. Special fund revenues will increase by an indeterminate amount as the board is required by the bill to set provisional license fees at a level sufficient to cover these administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners (BSWE) is a regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This department is directly responsible for overseeing the implementation of the new provisional licensing category, adopting necessary regulations, and managing the fiscal impact on the board's special funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners, which is the primary entity tasked with executing this bill's requirements, falls under this category of state entities authorized to address specific regulatory issues.

As the state's primary social service provider, DHS employs a significant number of social workers. Changes to the licensing pipeline, specifically the creation of a provisional license, directly impact their workforce recruitment and the legal practice status of their personnel.

Several USM institutions offer accredited bachelor's and master's programs in social work. This bill directly affects the transition from graduation to employment for their students and the requirements for supervised practice.

As a designated public urban research university with social work programs, Morgan State's graduates will be impacted by the creation of this provisional license as they enter the professional workforce.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and boards, including the Board of Social Work Examiners. They will likely be involved in reviewing the new regulations mandated by the bill and representing the board in any legal challenges.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. Licensing disputes or disciplinary actions related to the new provisional social work licenses would fall under their jurisdiction for independent review.

The bill addresses a healthcare workforce shortage by creating a path to provisional licensure. This aligns with the GWDB's mission to develop innovative workforce solutions and coordinate partnerships to improve economic mobility.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs social workers within correctional facilities and for parole/probation services. This bill affects the hiring pipeline for social work positions within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD utilizes social workers for parental defense and other social services. Changes to social work licensing categories impact their staffing and the professional certification of their employees.

The bill explicitly mentions the Social Work Licensure Compact and clarifies that provisional license holders do not qualify for a multistate license under the compact, which is an interstate agreement Maryland joined.

DBM oversees state personnel and fiscal efficiency. While the board is special-funded, DBM is responsible for the overall personnel policies and budget supervision that may be affected by the need for new staff at BSWE.

As an emergency bill requiring the Governor's approval and involving the appointment of the board members who will implement it, the Governor's Office maintains executive oversight over the policy change.

Synopsis: Requiring each health occupations board to allow an applicant seeking license or certificate renewal to receive continuing education credits for completing a certain human trafficking awareness training program, conduct outreach to make individuals regulated by the board aware of human trafficking awareness training options, and adopt certain regulations related to continuing education credits for a certain human trafficking awareness training program by January 1, 2027; establishing requirements for the training program; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Human Trafficking Awareness Training

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Trauma Informed Approach -see also- Mental&Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland health occupations boards to grant continuing education credits to applicants for license or certificate renewal who complete an approved human trafficking awareness training program. The Maryland Department of Health must approve the training program, which must be provided free of charge and cover topics including indicators of human trafficking, trauma-informed care, and reporting protocols.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and health occupations boards
stakeholders: Licensed and certified health care practitioners, health occupations boards, and human trafficking survivors.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of Health and the health occupations boards can implement the training approval, outreach, and regulatory requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for approving the human trafficking awareness training program. Additionally, the bill mandates that each health occupations board, which are units under MDH, adopt regulations, conduct outreach, and allow continuing education credits for the training.

The bill explicitly names the University of Maryland SAFE Center for Human Trafficking Survivors as an example of a local university program that MDH must collaborate with to approve the training program. Institutions within the University System of Maryland will likely serve as key partners in developing or providing the curriculum.

As a public institution with health and social work programs, Morgan State University falls under the bill's definition of a 'local university' that may be consulted or collaborate with MDH in the approval and development of the training program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires MDH to consult with the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force (MHTTF) to approve the training program. The MHTTF is an advisory body within this category that coordinates statewide efforts to combat human trafficking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, including human trafficking prevention, and often provides support or leadership for the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force mentioned in the bill.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees the public and private institutions of higher education (local universities) that are required to collaborate with MDH on the training program's approval.
The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the various health occupations boards as they draft and adopt the regulations required by the bill.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and its boards. The Governor also signed this bill into law and is responsible for overall executive policy regarding human trafficking.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health, rather than the Behavioral Health Administration and the Medical Care Programs Administration, to conduct a certain rate-setting study by June 30, 2028; establishing the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization in the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop transparent, cost-based reimbursement methodologies for certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers; etc.
Title: Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization - Workgroup Establishment and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a cost-driven rate-setting study for community-based behavioral health services by June 30, 2028. It also establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop transparent, cost-based reimbursement methodologies for behavioral health clinics, outpatient centers, and independent providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Community behavioral health providers (including certified community behavioral health clinics and outpatient mental health centers), independent outpatient providers, direct care staff, and individuals receiving behavioral health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $392,000 in FY 2027 and $356,100 in FY 2028. Specifically, Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $181,700 in FY 2027 and $158,500 in FY 2028 for staff to conduct the rate study. Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $210,300 in FY 2027 and $197,600 in FY 2028 for contractual staff and services to support the workgroup. There is no impact on state revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primarily tasks the Department of Health (MDH) with conducting an independent cost-driven, rate-setting study for behavioral health services and implementing the recommendations of the new workgroup. It also requires MDH to designate a technical liaison to work with the Maryland Health Care Commission.

The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC). MHCC is responsible for staffing the workgroup, providing analytical support and technical assistance to MDH, and submitting interim and annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization, which falls under this collective category of temporary bodies authorized by the General Assembly to address specific government policy issues.

The bill requires multiple reports to be submitted to the Governor regarding the progress of the rate-setting study and the impact of the payment system. As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the agencies (MDH and MHCC) implementing this policy.

The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in general and special fund expenditures for contractual staff and services. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and managing state personnel resources associated with these new positions.

As the primary legal representative for the state, the OAG would likely provide counsel to MDH and MHCC regarding the implementation of new reimbursement methodologies and the drafting of required regulations.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for residents with disabilities, many of whom utilize community-based behavioral health services. Rate modernization impacts the availability and quality of services for this population.

Modernizing behavioral health reimbursement methodologies and provider rates can have significant implications for the broader insurance market and consumer protection, which are regulated by the MIA.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits and performance evaluations. They would be responsible for eventually auditing the expenditures and performance of MDH and MHCC in executing the requirements of this bill.

The bill specifically requires the workgroup to analyze geographic variations in the cost of providing outpatient behavioral health services, which directly impacts the economic viability of providers in Maryland's rural counties.

Synopsis: Requiring an intake officer to file a petition alleging that a child under the age of 13 years is a child in need of supervision if the child is alleged to have committed an act that results in the death of a victim; and requiring a law enforcement officer to forward a complaint alleging that a child under the age of 13 years committed an act that resulted in the death of a victim to the Department of Juvenile Services for appropriate action.
Title: Juvenile Law - Child in Need of Supervision - Mandatory Petition (NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Known as the NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act, this bill requires law enforcement officers to forward complaints to the Department of Juvenile Services (DJS) when a child under the age of 13 is alleged to have committed an act that resulted in the death of a victim. It mandates that a DJS intake officer file a petition alleging that the child is a child in need of supervision (CINS) in such instances.
responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: Children under the age of 13, law enforcement agencies, victims' families, and the Department of Juvenile Services
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. While it creates mandatory reporting and petitioning requirements for certain cases involving children under 13, the volume is expected to be low enough to be handled within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates DJS intake officers to file petitions alleging a child is in need of supervision for any case involving a child under 13 whose actions resulted in a death. DJS is the primary agency responsible for the intake and supervision of youth in the juvenile justice system.
The bill requires the filing of petitions in the juvenile court system, which will impact court dockets, judicial proceedings, and the administrative operations of the state's judicial branch.

The bill requires law enforcement officers to forward complaints involving children under the age of 13 who have committed acts resulting in a death to the Department of Juvenile Services for appropriate action.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent juveniles. Mandatory petitions for 'child in need of supervision' cases will require legal defense and representation for the children involved.
The Governor oversees the Department of Juvenile Services and the Maryland State Police. This bill affects executive policy regarding juvenile justice and public safety enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates state public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal and juvenile justice policy, including efforts to reduce juvenile delinquency.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the Department of Juvenile Services and represents the state in related judicial matters or challenges to statutory implementation.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors the fiscal and personnel impacts on departments like DJS and the MSP, although the fiscal note indicates the impact is likely not material.

This office focuses on child well-being and coordinates supports for families. Changes in juvenile law specifically targeting children under 13 overlap with their policy interest in child welfare and community safety.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: While primarily focused on adults, the department has a general interest in public safety and the intersection of law enforcement activities with justice-involved individuals.

Synopsis: Requiring the governing body of Washington County and of a municipal corporation in Washington County to grant a 100% property tax credit against the county and municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated, and used to provide housing to veterans; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Washington County - Property Tax Credit - Platoon 22, Incorporated

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill requires Washington County and all municipal corporations within the county to grant a 100% property tax credit for real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated, provided the property is used to provide housing to veterans.
responsible_party: Governing body of Washington County and municipal corporations in Washington County
stakeholders: Platoon 22, Incorporated and veterans in Washington County
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures are not affected. Local property tax revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $9,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027, consisting of a $4,000 decrease for Washington County and a $5,000 decrease for the City of Hagerstown. This estimate is based on the assessment of one property currently owned by Platoon 22.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for the final review and signing of legislation into law and oversees the executive branch's policy coordination and legislative agenda.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and the General Assembly, reviewing legislation such as this for constitutional and legal sufficiency.
The bill mandates a property tax credit for real property used to provide housing to veterans, which aligns with the department's mission of ensuring access to safe and secure housing.
As the primary agency for veteran advocacy and services, this bill directly supports veteran housing efforts by providing a 100% property tax credit for a specific veteran-service organization.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes and may adjudicate appeals related to the eligibility or application of this property tax credit.

This agency provides administrative review for property tax assessment disputes, including those involving tax exemptions and credits, making it a relevant entity for potential appeals regarding this mandate.
The Secretary of State is the official custodian of Maryland's laws and records, responsible for processing and recording newly enacted legislation.

Synopsis: Extending to June 30, 2030, the authorization of a leaseholder of certain aquaculture leases, with prior written approval from the Department of Natural Resources, to place shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation, subject to certain requirements.
Title: Aquaculture - Placement of Shellfish, Bags, Nets, and Structures on Submerged Aquatic Vegetation - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Plants -see also- Invasive Species; Trees; Weeds

bill_summary: This bill extends the expiration date of an existing authorization that allows aquaculture leaseholders to place shellfish, bags, nets, and other structures on submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) with prior written approval from the Department of Natural Resources. The termination date for this authority is moved from June 30, 2027, to June 30, 2030.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Shellfish aquaculture leaseholders and small businesses engaged in aquaculture.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates the bill does not directly affect State or local finances. However, the bill is expected to have a potential meaningful economic impact on small businesses in the shellfish aquaculture industry by extending the period they can utilize areas with submerged aquatic vegetation for their operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Agriculture supports the economic viability of Maryland's agribusiness and seafood sectors, which include the small business aquaculture leaseholders directly impacted by this extension.

The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for managing aquaculture leases, granting written approval for activities on submerged aquatic vegetation, and enforcing related harvesting regulations.
The bill involves the management and protection of submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV), which is a critical component of water quality and environmental restoration overseen by this agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The council advises on the restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and coordinates interagency collaboration between DNR, MDE, and Agriculture regarding policies that affect SAV and resource management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services and loans to the seafood and aquaculture industries; the extension of these leasing rules impacts the long-term economic stability of the businesses they support.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and representation to the Department of Natural Resources regarding the administration and enforcement of aquaculture lease regulations.
The Council advocates for the interests of Maryland's rural counties, where the aquaculture industry serves as a vital component of the local economy and natural resource heritage.
This multi-agency initiative coordinates planning and restoration efforts for the Chesapeake Bay, aligning with the bill's focus on sustainable aquaculture and SAV preservation.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain members and former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System assigned as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit to receive credit for certain military service if the member receives military service credit in another retirement system; and prohibiting an individual from receiving credit more than one time.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Military Service Credit Eligibility - Helicopter Pilots

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill allows members or vested former members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) who serve or served as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit to receive up to five years of credit for military service, even if they already receive retirement benefits for that same service from another system (such as a military pension).
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Helicopter pilots in State law enforcement aviation units who are members or former members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) and have prior military service.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is expected to have no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because it applies to a very limited number of individuals. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances, as the bill pertains specifically to State employees within the LEOPS system.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) is responsible for the administration and management of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes LEOPS. The agency would be directly tasked with processing applications for military service credit, verifying eligibility, and adjusting retirement allowances for the helicopter pilots specified in the bill.

The Maryland State Police operates the state's primary Law Enforcement Aviation Command. The helicopter pilots employed in this unit are members of LEOPS and are the primary intended beneficiaries of the expanded eligibility for military service credit.

The Department of Natural Resources oversees the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are members of LEOPS. Any Natural Resources Police officers assigned as helicopter pilots in an aviation unit would be directly impacted by the bill's changes to military service credit eligibility.

As the central personnel agency for the state, the Department of Budget and Management oversees employee benefits and policies. It also monitors the fiscal impact of pension system changes on state contributions and liabilities.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Retirement Agency and the Maryland State Police. The office would be involved in interpreting the application of the bill and ensuring that the credit expansion complies with existing state and federal law.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Commerce to authorize an eligible fund manager to receive, use, and retain a certain management fee; and authorizing the Department to set an annual cap on the cumulative amount of certain management fees an eligible fund manager may receive.
Title: Economic Development - Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Accounts - Management Fees (Small Business Increased Access to Capital Act)

bill_summary: This bill allows the Maryland Department of Commerce to authorize fund managers of the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account to collect a management fee ranging from 1.5% to 3% of the total principal of each loan made. This fee is intended to cover administrative and lending-related expenses and is paid out of the account's existing funds.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses; eligible fund managers including local economic development corporations and private investment firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect the total funding for the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA). However, it allows for the diversion of funds from lending to management fees. The fiscal note estimates that approximately 600,000 could be diverted as management fees annually based on an account funding level of 20,000,000. State expenditures for the Department of Commerce may increase for oversight, while local economic development entities serving as fund managers may see an increase in fee revenue, offset by a decrease in available loan capital.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for administering the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA), authorizing eligible fund managers to receive management fees, and setting annual caps on those fees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office monitors socioeconomic procurement programs and supports the exact demographic (small, minority, and women-owned businesses) targeted by the SMWOBA fund modified by this bill.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning, which includes the management and oversight of special funds like SMWOBA.
The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, overseeing the distribution of state revenues such as the video lottery proceeds that fund SMWOBA.
The Treasurer's Office manages the state's funds and acts as a custodian for state deposits; they have oversight interest in the fiscal integrity of the SMWOBA special fund.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Commerce and would likely be involved in drafting or reviewing the regulations and agreements related to the new management fee structures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The SMWOBA fund is primarily sourced from a percentage of gross video lottery terminal proceeds regulated and collected by this agency.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Commerce, and is responsible for the final approval of the annual state budget and policy initiatives like the SERVE Act that might interact with economic mobility.
OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies; they would eventually audit the Department of Commerce's adherence to the management fee limits established by this bill.
As a quasi-governmental entity with significant financial and investment experience, MEDCO could potentially serve as an 'eligible fund manager' authorized to receive the fees described in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services to agricultural and rural businesses and could potentially qualify as an eligible fund manager under the criteria set by the Department of Commerce.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA). The fund is intended to support the department's mission by financing programs, services, and administrative activities, including personnel and partnership development. It is funded through investment earnings, departmental fees, and other contributions, and is designed to supplement rather than replace existing state appropriations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, their families, caregivers, and local area agencies on aging.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in an indeterminate increase in special fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Aging anticipates that initial investments into the fund will be modest and expects to manage the fund using existing budgeted resources. Additionally, local area agencies on aging may see an increase in revenues and expenditures if funds become available for their programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Aging Resilience Fund, which the Secretary of Aging is directly responsible for administering to support the department's mission, programs, and services.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Aging Resilience Fund separately and to invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other State money.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Aging Resilience Fund, and the Comptroller is the state's principal officer for managing revenue and accounting for such funds.

The bill creates a new special, nonlapsing fund that interacts with the State budget and contains provisions restricting the Governor's authority to reduce appropriations to the fund, which falls under DBM's fiscal oversight.

The Secretary of Aging is a member of the Governor's Executive Council, and the bill limits the Governor's constitutional and statutory authority to reduce appropriations for this specific fund in the State budget.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Aging and will likely assist in the legal framework and regulatory implementation of the newly created special fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity and a certain covenant or agreement that ensures affordable pricing of the dwelling; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Building Homes Act

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to establish a property tax credit for dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity and a covenant or legally binding agreement of at least 20 years that ensures affordable pricing and income/equity restrictions. The credit amount may be up to the difference between the tax on the full assessed value of the dwelling and the tax on the portion of the value for which the homeowner is responsible on their first mortgage.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Homeowners of affordable dwellings, nonprofit housing organizations (such as Habitat for Humanity), and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent the property tax credit is granted by local governments. The exact financial impact is indeterminate as the number of eligible dwellings and their specific selling prices cannot be reliably estimated. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary state entity responsible for affordable housing and homeownership. The bill creates a local tax credit for affordable dwellings subject to nonprofit mortgages and pricing covenants, which directly aligns with the department's core mission to ensure residents have access to safe and secure affordable housing.

The Governor's Office coordinates state policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. This bill represents a key policy initiative regarding affordable housing and economic mobility and was signed into law by the Governor.

The PTAAB is the independent agency responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments and the application of property tax credits. This bill creates a new credit that will be subject to their administrative review process for any disputes.

The Tax Court adjudicates appeals from the PTAAB. Any disputes regarding the calculation or eligibility of this new affordable housing property tax credit could reach this quasi-judicial body for final administrative review.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They provide guidance on the legal interpretation of the property covenants and Tax-Property Article changes introduced by this bill.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors all tax legislation and its impact on the state's broader fiscal health and revenue reporting, even when the taxes are local in nature.

DBM is responsible for long-term fiscal planning. While the fiscal impact is primary local, the agency monitors changes in local revenue capacities that can affect state budget allocations and fiscal coordination.

The team's mission includes enhancing economic mobility and reducing poverty. This bill provides an evidence-based tool for local governments to support affordable homeownership through nonprofit partnerships, aligning with the team's policy incubation goals.

The office focuses on reducing child poverty and improving economic opportunities for families. Stable and affordable housing is a fundamental component of reducing family poverty and promoting child well-being.

The AOC was identified as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis and oversees the judicial branch, which handles the recording of the mortgages and covenants required to qualify for the tax credit.

Synopsis: Specifying the intern fellowships that exist in the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program; increasing the maximum scholarship award amount under the Program from $5,000 to $6,000; and requiring the Governor, beginning in fiscal year 2028, to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation for the Program that is at least a 125% of the appropriation provided in fiscal year 2026.

bill_summary: The bill codifies the specific fellowships included in the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program, increases the maximum scholarship award from $5,000 to $6,000, and mandates that the Governor include a minimum appropriation for the program starting in fiscal 2028 equivalent to at least 125% of the fiscal 2026 appropriation.
responsible_party: The Shriver Center at the University of Maryland Baltimore County (UMBC)
stakeholders: College and graduate students pursuing public service internships, and public and nonprofit organizations in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $87,500 annually starting in fiscal 2028 to meet the bill's mandated appropriation level. This is based on a fiscal 2026 appropriation of $350,000, with the 125% mandate requiring a total of $437,500. Increasing the maximum scholarship award amount has no net effect on total spending but may result in fewer individual awards being granted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the Shriver Center, which is located at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC), a member institution of the University System of Maryland, administers the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program. The bill also mandates specific funding levels for UMBC for the program's implementation.

The bill establishes a mandated appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2028, requiring the Governor to include funding in the annual budget bill that is at least 125% of the fiscal 2026 appropriation. DBM is the principal agency responsible for developing the state's budget and supervising budget execution.

The bill identifies the 'Governor’s Summer Internship Program' as a core component of the scholarship program and requires the Governor to propose specific mandated funding levels in the annual budget. The bill's preamble also highlights the Governor's specific policy priorities regarding public service.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's preamble explicitly links the scholarship program to the Governor's commitment to public service and the mission of the Department of Service and Civic Innovation to develop the state's talent pipeline through service opportunities.

As the state's regulatory and coordinating board for higher education and financial aid, MHEC oversees the policies for public and private colleges and the administration of state financial aid programs, within which this scholarship program resides.

The bill formally recognizes the 'Sondheim Public Service Law Fellows Program.' The OAG, as the state's chief legal officer, is often a site for public service law internships and legal advocacy roles mentioned in the bill's priority criteria.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, in coordination with certain entities, to evaluate the use of blockchain technology for securely recording and verifying real property ownership and leases and to assess its potential for use by law enforcement and courts in resolving real property disputes involving squatting; and requiring the Department, by December 31, 2026, to report the results of the study to evaluate certain uses of blockchain technology to the Governor and the General Assembly.
Title: Study to Evaluate Blockchain-Based Real Property Lease and Title Recordation and Verification

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), in coordination with the Maryland Judiciary, law enforcement agencies, and other legal and technology stakeholders, to conduct a study evaluating the use of blockchain technology for recording and verifying real property titles and leases. The study also explores the potential for using blockchain technology to assist courts and law enforcement in resolving property disputes related to squatting. SDAT must report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Real property owners, the Maryland Judiciary, the Maryland State Police, local law enforcement agencies, the Office of the Attorney General, Maryland Legal Aid, the Public Justice Center, the Maryland Blockchain Association, and third-party technology vendors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill will have a minimal impact on state finances and is not expected to materially affect state or local government operations. While the Office of the Attorney General suggested that a part-time contractual assistant might be necessary to support the study, the Department of Legislative Services determined that the bill's requirements can be implemented using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the results of the study evaluating blockchain-based real property recordation to be reported to the Governor and involves policy coordination regarding real property law and technology.

The bill explicitly requires the Office of the Attorney General to coordinate on the study to evaluate blockchain technology for property titles and leases, and the fiscal note indicates a potential increase in legal workload for the agency.
The bill requires the Maryland Judiciary to coordinate on the study to assess how blockchain technology could assist the courts in resolving real property disputes and verifying ownership records.

The bill explicitly names the Maryland State Police as a coordinating entity to evaluate how blockchain technology can assist law enforcement agencies in resolving property disputes such as squatting.

The study focuses on the evaluation and potential implementation of blockchain technology, which falls under the purview of the state's principal information technology and telecommunications strategy agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates a collaborative study involving multiple state agencies and private stakeholders to conduct research and provide recommendations, which is the functional role of this collective entity.
