bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Department of Aging to provide grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging to foster social connections for seniors through 'multigenerational third places.' These are community spaces outside of the home or workplace where people of various ages can gather. The bill allows grant funds to cover operational costs, such as leases and administrative expenses, specifically for senior villages to facilitate access to these social spaces.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Seniors and older adults, nonprofit organizations, senior villages, and Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs)
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates that the Governor include at least 100,000 dollars in the annual budget for aging-in-place grants, with at least 20 percent of that funding dedicated to senior villages. According to the Fiscal Note, the bill primarily alters the permitted uses of existing funds, and any administrative changes for the Maryland Department of Aging can be handled with existing resources. Local governments may see an increase in expenditures and revenues if their Area Agencies on Aging receive these grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Department of Aging to administer grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging for aging-in-place programs and multigenerational third places, making it the primary implementing agency.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $100,000 in the annual budget bill for these grants, a process managed and supervised by the Department of Budget and Management.
The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Aging and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which must now include the mandated $100,000 appropriation for this program.

The Governor's Grants Office provides training and technical assistance to state agencies to help them manage grant programs and ensure compliance, which is relevant to the new grant authorities established by this bill.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of new grant agreements and any regulations adopted by the Department of Aging under this act.

Synopsis: Altering the cap on a certain assessment allocation percentage required to be calculated by the Board of Directors of the Industry Automobile Insurance Association; authorizing the Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund to establish an affordability program subject to certain requirements and modification under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
bill_summary: This bill allows the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) to establish an affordability program that provides discounted private passenger automobile insurance rates to low-income individuals (those with household incomes at or below 250% of the federal poverty level). Additionally, it reduces the maximum assessment allocation percentage that MAIF can charge other motor vehicle insurers in the state from 3% to 1% and grants the Maryland Insurance Commissioner oversight and modification authority over the affordability program.
responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Low-income Maryland drivers, the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), and private motor vehicle insurance companies operating in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances. However, MAIF revenues are expected to decrease in fiscal 2028 and 2029 compared to current law because the bill permits the continuation of premium discounts for certain policyholders that were otherwise scheduled for elimination by the Maryland Insurance Administration. The reduction of the assessment cap from 3% to 1% is not expected to have a material impact as projected assessments are currently below the 1% threshold.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MAIF is the primary agency authorized by the bill to establish the new affordability program and is directly affected by the reduction in the assessment allocation percentage cap.

The Insurance Commissioner at MIA is explicitly charged with reviewing, approving, and potentially modifying the affordability program and its associated rates to ensure they are not excessive or discriminatory.

The OAG serves as the legal representative for MAIF and MIA and would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the implementation and enforcement of the new program and regulatory changes.

The MVA requires proof of insurance for vehicle registration; as MAIF is the insurer of last resort, changes to its affordability directly impact the driving population and compliance environment managed by the MVA.

The bill's focus on making auto insurance affordable for households below 250% of the federal poverty level aligns with the Innovation Team's mandate to incubate strategies that reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, appoints the Insurance Commissioner, and coordinates the statewide policy initiatives regarding economic mobility that this bill aims to support.

Synopsis: Providing that the maximum annual salary of the clerks of the circuit courts and the registers of wills may not be more than the salary of a State employee at grade 26, step 20 of the State of Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale in effect on the day before the clerk or the register begins a new term of office; and repealing as obsolete a certain minimum salary requirement for the register of wills for Baltimore City.

bill_summary: This bill changes the way maximum salaries for circuit court clerks and registers of wills are calculated. Instead of a set dollar limit of $146,500, the maximum will now be tied to a specific step on the State of Maryland's standard salary scale (Grade 26, Step 20). It also removes an outdated minimum salary for the register of wills in Baltimore City and ensures that salary increases do not apply until the start of the next term of office.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill results in a total net general fund impact of $790,100 in FY 2027 and $1,354,400 annually thereafter. This includes an increase in general fund expenditures for the Judiciary ($403,800 in FY 2027; $692,300 annually) for clerk salaries and a decrease in general fund revenues ($386,300 in FY 2027; $662,100 annually) because register of wills salaries are paid from fees and receipts that otherwise would be deposited into the general fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the 24 elected Registers of Wills by altering their maximum annual salary and repealing obsolete minimum salary requirements specifically for the Baltimore City register.

The bill increases salaries for circuit court clerks, which the fiscal note indicates will result in significant general fund expenditure increases for the Judiciary, an entity supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Board of Public Works is the primary authority responsible for setting and determining the annual salaries for both clerks and registers based on workload, receipts, and the new statutory maximum.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works and is specifically responsible for authorizing fund transfers to cover expenses and salary deficiencies for the registers of wills from tax collections.

As the agency responsible for the state's personnel policies and salary scales, DBM oversees the Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale to which the new maximum salaries for clerks and registers are now tied.
The State Treasurer serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which is the body tasked with implementing the salary adjustments and setting compensation for the affected officials.
The Governor chairs the Board of Public Works, which sets the salaries for these officials, and the office oversees the executive branch departments impacted by these administrative changes.

bill_summary: This bill permits the Governor to appoint an employee of a county board of education as a regular member of the State Board of Education, provided that no more than two board members are local board employees at any time. The bill prohibits these members from being county superintendents, restricts their voting on specific personnel and disciplinary appeals, and adjusts the board's affirmative vote requirement to a majority of authorized voters when a member is legally barred from voting on a specific matter.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education
stakeholders: Employees of county boards of education, members of the State Board of Education, and the Maryland public school system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill is procedural in nature and has no direct effect on State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the composition and voting procedures of the Maryland State Board of Education, which is the governing body of the Department. It also assigns the Department responsibility for providing notice of vacancies and conducting elections for the teacher member.

The bill authorizes the Governor to appoint a specific type of member (an employee of a county board) to the State Board of Education and alters the criteria the Governor must consider for these appointments.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards. This bill adds a new category of eligible candidates for the State Board of Education that the office must manage and recommend.
The bill explicitly mentions that the Department of Education may consult with the Maryland State Retirement Agency to conduct the required election for the teacher member of the State Board.

As the primary legal counsel to state boards and the Department of Education, the OAG would be responsible for interpreting the bill's new voting threshold requirements and ensuring board actions comply with the revised membership rules.

Synopsis: Requiring an applicant for certain for-hire driver's licenses to submit to the Public Service Commission documentation verifying that the applicant completed a certain human trafficking awareness training program; prohibiting licensed taxicab drivers, for-hire drivers, or transportation network operators and applicants for a transportation network operators license from being held civilly or criminally liable for reporting or responding to in good faith a suspected incident of human trafficking; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires applicants for for-hire driver's licenses, including taxicab drivers and transportation network operators (TNOs), to complete a human trafficking awareness training program as a condition of licensure. It also prohibits transportation network companies (TNCs) from allowing drivers to provide services unless they complete the training within 30 days of their first prearranged ride. Additionally, the bill provides immunity from civil and criminal liability for drivers and operators who report or respond to suspected incidents of human trafficking in good faith.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Taxicab drivers, for-hire drivers, transportation network operators (TNOs), transportation network companies (TNCs), local licensing authorities, and the Maryland Public Service Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by 10000 in fiscal 2027 only for software modifications to ensure applicants view the required training. Special fund revenues increase by the same amount through assessments imposed on public service companies. Local governments are expected to implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements. It must collect and verify human trafficking awareness training documentation from for-hire and transportation network operator applicants, issue licenses, and modify its application software to accommodate these new requirements.

The bill explicitly requires Maryland driver applicants for for-hire licenses to allow the Public Service Commission access to their photographs through the Motor Vehicle Administration. The MVA also manages driving records which are checked as part of the application process modified by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires for-hire driver's license applicants to apply to the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which is housed within this department, for State criminal history records checks.

The bill establishes civil and criminal immunity for drivers and operators who report suspected human trafficking in good faith. The Judicial Branch, supported by the AOC, is responsible for adjudicating cases where such immunity may be invoked.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and would be responsible for interpreting the liability protection provisions and representing the state in related legal matters.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's primary coordinating body for human trafficking policy and public safety. While not the direct implementer of the driver training, it oversees the state's broader strategies related to trafficking awareness and victim services.

As the parent agency of the MVA and the entity responsible for statewide transportation policy, MDOT is impacted by regulations regarding for-hire drivers and has previously been tasked with implementing its own internal human trafficking training programs.
The OPC represents the interests of consumers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding regulated transportation services, which includes for-hire and taxicab drivers.

DBM oversees state agency expenditures and revenue assessments. The fiscal note indicates an increase in special fund expenditures and corresponding revenue for the Public Service Commission to implement the bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved in this bill (PSC, DPSCS, MDOT) and coordinates the policy initiatives related to public safety and human trafficking prevention.

Synopsis: Reestablishing the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with an altered membership and mandate; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2027.
Title: Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland - Reestablishment

bill_summary: This bill reestablishes the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland, expanding its membership and mandate. The commission is charged with studying and making legislative, regulatory, and programmatic recommendations concerning the prevention, detection, and suppression of lithium-ion battery fires across consumer, transportation, utility, and recycling applications, as well as evaluating risks at the Port of Baltimore and the viability of extended producer responsibility.
responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal
stakeholders: Lithium-ion battery manufacturers, recycling facilities, first responders, the Port of Baltimore, transportation and shipping industries, insurance providers, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $70,700 in FY 2027 and $30,100 in FY 2028 to hire one contractual management associate within the Office of the State Fire Marshal to staff the commission and prepare reports. Member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. There is no material effect on local government finances or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is required to submit its interim and final reports on findings and recommendations to the Governor.

The Secretary of the Environment appoints representatives from the department and the Land and Materials Administration to the Commission, which is tasked with studying lithium-ion battery recycling, storage, and decommissioning standards.

The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration is a member of the Commission and appoints several other members; the Commission's work regarding grid-scale storage and clean energy propulsion aligns with MEA's energy planning mission.
The Secretary of Natural Resources appoints a representative from the Power Plant Research Program to serve on the Commission to address utility-scale battery applications.
The Secretary of Transportation appoints members to the Commission, which is specifically tasked with studying lithium-ion battery risks on roads, rail, and tunnels throughout the state.

The Office of the State Fire Marshal, which is a division of the Maryland State Police, is mandated to staff the Commission and serve as a member, resulting in a direct general fund fiscal impact of approximately $70,700 for personnel.
The Chair of the Public Service Commission appoints a representative to the Commission to support the study of battery safety in utility and grid-scale applications.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner appoints industry representatives to the Commission, which is tasked with studying the impacts of lithium-ion battery risks on insurance providers and coverage availability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reestablishes a specific state commission to advance safety standards and regulatory recommendations for lithium-ion batteries.
The agency is a designated member of the Commission, and the study specifically includes assessing battery risks at the Port of Baltimore.

Synopsis: Authorizing licensed certified midwives to enter into therapy management contracts; repealing a requirement that authorized prescribers submit prescriber-pharmacist agreements to the health occupations board that regulates the authorized prescriber; authorizing pharmacists, under certain circumstances, to enter into prescriber-pharmacist agreements that authorize the pharmacist to treat an opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances drug therapy; etc.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Prescriber-Pharmacist Agreements

Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands the scope of therapy management contracts by authorizing licensed certified midwives to enter into them and allows pharmacists to treat opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances (CDS) drug therapy under certain conditions. It repeals the requirement for authorized prescribers to submit prescriber-pharmacist agreements to their own regulatory boards, though pharmacists must still submit them to the State Board of Pharmacy. Pharmacists providing CDS therapy must register with the Office of Controlled Substances Administration and the DEA, complete training, and consult the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program before initiating or modifying treatment.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (State Board of Pharmacy and the Office of Controlled Substances Administration)
stakeholders: Pharmacists, licensed certified midwives, authorized prescribers, and patients requiring treatment for opioid use disorder.
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $58,600 in FY 2027 to cover costs for a part-time administrative specialist and a one-time software update. General fund revenues are projected to increase by $72,000 in FY 2027 due to an estimated 600 pharmacists paying a $120 three-year CDS registration fee. The net impact in FY 2027 is a surplus of $13,400, followed by net expenditure increases in FY 2028 and FY 2029 until registration renewals occur in FY 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the state budget, requiring the addition of a new part-time administrative position and resulting in specific general fund expenditure and revenue increases as detailed in the fiscal note.

As the primary agency for health policy and professional regulation, MDH oversees the State Board of Pharmacy and the Board of Nursing, which are directly affected by changes to therapy management contracts and the expansion of prescriptive authority. MDH also manages the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program that pharmacists must now query.

The Lieutenant Governor oversees policy initiatives related to the state's response to the opioid crisis and directs the work of the Opioid Policy Advisor, making the bill relevant to their delegated duties in managing behavioral health strategies.

This agency is directly responsible for registering and regulating pharmacists who will now be authorized to treat opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances. The fiscal note specifies that this office will handle a significant increase in applications and require database software updates.

The OAG provides necessary legal counsel to the Department of Health and its various health occupations boards as they implement new regulatory protocols, update scope of practice rules for midwives, and manage the legal aspects of the opioid restitution fund.

Synopsis: Establishing certain public comment requirements and recording requirements for the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County; and requiring the members of the Board to undergo at least every 2 years, training specific to board governance, structure, responsibilities, and roles.
Title: Frederick Community College - Board of Trustees - Meeting and Training Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: The bill requires the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County to provide an opportunity for public comment at every meeting, record all meetings, and make those recordings available on the college's website. It also mandates that board members participate in governance training at least every two years and requires the board to maintain meeting records and minutes in perpetuity.
responsible_party: Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County
stakeholders: Members of the Frederick Community College Board of Trustees, students, staff, and residents of Frederick County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local expenditures for Frederick Community College may increase minimally to record and archive board meetings and to provide required biennial training. These costs are expected to be absorbable within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing the seven members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County, which is the subject of the bill.
As the state's coordinating and regulatory board for higher education, MHEC oversees policy and standards for community colleges. The agency was also consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards, including the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County.

The bill mandates that the Board maintain recordings and minutes in perpetuity. The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for state government records of permanent value and provides guidance on records retention.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state-authorized boards and commissions. The Board may require legal advice to ensure compliance with the bill's new public comment, recording, and perpetuity requirements.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property  tax imposed on the dwelling house of a surviving spouse of a military service member who is ineligible for a certain property tax exemption; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Property Tax Credit - Surviving Spouse of Military Service Member

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City, or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation, to establish a property tax credit for the primary residence of a surviving spouse of a military service member who is ineligible for the existing mandatory property tax exemption for such individuals.
responsible_party: The governing bodies of Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations, along with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of military service members who do not qualify for the standard property tax exemption under § 7–208 of the Tax – Property Article.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on State revenue or expenditures. Local property tax revenues will decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent that local governments choose to grant the property tax credit. Specific dollar estimates for this revenue loss are unavailable because the implementation, amount, and duration of the credit are at the discretion of local jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes a property tax credit for the surviving spouses of military service members. The Department of Veterans and Military Families is the principal agency for assisting military families in securing benefits and providing advocacy regarding housing and financial support.

This agency hears appeals regarding the valuation of property and disputes over tax exemptions and property tax credits. Since the bill establishes a new local property tax credit for surviving spouses, the board would be responsible for adjudicating related eligibility disputes.

As the Governor's senior military advisor and head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is concerned with policies that affect the welfare and benefits of service members and their families, particularly regarding line-of-duty death definitions.

The Maryland Tax Court provides the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including factual determinations regarding property tax credits and appeals from local taxing authorities or the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.

The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. This bill represents a policy change regarding benefits for military families, which falls under the office's mandate to support Maryland's military and veteran population.

The bill's definition of 'individual who died in the line of duty' directly impacts members of the Maryland National Guard serving on active duty. Their surviving spouses would be the primary beneficiaries of the authorized tax credit.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They may be required to provide legal interpretations regarding the eligibility requirements and implementation of this property tax credit.

Synopsis: Altering the eligibility for the Community College Promise Scholarship to include residents of Delmar, Maryland who graduated from Delmar High School in Delmar, Delaware; authorizing an institution of postsecondary education to award a scholarship under the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program to certain individuals including a surviving transportation worker and certain individuals related to a surviving transportation worker or a fallen transportation worker; etc.

bill_summary: The bill expands eligibility for the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship to include residents of Delmar, Maryland, who graduated from Delmar High School in Delaware. It also renames the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program to the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and expands eligibility to include surviving transportation workers (involved in accidents with at least $100 million in damages), their spouses, children, stepchildren, unmarried partners, and certain siblings. Additionally, the bill allows scholarship funds to be used for the total cost of attendance at any postsecondary institution, rather than just tuition and mandatory fees.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC)
stakeholders: Residents of Delmar, Maryland who graduated from Delmar High School in Delaware; surviving and fallen transportation workers and their families (including spouses, children, stepchildren, unmarried partners, and siblings); and Maryland institutions of postsecondary education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures are expected to increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to cover additional awards under the expanded Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and the increased costs associated with covering the total cost of attendance. While the exact increase for these changes is indeterminate, the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship has a mandated annual appropriation of $13,500,000; expanding its eligibility may lead to longer waiting lists if the funding level remains unchanged.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary agency responsible for administering the scholarship programs mentioned in the bill, including the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship and the newly renamed Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program. It manages the associated special fund and coordinates with postsecondary institutions.

The bill specifically creates and expands benefits for transportation workers. MDOT is required by the bill to provide MHEC with the names and contact information of the families of fallen or surviving transportation workers to facilitate scholarship awards.
The bill mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund, which is established as a special, nonlapsing fund.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the state budget, requiring general fund expenditures for scholarship awards and administrative adjustments. DBM is responsible for supervising the state's budget and execution.

USM institutions are 'institutions of postsecondary education' that will be responsible for determining student eligibility and receiving scholarship funds. Additionally, the maximum award amount for the transportation scholarship is benchmarked against tuition at USM institutions.

As a public institution of higher education and a state agency, Morgan State University is responsible for determining the eligibility of individuals who apply for these scholarships and reporting to MHEC.

As an independent public honors college and state agency, Saint Mary's College is an eligible institution that must verify student eligibility and report to MHEC regarding the scholarship programs altered by the bill.

The Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship applies to students in registered apprenticeship programs, which are supervised by the Department of Labor. Changes to eligibility for this scholarship indirectly affect workforce development pathways managed by the department.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and signs the bill into law. The bill also involves a special fund and scholarship programs that align with state policy priorities regarding workforce safety and education access.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MHEC and MDOT and may be involved in interpreting the bill's new legal definitions, such as the expanded criteria for 'unmarried partners' and 'surviving transportation workers'.

Synopsis: Exempting from the property tax property that is owned by the City of Hagerstown and used primarily for public social, recreational, and entertainment purposes; establishing that the exemption from the property tax for certain property owned by the City of Hagerstown or the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility shall apply retroactively beginning with fiscal year 2024; and requiring the State, Washington County, and the City of Hagerstown to pay a refund for any excess property tax paid due to the retroactive exemption.
Title: Property Tax - City of Hagerstown and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. - Exemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: This bill exempts real and personal property owned by the City of Hagerstown from property taxes if the property is used primarily for public social, recreational, and entertainment purposes. It also applies property tax exemptions for the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. retroactively to the 2023 taxable year (fiscal 2024), requiring the State, Washington County, and the City of Hagerstown to issue refunds for any taxes paid during the retroactive period.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), Washington County, and the City of Hagerstown
stakeholders: The City of Hagerstown, Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc., Washington County government and taxpayers, and the State of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is estimated to reduce state and local revenues. In FY 2027, State Annuity Bond Fund revenues are projected to decrease by $102,600, which includes $80,300 for retroactive refunds and $22,300 for the ongoing annual exemption. Local property tax revenues in Washington County are projected to decrease by $1,460,000 in FY 2027, comprising $1,300,000 for retroactive refunds ($575,700 from the county and $718,300 from the city) and a $160,000 recurring annual decrease for the city-owned property exemption.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill has a direct fiscal impact on the Annuity Bond Fund (ABF), which the Treasurer manages. The ABF revenues will decrease due to the property tax exemptions and retroactive refunds, potentially affecting the funding available for State general obligation bond debt service.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing state revenue collection and the issuance of refunds, both of which are mandated by this bill. The Comptroller also serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees state debt service.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for the state budget. The fiscal note indicates that a decrease in property tax revenue to the Annuity Bond Fund may require an increase in general fund expenditures to cover debt service payments.

The Board of Public Works oversees the state's fiscal integrity and bond issuances. The reduction in Annuity Bond Fund revenues directly impacts the fund used by the Board to pay debt service on the state's general obligation bonds.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, proposes the annual budget (which is impacted by the revenue loss), and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works. The Governor also signed this bill into law.

The bill provides a tax exemption for a multi-use sports and events facility. The Maryland Stadium Authority is the primary state agency responsible for the planning, financing, and management of such facilities in the state.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to the state and its agencies. It would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the interpretation and implementation of the bill's retroactive tax exemption and refund requirements.
The facility in question is used for public recreational and entertainment purposes, which supports the Department's mission to promote tourism and cultural assets in Maryland.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Tax Court would be the venue for any legal challenges regarding property assessments or eligibility for the exemptions established by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Fire Prevention Commission to adopt regulations that incorporate by reference sections 30.7.5 and 31.7.5 of the National Fire Prevention Association (NFPA) Life Safety Code (2024 Edition) and authorize the placement of trash and recycling in corridors and exits in accordance with the NFPA Life Safety Code.
Title: Public Safety – State Fire Prevention Code – Trash and Recyclable Materials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires the State Fire Prevention Commission to update the State Fire Prevention Code by incorporating specific sections of the 2024 National Fire Protection Association Life Safety Code. This change allows for 'valet trash' and recycling materials awaiting collection to be placed in the corridors and exits of new and existing apartment buildings, provided they follow safety regulations regarding container size and placement.
responsible_party: State Fire Prevention Commission
stakeholders: Apartment building owners and residents, valet trash and recycling collection services, and state and local fire safety officials
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Fire Prevention Commission can implement the bill with existing resources and State revenues are not affected. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government operations or finances, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies the State Fire Prevention Commission (SFPC) as being within the Department of State Police. The State Fire Marshal, also part of this department, is responsible for enforcing the State Fire Prevention Code which this bill modifies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically directs the State Fire Prevention Commission (SFPC), which is an executive commission, to adopt new regulations regarding the placement of trash and recyclable materials in corridors and exits of apartment buildings.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, such as the State Fire Prevention Commission, and would likely review the mandated regulations for legal sufficiency before they are adopted into the State Fire Prevention Code.
The Governor oversees the executive branch departments, including the Department of State Police, and appoints the members of the State Fire Prevention Commission tasked with implementing this bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a freeze in enrollment in the Child Care Scholarship Program from including certain individuals enrolled in certain governmental support programs, children with siblings enrolled in the Program, and children who are homeless; requiring the State Department of Education to establish a waitlist for the Program under certain conditions; requiring the Department to give priority for enrollment in the Program to certain individuals on the waitlist; requiring a new application for the program that collects certain information; etc.
Title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Freeze in Enrollment - Exceptions and Waitlist

Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a freeze in enrollment in the Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program from applying to specific populations, including families enrolled in the Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income programs, siblings of enrolled children, and children experiencing homelessness. It requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to establish a prioritized waitlist during any enrollment freeze, develop a new program application, and review the methodology used to determine job training eligibility for scholarship applicants.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Low-income families, children experiencing homelessness, child care center operators and employees, and participants in governmental support programs (TCA, TANF, and SSI).
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are projected to increase by approximately $350,000 in fiscal 2027 for reprogramming the Child Care Scholarship Administrative Tracking System and associated portals. While the bill expands enrollment eligibility during freezes, costs related to these exemptions are expected to be covered by savings from separate legislation (HB 1321) concerning copayment levels. There is no local fiscal impact, but small business child care providers may benefit from increased scholarship participation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the Child Care Scholarship Program, MSDE is tasked with implementing the enrollment freeze exceptions, establishing and managing the priority waitlist, developing a new application, and conducting a methodology review.

DHS administers the Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) programs; the bill explicitly exempts individuals in these programs from child care enrollment freezes, requiring coordination between DHS and MSDE.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel; the fiscal note identifies a $350,000 general fund expenditure for system reprogramming and highlights the fiscal impact of mandated budget appropriations for the program.

The Governor is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, and the bill mandates specific appropriation levels for the Child Care Scholarship Program and involves the Governor's authority via the Board of Public Works.

The bill's focus on maintaining child care access for low-income and homeless families directly aligns with this office's mission to reduce child poverty and coordinate supports for vulnerable children and families.

This team is charged with addressing the Governor's top priorities of reducing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility, both of which are central objectives of the Child Care Scholarship Program.
The bill explicitly references the Board of Public Works' authority to approve budget reductions that can trigger enrollment freezes or eligibility alterations within the program.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees significant state expenditures and would be involved in decisions regarding budget reductions that impact program enrollment.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer is involved in the fiscal oversight and approval of budget reductions that could affect the Child Care Scholarship Program.
The bill requires the modification of the CCS Administrative Tracking System and portals, which falls under the state's broader IT strategy and infrastructure oversight managed by DoIT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires MSDE to consult with the Office of Child Care Advisory Council, which is included in this collective entity, before conducting its biennial rate analysis.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and would likely be involved in interpreting the new statutory requirements for the waitlist and application process.

Synopsis: Requiring a home builder holding a property open to the public to display in a conspicuous manner a certain notice to prospective buyers disclosing the duties of a home builder sales representative.

Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill requires home builders to display a conspicuous notice at properties open to the public disclosing that the sales representative's loyalty is to the builder and informing prospective buyers of their right to obtain independent representation.
responsible_party: Home Builder Registration Unit in the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Home builders, registered sales representatives, and prospective home buyers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly impact State or local government finances or operations. The fiscal impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal, as builders must only provide and display a specific disclosure notice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General houses the Home Builder Registration Unit within its Consumer Protection Division, which is the primary entity responsible for the registration of home builders and the enforcement of the disclosure and signage requirements established by this bill.

The Maryland Department of Labor was consulted during the fiscal analysis and maintains general oversight of business regulations and professional standards that intersect with the activities of sales representatives in the construction and housing sectors.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted as an information source and may be responsible for managing any judicial proceedings or appeals that arise from enforcement actions related to these new consumer disclosure mandates.

The Governor's Office provides executive leadership over state regulatory agencies and is responsible for the ultimate approval and policy alignment of consumer protection legislation such as this bill.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council is a tax-exempt body politic and corporate.

bill_summary: This bill clarifies the legal status of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC) by designating it as a tax-exempt body politic and corporate. This technical clarification ensures the council's independence from State agencies while maintaining its role as an instrumentality of the State, facilitating its compliance with federal requirements under the Rehabilitation Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council
stakeholders: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council, Centers for Independent Living, and Maryland residents with disabilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill's provisions are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances, revenues, or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC) directly supports the Department's mission to coordinate and improve services for residents with disabilities, specifically regarding independent living strategies.
The MSILC works in conjunction with the Maryland State Division of Rehabilitation Services, which is managed within the Department of Education.

The Secretary of State oversees the registration of charitable and nonprofit organizations; the bill's clarification of the Council's tax-exempt status is relevant to these oversight and registration functions.
As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for managing and enforcing tax-exempt designations for state instrumentalities.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and commissions, and would be responsible for advising on the Council's legal status as a 'body politic and corporate.'
The Council was originally created via an executive order from the Governor and functions as an instrumentality of the executive branch.

bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility criteria for the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program to include correctional officers and individuals enrolled in certificate programs. It renames the program to the Maryland Police Officers, Probation Agents, and Correctional Officers Scholarship Program and requires recipients to fulfill a five-year service obligation within eight years of graduation.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC)
stakeholders: Correctional officers, police officers, probation agents, and students pursuing degrees or certificates to enter these professions, as well as public senior higher education institutions and community colleges in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $20,000 in fiscal 2027 for system enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System. While the bill expands scholarship eligibility to correctional officers and certificate programs, it does not mandate additional funding beyond the existing $2,000,000 annual statutory requirement for the program. Increased demand may lead to more individuals being placed on a waiting list if appropriations are not increased to meet the new applicant pool.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary agency responsible for administering the scholarship program, including selecting recipients, publicizing the program, and handling the fiscal and system enhancements required by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is a primary employer of correctional officers and probation agents who are the direct beneficiaries of this scholarship expansion. The bill serves as a recruitment and retention tool for their workforce.

DJS operates juvenile facilities and employs staff who perform correctional-related duties; they were consulted for the fiscal note and their workforce may benefit from the expanded scholarship eligibility.
USM institutions are specifically defined as 'eligible institutions' under the bill where scholarship recipients may use their tuition assistance.
As a public senior higher education institution, Morgan State is an 'eligible institution' where students can use the scholarships provided by this program.
As a public senior higher education institution, Saint Mary's College is an 'eligible institution' for scholarship recipients under the program's criteria.

The Maryland State Police are primary beneficiaries of the existing program which this bill renames and expands. Changes to the program's structure and the addition of correctional officers directly impact the pool of available scholarship funds.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget, which includes the mandatory annual appropriation of at least $2 million for this scholarship program, and manages personnel policies for the state employees (correctional officers) impacted.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategy and policy. Enhancing education and recruitment incentives for the correctional and law enforcement workforce aligns with their mission to improve the criminal justice system.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MHEC and DPSCS regarding the implementation of the bill and the enforcement of the scholarship's service obligation and repayment provisions.

The bill expresses the intent of the General Assembly that the Governor include at least $5,000,000 annually in the state capital budget for this program.
DBM is responsible for state budget development and personnel management; the bill requires new staffing positions and ongoing capital and general fund appropriations that DBM would oversee.
Eligibility for the grant program is tied to schools operating in conjunction with residential treatment centers licensed by the Maryland Department of Health.
Eligibility for the grant program is tied to schools operating in conjunction with residential treatment centers licensed by the Department of Human Services.
Eligibility for the grant program is tied to schools operating in conjunction with residential treatment centers licensed by the Department of Juvenile Services.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the IAC and MSDE, particularly for the development of the new regulations required to implement this grant program.
DGS is mentioned in the fiscal note as the agency typically responsible for reviewing design and construction documents for state-funded school construction projects.

Synopsis: Altering, to 45 days before voting and early voting for a primary election, general election, or vote on a proposition, the time period during which a common ownership community may restrict the display of candidate or proposition signs.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills

bill_summary: This emergency bill extends the minimum timeframe during which residents of common ownership communities—including condominiums, homeowners associations, and cooperative housing corporations—must be allowed to display signs for political candidates or ballot propositions. It requires that these communities permit the display of such signs for a period beginning at least 45 days before the start of early voting (or 45 days before the election if no early voting is conducted) and ending 7 days after the election.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Residents and property owners within common ownership communities (COCs), political candidates, and proponents or opponents of ballot questions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State or local government finances or operations, as stated in the official Fiscal Note. Small businesses are also unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is explicitly responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums. Since this bill amends the Maryland Condominium Act to alter regulations on candidate sign displays, it directly impacts a sector under the agency's oversight.

The Office of the Attorney General enforces consumer protection laws and provides legal counsel to state agencies. Disputes regarding resident rights and board restrictions in common ownership communities often fall under consumer protection oversight, and the OAG was cited as a source of information for this bill.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which would be responsible for adjudicating any civil disputes or litigation arising from the enforcement or violation of these new sign display regulations in common ownership communities.

The bill's mandated display periods are directly tied to the election calendar managed by the State Board of Elections, specifically referencing the start of early voting and the primary and general election cycles.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to register each local school system in the State as an associate member of a certain national membership organization; and requiring each local school system in the State to utilize the Educator Identification Clearinghouse to screen individuals who receive an offer of employment on or after August 1, 2026, for an educator position that requires a license and ensure that each individual who receives an offer applies for and obtains the appropriate license.
Title: Local School Systems - Educator Screening - Educator Identification Clearinghouse (School Personnel Vetting and Hiring Transparency Act)

Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.

Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
