bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education to register every local school system in the State as an associate member of a national membership organization that provides access to the Educator Identification Clearinghouse. The State Department of Education is responsible for paying all associated membership fees and dues. Local school systems must use this clearinghouse to screen job applicants for educator positions requiring a license and must ensure that these individuals obtain the proper licensing before interacting with children.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Local school systems, educator job applicants, Maryland State Department of Education, and public school students.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $28,600 annually starting in fiscal 2027 for the Maryland State Department of Education to pay subscription and membership fees. Local school system expenditures will decrease minimally (up to $2,400 per system) for those systems currently paying these fees themselves. No impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state agency responsible for overseeing public education and certifying educators, MSDE is the lead agency tasked with registering local school systems in the national membership organization (NASDTEC) and paying the associated dues and fees.

The Center, an independent unit within MSDE, coordinates school safety efforts. This bill's requirement for enhanced vetting of educators through a national disciplinary clearinghouse directly supports its mission to ensure safe learning environments and protects the welfare of students.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel management. The bill creates a new annual general fund expenditure of approximately $28,600 for MSDE to cover membership and subscription fees for the 24 local school systems.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and state agencies. It may be required to provide guidance on the implementation of the new screening requirements and ensure the use of the Educator Identification Clearinghouse complies with state and federal privacy and employment laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety in Maryland. The bill's focus on vetting school personnel to prevent contact between children and individuals with histories of professional discipline or misconduct aligns with the office's public safety and crime prevention mandates.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Information Technology to post on its website the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan within 1 year after the Governor is inaugurated in each gubernatorial term; requiring the Secretary of Information Technology to notify the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly if the plan is delayed; and requiring the Secretary of Information Technology, or the Secretary's designee, to provide a certain annual briefing to the General Assembly.
Title: Department of Information Technology - Statewide Information Technology Master Plan - Reporting

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to publish the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan on its website and submit it to the General Assembly within one year of a Governor's inauguration. It also mandates that the Secretary of Information Technology provide annual briefings to the General Assembly regarding the plan's implementation, changes, and deployment strategies, and establishes formal notification procedures if the publication deadline is missed.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology (DoIT)
stakeholders: Executive Branch state agencies, the Governor of Maryland, the Maryland General Assembly, and the public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Information Technology can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no estimated impact on State revenues or local government finances, and no impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Information Technology is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. It is mandated to develop, publicly post, and report on the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan, notify relevant officials of any delays, and provide annual briefings to the General Assembly regarding the plan's implementation across the Executive Branch.

The bill requires the Secretary of Information Technology to notify the Governor in writing if the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan is delayed. Additionally, the plan's mandatory submission cycle is directly tied to the beginning of each gubernatorial term, and the plan itself governs policy and management initiatives across the Executive Branch overseen by the Governor.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a railroad train used in connection with the movement of freight from being operated in the State unless it has at least two crew members, subject to certain exceptions; providing a penalty for a first offense of up to $10,000 or, in the case of a willful violation within the immediately preceding 3 years, a fine of up to $25,000; etc.
Title: Railroads - Required Crew for Movement of Freight

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires freight railroad trains sharing rail corridors with high-speed passenger or commuter trains to have a crew of at least two individuals. It establishes civil penalties for willful violations and is contingent upon the enactment of similar legislation in New York, Pennsylvania, and Virginia.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Railroad companies, freight train crews, the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA), and CSX Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill generally has no immediate material impact due to federal preemption and its contingent nature. However, if federal rules requiring two-person crews are repealed or invalidated, the Maryland Transit Administration may be required to reimburse CSX up to 6000000 annually for labor costs under an existing access agreement. Additionally, willful violations are subject to civil penalties of up to 10000 for a first offense and 25000 for repeat offenses. The Maryland Department of Labor's Railroad Safety and Health Program can handle enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Labor's Railroad Safety and Health Program, which is responsible for monitoring railroad safety practices and enforcing state-specific requirements. The Commissioner of Labor is specifically authorized to assess civil penalties for violations, and the department must notify the Department of Legislative Services when the bill's contingency is met.

The MTA has a contractual Access Agreement with CSX Transportation that requires the state to reimburse labor costs (up to $6 million annually) if Maryland mandates an increase in freight crew sizes. Since the bill targets freight sharing corridors used by commuter trains (like MARC), the MTA faces a direct and significant fiscal impact.

As the parent agency of the Maryland Transit Administration, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund, which would be the source of the estimated $6 million annual reimbursement to CSX. MDOT also manages the broader transportation network and modal administrations affected by rail safety regulations.

By statute, the Public Service Commission is responsible for funding the Railroad Safety and Health Program at the Maryland Department of Labor through its annual assessments of public service companies.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Department of Labor and MDOT regarding federal preemption issues and defending the state in potential litigation arising from the enforcement of these crew requirements.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and fiscal planning, including the potential multi-million dollar impact on the Transportation Trust Fund and the funding of positions within the Department of Labor.
OAH would be responsible for adjudicating contested cases if railroad companies appeal the civil penalties assessed by the Commissioner of Labor for violations of the crew size requirements.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for the bill's implementation and coordination of policy initiatives related to state safety and labor laws.

The agency's role in hazard mitigation and emergency preparedness is relevant as railroad staffing levels are often linked to safety and the effective response to rail-related disasters or emergencies.

This office assesses the state's readiness for emergencies and coordinates strategies for disaster prevention regarding critical infrastructure, which includes the rail corridors addressed in this safety legislation.

Synopsis: Altering certain apprenticeship requirements relating to public works contracts to require certain contractors and subcontractors to employ a certain number of qualifying new apprentices or journeyworkers necessary to meet a certain applicable percentage for the project; altering which projects are subject to certain apprenticeship requirements; altering certain provisions of law that authorize contractors and subcontractors to make certain payments to a certain apprenticeship program in lieu of employing certain apprentices; etc.
Title: Public Works Contracts - Apprenticeship Requirements (Maryland Workforce Apprenticeship Utilization Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Works -see also- Brg&Tun; Hwys; PublBlgFac; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Workforce Apprenticeship Utilization Act requires contractors and subcontractors on public works projects subject to prevailing wage laws to ensure that a specified percentage of total labor hours (initially 20%) are performed by qualifying apprentices or journeyworkers. The bill expands these requirements to include the University System of Maryland and Baltimore City Community College and modifies the administration and authorized uses of the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Public works contractors and subcontractors, registered apprentices, journeyworkers, the University System of Maryland, Baltimore City Community College, and state and local agencies managing public works projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund are expected to increase starting in FY 2027 as contractors may pay into the fund in lieu of meeting apprenticeship percentages, though a reliable estimate is unavailable. General fund revenues may increase minimally due to new fines of up to $10,000 for noncompliance. While increased use of apprentices could reduce project costs, state and local expenditures may increase if the bill's requirements reduce the number of bidders or increase administrative overhead for public works contracts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Secretary of Labor to file suit in any court of competent jurisdiction to enforce penalties, and the Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational support to the judicial system where these cases would be heard.

The bill requires the Board of Public Works to approve procurement policies for the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College regarding these new apprenticeship requirements.
The bill explicitly tasks the Comptroller with accounting for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, which will receive increased revenues and penalty payments under the new law.

The Board of Public Works may request comments from DBM on university and college contracts for services or capital improvements exceeding $1,000,000 that are now subject to these apprenticeship mandates.
The bill impacts the State Apprenticeship Training Fund which is used to support preapprenticeship and workforce development programs, areas where MSDE collaborates with the Department of Labor.
As a primary procurement and construction authority for the state, DGS manages public works projects that will be subject to the bill's apprenticeship utilization and reporting requirements.

The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency; the Secretary of Labor is responsible for setting utilization percentages, managing the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, adopting regulations, and enforcing compliance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department manages various public works and construction projects for correctional facilities that must comply with the new apprenticeship percentage requirements.
MDOT oversees five modal administrations that manage massive state-funded public works projects, all of which will be significantly impacted by the new apprenticeship utilization mandates.
The bill directly impacts the state's workforce strategy regarding apprenticeship growth and utilization, which falls within the board's policy-making and strategic advisory scope.
As an agency that owns and operates major airports, MAA manages significant capital improvement and construction projects subject to the bill's labor requirements.
The MPA manages state-owned port facilities and dredging operations, which involve public works contracts now subject to the bill's apprenticeship utilization standards.
The MSA plans, builds, and manages professional sports and public school facilities; its large-scale construction projects are considered 'covered projects' under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants the Board of Contract Appeals authority over contract claims related to procurement contracts for the University System of Maryland, Morgan State, and St. Mary's College, which now must include these apprenticeship terms.

The State Treasurer is designated by the bill to hold the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately and also serves on the Board of Public Works which must approve the updated procurement policies.
The MTA operates and builds transit infrastructure, including rail and bus facilities, which represent public works contracts impacted by the new labor utilization percentages.
The MDTA finances and maintains toll facilities; its construction and repair projects are subject to the apprenticeship requirements for public works.
The bill explicitly removes exemptions and requires Morgan State University to comply with Title 17 apprenticeship requirements for its public works procurement.
As a modal administration of MDOT, the MVA's facility construction and renovation projects are subject to the bill's public works requirements.
OLA is responsible for auditing state agencies and funds; it would oversee fiscal compliance for the expanded State Apprenticeship Training Fund and agency adherence to the new mandates.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the universities regarding the implementation of the Act and may represent the Secretary in litigation to recover penalties.
The bill explicitly requires St. Mary's College of Maryland to adhere to the apprenticeship utilization requirements for its public works contracts.
The SHA manages the state's largest portfolio of non-toll highway and bridge construction projects, all of which will be directly impacted by the new apprenticeship labor hour requirements.
The bill explicitly subjects the University System of Maryland and its 12 institutions to the apprenticeship requirements for public works contracts, altering their previous procurement exemptions.

Synopsis: Extending the deadline for the report of findings and recommendations from the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing from June 1, 2025, to December 1, 2028; and extending the termination date for the Workgroup from June 30, 2026, to December 31, 2028.
Title: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing from June 30, 2026, to December 31, 2028. It also extends the deadline for the workgroup to submit its report of findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly from June 1, 2025, to December 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill's requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances. The analysis assumes the workgroup will be maintained despite the bill's effective date occurring one day after the workgroup's original termination date.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary administrative and staffing body for the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, which is being extended by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts this category by extending the termination date and reporting deadline of a specific state workgroup.
The Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is a unit within the Governor's Office, and the workgroup is required to submit its report to the Governor.

As the state's primary educational institution for the target population, the workgroup's study and recommendations regarding educational and social opportunities directly affect the school's mission and stakeholders.

This department is the principal agency for coordinating services to residents with disabilities, including those who are deaf, deafblind, or hard of hearing, and will be impacted by the workgroup's policy recommendations.
As the fiscal and personnel agency, DBM monitors the continuation of state entities and was consulted for the fiscal analysis of this extension.

The workgroup is tasked with studying health opportunities for deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals, which directly overlaps with the department's public health and care financing responsibilities.
The workgroup assesses and makes recommendations regarding educational opportunities, impacting the oversight responsibilities of MSDE.
The workgroup studies employment opportunities and challenges like underemployment for deaf individuals, which falls under the purview of the Department of Labor's workforce development programs.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning on July 1, 2026, a county or municipality to notify the Department of the Environment within 10 business days  after a county or municipality accepts the permit application for a new building that has a proposed gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more.
Title: Environment - Permit Applications for New Buildings - Notice (Large Buildings for Tomorrow Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.

bill_summary: The Large Buildings for Tomorrow Act requires counties and municipalities to notify the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) within 10 business days of accepting a building permit application for any new building with at least 35,000 square feet of gross floor area (excluding parking garages). The notification must include the building's address, permit number, square footage, type, planned energy sources, and owner contact information. This reporting requirement applies to new construction for which permit applications or utility service requests are filed after the bill's effective date.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), and Maryland counties and municipalities.
stakeholders: Property owners and developers of new buildings with 35,000 square feet or more of gross floor area, local government permit offices, and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has a minimal fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of the Environment can receive the required permit notices with existing resources, and local governments can send the notifications using existing resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill, as it is the recipient of the required building permit notices from counties and municipalities. This administrative role is critical to MDE's oversight of the Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) established under the Climate Solutions Now Act.

The Department of Labor is responsible for the Maryland Building Performance Standards (MBPS). Although specific new regulatory mandates for Labor were removed from the bill by amendment, the department remains highly relevant as it oversees the underlying building codes and energy conservation requirements that these large buildings must eventually satisfy.

DGS is the primary agency for the construction and management of state-owned facilities. As 'covered buildings' under the bill include state-owned structures over 35,000 square feet, DGS will be impacted by the new notice requirements and the associated tracking of energy sources during the permitting process.

MDOT manages a vast portfolio of large facilities, including airport terminals, port buildings, and transit centers. New construction projects exceeding the 35,000 square foot threshold will be subject to the notice requirements provided to MDE.

USM institutions frequently undertake large-scale construction projects for academic, research, and residential purposes. The university system is impacted as an owner and developer of facilities that meet the bill's size threshold for permit notification.
As a state agency that manages and develops large urban campus facilities, Morgan State University will be subject to the permit notice requirements for new buildings exceeding 35,000 square feet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees large correctional facilities and detention centers. Any new construction or significant expansion projects meeting the size criteria will be flagged through the local permit notice system to MDE.
DJS operates residential facilities for youth. New facility construction exceeding the 35,000 square foot threshold will trigger the notice requirements established by the bill.

MSA is responsible for the planning and construction of large sports, entertainment, and public school facilities. Given that its projects are typically of significant scale, they will frequently fall under the bill's permit notification mandate.

The Department of Planning provides technical assistance to local governments and coordinates state land-use policies. It is relevant due to its role in promoting sustainable growth and managing data related to significant new developments.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE, the Department of Labor, and other state agencies regarding the implementation of the new notice requirements and compliance with state building and environmental laws.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch's policy coordination, specifically relating to climate change and energy efficiency goals like those found in the Climate Solutions Now Act, which this bill supports.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for certain local law enforcement officers if the Seat Pleasant Police Department becomes a participating governmental unit; and providing that a certain individual is entitled to eligibility service and creditable service that was earned before the effective date of the Seat Pleasant Police Department's participation in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Seat Pleasant Police Department

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires law enforcement officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department to join the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) as a condition of employment, provided the city elects to become a participating governmental unit. It further ensures that participating officers receive eligibility and creditable service for their years of employment with the department prior to joining the state system.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department and the City of Seat Pleasant
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Locally, based on an actuarial analysis, Seat Pleasant's pension liabilities are estimated to increase by $2,104,315. Net annual employer contributions for the city are projected to increase by $541,380 starting as early as fiscal 2028, which reflects a gross increase of $680,330 offset by a new entrant liability credit of $138,950 per year for 25 years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS), this agency is directly responsible for managing the entry of the Seat Pleasant Police Department as a participating governmental unit and calculating the resulting service credits.

DBM is the principal personnel and fiscal agency for the state, responsible for overseeing state employee benefits and policies, including the fiscal impacts of pension legislation on the State Retirement and Pension System.

The State Treasurer acts as the chief financial officer for state funds, serves as the principal custodian of retirement system assets, and holds a key position on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to the State Retirement Agency regarding the implementation of statutory changes to pension systems.
The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and serves as a member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, overseeing the fiscal integrity of the system.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the primary implementing agencies, and is responsible for signing this bill into law and coordinating the associated policy initiatives.

Synopsis: Increasing from three to five the membership of the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County; requiring the Governor to appoint members to the Board from a list of individuals recommended by the Anne Arundel County delegations to the General Assembly; altering eligibility requirements for Board membership; and requiring the Board to adopt and publish a certain ethics policy.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill expands the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members and requires the Governor to appoint these members from a list of recommendations provided by the Anne Arundel County House and Senate delegations. It establishes new residency and political party limits for board members and mandates that the board adopt and publish a written ethics policy regarding conflicts of interest and recusal.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Residents and alcoholic beverage licensees of Anne Arundel County, and potential candidates for the Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Anne Arundel County expenditures are projected to increase by $39,995 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to account for the salaries of two additional board members ($15,000 each), fringe benefits, and incidental expenses. There is no impact on county revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the primary authority responsible for appointing members to the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners. This bill directly alters the Governor's appointment process by requiring selections from a list provided by legislative delegations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. This bill changes the criteria and process for filling vacancies on the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners.

The bill requires the Board to adopt and publish a written ethics policy regarding conflicts of interest and recusal. The State Ethics Commission oversees state ethics laws and ensures that local government and board ethics policies meet minimum state standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of License Commissioners is a permanent body authorized by the General Assembly and appointed by the Governor to address the regulation of alcoholic beverages in the county, making it a relevant entity within this collective designation.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and state boards. They may be required to advise on the legal implementation of the new appointment process and the mandatory ethics policy required by the bill.

The Comptroller is the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry. As the bill modifies the composition and governance of a local board responsible for issuing and enforcing retail alcoholic beverage licenses, it impacts the broader regulatory framework the Comptroller oversees.
The Secretary of State serves as the custodian of state records and processes the official commissions for individuals appointed by the Governor to state and local boards.

Synopsis: Extending the presumption of compensability under the workers' compensation law to include, subject to certain conditions, Carroll County correctional deputies who suffer from heart disease or hypertension resulting in partial disability or death; and altering a certain definition of "public safety employee" so as to apply a certain workers' compensation provision relating to permanent partial disability benefits to correctional deputies employed by Carroll County.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Heart Disease and Hypertension Presumption and Permanent Partial Disability - Carroll County Correctional Deputies

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill grants Carroll County correctional deputies a workers' compensation presumption that heart disease or hypertension is a compensable occupational disease. It also reclassifies these deputies as 'public safety employees,' which entitles them to enhanced (doubled) permanent partial disability benefits for certain claims.
responsible_party: Carroll County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Carroll County correctional deputies and the Carroll County government
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances, but it increases Carroll County expenditures starting in fiscal 2027. The increase results from the new occupational disease presumption and the 'public safety employee' designation, which doubles the maximum weekly benefits for certain disability awards. According to the fiscal note, a single enhanced award could cost the county up to 18,944 dollars more than a standard award, though total annual costs are indeterminate as the number of claims cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicating claims, this agency must implement the new presumption for Carroll County correctional deputies and handle the increased claim volume and specific medical reporting requirements established by the bill.

The bill establishes specific conditions for the compensability of heart disease or hypertension based on whether the condition is more severe than pre-existing conditions. The Subsequent Injury Fund is responsible for investigating claims involving pre-existing health conditions that increase disability, which is a core component of how this bill will be applied.

The bill contains provisions (Section 9-503(e)) requiring that workers' compensation benefits be adjusted or capped when combined with retirement benefits from the state system. The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers these retirement systems and would be involved in the coordination and calculation of these benefits.

While this agency primarily handles claims for state employees, it is specifically identified in the fiscal note as a source of information. Furthermore, its private successor (Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) serves as a common insurer for local government entities that may be affected by changes to public safety employee benefit classifications.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that the Governor include in the annual budget bill a $350,000 appropriation to the State's Consumer Health Information Hub; requiring the Hub to carry out certain duties to the extent funding is available; and repealing the termination date for certain provisions of law related to consumer health information and the State's Consumer Health Information Hub.
Title: Consumer Health Information - Termination Date and Mandatory Funding for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub - Repeal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: This bill makes the State’s Consumer Health Information Hub permanent by repealing its June 30, 2026, termination date. It also removes the requirement for the Governor to provide a $350,000 annual appropriation for the Hub, specifying that the Hub shall carry out its duties only to the extent that funding is available.
responsible_party: University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy
stakeholders: Maryland residents, state and local government agencies, health systems, and community-based organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill repeals the $350,000 mandated annual appropriation for the State’s Consumer Health Information Hub and removes the Hub's June 30, 2026, termination date. The Department of Legislative Services notes that there is no material fiscal impact because the mandate was already scheduled to expire at the end of fiscal 2026 and the Hub's future operations are contingent on available funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy, which is a component of the University of Maryland (a USM institution), as the State's Consumer Health Information Hub. The bill extends the Hub's statutory existence and modifies its funding requirements.

The bill addresses consumer health information and health literacy. The Hub is required to engage with state and local government agencies to promote plain language in health communications, and the Maryland Department of Health is a primary agency for health policy and oversight of local health departments.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and supervision. The bill repeals a mandated $350,000 annual appropriation to the Hub, shifting the fiscal structure to depend on available funding, which directly impacts DBM's budget planning.

The bill repeals the requirement for the Governor to include a mandatory $350,000 appropriation for the Hub in the annual budget bill, thereby modifying the Governor's statutory budgetary obligations.
The bill specifically tasks the Consumer Health Information Hub with supporting the public reporting of health care quality reports generated by the Maryland Health Care Commission.

The bill mandates that state agencies use plain language in public communications regarding social services benefits. As the primary provider of such benefits in Maryland, DHS is directly impacted by these communication standards.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Wicomico County and the governing body of a municipal corporation in Wicomico County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain real property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.
Title: Wicomico County - Property Tax Credit - Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing body of Wicomico County or any municipality within the county to grant a property tax credit for real property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. To qualify, the property must be held for development, rehabilitation, and eventual transfer to a private owner and cannot be used for administrative or warehouse purposes.
responsible_party: The governing body of Wicomico County and municipal corporations in Wicomico County
stakeholders: Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc., Wicomico County, and municipal governments within Wicomico County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Local property tax revenues for Wicomico County and its municipalities will decrease by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent the optional credit is granted. As a point of reference, Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. paid a total of $3,611 in property taxes for 14 parcels in fiscal 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill supports Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc., a non-profit dedicated to expanding affordable homeownership and community revitalization in Wicomico County. This aligns directly with the Department's mission to support affordable housing and municipal infrastructure projects through community revitalization investments.

As the state's principal tax collector and chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the oversight of tax laws and state revenues. Although property taxes are primarily collected at the local level, changes to the state's Tax-Property Article fall within the Comptroller's broader policy interests.
The bill's purpose involves property used for development, rehabilitation, and transfer, which falls under the Department's scope of promoting sustainable growth and community revitalization.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, including property tax assessments and credits. If disputes arise regarding the application of this specific tax credit, the Tax Court would have the authority to hear the appeal.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative of the state and provides legal counsel to the General Assembly regarding the legality and implementation of amendments to the Annotated Code of Maryland, including the Tax-Property Article.

As the state's chief executive, the Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing bills into law or vetoing them. The bill also impacts the administration of state laws that the Governor is tasked with enforcing.

bill_summary: The Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act promotes transit-oriented development (TOD) by providing financial incentives and reducing local land use barriers. It allows local governments to automatically designate TOD areas near rail stations as enterprise zones, which offers property and income tax credits to businesses. The bill also requires the Maryland Economic Development Corporation to prioritize redevelopment projects near rail stations for infrastructure loans, limits the ability of local governments to impose minimum parking requirements or other land use restrictions near transit, and delays the collection of local development impact fees and excise taxes for qualifying mixed-use projects until construction is complete.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Economic Development Corporation, and the Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Real estate developers, local governments, businesses and residents near rail transit stations, and state transportation and economic development agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's fiscal impact is indeterminate but will result in increased State general fund expenditures to reimburse local jurisdictions for enterprise zone property tax credits. State revenues from the general fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund are expected to decrease due to newly eligible businesses claiming enterprise zone income tax credits. Local governments will see a decrease in property tax revenue from these credits and a delay in revenue collection from development impact fees and excise taxes. These impacts are contingent on local participation and the volume of future development.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns specific duties to the Department, including approving transit-oriented development plans for state-owned land and reviewing/concurring with local parking studies for areas near rail stations.
The bill explicitly mandates that MEDCO prioritize certain redevelopment projects contiguous to rail transit stations when making loans under the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program.

The Department oversees the Enterprise Zone program. The bill provides for the automatic designation of transit-oriented developments as enterprise zones, directly impacting the Secretary of Commerce's designation authority and program limits.

The agency oversees sustainable growth and land use visions. It is a key member of the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, which is involved in designating transit-oriented developments and receiving notice of local government elections regarding enterprise zones.

The bill (Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act) aims to increase housing supply and affordability by incentivizing residential and mixed-use development near transit, aligning with the department's core mission.
This is an administration bill that coordinates policy across the executive branch via the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet to address housing and transit priorities.
The fiscal note indicates a significant impact on state general fund expenditures and revenues due to enterprise zone property tax remittances and income tax credits.
The bill impacts state revenues through the creation of new enterprise zones and associated tax credits, which the Comptroller is responsible for collecting and administering.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, an executive body, is responsible for designating transit-oriented developments and receiving official notices from local governments regarding zoning elections.
The Treasurer monitors the state's fiscal health and sits on the Board of Public Works, which may oversee the transfer or lease of state-owned land redeveloped under this Act.
The bill promotes the redevelopment of land owned by the State, which may require the Board's approval for significant contracts or property transfers.
The bill specifically excludes rail stations located on the campus of institutions of higher education from certain parking and land use limitations.
USM institutions are excluded from certain parking and mixed-use development mandates for rail stations located on their campuses.
As an institution of higher education, rail stations on its campus are excluded from specified parking and mixed-use development requirements under the bill.
Rail stations on its campus are specifically excluded from certain local land use restrictions and mandates defined in the bill.
The team focuses on enhancing economic mobility and pilot initiatives for the Governor's priorities, which include transit-oriented housing development and economic growth.

bill_summary: The Protection From Predatory Pricing Act prohibits food retailers operating establishments of at least 15,000 square feet and third-party food delivery service providers from utilizing dynamic pricing or personal data to set higher prices for tax-exempt food items for specific consumers. It also prevents these entities from using protected class data to offer or sell goods in a way that denies consumers privileges or accommodations. Violations are categorized as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, enforceable by the Office of the Attorney General, although the bill does not authorize a private right of action.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, food retailers with at least 15,000 square feet of space, and third-party food delivery service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by approximately 325,000 per year beginning in fiscal 2027 for the Office of the Attorney General to hire an Assistant Attorney General and a technologist for enforcement and investigations. The Department of Legislative Services notes that actual costs will depend on the volume of consumer complaints. The bill's civil and criminal penalty provisions are not expected to have a material impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) is the primary agency responsible for enforcing the bill. The legislation designates violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the OAG's Consumer Protection Division. The fiscal note indicates that OAG will require additional staff and technical expertise to handle investigations and the mandated notice-and-cure process.

This is an administration bill introduced at the request of the Governor. The office is responsible for the overall policy initiative, legislative coordination, and overseeing the executive branch's enforcement of the new regulations on dynamic pricing and data usage in the food retail sector.

The bill prohibits food retailers and delivery providers from using 'protected class data' to withhold or deny advantages or privileges to consumers. This aligns with the Commission's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws in public accommodations and commercial practices, though the bill places specific enforcement power with the Attorney General.

The bill defines the scope of regulated 'food retailers' and 'third-party delivery service providers' based on whether they sell food that is exempt from sales and use tax under Section 11-206(c) of the Tax - General Article. As the state's principal tax collector and authority on sales tax exemptions, the Comptroller's classifications are central to identifying entities subject to the bill.

According to the fiscal note, the bill will increase general fund expenditures due to the need for additional personnel and technical resources at the Office of the Attorney General. The Department of Budget and Management will be responsible for overseeing these budget adjustments and long-term fiscal planning.

The bill regulates the pricing and data strategies of major participants in Maryland's retail economy, including large-scale grocery stores and delivery services. This impacts the commercial landscape and business practices within the state, which are of direct interest to the Department's economic development mission.

The bill amends the Commercial Law Article to establish that certain violations do not authorize a private right of action and requires a cure period before enforcement actions can proceed. These procedural changes affect the litigation of consumer protection claims in the state court system.

As an agency that protects both consumers and the public while fostering economic growth, the Department of Labor has a secondary interest in the regulation of merchants and business practices. The agency was noted as an information source in the fiscal analysis regarding the bill's impact on commercial activities.

Synopsis: Establishing the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Military Department to provide funds for State active duty mobilization of the National Guard.
Title: Military Department - National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund
bill_summary: The bill establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Military Department's Office of the Adjutant General. Its purpose is to provide immediate funding for personnel and equipment during State active duty mobilizations of the National Guard as ordered by the Governor, ensuring rapid and effective response to emergencies such as disasters or public crises.
responsible_party: Office of the Adjutant General within the Military Department
stakeholders: Maryland National Guard personnel, the Military Department, and Maryland citizens impacted by state emergencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are expected to increase by at least 1,000,000 in FY 2027 to initially capitalize the fund, with corresponding increases in special fund revenues. Ongoing general fund expenditures will be required to replenish the fund as it is used. The bill accelerates spending that would likely occur via deficiency appropriations or budget amendments to create a more efficient funding mechanism. Investment earnings from the fund are credited to the general fund. There is no anticipated material impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the fund within the Office of the Adjutant General and designates the Adjutant General as the administrator responsible for managing the fund's assets for National Guard mobilizations.
The fund is created specifically to finance the personnel and equipment costs associated with the State active duty mobilization of the National Guard.

The Governor serves as the commander-in-chief who orders National Guard mobilizations, which triggers the use of this fund. Additionally, the Governor proposes the state budget which capitalizes and replenishes the fund.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established special fund.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the budget appropriations and replenishments required to maintain the fund's operational effectiveness as described in the fiscal note.
National Guard mobilizations typically occur in response to emergencies and disasters which MDEM is responsible for coordinating statewide.

bill_summary: The Delivering Economic Competitiveness and Advancing Development Efforts (DECADE) Act modifies and extends various Maryland economic development programs and tax credits. Key changes include renaming the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account to the Strategic Closing Fund and placing it under the Department of Commerce, transferring the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone and Build Our Future Grant programs to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO), and extending several major tax credits for job creation, research and development, and security clearance costs. Additionally, it establishes a sales and use tax exemption for certain internal transactions of information technology services and digital products between affiliated business groups.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO)
stakeholders: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses, technology companies (including quantum computing, biotech, and aerospace), film production entities, and local Maryland governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill results in a significant net decrease in State funds. In fiscal 2027, State revenues are projected to decrease by a total of 37300000 (35500000 from the general fund and 1800000 from special funds) primarily due to new sales and use tax exemptions. By fiscal 2028, the net negative impact reaches 71800000 due to the combined effect of revenue losses from tax credit extensions and an estimated 10600000 increase in general fund expenditures for program funding and backfilling lost education revenue. Local governments will experience a decrease in highway user revenues and potential property tax revenue shifts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is an Administration bill introduced at the request of the Governor. The office oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget, which is directly impacted by the fund transfers and tax revenue changes in this act.

The Comptroller is responsible for tax collection, auditing, and accounting for the state's revenues. This bill introduces major sales and use tax exemptions, alters income and insurance premium tax credits, and requires the Comptroller to evaluate the film production tax credit and track tax credit carryforwards.

The Treasurer is responsible for the investment and custody of state funds. The bill establishes and modifies several special funds, including the Strategic Closing Fund and the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, which require management by the Treasurer.

Agriculture is designated as one of the eligible technology sectors for the Build Our Future Grant Program, and the bill also mentions aquaculture projects as eligible for financial assistance under the MEDAAF program.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the state's budget development and revenue estimation. This bill has a significant fiscal impact, decreasing general fund revenues by tens of millions of dollars and altering the structure of major economic development funds.

Commerce is the primary implementing agency for the majority of the programs altered by the bill, including MEDAAF, MSBDFA, SMWOBA, and various tax credits. The bill also relocates the Strategic Closing Fund directly under Commerce's administration.

The bill's sales and use tax exemptions reduce revenues for the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, which supports the state's public education system. Additionally, MSDE oversees the Maryland Center for School Safety, and school construction entities are mentioned in related economic contexts.
The bill provides for financial assistance for the redevelopment of qualified brownfields sites through MEDAAF, which is an environmental restoration activity regulated by MDE.

DHCD is mentioned as an agency that RISE zone concierges will coordinate with to assist businesses. The department also jointly administers certain economic development block grants with the Department of Commerce.

The bill provides for a significant sales and use tax exemption for information technology services and digital products among affiliated groups, which directly relates to the state's IT strategy and industry oversight.

The bill impacts workforce development and employment data through reporting requirements and RISE zone concierge coordination. It also relates to unemployment rates as criteria for certain economic development opportunities.

MDP is involved in the designation of priority funding areas and coordinate strategies for sustainable development, which are factors in the eligibility and application of RISE zones and other economic development programs.

The bill's expansion of corporate income tax credits results in a decrease in the Transportation Trust Fund's share of revenue, which impacts local highway user revenue grants. RISE zone concierges also coordinate with MDOT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reallocates $5 million of video lottery terminal (VLT) proceeds from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account to the newly established Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund.
The bill significantly expands the reporting requirements and performance metrics for multiple economic development programs, including tracking salaries, benefits, and job retention outcomes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes substantial changes to the Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) and the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account (SMWOBA), which are core focus areas for this office.
The bill involves changes to civil and criminal penalties related to false statements in business applications and tax disputes that may be adjudicated within the court system.
The bill includes provisions regarding the request of additional money for small business development funds from the Board of Public Works via the General Emergency Fund.

The bill transfers the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program and the Build Our Future Grant Program from the Department of Commerce to MEDCO, making it a primary implementing agency.

MHEC establishes policies for public and private colleges and universities, which are defined as 'qualified institutions' for the RISE Zone Program and are eligible recipients for Build Our Future Grants.
Several tax credits extended by the bill, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit and the Businesses that Create New Jobs Program, can be claimed against the insurance premium tax regulated by the MIA.
The bill establishes that a primary purpose of the film production activity tax credit is to boost tourism, an area directly overseen by this office.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, the Tax Court would be responsible for hearing appeals related to the various tax credits and property assessments mentioned in the bill.

TEDCO is listed as an agency that RISE zone concierges must coordinate with, and its focus on early-stage technology businesses aligns with the eligible technology sectors defined for the Build Our Future Grant Program.
As a public university, Morgan State is a 'qualified institution' for the RISE zone program and an eligible recipient of grants from the Build Our Future Grant Program.
OLA is responsible for auditing the executive agencies and programs affected by this bill, including the newly structured funds at the Department of Commerce and MEDCO.
The bill alters property tax credits for RISE zones and modifies reporting requirements for businesses receiving new job tax credits, which may lead to appeals handled by these boards.
The bill was reviewed by the PSC regarding small business eligibility requirements for contracts involving utilities, as mentioned in the fiscal note.
As an independent public college, St. Mary's is an eligible 'qualified institution' for RISE zones and technology-based grant funding under the programs transferred to MEDCO.
The USM institutions serve as anchor 'qualified institutions' for the RISE Zone Program and are primary collaborators/recipients for the Build Our Future Grant Program.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits private home detention monitoring agencies, their agents, and employees of courthouses or correctional facilities from soliciting business or advertising monitoring services on the grounds of a courthouse or correctional facility. It establishes misdemeanor penalties, including fines and license suspensions, for violations of these prohibitions.

stakeholders: Private home detention monitoring agencies and their agents, courthouse employees, correctional facility employees, and individuals required to use home detention monitoring services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impacts are expected to be minimal. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. While the bill establishes misdemeanor fines of up to $2,500 for a first offense and $5,000 for subsequent offenses, these penalty provisions are not anticipated to have a meaningful effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

The bill prohibits solicitation on the grounds of correctional facilities managed by DPSCS and requires that any licensed person convicted of a violation be referred to DPSCS for appropriate regulatory action.

This bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly affects courthouse operations by prohibiting solicitation on courthouse grounds and placing restrictions on courthouse employees. The AOC provides administrative and operational support to the judicial branch.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services regarding the interpretation and enforcement of these new misdemeanor and licensing provisions.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits law enforcement agencies from assigning officers to non-administrative duties without providing protective body armor that meets National Institute of Justice standards and is not expired. Law enforcement agencies must replace armor before its manufacturer-indicated replacement date and notify the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission if they fail to do so within 31 days. The bill also authorizes the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to withhold certain grant funds from agencies that fail to comply with these replacement and reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission and the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement officers, state and local law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland Department of Health
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $55,300 in fiscal 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to purchase 45 sets of protective body armor for its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit. Other state agencies and local governments are expected to implement the bill using existing resources. The bill includes provisions for withholding grant funds from law enforcement agencies that do not comply with armor replacement or reporting mandates, which could result in an indeterminate impact on grant disbursements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary agency responsible for the bill's enforcement mechanism. It is tasked with withholding grant funds from law enforcement agencies that fail to comply with body armor replacement and reporting requirements, and it manages the Protective Body Armor Fund.

The fiscal note identifies a direct general fund expenditure increase of $55,305 for the Maryland Department of Health in FY 2027 to purchase protective body armor for its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit (STIU) to comply with the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which falls under this category of executive bodies, to receive notifications from non-compliant law enforcement agencies and subsequently notify GOCPP.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly subject to the bill's requirements for issuing, replacing, and reporting on protective body armor for its officers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is relevant as the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission is administratively housed within it. Additionally, the fiscal note mentions the agency's Division of Parole and Probation in relation to the Protective Body Armor Fund.
The Comptroller's Office employs sworn law enforcement officers who are subject to the bill's standards and reporting requirements regarding protective body armor.
The Department of Natural Resources employs the Natural Resources Police, who are subject to the bill's requirements for protective body armor issuance and replacement.
MDOT oversees several modal administrations with law enforcement units (such as the Maryland Transit Administration Police) that must comply with the bill's body armor standards.
The MDTA maintains its own police force, which is subject to the bill's requirements for protective body armor and the associated reporting mandates.
The university's campus police department is a law enforcement agency affected by the bill's requirements for issuing and replacing protective body armor.
The USM includes several institutions with campus police departments that are subject to the bill's standards for protective body armor and the risk of grant withholding for non-compliance.
The Maryland Department of Labor employs sworn personnel who are subject to the bill's requirements for protective body armor.
As the successor to the cannabis regulatory and enforcement duties mentioned in the fiscal note, the MCA employs enforcement personnel subject to the bill's body armor requirements.
DBM is relevant due to its oversight of state personnel and the fiscal impact on the Department of Health, as well as its role in supervising the execution of state budgets involving grant funds.

The OAG may be required to provide legal counsel to GOCPP and other state agencies regarding the implementation of the grant-withholding enforcement provisions and compliance with the Public Safety Article.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments involved in this bill and the Governor is responsible for signing the legislation into law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulation of various industries, including the horse racing industry via the State Racing Commission. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor appoint five members to the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners (an increase from three) and defines the Governor's authority and procedures for removing members for misconduct or incompetence.

As the unit within the Governor's Office tasked with recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards, this office will lead the administrative effort to expand the board from three to five members.

Annual expenditures for grants are expected to continue at $88,000 thereafter. There may be a minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor due to licensing fees paid by grant recipients.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the primary agency responsible for establishing and administering the PAREA Grant Program as mandated by the bill.
This agency is the primary implementing body responsible for administering the new PAREA Grant Program and managing the associated state funding.
The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers and will be responsible for licensing grant recipients, resulting in a fiscal impact on special fund revenues.
The bill aligns with the agency's mission to address redlining and appraisal gaps, similar to their existing Appraisal Gap from Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program.
The agency is responsible for overseeing the fiscal implementation, budget execution, and potential personnel resources for the new grant program.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Higher Education Commission for the development of the program's regulations and implementation.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates high-level policy initiatives related to economic equity and addressing the impacts of redlining.
The bill aims to diversify the appraisal profession, which aligns with the board's mission to set the statewide vision for workforce development and economic goals.
The university was consulted as a stakeholder for the fiscal note and is a key educational partner for students from underrepresented communities targeted by this grant.
The system was consulted for information regarding the bill's fiscal impact and provides educational programs that align with the appraisal field.
The college was consulted as a stakeholder for the fiscal note regarding the creation of the new grant program within the state's education article.

bill_summary: This bill regulates the land application of sewage sludge containing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), specifically PFOA and PFOS. Starting October 1, 2028, it prohibits applying sewage sludge to agricultural or marginal land if PFAS concentrations are 50 parts per billion (ppb) or higher. Sludge with concentrations between 25 and 50 ppb is subject to strict management measures, source tracking studies, and mitigation plans. The bill also authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment and local authorities to establish pretreatment standards and fees for industrial users that discharge PFAS into wastewater systems.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Sewage sludge generators (wastewater treatment plants), industrial users discharging to wastewater systems, agricultural and marginal landowners, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $248,100 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to implement and oversee the program, with costs rising to $331,800 by FY 2031. Local government expenditures may increase significantly for jurisdictions whose wastewater treatment plants produce sludge exceeding PFAS thresholds; for example, the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission estimates annual management cost increases between $4,100,000 and $8,200,000. Local revenues may increase through the collection of new rates and fees from industrial users.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. It is tasked with adopting regulations, establishing monitoring protocols for PFAS, reviewing and approving source tracking studies and mitigation plans from sewage sludge generators, and establishing pretreatment standards for industrial users.

The bill explicitly includes the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) in the definition of a 'sewage sludge generator.' MES operates approximately 90 wastewater treatment plants and will be directly impacted by the new testing, monitoring, and reporting requirements, as well as potential mitigation costs.

The bill mandates that MDE cannot adopt regulations regarding the land application of sewage sludge without the approval of the Department of Agriculture. Additionally, MDA provides recommendations for nutrient requirements on agricultural land where sludge is applied.

The fiscal note indicates that MDE will require three additional positions (one regulatory engineer and two natural resource planners) to implement the bill. DBM is responsible for managing state personnel resources and budget execution for these additions.

The bill may have a meaningful impact on small businesses and industrial users who discharge into wastewater systems, as they may face new pretreatment standards, mitigation costs, and increased rates or fees. The Department of Commerce is the primary agency for business retention and economic development.

The OAH provides an impartial hearing process for contested cases. If MDE determines a sewage sludge generator is out of compliance with an approved mitigation plan and prohibits land application, the generator may appeal the decision through OAH.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE and MDA during the regulatory process and represents the state in civil or criminal enforcement actions related to violations of the new sewage sludge and PFAS standards.

The BPW oversees significant state expenditures and procurement contracts. Any major infrastructure projects or large-scale consulting contracts initiated by MDE or MES to address PFAS mitigation may require BPW approval.
The Comptroller manages the collection of state revenues, including the annual generator fees paid by sewage sludge generators into the Maryland Clean Water Fund.

The bill was assigned to the Health Committee in the House. MDH regulates health care facilities and professionals and has a vested interest in public health outcomes related to PFAS contamination in the environment.
The bill requires MDE to consider the nearness of land application sites to sensitive areas such as wetlands and flood plains, which are under the conservation and management purview of DNR.

The bill requires MDE to consider the character of nearby planned land uses and transport routes when adopting regulations for land application, which falls under MDP's land use planning responsibilities.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the primary implementing agencies (MDE and MDA), and the Governor must sign the bill into law and propose the budget for its implementation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services to agricultural and seafood industries. Farmers impacted by restrictions on sewage sludge application or those needing to implement new soil management practices may seek assistance through MARBIDCO's programs.
The Treasurer acts as the custodian of state funds and manages the investment of revenues collected in state funds, including those used for environmental programs.
As an urban research institution, MSU may be an industrial user of a wastewater system or participate in research related to the environmental and public health impacts of PFAS.

OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive branch agencies; it will likely review MDE's management and enforcement of the new PFAS regulatory framework in future audit cycles.

The RMC advocates for the interests of rural counties. Since the land application of sewage sludge occurs primarily on agricultural and marginal lands in rural areas, the council has a stake in the bill's implementation.
As a state agency and educational institution, the college may be classified as an industrial user discharging into a public wastewater system subject to new pretreatment standards or fees.

This multi-agency initiative promotes sustainable development and environmental protection. The regulation of PFAS in biosolids aligns with the initiative's goals of protecting the Chesapeake Bay and preserving agricultural resources.
USM institutions may be impacted as industrial users of wastewater systems or as research partners providing data on PFAS mitigation and environmental impacts.
