bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to establish multidisciplinary local suicide fatality review teams. These teams are tasked with reviewing suicide deaths to identify systemic risk factors, improving coordination among prevention and crisis response entities, and developing recommendations to prevent future suicides. The bill also establishes protocols for membership, data confidentiality, and immunity from liability for team members.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and local health departments
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local health officers, law enforcement, behavioral health professionals, social service agencies, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) may increase by approximately $163,289 starting in fiscal 2027 for a data analyst and program administrator, though the Department of Legislative Services suggests these costs might be absorbed within existing resources. Local health department expenditures are estimated to increase by $30,000 to $50,000 for each jurisdiction that chooses to establish a team. Penalty provisions for confidentiality violations are not expected to materially affect finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary state agency for health policy and oversees local health departments and behavioral health authorities, both of which are mandated members of the local review teams. Additionally, the department is authorized to adopt regulations to carry out the subtitle.

The bill requires local departments of social services, which are part of DHS, to be represented on the suicide fatality review teams. The agency also coordinates child fatality review teams mentioned in the bill.
The bill requires local superintendents of schools to be represented on the local review teams, and the Department of Education oversees these local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local teams to coordinate with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee, which is a state-level committee tasked with identifying suicide trends and prevention strategies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Emergency medical services providers are designated members of the local suicide fatality review teams. MIEMSS is the state agency responsible for overseeing and regulating the EMS network.
State law enforcement officers are listed as potential members of the multidisciplinary local teams. The Maryland State Police is the primary state-level law enforcement agency.
The bill contains significant legal provisions regarding confidentiality, Open Meetings Act exemptions, and immunity from liability, requiring legal counsel and interpretation from the OAG.

The bill establishes rules regarding the use of records as evidence, subpoenas, and discovery in judicial proceedings, as well as providing immunity from liability for team members, which impacts the court system.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for assessing the fiscal impact of the bill on state agencies, including the Maryland Department of Health's potential need for additional resources.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved in these review teams and coordinates the policy initiatives related to public health and suicide prevention.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for developmental disabilities services to individuals who received certain services in another state and relocated to the State; and requiring the Department to begin the determination process before an individual establishes residency in the State under certain circumstances.
Title: Developmental Disabilities Services - Expedited Eligibility Determinations for Recently Relocated Individuals (Ralph's Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Home Care Services -see also- Respite Care
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: Known as Ralph's Act, this bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for developmental disabilities services to individuals who move to Maryland after receiving similar services in another state for at least 10 years. To qualify, the individual must be a dependent of an immediate family member who has lived in Maryland for at least two years and moved because their caretaker died or became incapacitated. The department must complete the determination within 60 business days and may begin the process before the individual has established residency in the State.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities relocating to Maryland and their immediate family members who are Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can likely handle the bill's requirements using existing resources, as the number of eligible individuals is expected to be very limited. However, if application volume increases significantly, an additional position costing approximately $80,000 annually (shared between general and federal funds) might be required. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), the Department is tasked with establishing and implementing the expedited Medicaid eligibility determination process and providing services to individuals who meet the new criteria.

This agency is the principal state entity for coordinating services for residents with disabilities and works with other departments to ensure inclusive services, making the streamlining of eligibility for disabled residents highly relevant to its mission.

The Exchange administers the state's health insurance marketplace and determines eligibility for Medicaid; since the bill requires an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for these specific services, coordination with the Exchange's systems and protocols may be necessary.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies including the Department of Health; any appeals or disputes regarding the new expedited eligibility determinations or service priority assignments would likely be heard by this office.

The fiscal note indicates potential administrative burdens and staffing needs at MDH to manage the expedited process, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget, personnel, and fiscal planning.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDH and would likely be involved in ensuring the new expedited process complies with federal Medicaid waiver requirements and assisting with any necessary CMS approvals mentioned in the fiscal note.

This office focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and families, particularly those in vulnerable situations; the bill specifically addresses families where a caretaker has died or become incapacitated, requiring support for their dependents.

The bill mandates a specific timeline for eligibility determinations (60 business days), making the tracking and oversight of this new performance metric relevant to GOPI's mission of enhancing government responsiveness.

The team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and address child poverty; the bill's focus on helping vulnerable relocated families access services aligns with the team's multidisciplinary mission.

Military families relocate frequently, and the provisions for expedited eligibility for dependents of residents relocating to Maryland may impact military families moving into the state who have dependents with developmental disabilities.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy coordination; the bill is presented for the Governor's approval and involves significant policy changes regarding the prioritization of state services.

The Department of Aging supports caregivers and older adults; the bill addresses situations where a caretaker's death or incapacitation (often an aging parent or relative) necessitates a move, which intersects with the department's long-term care advocacy.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law establishing that certain noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in certain employment contracts are null and void as being against the public policy of the State to licensed architects employed by certain employers that relocate the majority of its employees outside the State or have its principal place of business outside the State.
Title: Noncompete and Conflict of Interest Clauses - Licensed Architects - Employer Workforce Relocation and Out-of-State Employers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The bill establishes that noncompete and conflict of interest clauses in employment contracts for licensed architects are null and void if the employer relocates its principal place of business outside of Maryland or if the majority of its employees no longer work from Maryland-based sites. This rule applies to employers who had more than 30 Maryland-based employees at the time the architect was hired and targets contracts executed on or after the bill's effective date.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Licensed architects and architectural firms or other employers with more than 30 employees that relocate their operations outside of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. There is a potential meaningful impact on small businesses (those with 30 to 50 employees) that relocate their headquarters or the majority of their workforce outside of Maryland, as they will be prohibited from enforcing existing noncompete provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article and falls under the jurisdiction of the Maryland Department of Labor. Additionally, the department oversees the Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing, which is responsible for the 'licensed architects' specifically mentioned and protected by the bill's provisions.

The bill defines legal standards for 'judicial enforcement' and declares certain contract provisions 'null and void as being against the public policy of the State.' This directly impacts how state courts adjudicate employment contract disputes and noncompete enforcement actions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and represents the state in matters concerning the enforcement of labor laws and public policy. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal implications of these new contract restrictions.

The bill specifically addresses employers that relocate their principal place of business or the majority of their workforce outside of Maryland. As the state's primary economic development agency, this policy regarding business relocation and the retention of skilled professionals (architects) is relevant to their mission.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State or a unit of local government from approving the construction or operation of a building, structure, or other real property for use as a detention facility by a private entity; establishing that a building, structure, or other real property is considered proposed for use as a detention facility, regardless of how the use is descried in an application or permit request under certain circumstances; establishing a certain penalty; authorizing the Attorney General to bring a civil action to enforce the Act; etc.
Title: Correctional Services - Private Detention Facilities - Zoning Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This emergency bill prohibits the State and local governments from approving the use of any building or property as a detention facility, including immigration detention facilities, by a private entity. It authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions to enforce the prohibition and establishes a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per day for each violation. The bill also includes contingent provisions that would impose strict zoning and public notice requirements for private detention facilities if the absolute prohibition is ever ruled unenforceable by a court.
responsible_party: Maryland Attorney General, State government, and units of local government
stakeholders: Private entities operating detention facilities, individuals detained for civil or criminal violations, and State and local government units involved in zoning and corrections.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It establishes a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per day for violations, which would provide indeterminate revenue to the State only in the event of noncompliance by private entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions to enforce the prohibition against private detention facilities and to seek temporary or permanent injunctive relief.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Correctional Services Article, which is the primary regulatory domain of the department, and establishes new standards for what constitutes a detention facility in Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, this office is relevant to the bill's policy shift regarding the management and privatization of detention facilities.
The bill authorizes the Judiciary to hear civil actions brought by the Attorney General and to issue injunctions and civil penalties of up to $10,000 per day.

Section 2 of the bill introduces specific land use and zoning requirements for private detention facilities, areas where the Department of Planning provides technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments.

The bill provides specific exclusions for health care facilities licensed by the Department of Health, requiring the agency to ensure its licensed facilities are not misclassified under the new detention facility criteria.

The bill provides specific exclusions for residential child care programs and child placement agencies licensed by the Department of Human Services, requiring coordination to ensure these programs are not affected by the detention facility prohibition.

The department manages and supervises youth in detention; the bill's restrictions on private detention facilities intersect with the department's oversight of residential facilities and rehabilitative services.
As the agency responsible for state real estate management and facilities, DGS is impacted by the prohibition on the state approving the use of real property for private detention facilities.

The Board oversees significant state contracts and the transfer or lease of state property, which is directly relevant to the bill's prohibition on the state approving real property for use as a private detention facility.
The State Police were identified as a contributing agency in the fiscal note and may be involved in issues regarding involuntary custody and the secure confinement features described in the bill.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising the fiscal impacts of the bill, including the collection of any civil penalties generated by violations.

Synopsis: Repealing the option for an applicant for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services to pass a practical and written examination administered by the State Board of Cosmetology in order to be licensed; etc.
Title: State Board of Cosmetologists - Licensing - Eyelash Extensions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill repeals the option for an applicant for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services to qualify for the license by passing a practical and written examination without completing specific training. Applicants must now meet alternative requirements, which include either serving as a registered apprentice for at least three months or successfully completing 100 hours of instruction in an approved cosmetology school, in addition to passing the board-administered examination.
responsible_party: State Board of Cosmetologists
stakeholders: Applicants for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services, registered apprentices, and approved cosmetology schools in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the State Board of Cosmetologists can implement the licensing changes with existing resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact. Small businesses are expected to experience a minimal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various professions, including the State Board of Cosmetologists, which is the primary body responsible for implementing the licensing changes for eyelash extension services mandated by this bill.

The bill explicitly mentions that the instruction required for an eyelash extension license must be completed in a cosmetology school approved by the State Department of Education. By removing the examination-only path, this agency's role in approving and overseeing these educational programs becomes a mandatory part of the licensing process.

The bill specifies that the required instruction for eyelash extension services can be completed in schools approved by the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The removal of the exam-only qualification option makes the commission's oversight of these vocational training programs more central to the licensing requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Cosmetologists. They would be responsible for advising the board on the regulatory updates and legal implications of changing license qualification requirements.

Synopsis: Authorizing a merchant to round the portion of the price of a certain  transaction for which a customer pays using cash in a certain manner or round the amount of change due to a customer in a certain manner; providing that certain provisions of the Act shall preempt existing regulations, rules, and ordinances that conflict with certain provisions of the Act; and altering the definition of "taxable price" for certain purposes to clarify the exclusion from tax of a certain amount collected due to rounding the price.
Title: Business Regulation - Rounding Cash Transactions - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes merchants to round the final price of cash-based transactions to the nearest five-cent increment. Transactions ending in 1, 2, 6, or 7 cents are rounded down, while those ending in 3, 4, 8, or 9 cents are rounded up; transactions totaling less than 5 cents may be rounded up to 5 cents. The bill also adjusts the state tax code to ensure that these rounded amounts are excluded from the 'taxable price' used to calculate sales and use tax.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Merchants engaged in the sale of goods or services and customers who pay for transactions using cash.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances. The Maryland Department of Labor is expected to handle any increase in compliance monitoring or wage payment claims using existing resources. While the definition of 'taxable price' is modified to exclude rounding adjustments from the State sales and use tax, the overall fiscal impact is described as minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Tax - General Article to alter the definition of 'taxable price' for State sales and use tax purposes, excluding amounts added or subtracted during rounding. As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing and enforcing these tax laws.

The bill adds a new subtitle to the Business Regulation Article and explicitly authorizes the Secretary of Labor to adopt regulations to carry out the provisions related to rounding cash transactions in trade or business.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Comptroller regarding the implementation of new laws and represents the state in matters related to business regulation and tax law enforcement.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies implementing this law (Labor and Comptroller) and the Governor was responsible for signing the legislation into law.
The bill establishes new regulations for how merchants in Maryland handle cash transactions, which affects the general business and economic environment overseen by the Department of Commerce.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Office of the State Prosecutor to investigate a threat made against a judge or judge-elect.
Title: Office of the State Prosecutor - Investigation of Threats - Judges

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Prosecutor to investigate threats made against a judge or a judge-elect, adding these violations to the list of specific criminal offenses the office is empowered to investigate.
responsible_party: Office of the State Prosecutor
stakeholders: Maryland judges, judge-elects, and the Office of the State Prosecutor
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect the workload of the State Prosecutor or otherwise impact State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the investigatory jurisdiction of the Office of the State Prosecutor, authorizing them to investigate criminal threats made against judges or judge-elects.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Judicial Branch; this bill specifically protects the personnel of the judiciary (judges) and was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference.

The Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and is one of the specific entities authorized by the bill's section of the Criminal Procedure Article to request that the State Prosecutor initiate an investigation.
The Governor is authorized by statute to request that the State Prosecutor investigate offenses within their jurisdiction, which would now include threats against judges.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state responsible for criminal investigations, the Maryland State Police are impacted by the authorization of an alternative body (the State Prosecutor) to investigate specific criminal threats.

The State Ethics Commission is specifically listed in the amended section of the Criminal Procedure Article as an entity that can request the State Prosecutor to investigate an alleged offense under the expanded jurisdiction.

bill_summary: House Bill 1047 requires individuals to register as limited X-ray machine operators with the Maryland Board of Physicians to perform specific X-ray procedures. It establishes educational and clinical training requirements, examination standards, and disciplinary procedures for these registrants. The bill also specifies conditions under which physician assistants may perform X-ray duties and recodifies existing laws regarding the delegation of duties to cardiovascular invasive specialists and supervised medical graduates.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Limited X-ray machine operators, physician assistants, physicians, radiographers, supervised medical graduates, and healthcare facilities including hospitals and physician offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Board of Physicians can implement the registration and oversight requirements using existing resources. While the bill authorizes the collection of registration and renewal fees and allows for civil penalties (up to $5,000 for hospitals/offices and $1,000 for individuals), these are not expected to have a material impact on State revenues. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly impacts the Maryland Department of Health as it expands the regulatory authority of the State Board of Physicians, which is housed within the department. It requires the department's Secretary to make final decisions on joint regulations if boards cannot agree and oversees the new registration and disciplinary framework for limited X-ray machine operators.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Board of Physicians. The bill specifically mandates that the OAG file certified docket entries with the Board in cases of criminal convictions to trigger mandatory registration suspensions or revocations.

The bill establishes a disciplinary process for limited X-ray machine operators that includes the right to a hearing. The OAH is the agency responsible for conducting these administrative hearings for contested cases involving regulatory enforcement by the Board of Physicians.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its agencies, including the Department of Health. The Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the administration of the boards that implement these regulations.

The bill establishes registration and renewal fees as well as civil penalties. The fiscal note indicates that these fines are paid into the State's general fund, which the Comptroller's office manages as the state's principal tax and revenue collector.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the budget execution for the Board of Physicians. While the fiscal note suggests MBP can handle the bill's requirements within existing resources, DBM maintains oversight of the personnel and budgetary shifts related to the new registration program.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in selecting and vetting members for the State Board of Physicians, which is the primary body tasked with adopting regulations and adjudicating the new registration categories created by the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing a majority of the board of a surviving credit union to approve a proposed merger without the affirmative vote of a majority of the members of the surviving credit union, subject to certain requirements.
Title: Credit Unions - Mergers and Consolidations - Alteration of Voting Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the voting requirements for credit union mergers by allowing the board of a surviving credit union to approve a merger without a mandatory vote from its members. Under the bill, while a vote by the members of the surviving credit union becomes optional, the members of the merging credit union (the entity being absorbed) must still provide an affirmative majority vote to approve the merger.
responsible_party: Commissioner of the Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Maryland credit unions, their boards of directors, and credit union members.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, is the primary regulator for state-chartered financial institutions. This bill directly amends procedures for credit union mergers and consolidations, specifically regarding membership voting requirements and the oversight authority of the Commissioner.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, assisting in the interpretation and enforcement of the Financial Institutions Article as modified by this bill.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Labor and is responsible for signing this legislation into law.

Synopsis: Altering the composition of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf from 19 members to 13 members and requiring that at least 7 members be deaf.
Title: Maryland School for the Deaf - Membership of Board of Trustees - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill reduces the number of members on the Board of Trustees for the Maryland School for the Deaf from 19 to 13 and increases the minimum number of deaf members required on the board from six to seven. It also establishes a process for phasing out six board positions as current terms expire.
responsible_party: The Governor and the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf
stakeholders: Current and future members of the Maryland School for the Deaf Board of Trustees and the Maryland deaf community.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Maryland School for the Deaf are expected to decrease minimally due to reduced meal costs for quarterly board meetings resulting from the smaller board size. No specific dollar estimates are available as the decrease is expected to be minimal. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition and size of the Maryland School for the Deaf's Board of Trustees, which is the agency's governing body. The school will also experience a minimal fiscal impact due to decreased meal costs for fewer board members.
The Governor is the appointing authority for the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf and is responsible for prioritizing the appointment of deaf members as mandated by the bill.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for the Board of Trustees and will be responsible for managing the transitions and specific membership requirements defined in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for the welfare of deaf residents and ensures state programs are inclusive; the bill's focus on increasing deaf representation on the governing board of the state's school for the deaf is highly relevant to its mission.

Synopsis: Authorizing a circuit court to authorize or direct a transaction that grants access to financial records or establishes eligibility for government assistance programs for a minor or disabled person under a certain circumstance.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Jurisdiction Over Property of Minors or Disabled Persons - Authorized Transactions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill expands the list of transactions a circuit court may authorize or direct regarding the property, service, or care of a minor or disabled person without appointing a guardian. Specifically, it allows the court to authorize transactions that grant access to financial records or establish eligibility for government assistance programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Circuit Courts
stakeholders: Minors and disabled persons in Maryland, their families or representatives, and the Maryland Judiciary.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. The changes align the Estates and Trusts Article with Maryland Rule 10-304.2, which is scheduled to take effect in July 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch by authorizing circuit courts to direct specific financial and eligibility transactions for minors or disabled persons without the appointment of a guardian. The AOC provides central support and implements policies for the state's courts.

The bill allows courts to establish eligibility for government assistance programs, specifically mentioning Medical Assistance (Medicaid) in the fiscal note, which is administered by the Department of Health.

As the primary provider of social services like SNAP and cash assistance, DHS is impacted by court-authorized transactions that establish eligibility for the government assistance programs they manage for minors and vulnerable adults.

The bill provides a less restrictive legal alternative to guardianship for disabled persons to access financial records and government benefits, which directly aligns with the department's mission to improve service delivery and community living for individuals with disabilities.

The department serves older adults and people with disabilities who may require court intervention to access records or establish program eligibility. This bill streamlines that process for the population the agency serves.
The office focuses on child well-being and reducing poverty; the bill's provisions for establishing eligibility for assistance programs for minors support these policy goals.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and state agencies, including those administering the assistance programs for which eligibility would be established under this bill.
This agency assists veterans, many of whom are disabled persons, in securing state and federal benefits. The bill provides a legal mechanism to help establish such eligibility through the courts.

The Governor’s Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including those related to the welfare of minors and disabled persons and the administration of state assistance programs.

While the bill focuses on the Circuit Court, the Register of Wills manages administrative probate and records related to decedents' estates and some guardianship matters, which are in the same legal field as the property of minors and disabled persons.

Synopsis: Providing that the Department of Natural Resources may authorize the reduction of the deer population on certain property with deer damage using certain methods; altering the time restrictions for Sunday deer hunting in certain counties during deer firearms season; repealing certain time restrictions that apply to the hunting of game birds and mammals on certain Sundays on private property in Wicomico County; authorizing the Department to allow a person to hunt deer on each Sunday of the deer bow hunting season in Baltimore City; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Hunting - Management

bill_summary: The bill authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to permit deer population reductions on properties of at least 10 acres with documented deer damage, including the issuance of permits for Sunday shooting in most areas. It expands Sunday hunting hours in Kent, Talbot, and Wicomico counties and allows Sunday deer bow hunting in Baltimore City. Additionally, from July 2027 through June 2030, the bill shifts the authority to manage Sunday hunting schedules from the General Assembly to DNR regulations, requiring the department to maintain existing hunting levels and report on management effectiveness and safety.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters, farmers and landowners experiencing deer damage, outdoor recreationists (hikers, bikers, equestrians), and residents of Baltimore City and various Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances, and the Department of Natural Resources can implement its requirements using existing resources. There is a potential meaningful positive economic impact on small businesses, specifically for farms through reduced crop damage and for businesses related to hunting equipment, food, and lodging due to expanded hunting opportunities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the DNR is responsible for documenting deer damage, issuing hunting permits, mapping affected areas, and adopting new statewide hunting regulations. The bill also requires the DNR to report annually on deer management and hunter safety.

The bill defines 'deer damage' to include the destruction of agricultural crops. The DNR's expanded authority to manage deer populations directly supports the Department of Agriculture's mission to promote the economic viability of farming and protect agricultural interests.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies like the DNR and manages intergovernmental relations. The bill establishes a process for local governments to request changes to hunting regulations via letters from county executives and local delegations, which involves the office's coordination functions.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new regulations the DNR is mandated to adopt under the bill, as well as providing guidance on the permitting processes.

The fiscal note indicates that managing the deer population may lead to a reduction in deer-vehicle collisions, which is relevant to the Department's oversight of highway safety and the State Highway Administration's management of roadway safety.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations that consider certain best management practices for stormwater management for agritourism; requiring Montgomery County and the Montgomery Soil Conservation District, in consultation with the Department, to review certain processes for reviewing and approving certain stormwater management plans and submit their findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2026; etc.
Title: Environment - Stormwater Management for Agritourism

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations defining 'agritourism' and to consider specific best management practices for stormwater management on land used for agritourism, including standard plans for temporary parking and the use of pasture or cropland for runoff treatment. It also mandates that Montgomery County and the Montgomery Soil Conservation District review and report on their local processes for approving agritourism stormwater management plans by the end of 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Farmers and agricultural operators engaged in agritourism, Montgomery County government, local soil conservation districts, and small business owners in the agricultural sector.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Legislative Services indicates that the bill's requirements can be managed within existing budgeted resources at both the state and local levels, resulting in no impact on revenues. Small business agricultural operations may benefit from more tailored and flexible stormwater management regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for adopting the regulations mandated by the bill and updating the Maryland Stormwater Design Manual to include agritourism-specific best management practices.

The bill requires MDE to consult with the Department of Agriculture to define 'agritourism' and involves stormwater management practices on agricultural land, which falls under MDA's mission to support the economic viability of farming and oversee soil conservation programs.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies (MDE and MDA) tasked with implementation and is the direct recipient of the report from Montgomery County regarding its stormwater management review.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE and MDA and would be responsible for reviewing the new regulations and model ordinances for legal sufficiency.
As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce is interested in agritourism as a growth sector for Maryland's economy and its role in promoting the state's assets.
Agritourism is a key component of Maryland's tourism strategy; regulatory changes impact the viability of these attractions which are promoted by this office within the Department of Commerce.
The Council advocates for the economic development and interests of rural counties, where agritourism is a critical industry impacted by environmental regulations on agricultural land.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial support to enhance the profitability of agricultural businesses; regulatory changes that tailor compliance costs for agritourism directly support its mission of ensuring industry sustainability.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable development and protecting the Chesapeake Bay while preserving farmland, which are core themes of the bill's focus on agricultural stormwater management.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility under the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include students attending the University of Maryland Eastern Shore and enrolled in certain degree programs.
Title: Higher Education - Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program - Eligible Institutions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include students enrolled at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore in specific graduate programs, including Master of Medical Science in Physician Assistant Studies, Doctor of Pharmacy, Doctor of Physical Therapy, and Doctor of Veterinary Medicine.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Graduate and professional students at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore, the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and other institutions of higher education participating in the scholarship program.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not require additional State spending as program funding is provided through the annual State budget; the fiscal 2027 budget includes $1,200,000 for the program. Expanding eligibility will result in a redistribution of existing funds, potentially decreasing allocations to other currently eligible institutions. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Commission to establish and administer the Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program, allocate grants to eligible institutions, establish guidelines, and adopt necessary regulations for implementation.

The bill specifically adds the University of Maryland Eastern Shore (UMES), a member institution of the University System of Maryland, as an eligible institution for several professional degree programs under the scholarship program.

The bill specifies that funds for the scholarship program shall be as provided in the State budget, which is developed and supervised by DBM. The fiscal note also discusses program funding levels within the State budget.

The Governor's Office is responsible for proposing the annual state budget which includes funding for this scholarship program and oversees the executive branch agencies (MHEC) implementing the changes.

Synopsis: Requiring each public senior higher education institution and community college to submit a report on contraception access to the Maryland Higher Education Commission each year; requiring the Commission to submit a report on contraception access to the General Assembly each year beginning October 1, 2026; and requiring each community college to provide students with access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception.
Title: Higher Education Institutions - Over-the-Counter Contraception - Access and Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland's public four-year universities and community colleges to provide students with access to all methods of over-the-counter (OTC) contraception. It mandates that these institutions submit annual reports to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) detailing how access is provided, the types and amounts of contraception available, and student consultation efforts. MHEC must then compile and submit a summary report to the General Assembly each year.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students attending Maryland public senior higher education institutions and community colleges
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local higher education expenditures and revenues are expected to increase at least minimally as community colleges expand their over-the-counter contraception offerings. Additional costs may arise from purchasing contraception supplies, installing vending machines, or increasing staffing, which may be partially offset by student fees. While most institutions and MHEC are expected to manage the new reporting requirements with existing resources, some institutions without existing health centers may face administrative challenges in tracking the specified data.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the central body responsible for collecting annual contraception access reports from all public senior higher education institutions and community colleges, providing the necessary reporting forms, and submitting a consolidated annual report to the General Assembly.

As a defined public senior higher education institution, the system's constituent institutions are directly mandated to provide access to all over-the-counter contraception methods and submit detailed annual reports regarding their provision and student consultation to the Commission.

Morgan State University is explicitly identified as a public senior higher education institution required to provide on-campus access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception and comply with new annual reporting requirements regarding its provision.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly identified as a public senior higher education institution required to provide on-campus access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception and comply with new annual reporting requirements regarding its provision.

The Department is authorized to provide assistance to institutions in developing reproductive health plans and to offer expertise in collaborating with organizations for provide contraception access via vending machines.

DBM is relevant due to the fiscal impact on state-supported higher education institutions and the potential administrative resource needs of the Higher Education Commission for managing the new data collection and reporting mandates.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies tasked with implementation and has final approval authority over the legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service in the Maryland Transit Administration as a governing body with certain authority over the provision of Baltimore Core Transit Service; establishing the Commuter Services Advisory Board to provide certain oversight over and guidance for certain Administration commuter rail and bus services in the State; repealing the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission as an advisory commission for transit in the Baltimore City region; etc.
Title: Maryland Transit Administration Reform Act

bill_summary: This bill restructures the oversight of the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) by replacing the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission with two new bodies: the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board. It mandates specific staffing levels for these boards, including Deputy Administrators and analysts, and transfers authority to determine qualifications and compensation for certain MTA management positions to the Maryland Transportation Commission. Additionally, the bill requires a technical study to be conducted on the potential creation of a statewide rail authority.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration and Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Transit riders in the Baltimore metropolitan area, MARC and commuter bus passengers, MTA employees, labor unions, and residents of Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, known Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures increase by a net of 319,456 in FY 2027, with subsequent annual net increases ranging from 210,500 to 310,100 through FY 2031. These estimates reflect the cost of five new staff positions and a 100,000 one-time study fee, offset by approximately 500,000 in annual savings from the repeal of the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission. Additional indeterminate expenditures, potentially totaling several hundred thousand dollars annually, may result from management salary adjustments determined by the Maryland Transportation Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor has significant appointment power under the bill, including appointing five members and the chair of the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service, as well as the chair and members of the Commuter Services Advisory Board.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is required to review proposed salary adjustments for specific MTA management positions to determine if they pose an adverse impact on special fund expenditures. DBM also manages state personnel resources and benefits.

MDOT is the parent agency of the MTA. The bill reforms MDOT's transit operations, requires the Secretary to serve on the new boards, and mandates that MDOT contract for a technical study on a potential rail authority.

This bill is the primary reform act for the MTA, establishing two new oversight boards, requiring new staffing (Deputy Administrators and analysts), and changing how management personnel are appointed and compensated.
As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of the new boards, their bylaws, and the modified personnel rules for MTA management.

The bill specifies that management personnel appointed under the new Maryland Transportation Commission guidelines are state employees entitled to participate in the State Retirement and Pension System.
The Office of Appointments will be responsible for recruiting and vetting the various individuals the Governor must appoint to the two new boards established by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes two new oversight and advisory bodies: the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board.
The bill requires the new boards to establish conflict of interest standards consistent with the Maryland Public Ethics Law, which is administered and enforced by this commission.

OLA is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies and will likely review the MTA's compliance with the new personnel and board staffing requirements mandated by this bill.

The bill requires that both the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board include a member who represents riders with accessibility challenges, which aligns with this department's mission.
The bill involves employees who are members of labor unions and references collective bargaining agreements, fall under the jurisdiction of the PERB for labor-management relations.

Synopsis: Requiring, by January 1, 2028, each health care facility that performs surgical procedures to adopt and implement policies that require the use of a smoke evacuation system during a surgical procedure that may generate surgical smoke.
Title: Health Care Facilities - Surgical Smoke - Smoke Evacuation Systems

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires health care facilities, including hospitals and ambulatory surgical facilities, to adopt and implement policies by January 1, 2028, that necessitate the use of smoke evacuation systems during surgical procedures likely to generate surgical smoke.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ)
stakeholders: Health care facilities, surgical staff (surgeons, nurses, anesthesiologists, and surgical technologists), and patients.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) can monitor compliance within its existing budgeted resources. The bill has no impact on State revenues or local government finances. While health care facilities will incur costs to implement smoke evacuation systems, the fiscal note indicates no small business effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires health care facilities, such as hospitals and ambulatory surgical facilities, to implement surgical smoke policies. The Maryland Department of Health, specifically the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), is responsible for regulating these facilities and ensuring compliance with state health and safety standards.

The bill addresses surgical smoke, which is a workplace health and safety hazard. The Department of Labor oversees workplace safety and labor laws (including the Maryland Occupational Safety and Health program), making them relevant to the enforcement of standards that protect surgical staff.

As the operator of major academic medical centers and affiliated hospitals that perform surgical procedures, the University System of Maryland must ensure its facilities adopt and implement the required smoke evacuation policies.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and would assist in drafting regulations or defending enforcement actions related to the new surgical smoke evacuation requirements.

The OAH would be responsible for adjudicating any contested cases or appeals if a health care facility's license is challenged by the Department of Health for non-compliance with the bill's requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department operates correctional facilities that may include medical units or infirmaries where surgical procedures are performed. These facilities would need to comply with the bill's mandate to use smoke evacuation systems.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain insurers and dental plan organizations from prohibiting an assignment of benefits to a provider who is a dentist by an insured or refusing to directly reimburse a nonpreferred provider who is a dentist; requiring a nonpreferred provider who is a dentist and who seeks an assignment of benefits from an insured or enrollee to provide certain information to the insured or enrollee before performing a health care service and submit a disclosure form to document the assignment of benefits; etc.
Title: Health Insurance and Dental Plan Organizations - Dentists - Assignment of Benefits and Reimbursement of Nonpreferred Providers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurers and dental plan organizations to allow patients to assign their insurance benefits to a dentist, ensuring that the dentist is reimbursed directly by the insurance provider regardless of whether they are a preferred provider. Dentists who seek an assignment of benefits must provide patients with specific disclosures, including cost estimates and a notice of their nonpreferred status, before performing services.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Dentists, dental plan organizations, health insurance carriers, and dental patients
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill results in a minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration starting in FY 2027 due to $125 rate and form filing fees. Any additional workload for the agency can be managed within existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact, though small business dental practices may see a meaningful impact by gaining the ability to receive direct reimbursement through assignment of benefits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary implementing agency. The Insurance Commissioner is explicitly charged with developing the required disclosure forms for dentists and overseeing compliance by insurers and dental plan organizations. The agency will also collect form filing fees associated with the bill.

The bill regulates the conduct of dentists, who are licensed and regulated under Title 4 of the Health Occupations Article. The Department of Health oversees the boards that govern these medical professionals and their clinical practices.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal counsel for the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health. They would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new disclosure forms and defending any regulatory challenges to the new reimbursement rules.

As the administrator of Maryland's health insurance marketplace, the Exchange must ensure that dental plan organizations (DPOs) offering coverage through the marketplace comply with these new assignment of benefits and reimbursement requirements.

The Commission is responsible for health system planning and promoting transparency in health care costs. The bill's requirements for dentists to provide cost estimates and balance billing disclosures to patients align with the Commission's mission to improve informed decision-making.

The Office of Administrative Hearings may be required to adjudicate contested cases involving insurers or dental plan organizations that fail to comply with the reimbursement and assignment of benefits mandates established by the bill.
