bill_summary: This bill streamlines the credentialing process for health care providers joining insurance carrier panels by shortening notification deadlines, requiring the use of a centralized online credentialing system, and prohibiting carriers from charging application fees. It also requires carriers to maintain accurate provider directories, expands protections for essential community providers, and establishes civil penalties for carriers that fail to meet procedural timelines.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health care providers, health insurance carriers, health care facilities, and health insurance enrollees.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, any impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration can be handled with existing budgeted resources, and State revenues are not affected. The bill repeals the authorization for carriers to charge provider application fees and establishes civil penalties of 500 dollars per day for carriers that fail to meet specified notification deadlines, with penalties paid directly to the provider. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of the state's insurance market, the Maryland Insurance Administration is the lead agency responsible for implementing the bill. The Insurance Commissioner is tasked with adopting regulations for the online credentialing system, designating uniform credentialing forms, collecting vendor reports, and enforcing carrier compliance with notice and directory update requirements.

The bill's definition of 'carrier' includes Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), which are overseen by the Department of Health as part of the Medicaid program. Additionally, the bill provides specific credentialing protections and panel participation requirements for behavioral health providers, local health departments, and Federally Qualified Health Centers, all of which fall under the department's scope.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the Maryland Insurance Administration. The OAG would be involved in the drafting of new regulations required by the bill and would provide legal support for the enforcement of civil penalties against insurance carriers that fail to meet notice requirements.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange administers the state's insurance marketplace (Maryland Health Connection) and relies on the accuracy of provider directories. The bill's mandates for carriers to use the online credentialing system as the primary source for updates and to increase update frequency directly impact the quality of data provided to consumers on the Exchange.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for planning for health system needs and improving access to care. The bill's focus on streamlining provider credentialing and ensuring the accuracy of provider networks aligns with the Commission's mission to increase accountability and transparency in the healthcare system.

The bill explicitly includes school-based health centers in the list of providers that carriers are prohibited from limiting on their provider panels, which is relevant to the department's role in overseeing health services provided within the public school system.

The Office of Administrative Hearings may be required to adjudicate disputes if insurance carriers contest civil penalties or regulatory enforcement actions taken by the Maryland Insurance Administration under the provisions of this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing that insureds and any other persons covered by certain health insurance policies, contracts, or certificates are entitled to reimbursement for the services rendered by a graduate-level counseling, social work, or psychology clinical intern under certain circumstances; providing the services are reimbursable if provided at an outpatient health care facility by a graduate level counseling clinical, social work clinical, or psychology clinical intern under the direct supervision of a licensed practitioner; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Graduate-Level Clinical Interns - Required Reimbursement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance policies, contracts, and certificates to provide reimbursement for services rendered by graduate-level counseling, social work, and psychology clinical interns. To be eligible for reimbursement, the services must be provided at an outpatient health care facility, under the direct supervision of a specified licensed professional, and billed by the supervisor.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Graduate-level clinical interns in counseling, social work, and psychology; licensed clinical professional supervisors; health insurance carriers; outpatient health care facilities; and insured patients.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in fiscal 2027 due to $125 rate and form filing fees. There is no impact on local government finances. Small business behavioral health clinics may see a meaningful increase in revenue from reimbursements for services provided by clinical interns.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of health insurance in the state, the MIA is responsible for enforcing the reimbursement mandate and reviewing the resulting rate and form filings from insurers. The fiscal note explicitly mentions a minimal increase in MIA special fund revenues from these filings.

The bill directly involves the scope of practice and clinical supervision requirements for counselors, social workers, and psychologists, all of whom are licensed by boards under the Department of Health. The department was also a key information source for the fiscal note.
The bill's mandates apply to individual and group health insurance policies, which include plans offered and administered through the state's health insurance marketplace.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health, and will likely be involved in interpreting and defending the legal application of the new reimbursement requirements.

The commission oversees the standards and approval of the graduate programs in counseling, social work, and psychology that the clinical interns must be enrolled in to qualify for reimbursement under this bill.

The University System of Maryland includes several institutions that offer the graduate-level programs and clinical internship opportunities targeted by this legislation, directly impacting their students' clinical training and placement ecosystem.

As a state agency and public university with graduate programs in these fields, Morgan State's clinical interns and their associated outpatient training partners are affected by the new reimbursement structure.
As a public higher education institution, any of its students participating in relevant clinical graduate programs would be affected by the insurance reimbursement changes for their services.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Calvert County to grant a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on certain real property that was formerly used solely as a tobacco barn; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Calvert County - Property Tax Credit - Tobacco Barns

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Tobacco and Nicotine -see also- Cigarettes; Smk&Vap

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Calvert County government to grant a property tax credit for real property that was previously used exclusively as a tobacco barn. To be eligible for the credit, the property must be located on land that is either subject to a tobacco buyout agreement or qualifies for an agricultural use assessment and is used for an agricultural activity approved by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
responsible_party: Governing body of Calvert County
stakeholders: Owners of former tobacco barns in Calvert County that are situated on eligible agricultural land.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on state finances. Calvert County property tax revenues will decrease starting in fiscal 2027 if the local governing body chooses to grant the credit. A specific fiscal estimate is unavailable because the county lacks an inventory of eligible properties, and the county government has the discretion to determine the credit's amount and duration.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the agencies involved in state tax policy and agricultural support.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly, and would be responsible for interpreting the legal requirements of the new tax credit and representing the state in related litigation.

The bill focuses on properties formerly used for tobacco farming and land qualifying for agricultural use assessments, which falls under the department's mission to promote the economic viability of Maryland's agricultural industry.
The agency is involved in sustainable growth and land-use planning; property tax credits for agricultural land are a mechanism used to influence rural land preservation and development patterns.
The Tax Court is the final administrative body for adjudicating tax disputes, including appeals regarding property tax assessments and credits that have passed through the local appeals board.

This agency is specifically tasked with hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments and credits; it would be the primary body to resolve disputes if a taxpayer is denied the Calvert County tobacco barn credit.
The Council advocates for the interests of Maryland's rural counties, including Calvert County, and supports agricultural preservation and economic development within those regions.

Synopsis: Requiring the collector for each county to include in the written materials sent with each property tax bill a website address or quick-response code for a county government webpage that lists each property tax credit that is available to taxpayers in the county and includes an explanation of how to apply for the tax credits.
Title: Property Tax Credits - Notice Through Property Tax Bill

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires each county property tax collector to include a website address or quick-response (QR) code in the materials sent with property tax bills. This link must lead to a county government webpage that lists all available property tax credits and provides instructions on how to apply for them.
responsible_party: The collector for each county
stakeholders: Maryland property owners and taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no impact on State finances. Local county expenditures are not expected to be significantly affected by the requirement to include a website address or QR code on tax bills, and there is no direct impact on county revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board (PTAAB) is directly responsible for hearing disputes over various property tax credits. By requiring clearer notice of available credits on tax bills, this legislation is likely to increase taxpayer awareness and participation, which may subsequently impact the volume of appeals and inquiries handled by the 24 local boards.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from PTAAB decisions regarding property tax credits. Increased visibility of these credits could lead to an increase in the number of cases adjudicated by the Court if credits are denied or disputed.

The Department of Aging advocates for older adults, many of whom are eligible for specific property tax relief programs such as the Homeowners' Tax Credit. Improved notice through digital means like QR codes directly assists this agency's constituency in accessing financial support that improves their quality of life and housing security.

The Department of Disabilities works to ensure accessible housing and community living for individuals with disabilities. Several property tax credits are specifically designed for people with disabilities or disabled veterans, and this bill facilitates easier access to those benefits.

Many Maryland counties offer property tax credits specifically for veterans and their families. This agency is responsible for assisting veterans in securing state benefits, and improved notice of these credits on property tax bills aligns with their mission of advocacy and resource access.

The Innovation Team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and improve services for Maryland families. Using digital technology like QR codes to facilitate access to property tax credits is an example of the service-delivery improvements the team is designed to support.

The Governor's Office of Performance Improvement (GOPI) focuses on enhancing the responsiveness and efficiency of government operations. The bill's requirement to utilize data-driven and accessible communication methods (QR codes and centralized webpages) to deliver government services (tax credits) fits within GOPI's mandate.

As the state's principal tax official, the Comptroller has a general interest in the administration of tax laws and the distribution of information regarding tax credits, even though property taxes are primarily administered at the local level.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill aligns with the Governor's broader priorities regarding economic relief and modernized service delivery.

This office focuses on enhancing economic mobility and reducing poverty. Property tax credits serve as a significant financial relief tool for low-income families, contributing to the office's core mission.

Synopsis: Specifying that certain documentation may establish lawful authority to sell certain telecommunications equipment as junk or scrap metal; requiring certain junk dealers, scrap metal processors, and antique dealers to register and provide a description including certain information of purchased telecommunications equipment with a certain law enforcement official; prohibiting certain individuals from destroying telecommunications infrastructure in a certain manner; and providing certain penalties for violations of the Act.
Title: Telecommunications Infrastructure - Protections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the reckless or malicious defacement, damage, or destruction of telecommunications infrastructure and establishes these actions as a misdemeanor. It also expands the definition of junk or scrap metal to include telecommunications equipment and requires junk dealers and scrap metal processors to verify a seller's legal authority to sell such items through specific documentation, such as a bill of sale or a letter of authorization.
responsible_party: Junk dealers, scrap metal processors, and State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Telecommunications companies, junk dealers, scrap metal processors, law enforcement agencies, and individuals selling scrap metal
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It establishes a misdemeanor penalty for damaging infrastructure, which includes a fine of up to $500 and/or imprisonment for up to six months. Small business impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and has final approval authority over the bill. The legislation aligns with executive priorities regarding public safety and the protection of critical state infrastructure.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies implementing the bill, such as the Department of Labor and Maryland State Police, and represents the state in criminal appeals resulting from the new misdemeanor offense.
As the agency responsible for the state's telecommunications strategy and infrastructure, DoIT is a key stakeholder in the protection of broadband and fiber optic networks defined in the bill.

The Department of Labor is the primary regulator of junk dealers and scrap metal processors. The bill adds significant new identification, documentation, and record-keeping requirements for these businesses under the Business Regulation Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the state's correctional facilities and community supervision. The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense with potential imprisonment of up to six months, which falls under their oversight of justice-involved individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with the new misdemeanor for defacing or destroying telecommunications infrastructure.

The Judicial Branch, supported by the AOC, will process and adjudicate the new criminal cases and potential civil disputes arising from the expanded regulations on junk dealers and infrastructure protection.

The Maryland State Police is the primary law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing the state's criminal laws, investigating the destruction of infrastructure, and receiving transaction records from junk and scrap metal dealers.
The PSC regulates many of the telecommunications and utility companies whose infrastructure (such as telephone poles and small cell facilities) is specifically protected by the bill's new provisions.

Synopsis: Establishing a temporary to-go event permit in Worcester County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to issue a temporary to-go event permit to a holder of a Class B liquor license or a Class D license under certain circumstances; establishing a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license in the county; authorizing the Board to issue a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license to certain municipalities in the county; etc.
Title: Worcester County - Alcoholic Beverages - Temporary To-Go Event Permit and Class C Per Diem Municipal To-Go Beer, Wine, and Liquor License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill establishes a temporary to-go event permit and a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license in Worcester County. The license allows the towns of Berlin, Pocomoke City, and Snow Hill to designate special event areas for up to seven days, while the permit authorizes local Class B and Class D license holders to sell alcoholic beverages in approved to-go cups for consumption within those designated areas.
responsible_party: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Municipal governments of Berlin, Pocomoke City, and Snow Hill; Class B and Class D alcoholic beverage license holders in Worcester County; and residents and visitors of these municipalities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Worcester County revenues will increase starting in fiscal 2027 based on the issuance of new licenses and permits. The fee for the Class C per diem municipal to-go license is $45 per day, and the fee for the temporary to-go event permit is $20 per day. Total revenue increases cannot be reliably estimated as they depend on the number of applications. There is no impact on State finances, and local monitoring can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing legislation into law and overseeing the executive branch's enforcement of state laws. This bill requires the Governor's signature to take effect and impacts the regulatory duties of the executive branch regarding alcoholic beverages.

As the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the enforcement of tax laws and industry regulations. This bill establishes new license and permit types within the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which falls under the Comptroller's general regulatory and oversight scope.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel to state boards and commissions, including the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners, on the interpretation and enforcement of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

The bill creates 'special event areas' and to-go beverage permits in municipal centers of Worcester County, such as Berlin and Snow Hill. These measures are designed to enhance recreational attractions and promote tourism within the county's historic and commercial districts.

The Maryland State Police provide support to local law enforcement and ensure public peace across the state. This bill mandates the adoption of regulations regarding public safety and event security for special event areas where alcohol consumption is authorized, which may require coordination or support from the State Police during regional events.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain local detention center officers of Allegany County in the event Allegany County becomes a participating governmental unit in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System; and providing that certain local detention center officers who join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System and receive certain service credit shall no longer be members of the Employees' Pension System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Allegany County
bill_summary: This bill mandates that Allegany County detention center officers become members of the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System (CORS) if the county elects to participate in the system. It provides for the transfer of service credits from the Employees’ Pension System (EPS) to CORS and exempts transferring officers from paying the difference in member contribution rates for their prior service.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Allegany County detention center officers and the Allegany County government
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. For Allegany County, an actuarial analysis indicates that pension liabilities would increase by approximately $2.4 million. Net employer contributions are estimated to increase by approximately $165,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2028, reflecting the higher employer contribution rate for CORS compared to EPS, partially offset by a new entrant liability credit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The SRA is the primary agency responsible for the administration and management of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes both the Employees' Pension System and the Correctional Officers' Retirement System. This bill directly mandates the SRA to manage the transfer of membership and creditable service for Allegany County detention center officers into the state-administered CORS.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the State Retirement Agency. They would be responsible for the legal interpretation and implementation of the bill's specific provisions regarding the transfer of service credits and the exemption from standard pension transfer laws (Title 37).

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency for Maryland, DBM oversees the state's employee resources and benefits. While the fiscal impact of this bill is localized to Allegany County, the department maintains a general interest in the policy changes affecting the state-run pension systems and personnel classifications within CORS and EPS.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps; requiring the Department to notify each health officer for a county of a certain procurement to offer the opportunity for the county health department to join the procurement; requiring the Department of Legislative Services to develop a process to assess the health equity impacts of relevant legislation; requiring the Department to convene a workgroup to review local health department recruiting and classification processes; etc.
Title: Public Health Reform Act

bill_summary: The bill restructures aspects of Maryland's public health system by requiring the Maryland Department of Health to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps, establishing the Public Health Workforce Development Fund to support education and training, and altering the membership and leadership of the Commission on Public Health. It also grants county health officers increased autonomy regarding personnel and contracts, requires the Department of Legislative Services to develop a process for health equity impact assessments of legislation, and mandates a workgroup to improve local health department recruitment.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Local health departments, county health officers, public health workforce members, and volunteers in the Medical Reserve Corps.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the Public Health Workforce Development Fund, with special fund revenues and expenditures increasing accordingly. Minimal additional expenditures are expected in fiscal 2027 and 2028 to support the extended operation of the Commission on Public Health. General fund expenditures could potentially become significant if the Department of Legislative Services requires additional staff to implement health equity impact assessments for legislation. Local health departments may see a revenue increase if they receive support from the new workforce fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Commission on Public Health and the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board. The Governor also receives the annual report from the Commission on the implementation of its recommendations.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund, which is exempt from the requirement that interest earnings accrue to the General Fund.
The State Treasurer is responsible for holding the Public Health Workforce Development Fund separately and investing its money, ensuring interest earnings stay within the fund.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is added as a member of the Commission on Public Health. Additionally, the department must participate in a workgroup convened by MDH to review local health department recruitment and classification processes.
The bill requires the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps to be integrated into community emergency systems to facilitate coordinated volunteer management during public health emergencies and disasters.

MDH is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for organizing the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps, managing electronic health record procurements with local departments, staffing the Commission on Public Health under certain conditions, and overseeing the Public Health Workforce Development Fund through its Community Health Resources Commission.

The Secretary of Information Technology is added as a member of the Commission on Public Health. The bill also involves state procurement of electronic health records systems, which aligns with the department's role in statewide IT strategy and infrastructure.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board, which is situated within this department. The program provides service opportunities and completion awards, and the board will now include a local health officer.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions, including the changes to the Commission on Public Health and the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board specified in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes significant changes to the Commission on Public Health, including its membership, leadership selection, duties, and termination date. It also impacts the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board.

The HSCRC is authorized to transfer money from the Population Health Improvement Fund to the Public Health Workforce Development Fund, provided the transfer is consistent with the AHEAD Model State Agreement.
The Commission on Public Health must include a faculty member from a public health program at a historically Black college or university (HBCU), such as Morgan State University.

The Commission on Public Health membership includes representatives from State academic institutions with expertise in public health systems, which directly involves member institutions of the University System.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for providing notice to interested parties when a county or municipal corporation files a complaint for a judicial in rem foreclosure on certain vacant and abandoned property.
Title: Judicial In Rem Tax Foreclosure - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the requirements for providing notice to interested parties when a county or municipal corporation files a complaint for a judicial in rem foreclosure on vacant and abandoned property. It requires the local government to serve the complaint on each interested party in accordance with the Maryland Rules, replacing a previous requirement to send notice and a copy of the complaint by first-class and certified mail within five days of filing.
responsible_party: County or municipal corporations
stakeholders: Owners and mortgagees of vacant and abandoned property, and county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances. According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the legal requirements for providing notice and serving complaints in judicial in rem tax foreclosure actions filed in the state's circuit courts. As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is responsible for overseeing court operations and ensuring that procedures align with the Maryland Rules cited in the bill.

This bill specifically addresses tax foreclosures on vacant and abandoned property. The DHCD is the state agency responsible for community revitalization and ensuring access to safe, secure housing; these judicial tools are often used by local governments in partnership with DHCD initiatives to address blight and redevelop vacant lots.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the Judiciary and the General Assembly. They would be involved in interpreting the legal implications of shifting notice requirements to conform with the Maryland Rules and ensuring the statutory changes are correctly integrated into state law.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives related to local government authority and property law. The Governor is also responsible for signing the bill into law or exercising veto power over changes to the Tax - Property Article.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for screening for perinatal behavioral health conditions at certain times; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to identify certain screening tools and to assist certain health care providers with accessing resources and referral services related to screening for perinatal behavioral health conditions; etc.
Title: Health, Health Insurance, and Health Occupations - Perinatal Behavioral Health Conditions

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) to provide coverage for perinatal behavioral health screenings during a child's first year of life. It mandates that health care providers perform these screenings at specific well-child visits and provide educational information to pregnant and postpartum patients. The bill also requires carriers to provide standing referrals to behavioral health care providers for pregnant and postpartum members, establishes a $1,000 refundable State income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child, and directs health occupations boards to grant double continuing education credits for perinatal behavioral health training.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Insurance Administration, Maryland Health Care Commission, and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum individuals, parents of stillborn children, health care providers, and health insurance carriers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 due to the establishment of a $1,000 refundable income tax credit for parents of stillborn children. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in fiscal 2027 from $125 rate and form filing fees. The Maryland Department of Health, Medicaid, and the Maryland Health Care Commission can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency. It is responsible for identifying perinatal behavioral health screening tools, developing provider training programs, administering Medicaid coverage for these screenings, and disseminating information to local WIC agencies.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct an analysis and report on the impact of requiring coverage for perinatal behavioral health screenings and prohibiting certain cost-sharing practices.

The bill establishes a $1,000 refundable State income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child, which the Comptroller is responsible for administering and overseeing as the state's principal tax collector.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating health insurance carriers and ensuring they comply with the bill's requirements for mandatory screenings, coverage, and standing referrals to behavioral health providers.
The bill impacts the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which is managed by DBM. The agency reviewed the bill for potential fiscal impacts on the state plan.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the various state agencies and boards tasked with implementing the new health regulations and tax provisions.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies implementing this bill, and the bill requires a report to be submitted to legislative committees regarding health care impacts.

bill_summary: This bill allows U.S. Foreign Service members and their spouses who relocate to Maryland on official assignment to practice their profession using a valid occupational or professional license from another state. Eligible individuals are exempt from Maryland's standard licensing requirements for the duration of their assignment, provided they meet specific criteria such as remaining in good standing with their original licensing authority and complying with Maryland's standards of practice and continuing education.
responsible_party: Maryland State licensing authorities (including the Department of Agriculture, Department of Labor, State Department of Education, and Department of Health)
stakeholders: U.S. Foreign Service members and their spouses relocating to Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general and special fund expenditures will increase by an estimated $45,000 in FY 2027 for one-time software updates to licensing platforms ($30,000 for the Maryland State Department of Education and $15,000 for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners). Additionally, general and special fund revenues are expected to decrease indeterminately starting in FY 2027 because eligible individuals will be practicing under out-of-state licenses rather than paying Maryland licensing fees. Local government finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts certain business licenses (peddler, junk dealer, scrap metal processor, etc.) that are issued by the clerks of the circuit courts, which are supported and operationally managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The bill specifically modifies requirements for transient vendor licenses, which are administered by the State Comptroller.
The bill modifies licensing and certification requirements for several professions overseen by the Department of Agriculture, including veterinary medicine, pest control, and nutrient management.
As the central personnel agency, the department is indirectly affected by changes to professional licensing portability which impacts the state workforce and general employment regulations.

The bill significantly impacts teacher and school counselor certification processes, which are core responsibilities of the Maryland State Department of Education and the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board.
The bill affects a vast range of health professional boards under the Department of Health's jurisdiction, including nursing, pharmacy, dentistry, and medicine.
The Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing oversees many of the boards and commissions impacted by this bill, including public accountancy, architects, and barbers.
The bill modifies licensing requirements for professions regulated by the DNR, specifically taxidermists and tree experts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

bill_summary: This bill authorizes a pharmacist to order vaccinations for individuals who are at least three years old without requiring the pharmacist to also administer the vaccine. The authorization covers influenza, COVID-19, and public health emergency vaccines, as well as other FDA-approved or CDC-recommended vaccines for older age groups. Synopsis: Clarifying the Consumer Price Index used to determine the cost-of-living adjustments for retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System in certain years.

bill_summary: This emergency bill establishes a methodology for determining the Consumer Price Index (CPI) value for October 2025, which was not published by the federal government due to a shutdown. For the purposes of calculating retiree cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) effective July 1, 2026, and July 1, 2027, the bill mandates that the October 2025 CPI value be the average of the September 2025 and November 2025 CPI values.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Retirees of the Maryland State Retirement and Pension System and participating local government units.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates the bill likely has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates. Although the bill's methodology results in a slightly higher calculated COLA rate (0.067 percentage points) than one interpretation of current law, the impact is mitigated by statutory COLA caps and the fact that any change in liabilities is amortized over 10 to 15 years. No effect on revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary agency responsible for managing the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and calculating the cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) for retirees. This bill directly dictates the methodology they must use to address a missing CPI data point for their calculations.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for the state's long-term fiscal planning and the state budget, which includes funding for pension contribution rates. Any change in COLA calculations affects pension liabilities and the overall state budget.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer responsible for paying state bills and employees, including distributing pension benefits to retirees that will be adjusted based on the bill's methodology.

The State Treasurer manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees fiscal integrity. The SRPS is a significant component of the state's financial management and long-term liabilities.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures and protects the state's fiscal integrity. Pension liabilities are a major factor in the state's long-term financial health.

The Office of Legislative Audits conducts fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies, including the State Retirement Agency, and will be responsible for ensuring the COLA calculations comply with this new statutory methodology.
Maryland's public school teachers are members of the Teachers' Retirement and Pension Systems, one of the primary groups whose retirement benefits are adjusted by the COLAs addressed in this bill.
Members of the Maryland State Police are part of the State Police Retirement System, which receives COLAs that will be calculated using the method established by this bill.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Legacy Protection Program to help heirs who inherit a home become the legal title holders and prevent property tax sales. It creates the Legacy Protection Fund, financed by state and county contributions, to provide grants for legal assistance and probate fees. Additionally, the bill expands eligibility for the homeowners' and homestead property tax credits to include heirs who are not yet the record title holders for up to three years and allows the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to assist estates and personal representatives of deceased homeowners.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Heirs and legatees of deceased homeowners, particularly those who are low-income, elderly, or disabled; legal services organizations; and Maryland county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2028, the bill mandates an annual state general fund expenditure of $250,000 and a collective local government payment of $500,000 to the Legacy Protection Fund, resulting in $750,000 in annual special fund revenues and expenditures. Expanding eligibility for the homeowners' and homestead property tax credits is expected to cause an indeterminate, though likely limited, decrease in state and local property tax revenues starting in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the department implementing the program (SDAT). The Governor is responsible for proposing the annual budget, which must now include a $250,000 mandated appropriation for the Legacy Protection Fund.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Legacy Protection Fund and managing the accrual of interest on State money, which is specifically altered by this bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2028.

The Treasurer is responsible for holding, investing, and allocating net interest for the newly created Legacy Protection Fund, and manages the state's debt service which is impacted by the reduction in property tax revenues for the Annuity Bond Fund.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Tax Sale Ombudsman and SDAT, regarding the implementation of the new Legacy Protection Program and the processing of grants.

The bill directs the Ombudsman to establish grant eligibility criteria that prioritizes elderly heirs, which aligns with the Department of Aging's mission to protect the rights and quality of life for older adults.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for budget development. This bill creates a mandated appropriation and has a notable fiscal impact on general fund expenditures and revenue accounting.
The bill directs the Ombudsman to establish grant eligibility criteria that prioritizes disabled heirs, aligning with the department's role in improving services for residents with disabilities.

The bill's purpose is to prevent tax sales and allow heirs to remain in their homes, directly supporting the department's mission of ensuring access to secure housing and providing homeless solutions.
The Legacy Protection Program assists residents in economic need to prevent the loss of their homes, which is a core focus of the social services provided by DHS.
The bill establishes a new grant program for legal services organizations and individual heirs. The GGO assists state agencies in managing such funding and ensuring compliance.

The bill requires the creation of guides for probating estates, a process handled by the judicial branch. The AOC provides operational and legal support to the state's courts during these proceedings.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and contracts; the bill requires the Ombudsman to contract with a vendor for an installment payment program.
The bill addresses the Governor's priorities of reducing child poverty and enhancing economic mobility by protecting intergenerational wealth and family housing.
The Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for disputes regarding property tax assessments and credits, which are substantively altered by this bill for heirs.

The bill explicitly requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to collaborate with the Registers of Wills to develop step-by-step guides for heirs to navigate probate and become record title holders.
The bill addresses property tax challenges that impact rural homeowners and heirs, aligning with the Council's mission to foster economic development and improve quality of life in rural counties.

stakeholders: Business entities that have permanently ceased operations with outstanding State debt, the Comptroller's Office, and local jurisdictions receiving shared tax revenues.
fiscal_impact_summary: State tax revenues (general and special funds) are projected to increase by approximately $250,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. The bill requires settlement sums to be paid into the State Treasury. As the chief financial agency responsible for receiving and depositing state funds, the Treasurer's Office is directly involved in the fiscal workflow established by this legislation.

The HSCRC regulates hospital rates and revenues; the bill updates the statutory name of a hospital that is authorized to receive county appropriations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Public Service Commission to require a water company, sewage disposal company, or water and sewage disposal company to adopt a certain limited-income mechanism subject to the approval of the Commission; and requiring the Commission to study the feasibility of requiring certain companies to adopt a limited-income mechanism to benefit limited-income customers and to report its findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Water Companies, Sewage Disposal Companies, and Water and Sewage Disposal Companies - Limited-Income Mechanisms

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Water -see also- Coastal Bays; Riv,Str,Lks; Wastewater; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC) to study the feasibility of requiring water and sewage disposal companies to implement limited-income mechanisms to assist low-income customers. Effective July 1, 2027, the PSC is authorized to require these companies to adopt such mechanisms—including programs, credits, or special rates—to benefit customers with incomes at or below 175% of the federal poverty level, or 200% for customers aged 67 and older.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Privately owned water and sewage disposal companies, eligible limited-income residential customers, and other utility ratepayers including local governments and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented using the Public Service Commission's existing budgeted resources. There is no material effect on State expenditures or revenues. However, utility rates for non-limited-income customers (including residential, local government, and small business users) may increase as early as fiscal 2028 to fund the mechanisms if they are adopted by the companies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Public Service Commission (PSC) to study the feasibility of limited-income mechanisms for water and sewage companies, authorizes them to require these mechanisms, and expands their evaluation criteria for utility rates.

The Office of the People's Counsel is the statutory advocate for residential utility consumers, including those of private water and sewage services. This bill directly impacts utility rate structures and assistance mechanisms for the consumers they represent.

The bill explicitly requires the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is administered by the Department of Human Services, to certify eligible limited-income customers for participation in these utility mechanisms if required.
The bill specifies that eligible customers may also participate in assistance programs offered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and requires coordination of benefits.
The Public Service Commission is required to report its study findings on the feasibility of these limited-income mechanisms to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

Synopsis: Requiring certain apprenticeship programs utilized in certain State procurements to have at least a 25% completion rate, as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor.
Title: State Procurement - Apprenticeship Program Accountability and Completion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires apprenticeship programs used for State procurement contracts to maintain a completion rate of at least 25% once they have graduated at least one cohort. The requirement applies to 'covered procurements' valued at $1,000,000 or more, prevailing wage public works worth $250,000 or more, and other public works valued at $500,000 or more. The Maryland Department of Labor is responsible for verifying these completion rates, and contractors who do not utilize a qualifying program must pay into the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Contractors and subcontractors on State and local public work projects, registered apprenticeship program sponsors, and State procurement units.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State special fund revenues will increase beginning in FY 2027 as more contractors may pay into the State Apprenticeship Training Fund (SATF) as an alternative to using an apprenticeship program that meets the new criteria; however, a specific estimate is not feasible. Additionally, project costs for State and local governments may increase if the bill reduces the number of eligible bidders or offerors for specified contracts. The Maryland Department of Labor and other State agencies can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for calculating and verifying the 25% completion rate for apprenticeship programs, managing the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, and enforcing the bill's requirements.
DGS houses the Chief Procurement Officer, who is tasked with adopting regulations for 'covered procurements' and managing state construction projects impacted by these apprenticeship standards.
The Secretary of Information Technology must be consulted by the Chief Procurement Officer regarding 'covered procurements' related to IT contracts under Title 3.5.
MDOT oversees massive public works and infrastructure projects (highways, transit, etc.) that utilize state funds and are subject to the bill's apprenticeship completion requirements.
The Board approves significant state procurements and contracts, which will now be subject to these new accountability and completion standards for apprenticeship programs.
The Comptroller is explicitly tasked with accounting for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund and serves on the Board of Public Works which oversees affected contracts.
The State Treasurer is explicitly tasked with holding the State Apprenticeship Training Fund and serves on the Board of Public Works.
The Authority plans and manages large-scale construction projects using state capital funds, making their contracts subject to the new apprenticeship completion rate mandates.
The System and its member institutions frequently manage capital construction projects funded by the state budget that are subject to these apprenticeship standards.
The IAC oversees public school construction projects that use state funds and typically involve the use of apprentices in the building trades.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency overseeing state budget execution and procurement policies, which are altered by these apprenticeship requirements.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on procurement law and would be responsible for representing the state in enforcement or compliance litigation.
The bill's definition of 'public work' specifically includes infrastructure like waterworks and sewage disposal plants, which are regulated or overseen by MDE.
As a state agency with its own board, Morgan State manages capital projects subject to the bill's procurement and apprenticeship requirements.
As a public honors college, St. Mary's manages construction and procurement activities that are subject to these apprenticeship completion standards.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and procurement policy, and the Governor serves on the Board of Public Works which approves affected contracts.
The Commission is mentioned in the definition of 'public work' regarding structure or work performed by public service companies under their order.

Synopsis: Altering the matters on which the student member of the Howard County Board of Education may vote.
Title: Howard County Board of Education - Student Member - Voting Ho. Co. 7-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill expands the voting authority of the student member of the Howard County Board of Education. It allows the student member to vote on several previously restricted topics, including school attendance areas, property acquisition, school construction, donations, budgetary matters, and student discipline such as suspension and expulsion. The student member remains restricted from voting on matters involving the county superintendent's salary, staff appointments, and collective bargaining.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of Education
stakeholders: Student member of the Howard County Board of Education, Howard County public school students, and the Howard County Board of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact. The changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect Howard County school finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides oversight and leadership for Maryland's 24 local school systems, including the Howard County Board of Education. This bill directly alters the governance and voting procedures of a local board by expanding the voting rights of its student member on significant policy and budgetary matters.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel regarding the interpretation and sufficiency of the Education Article. This bill modifies statutory voting rights within that article, requiring legal oversight for consistency with state law.

The bill specifically expands the student member's voting authority to include matters relating to school construction and the acquisition and disposition of real property. The IAC is the primary state agency responsible for overseeing the planning, funding, and execution of such projects across local jurisdictions.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing state policy initiatives and signing local delegation bills into law, including those that modify the structure and authority of local boards of education.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that a certain individual designate a certain representative as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Howard County Economic Development Authority; altering the frequency of certain Board meetings from at least once each month to at least once every other month; and amending the title of certain staff for the Authority.
Title: Howard County - Economic Development Authority - Alterations Ho. Co. 14-26
bill_summary: This bill makes administrative alterations to the Howard County Economic Development Authority. It removes the requirement for a representative from the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council to serve as an ex officio member of the board, reduces the required frequency of board meetings from once a month to once every other month, and updates the title of the Executive Director to Chief Executive Officer.
responsible_party: Howard County Economic Development Authority
stakeholders: Board of Directors of the Howard County Economic Development Authority, Howard County government, and the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no State fiscal impact and does not materially affect Howard County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing local legislation passed by the General Assembly into law.
As the primary state agency for economic development, the Department of Commerce maintains collaborative relationships with local entities like the Howard County Economic Development Authority.

The bill removes a representative of the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council from the Authority's board; the Department of Labor oversees workforce development programs and policies related to such councils.

The board coordinates statewide workforce solutions and partnerships; changes to the representation of workforce-related council members on local economic development boards are relevant to their coordination mission.

Synopsis: Requiring, in the submission of the annual budget to the Howard County Council, the Howard County Executive to include the percentage of the county's general fund revenue, excluding one-time expenses, that is allocated to the operating budget of the Howard County Board of Education and operating costs associated with the Howard County school system; requiring that a copy of the budget be placed on the county board's public-facing website, in an easily identifiable location; etc.

bill_summary: The bill requires the Howard County Executive to calculate and report the percentage of the county's general fund revenue, excluding one-time expenses, that is allocated to the Howard County Board of Education and associated operating costs (such as pensions, benefits, and debt service) when submitting the annual budget. The Howard County Council must also include this percentage in the final approved budget.
responsible_party: Howard County Executive and Howard County Council
stakeholders: Howard County Board of Education, Howard County Public School System, and Howard County residents and taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no State effect. Howard County can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, and there is no impact on county revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires Howard County to send a copy of its approved budget, which must now include specific percentage calculations of general fund revenue allocated to education, to the State Superintendent. The State Superintendent heads the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the Department of Education and is responsible for the final approval and signing of the bill, which amends the Education Article of the Maryland Code.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the State Superintendent, who are designated recipients of the budget reports mandated by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a municipality that is seeking to annex land that is located in a different legislative district than a legislative district in which the municipality or any part of the municipality is located to notify the members of the General Assembly for the district in which the land is located and for the district to which the land is being annexed by electronic communication and the United States Postal Service.
Title: Municipalities - Annexation - Limitations

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires a municipality seeking to annex land located in a different legislative district than its own to provide written notice via electronic communication and the United States Postal Service to the General Assembly members representing both the district where the land is located and the district to which the land is being annexed.
responsible_party: Municipalities
stakeholders: Municipal governments, members of the Maryland General Assembly, and residents or property owners in areas proposed for annexation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances, as indicated in the Fiscal and Policy Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning is the state's primary agency for coordinating with local governments on land use and sustainable growth. Since municipal annexation is a core land use planning action and the department is listed as an information source for the fiscal note, the bill is relevant to their role in providing technical assistance and data analysis for local government boundaries.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and manages intergovernmental relations between the state and local jurisdictions. This bill modifies the procedural requirements for how local municipalities communicate with state legislators, which falls under the Governor's broader responsibility for state-local policy coordination and the signing of emergency legislation.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They may be required to provide legal interpretations of the Local Government Article or advise on the validity of municipal annexations if the newly mandated notification procedures are not followed.

Synopsis: Requiring instead of authorizing the Board of Architects to deny, reprimand, or suspend a license to practice architecture or a permit to operate a business through which an individual may practice architecture under certain circumstances; authorizing the Board to establish an electronic portal to allow the anonymous reporting of a suspected violation of certain provision of law relating to the practicing of architecture; requiring a code official to verify a licensee's credentials; etc.
Title: State Board of Architects - Grounds for Discipline and Anonymous Complaints

bill_summary: This bill mandates the State Board of Architects to take disciplinary action, including license denial, reprimand, or suspension, for fraudulent misrepresentation of credentials. It requires the Board to notify county code officials of license status changes and authorizes an optional electronic portal for anonymous violation reporting. Additionally, local code officials must verify an architect's seal and license credentials before processing building permits.
responsible_party: State Board of Architects
stakeholders: Architects, architectural firms, and county building code officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Architects can likely implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. Discretionary special fund expenditures may increase minimally for an optional electronic portal. Local code officials can perform the required credential verifications with existing resources. Revenues from penalties are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is a regulatory body housed within the Department of Labor. This agency is directly responsible for implementing the bill's requirements regarding professional licensing, disciplinary actions, and the potential creation of an anonymous reporting portal.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions. It would be responsible for advising the State Board of Architects on the implementation of mandatory disciplinary actions and representing the Board in legal matters.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. If the State Board of Architects denies, suspends, or revokes a license as mandated by this bill, affected individuals may appeal those decisions to the OAH for a hearing.

The bill requires that all penalties collected by the State Board of Architects be paid into the General Fund of the State. As the state's chief financial officer and revenue collector, the Comptroller oversees these funds.

DBM is responsible for state budget oversight. While the fiscal impact is expected to be minimal, the department would oversee any expenditures related to the optional development of an electronic portal for anonymous reporting.

Synopsis: Altering provisions relating to children who are placed in an out-of-home placement by a local department of social services under a voluntary placement agreement; requiring, by October 1, 2029, the Department of Human Services and the Maryland Department of Health to jointly submit a report to certain entities concerning children who are placed in an out-of-home placement under a voluntary placement agreement; and establishing that certain child support due to the State before the effective date of the Act is uncollectable.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the regulations for placing children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses in out-of-home care through voluntary placement agreements (VPAs). It prevents local departments of social services from requiring parents to give up legal custody to access treatment, establishes a 5-business-day deadline for assessment meetings and eligibility determinations, and requires trauma-informed training for state staff. Additionally, it makes any child support owed to the State under these agreements prior to the bill's effective date uncollectible and mandates annual data reporting on placement outcomes and hospital stay durations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses, their parents or legal guardians, and local departments of social services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $94,700 in FY 2027 for the Department of Human Services to hire a program manager, with annual costs reaching $127,700 by FY 2031. Montgomery County anticipates a local expenditure increase of approximately $162,000 annually for additional social workers and technology upgrades. State revenue from Child Support Foster Care Offsets will decrease due to the elimination of prior debts and new restrictions on seeking child support orders that might impede family reunification.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires juvenile courts to make specific findings regarding the best interests of a child for placements exceeding 180 days and involves court proceedings for the modification of existing child support obligations.

The fiscal note indicates a need for an additional program manager position at the Department of Human Services to ensure compliance and handle reporting, which impacts the state's personnel and budget oversight managed by DBM.

The bill specifically addresses the placement and treatment of children with developmental and mental disabilities, aligning with the department's mandate to coordinate and improve services for residents with disabilities.

MDH is a primary partner in the bill's implementation, required to consult on annual training for local staff, receive referrals for Medicaid-eligible children via local behavioral health authorities, and co-author a joint report on VPA outcomes.

DHS is the primary implementing agency, as its Social Services Administration and Child Support Administration are responsible for managing the voluntary placement program, reporting data, and filing motions for child support modifications.
The Governor's Office receives the required joint report from DHS and MDH concerning children in out-of-home placement and the status of voluntary placement agreement reforms.

The bill's focus on the well-being and placement outcomes of vulnerable children with disabilities aligns with the office's mission to coordinate support networks and improve outcomes for Maryland's children.

Synopsis: Authorizing an employee of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission who is suspended for disciplinary purposes to appeal to the Office of Administrative Hearings; and requiring the Office to dispose of a case or conduct a hearing and issue a final decision in an appeal under the Act.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes employees of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) who are suspended for disciplinary purposes to appeal that suspension to the Maryland Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH). It mandates that the OAH conduct hearings and issue final decisions on these suspension appeals, mirroring the existing process for WSSC employee removals.
responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission and the Office of Administrative Hearings
stakeholders: Employees of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of Administrative Hearings and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission both report that the bill can be implemented using existing resources. No state or local revenue impact is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) to hear and issue final decisions on appeals regarding disciplinary suspensions of Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) employees. The fiscal note indicates OAH will implement this new caseload within existing resources.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Office of Administrative Hearings and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (a bi-county state agency). It will be responsible for advising these entities on the implementation of the new disciplinary appeal procedures and representing them in related legal matters.

As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM oversees the State Personnel and Pensions Article, which this bill amends. Furthermore, the fiscal note mentions that OAH operates under authority delegated by DBM to conduct State Personnel Management System hearings, which is the framework used for these new WSSC appeals.

Synopsis: Repealing certain provisions of law authorizing a peer-to-peer car sharing program's motor vehicle liability insurance policy on a replacement vehicle to be secondary coverage for a shared vehicle driver; altering and establishing certain motor vehicle liability insurance requirements applicable to peer-to-peer car sharing programs; providing that the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is not required to provide coverage to a shared vehicle driver for the use of a shared vehicle that is not a replacement vehicle; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates the insurance and liability framework for peer-to-peer car sharing programs in Maryland. It modifies primary insurance requirements, allowing shared vehicle drivers to provide coverage, and clarifies that the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is not required to cover shared vehicles except in specific replacement cases. Additionally, the bill allows peer-to-peer car sharing programs to transfer liability for tolls and traffic citations to the shared vehicle driver and excludes these programs from being considered 'owners' for red light camera violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Peer-to-peer car sharing programs, shared vehicle owners, shared vehicle drivers, motor vehicle insurance companies, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in fiscal year 2027 due to rate and form filing fees. Enforcement and administrative tasks can be managed with existing resources. There is no projected local fiscal impact, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund's finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected. Specific dollar estimates for the revenue increase are not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of the state's insurance market, the MIA is responsible for overseeing the bill's significant changes to motor vehicle liability requirements for peer-to-peer car sharing programs, including the review and approval of new rate and form filings.

The bill explicitly modifies the statutory obligations of MAIF by providing that it is not required to provide coverage to a shared vehicle driver for the use of a shared vehicle that is not a replacement vehicle.

The bill amends several sections of the Transportation Article and affects multiple modal administrations (MVA, MDTA, MAA, SHA) regarding vehicle owner definitions, toll liability, and airport concession fees.

An agency within MDOT, the MVA is responsible for driver and vehicle services; the bill alters the definition of 'owner' for traffic control citations and regulates the operation of peer-to-peer car sharing programs.

The MDTA operates the state's toll facilities; the bill specifically authorizes peer-to-peer car sharing programs to transfer monetary liability for tolls, fees, and fines to the shared vehicle driver.
The bill addresses the recovery of concession fees paid to government-operated airports, which directly impacts the MAA's management of facilities like BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport.

The bill clarifies liability and the definition of 'owner' for citations issued via traffic control signal monitoring systems, which are adjudicated through the state's judicial system supported by the AOC.
The MSP is responsible for traffic safety and law enforcement; the bill's provisions regarding citations for traffic control signal monitoring systems relate to their enforcement context.
The SHA manages traffic signals on state-numbered highways; the bill's changes to the definition of 'owner' for red-light camera citations impact the administrative framework for these systems.

bill_summary: This bill increases the membership of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters from 7 to 11 and adjusts its quorum and removal rules. It extends the timeline for the board to establish licensing requirements and for interpreters to obtain licenses, moving the general deadline to January 1, 2028, and the educational deadline to July 1, 2028. The bill also mandates a report on specialist interpreter areas and sets conditions for licensing waivers for out-of-state applicants.
responsible_party: State Board of Sign Language Interpreters

fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues from license fees are delayed until FY 2028. There is no local fiscal impact.
