bill_summary: This bill extends collective bargaining rights to police officers employed by the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission (ATCC) who are authorized to make arrests, provided they are not supervisory, managerial, or confidential employees. The bill allows these officers to be represented by the State Law Enforcement Officers Labor Alliance (SLEOLA).
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: Police officers of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission (ATCC) and the State Law Enforcement Officers Labor Alliance (SLEOLA)
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are expected to be minimal and can be absorbed within the existing budget of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission. The bill affects approximately 30 police officers. Because these officers were previously treated as members of the State Law Enforcement Officers Labor Alliance (SLEOLA) until recently, the fiscal impact of re-integrating them into collective bargaining is expected to be negligible. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for administering collective bargaining for the public sector, PERB will oversee union representation elections, certify the exclusive representative for the ATCC police officers, and adjudicate any unfair labor practice charges.
DBM is the state's central personnel agency and is responsible for managing employee benefits, policies, and the fiscal impact of collective bargaining agreements on the state budget.

The fiscal note explicitly states that the Office of Administrative Hearings will be responsible for hearing and resolving any additional grievances that may arise from the expansion of collective bargaining rights to ATCC police officers.

The Governor is responsible for proposing the state budget, which must accommodate any negotiated costs from collective bargaining agreements, and must also ratify the Memoranda of Understanding resulting from the bargaining process.

The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission's police functions were originally transferred from the Comptroller's Field Enforcement Division, and the Comptroller retains a regulatory role in related industries.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of Human Services to study and report on how the federal One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 affects household eligibility for the Heat and Eat Program within the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The study must specifically analyze the number of households no longer eligible for the automatic standard utility allowance, the reduction in benefits experienced by these households, and the administrative costs and logistics associated with providing alternative assistance for eligibility verification.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Low-income households in Maryland receiving SNAP or Heat and Eat Program benefits, particularly those without elderly or disabled members who are impacted by changes to federal utility allowance eligibility.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Department of Human Services can complete the required study and report using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department is the primary agency tasked by the bill to conduct the study on the Heat and Eat Program, compile data on SNAP participants, evaluate administrative impacts, and report findings to the General Assembly.

The bill requires an evaluation of administrative costs and logistics for the Department of Human Services, which aligns with the Department of Budget and Management's role in supervising budget execution and personnel efficiency.

The study's focus on the reduction of SNAP benefits—a key program for addressing food insecurity and child poverty—directly pertains to the Office's goal of improving well-being for Maryland's families and children.

Synopsis: Providing that during the trial of a criminal case in which a defendant is charged with an assault in the second degree, a certain statement is not excluded by the hearsay rule if the statement is offered against a party that has engaged in, directed, or conspired to commit wrongdoing that was intended to and did procure the unavailability of the declarant of the statement, under certain circumstances.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Admission of Out-of-Court Statements - Assault in the Second Degree
bill_summary: This bill expands an exception to the hearsay rule in criminal trials to include cases where the defendant is charged with assault in the second degree. It allows for the admission of a declarant's out-of-court statement if the defendant engaged in, directed, or conspired to commit wrongdoing that was intended to and did procure the unavailability of the declarant.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Criminal defendants charged with second-degree assault, witnesses and declarants in criminal cases, State's Attorneys' offices, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. No specific dollar estimates were provided in the Fiscal Note as the impact is considered immaterial.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial process by expanding the hearsay rule exception for second-degree assault cases, requiring the courts to hold specific evidentiary hearings outside the presence of the jury as part of their operational duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency providing legal representation to indigent defendants, this expansion of admissible hearsay evidence directly affects their litigation of second-degree assault cases and their defense of constitutional rights in criminal proceedings.

The OAG represents the state in all criminal appeals; changes to evidentiary rules like hearsay exceptions for assault cases are highly relevant as they frequently form the basis of appellate litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and public safety policy; the addition of second-degree assault to the hearsay exception is a significant policy shift in the state's criminal justice system.
The Governor's Office oversaw the executive branch's involvement in the legislative process and the Governor signed the bill into law as the state's chief executive.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is responsible for the supervision of justice-involved individuals; changes to evidentiary rules that may facilitate convictions for assault can impact the population managed by correctional and parole facilities.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, troopers frequently investigate and testify in assault cases where these out-of-court statement rules will be applied during trial.

Assault in the second degree is a charge that frequently involves youth in the juvenile justice system, and evidentiary changes in criminal procedure often influence the standards used in juvenile court proceedings managed by this agency.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Highway Administration (SHA) and local jurisdictions to implement speed monitoring systems in 'safety corridors,' which are segments of highways identified as high-risk areas for vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and cyclists. It establishes a tiered civil penalty structure for speeding violations, requiring a 30-day warning period for newly installed systems. Revenue generated from these citations will be used to fund the program's administration, with remaining balances directed to the Transportation Trust Fund for highway safety and infrastructure preservation.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists, pedestrians, bicyclists, and local government jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State special fund revenues and expenditures, potentially by millions of dollars annually; the Fiscal Note provides an illustrative estimate of $26,800,000 in citation revenue based on specific deployment scenarios. Revenue will first cover SHA's administrative costs, with the remainder supporting highway safety and system preservation. Local governments that choose to implement their own safety corridor programs will also see increases in both revenues and expenditures. General fund revenues may increase slightly from contested cases in the District Court.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration is the primary implementing agency authorized by the bill to identify safety corridors, implement speed monitoring systems, and manage the resulting permit program for local jurisdictions.

The District Court has exclusive original jurisdiction over contested speed monitoring citations. The Chief Judge is also responsible for adopting procedures for citation issuance and penalty collection in consultation with SHA.
The MVA is responsible for refusing to register or suspending the registration of motor vehicles when owners fail to pay civil penalties or contest violations.

MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration and the Motor Vehicle Administration. The bill also directs citation revenue (after administrative costs) into the Transportation Trust Fund managed by MDOT.
The Comptroller is explicitly required to distribute revenue from civil fines collected through State-controlled safety corridor speed monitoring systems into a special fund.
The MDTA is identified as an agency that can operate speed monitoring systems and may receive civil penalty payments for violations recorded by its systems.
The bill prohibits insurers from considering these civil penalties when reclassifying an insured or increasing premiums, a regulation falling under the oversight of the MIA.
The bill's primary purpose is the protection of vulnerable road users, which the legislation explicitly defines to include individuals using wheelchairs and mobility devices.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is involved in the enforcement of motor vehicle laws and preservation of traffic safety on state highways impacted by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The bill requires the use of recorded images and data processing that must comply with state standards for automated enforcement systems, which are governed by DoIT’s IT and data security policies.

As an insurer of last resort for Maryland residents, MAIF is subject to the bill's provisions prohibiting the use of these specific speed citations for premium reclassification or insurance coverage decisions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the implementing agencies, including SHA and the Judiciary, and represents the State in legal matters involving traffic enforcement laws.

bill_summary: This bill implements the federal Workforce Pell Grant Program in Maryland, allowing students enrolled in eligible short-term vocational programs to receive Pell Grant funding. It establishes a process where the Governor, in consultation with the Governor’s Workforce Development Board, approves programs that meet specific criteria including instructional hours, completion rates, job placement rates, and alignment with high-demand industries. The bill also sets tuition caps for these programs and requires annual data reporting and compliance monitoring.
responsible_party: The Governor, Governor’s Workforce Development Board (GWDB), and Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC)
stakeholders: Institutions of postsecondary education (including public universities, community colleges, and private career schools) and students seeking short-term workforce training credentials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by 300000 in FY 2027 due to a contingent appropriation for administrative and staffing costs at GWDB and MHEC. MHEC is designated to adopt regulations, collect application fees, verify program compliance, and provide annual summaries to the General Assembly regarding the Workforce Pell Grant Program.

The department staffs the Governor's Workforce Development Board and oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council, which is explicitly referenced for the approval of registered apprenticeship programs mentioned in the bill.
The bill requires the Governor to revoke program approval if the Attorney General finds that an institution engaged in unfair, deceptive, or abusive trade practices related to the program.

As a primary provider of postsecondary education in Maryland, the system's institutions may seek approval for short-term programs, impacting their revenues and requiring them to comply with reporting and data collection requirements.
As an institution of postsecondary education, Morgan State may choose to offer short-term programs eligible for Pell Grants, making it subject to the bill's compliance and reporting mandates.
As an independent public honors college and postsecondary institution, it is eligible to offer approved short-term programs under the new regulatory framework established by the bill.

The fiscal note indicates a contingent appropriation of $300,000 for FY 2027 to implement the bill and notes ongoing staffing costs, which fall under DBM's oversight of the state budget and personnel.

Synopsis: Increasing the penalties for stalking to a period of imprisonment of up to 10 years or a fine of up to $10,000 or both if the victim had a protective order in effect against the defendant at the time of the offense or the defendant had previously been convicted of stalking.

bill_summary: This bill alters the penalties for the crime of stalking, elevating the offense from a misdemeanor to a felony under specific aggravating circumstances. These circumstances include if the offender was subject to a protective order or a court order prohibiting the conduct at the time of the offense, or if the offender has a prior stalking conviction in Maryland or another state. The felony conviction carries a maximum penalty of 10 years imprisonment and/or a $10,000 fine.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of stalking under aggravating circumstances, victims of stalking, the Maryland court system, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. State general fund expenditures may increase slightly due to longer incarceration periods associated with felony sentences. There may be a minimal shift in revenue: State general fund revenues from fines may decrease as cases move from District Court to circuit courts, while local revenues from circuit court fines may see a corresponding minimal increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the classification of certain stalking offenses from misdemeanors to felonies, which shifts jurisdiction from the District Court to the Circuit Court. The court system also issues the protective orders and court orders that serve as the triggers for the enhanced penalties under the bill.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is involved in the collection and management of state revenues. The bill's change in fines for stalking violations affects the general fund revenue collected from criminal convictions.

DBM oversees the state budget and fiscal planning. This bill is projected to increase general fund expenditures due to higher costs associated with longer incarceration periods for felony stalking convictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary implementing body for the bill's penal changes. It is responsible for the incarceration of individuals sentenced to prison and for the supervision of individuals placed on probation for stalking offenses.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget. The bill impacts state fiscal resources and requires executive oversight of the law enforcement and correctional agencies implementing the changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is Maryland's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy. It advises the Governor on the impact of criminal justice strategies such as the penalty enhancements proposed in this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender is responsible for representing indigent defendants. The reclassification of stalking as a felony significantly increases the legal stakes for their clients and may require more intensive legal resources for defense.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating stalking cases and enforcing the criminal law provisions that this bill modifies.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer and represents the state in criminal appeals. The creation of new felony penalties and enhanced sentencing criteria will require the OAG to handle potential appeals and provide legal guidance to state agencies on the new law.

stakeholders: Health insurance enrollees, primary care and behavioral health providers, health systems and hospitals, and health insurance carriers.

While the bill allows the Insurance Commissioner to impose a fine of $5,000 per day for carriers that fail to file required access plan updates, these penalties are not expected to have a material impact on State revenues. The bill establishes a new Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for individuals enrolled in the Individual Exchange who are patients of a provider that is terminated from a plan's provider panel. MHBE is responsible for administering these enrollment periods.

The bill adds requirements to the Health-General Article for health systems (hospitals and their affiliates) regarding contract terminations. It also specifically impacts notification requirements for behavioral health providers and applies to Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) which are overseen by the department.

As the agency responsible for managing state employee benefits and personnel policies, DBM is impacted because material changes to carrier provider networks may affect the administration and cost of health plans provided to state employees.

The Governor oversees the executive branch departments implementing this bill (MIA, MDH) and signs the legislation into law. The bill also impacts broader health policy initiatives managed by the executive branch.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense for violating the prohibition on unsolicited checks, which will be adjudicated within the state court system.

bill_summary: This bill mandates that the Governor include a $1,000,000 annual appropriation in the state budget for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund beginning in fiscal year 2027. This fund is utilized to subsidize the activities of the State-designated Patient Safety Center, which is responsible for developing and implementing statewide patient safety initiatives.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Maryland Patient Safety Center, health care providers, and patients and families in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2028 to reflect the mandated appropriation; special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund increase accordingly. While the bill applies the mandate starting in fiscal 2027, the fiscal note indicates the mandate formally begins in fiscal 2028 due to the bill's effective date of July 1, 2026, although $1,000,000 is already included in the fiscal 2027 budget as passed by the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include a $1.0 million appropriation in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund starting in fiscal 2027.
As the primary agency for state budget development, DBM is responsible for implementing and supervising the $1.0 million mandated appropriation required by the bill.

The Commission is the primary agency responsible for designating the Patient Safety Center, administering the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund, and reporting on safety initiatives to the General Assembly.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent regulatory agency within the Department of Health, and the bill's focus on patient safety directly supports the Department's public health mission.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund separately and invest the money of the Fund in accordance with state law.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund as part of its responsibilities as the state's chief financial officer.

Synopsis: Altering the ownership and control percentage requirement for a social equity applicant for a cannabis license; prohibiting cannabis advertising from directly targeting individuals under the age of 21 years; authorizing a standard dispensary to place exterior signage for a certain limited purposes; requiring the Maryland Cannabis Administration to accept certain advertising audience composition data and develop a process for accepting a certain attestation from a certain person regarding audience composition; etc.
Title: Cannabis - Advertising - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill reduces the ownership threshold for social equity cannabis license applicants from 65% to 55% and modifies regulations regarding cannabis advertising. It permits standard dispensaries to use specific exterior signage for identification and safety purposes, requires the Maryland Cannabis Administration to develop new processes for verifying audience age demographics for advertisements and event sponsorships, and creates exceptions for the non-commercial use of cannabis trademarks in editorial content such as news articles.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: Social equity cannabis license applicants, cannabis dispensary licensees, media entities, and individuals under the age of 21.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) estimates a need for $85,600 in fiscal 2027 to hire an administrator to oversee the new advertising and audience verification standards, though the Department of Legislative Services believes these requirements can likely be met with existing budgeted resources. There is no expected material impact on state revenues or local government finances. Small businesses in the cannabis industry may benefit from relaxed advertising and signage restrictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of the state's cannabis industry, the Maryland Cannabis Administration is the principal agency responsible for implementing this bill, adopting new advertising regulations, managing the altered social equity applicant criteria, and submitting required progress reports.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Maryland Cannabis Administration. The bill requires the Administration to submit an interim and final report on implementation progress to the Governor and the General Assembly.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for oversight of MCA's budget and resource allocation, particularly concerning the staffing needs discussed in the bill's fiscal note to manage new regulatory and data-review duties.

The bill defines a social equity applicant based on attendance at 4-year institutions of higher education in the State with high Pell Grant eligibility, which are institutions and policies coordinated by MHEC.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Cannabis Administration and would be involved in drafting the required regulations for advertising audience composition and enforcement procedures.

The OAH adjudicates administrative disputes for executive branch agencies; it would likely handle any contested cases or appeals arising from MCA's enforcement of the new advertising restrictions or licensing decisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is responsible for implementing socioeconomic procurement and business programs; the bill's alterations to social equity applicant criteria for cannabis licenses directly impact the state's broader economic equity and inclusion strategies.

The bill sets standards for cannabis advertising that makes therapeutic or medical claims and requires dispensary signage to include contact information for the Maryland Poison Center, which relates to public health safety and policy.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and tax collector; the Maryland Cannabis Administration is funded through distributions from adult-use cannabis sales and use tax collections managed by the Comptroller's office.

As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce is interested in the growth and regulation of the cannabis business sector and the expansion of advertising opportunities for standard dispensary licensees.

The bill's criteria for social equity applicants include individuals who attended public schools in disproportionately impacted areas, which are part of the public education system overseen and led by MSDE.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership in the University System of Maryland to provide a single nexus for certain stakeholders in artificial intelligence initiatives to advance artificial intelligence in the State; establishing the Artificial Intelligence Public Services Fellowship in the University System of Maryland; establishing, subject to a certain condition, the Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab in the University System of Maryland to assist State agencies for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership within the University System of Maryland to coordinate artificial intelligence initiatives, develop a strategic plan, and create regional Technology Extension Hubs to support small businesses. It additionally creates an Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab to help State agencies adopt AI responsibly, establishes an Artificial Intelligence Public Service Fellowship for students at public higher education institutions, and tasks Morgan State University’s Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems with coordinating research on the productive and ethical use of AI.
responsible_party: University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, students at public institutions of higher education, small business owners, and the Maryland workforce.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least 500,000 in FY 2027 to establish the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership and Technology Extension Hubs, satisfying a contingent appropriation in the State budget. Additional expenditures for the AI Incubation Lab and the AI Public Service Fellowship are anticipated and may be significant, but specific dollar estimates are currently indeterminate. Higher education revenues and expenditures increase accordingly based on State allocations and potential external funding. Local fiscal impacts on workforce development boards and community colleges are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership, the Artificial Intelligence Public Service Fellowship, and the Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab within the University System of Maryland, making it the primary implementing agency.

The bill designates the Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems at Morgan State University as a statewide resource and hub to support ethical AI use and conduct research requested by the Governor's AI Subcabinet.
The bill requires DoIT to provide policy guidance to the AI Incubation Lab and support the integration of the Lab's work into State agencies, while coordinating with its own existing AI programs.

DBM is tasked with entering into a memorandum of understanding for the AI Incubation Lab, consulting on the fellowship program, and approving the repurposing of funds by State agencies to support fellows.
The Maryland Department of Labor is a mandated partner in establishing Maryland Technology Extension Hubs and may collaborate with the Partnership on their strategic priorities.

The bill empowers the Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet to request research, provide consultation on implementation, and receive progress reports, directly involving the executive leadership structure.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet, falling under this category, is granted specific statutory duties to request research and oversee the development of the State's AI strategic plan and incubation lab.
As the regulatory board for higher education, the Commission oversees the institutions (USM and MSU) that are tasked with implementing the bill's primary programs and fellowships.
The bill focuses on AI as a driver for innovation and economic growth, including connecting small businesses to AI resources, which aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission.
TEDCO's mission to foster technology-based businesses is relevant to the bill's goal of establishing technology extension hubs and advancing AI innovation across the state's economy.
The bill identifies AI workforce readiness as a key priority and requires the Partnership to consult with workforce development boards to expand training and career pathways.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Transportation Authority to submit a certain report to certain committees of the General Assembly by September 1, 2026, on E-ZPass discount plans and unused commuter trips that contains certain data; requiring the Authority to provide recommendations for lowering the amount of unused commuter trips and mitigating consumer harm; requiring the Authority, under certain circumstances, to submit a certain corrective action plan or eliminate certain forfeitures; etc.
Title: Maryland E-ZPass Commuter Fairness and Transparency Act of 2026

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: The Maryland E–ZPass Commuter Fairness and Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) to submit a report to the General Assembly by September 1, 2026, regarding E-ZPass discount plans and unused commuter trips. The report must analyze data from 2023 to 2025 and provide recommendations to reduce the forfeiture of prepaid funds, such as extending usage windows or allowing trip rollovers. If more than 25% of discount plans have unused trips, the MDTA must also submit a corrective action plan to mitigate consumer harm.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
stakeholders: Maryland commuters, E-ZPass discount plan holders, low-income and underbanked motorists, and the Maryland Transportation Authority.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State expenditures for the Maryland Transportation Authority to complete the required report are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. No impact on State revenues or local government finances is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) as the primary agency responsible for analyzing E-ZPass data, submitting the required report, providing recommendations for lowering unused commuter trips, and implementing corrective action plans if necessary.

MDTA is a modal administration closely associated with MDOT. The bill affects the broader state transportation network operations, particularly how commuters use toll facilities versus other state-maintained highways and transit systems overseen by MDOT.

GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to enhance state government responsiveness and eliminate waste. The bill's requirement for a data-driven report on unused prepaid funds and a corrective action plan to mitigate consumer harm aligns with GOPI's mission.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. The bill requires reports to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee and the House Appropriations Committee regarding toll revenue forfeitures and prepaid commuter funds.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives. The bill addresses significant public policy concerns regarding equity, transparency, and consumer protection for Maryland residents and commuters.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies, including MDTA. They would likely be involved in reviewing the legal implications of 'forfeiture of unused commuter trips' and the consumer protection aspects mentioned in the bill's preamble.

The bill's preamble highlights inequitable barriers to compliance for unbanked and underbanked residents and the disproportionate financial burden on low-income motorists, which falls under the commission's focus on anti-discrimination and civil rights.
DHS assists residents in economic need. The bill addresses financial burdens and banking access issues that directly impact the vulnerable populations DHS serves.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive branch agencies. If MDTA fails to accurately report on the fiscal impact of unused commuter trips, OLA could be tasked with auditing these accounts.

MVA handles vehicle registration and is often involved in the enforcement of toll violations (e.g., registration holds for unpaid tolls). The bill's focus on commuter fairness and transparency in tolling systems interacts with MVA's customer service and enforcement functions.

E-ZPass is part of a multi-state interstate compact/network. Any changes to the discount structures or usage windows in Maryland may require coordination with interstate partners or impact interstate tolling agreements.

The Innovation Team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and address the needs of Maryland families. The bill's requirement for a 'corrective action plan' to reduce consumer harm for commuters fits this incubator mission.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain line-of-duty disability allowance to be paid to a member of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System or the State Police Retirement System who is found to be totally and permanently incapacitated, either mentally or physically, for the further performance of duty, and unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and State Police Retirement System - Line-of-Duty Catastrophic Injury Disability

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a catastrophic disability benefit for members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS). Eligible members who are totally and permanently incapacitated by a line-of-duty physical accident and unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity receive a benefit equal to 100% of their average final compensation plus an annuity. The bill includes provisions for annual income verification and benefit reduction if the retiree returns to gainful employment.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS)
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill likely has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates because the catastrophic disability benefit is expected to apply in only a very limited number of circumstances. The State Retirement Agency can implement the administrative requirements, such as processing applications and reporting to the Joint Committee on Pensions, with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the primary administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the State Police Retirement System (SPRS). It is responsible for processing disability applications, managing medical board certifications, verifying income through tax returns, and submitting annual reports on the new catastrophic disability benefit.

The bill directly impacts the retirement and disability benefits of Maryland State Police officers, as it amends the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) to include a 100% disability benefit for catastrophic injuries.
As the principal personnel agency for the state, DBM manages employee benefits and policies. It oversees the fiscal and personnel impacts of pension system changes on state government resources.

The department employs the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and thus eligible for the enhanced disability benefits provided by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency employs law enforcement personnel, such as those in the Division of Parole and Probation and internal investigative units, who are members of LEOPS and directly affected by changes to line-of-duty disability allowances.
MDOT oversees several administrations with law enforcement components, including the Maryland Transportation Authority Police, whose members are covered by the LEOPS retirement system.

The MDTA maintains its own police force, which is part of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). Its officers are directly impacted by the new catastrophic disability benefit provisions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Retirement Agency and the Maryland State Police. It would be involved in interpreting the legal standards for 'substantial gainful activity' and 'catastrophic injury' defined in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advises the Governor on public safety and criminal justice strategies. Enhancing disability benefits for law enforcement officers is a significant policy area for this agency.
The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the state's law enforcement agencies, and is responsible for the state budget which includes pension contributions affected by benefit changes.

The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and is a member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, which oversees the administration of these benefits.
The Treasurer is a key member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and is responsible for the management and distribution of state funds used for pension benefits.

The Board, composed of the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees significant state fiscal matters and integrity, overlapping with the leadership of the pension system impacted by this legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing that filing a certain complaint with the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights satisfies certain prerequisites to commencing a civil action alleging the violation of a county discrimination law.
Title: Human Relations - Violations of County Discrimination Laws - Complaints

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: This bill establishes that filing a discrimination complaint with the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) satisfies the administrative exhaustion requirements or prerequisites necessary to file a civil action alleging a violation of a county or local discrimination law.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
stakeholders: Individuals filing discrimination complaints, employers, and local human relations commissions in Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The fiscal note indicates no significant revenue or expenditure changes for the State or local jurisdictions, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state agency responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination laws, the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is directly impacted because the bill establishes that filing a complaint with the Commission satisfies the exhaustion of remedies required for civil actions under county discrimination laws.

The bill establishes procedural rules for commencing civil actions in the state's circuit courts for violations of county discrimination laws, specifically regarding the timing and prerequisites (exhaustion of remedies) for such lawsuits.

The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) is responsible for adjudicating contested cases for the Commission on Civil Rights. Changes to the procedural requirements for discrimination complaints can affect the administrative process and the subsequent path to litigation.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for the State and its agencies, including the Commission on Civil Rights. They provide counsel on the implementation of these procedural changes and represent the state's interests in related litigation.

Synopsis: Authorizing, for purposes of determining the Maryland estate tax, a qualified recipient to transfer ownership of qualified agricultural property to a limited liability company; providing that qualified agricultural property transferred in accordance with the Act is not subject to estate tax recapture if the ownership of the company consists only of qualified recipients and the property is used for farming purposes for at least 10 years after the decedent's death; etc.
Title: Maryland Estate Tax – Qualified Agricultural Property – Transfer to Limited Liability Company

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Farmers and Farming -see also- Agriculture; Farmland

bill_summary: This bill allows a 'qualified recipient' of agricultural property to transfer legal ownership of that property to a limited liability company (LLC) without triggering Maryland estate tax recapture, provided the LLC is owned exclusively by qualified recipients and the property is used for farming for at least 10 years following the decedent's death.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Qualified recipients of agricultural property, farming families, and family-owned agricultural limited liability companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease starting in fiscal 2028 due to potentially increased utilization of estate tax exclusions for qualified agricultural property. The exact financial impact is indeterminate. There is no local fiscal impact. The Comptroller's Office can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and is explicitly mandated by the bill to adopt regulations to implement the new provisions regarding the transfer of qualified agricultural property to LLCs for estate tax purposes.

The Register of Wills is responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes. Changes to estate tax recapture rules and property transfer qualifications directly impact the administration of decedents' estates under their jurisdiction.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court would adjudicate cases where a qualified recipient and the state disagree on the applicability of estate tax recapture or the validity of an LLC transfer.

The bill focuses on qualified agricultural property and farming purposes. The MDA provides expertise on the economic viability of farming and was consulted as an information source for the fiscal note regarding these specific land-use definitions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Comptroller's Office and would likely assist in drafting the required regulations and defending the state's position in complex estate tax litigation arising from the new LLC transfer rules.

DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and monitoring the general fund. The bill is noted to potentially decrease general fund revenues through increased utilization of estate tax benefits for agricultural property.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the state budget; the bill impacts state revenue and requires the Governor's final approval for enactment into law.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "virtual currency kiosk operator" to include a person who installs or operates certain software that enables a certain device to provide certain virtual currency services; altering the definition of "virtual currency services" to exclude the accepting or dispensing of cash in connection with a credit, deposit, or convenience account; and clarifying that a virtual currency kiosk operator shall ensure the kiosk does not offer the same services as an automated teller machine.
Title: Financial Institutions and Activities - Virtual Currency Kiosks - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands the regulatory definition of a virtual currency kiosk operator to include individuals who install or operate software enabling virtual currency services on stand-alone devices. It distinguishes these kiosks from traditional automated teller machines (ATMs) by excluding standard banking transactions from the definition of virtual currency services and prohibiting kiosks from offering the same services as ATMs.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation, Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Virtual currency kiosk operators, software installers and operators for currency kiosks, consumers using virtual currency services, and small businesses operating kiosks.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no local fiscal impact. Small businesses operating virtual currency kiosks may incur potential meaningful expenses related to ensuring software installers and operators comply with existing registration requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor, specifically through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, is the primary agency responsible for the registration and regulation of virtual currency kiosks and their operators in Maryland. This bill directly expands the regulatory scope and definitions that the department must enforce.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, and would be involved in the enforcement of the registration requirements and legal interpretations of the new definitions.

The Office of Administrative Hearings is responsible for adjudicating contested cases and appeals resulting from regulatory or licensing decisions made by state agencies, including disputes involving the registration of virtual currency kiosk operators.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the fiscal operations and personnel of executive agencies like the Department of Labor. While the fiscal note indicates the impact is not material, DBM monitors the resources required for implementing these regulatory changes.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Labor. The Governor also appoints the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, who is tasked with identifying and regulating virtual currency services.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Commerce to develop and maintain a searchable online database, to be known as the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, to connect businesses in the State with local sources for supplies and inventory; and requiring the Department to report on or before December 31 each year on the use and effectiveness of the portal.
Title: Economic Development - Local Sourcing Database

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Commerce to develop and maintain the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, a searchable online database designed to connect Maryland businesses with local suppliers for inventory and tariff-impacted goods. Participation by local sources is voluntary, and the Department must coordinate with other state agencies to identify potential participants and report annually to the General Assembly on the portal's effectiveness.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Maryland businesses looking for local supplies, local business entities headquartered or with a principal place of business in Maryland, and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $142,900 in FY 2027 for system development costs ($75,000) and the hiring of one contractual data analyst. Ongoing operating and personnel expenditures are estimated to be between $91,800 and $102,100 annually through FY 2031. The bill has no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency tasked with developing, maintaining, and reporting on the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, Commerce is the lead implementing authority responsible for identifying tariff-impacted goods and managing the database.

The bill explicitly authorizes Commerce to coordinate with DoIT to leverage existing digital infrastructure and requires the portal to comply with specific state digital accessibility and data security standards.
The Comptroller is explicitly named as a coordinating partner that Commerce may work with to identify potential local business sources for the portal's database.

DBM is responsible for overseeing the fiscal impact of the bill, including the allocation of general funds and the creation of a new contractual data analyst position within the Department of Commerce.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The portal's objective to connect Maryland businesses with local suppliers directly aligns with this office's mission to facilitate economic opportunities and growth for small, minority, and women-owned businesses.

The OAG will likely provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act standards and the 'held harmless' liability provisions established for the state and its employees.
The Governor's Office provides executive oversight for the Department of Commerce and general policy direction for state-level economic development initiatives.

Synopsis: Approving certain projects for the acquisition, development, and improvement of certain academic facilities for the University System of Maryland; authorizing the issuance of bonds by the University System of Maryland in a certain total principal amount for financing the projects; and providing that the bonds are not a debt or obligation of the State or any of its subdivisions.
Title: University System of Maryland - Academic Facilities Bonding Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: The bill authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue up to $50 million in academic facilities bonds to fund specific acquisition, development, and improvement projects at Towson University, the University of Maryland, College Park, and the Rita Colwell Center, as well as systemwide capital renewal projects.
responsible_party: University System of Maryland
stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions, including students, faculty, and staff at Towson University and the University of Maryland, College Park.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State revenues and expenditures from bond proceeds increase by $50,000,000 in fiscal 2027. Higher education expenditures are projected to increase by approximately $4,200,000 annually starting in fiscal 2028 to pay debt service on the revenue bonds. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental request from the University System of Maryland and directly authorizes them to issue $50 million in academic facilities bonds for specific projects at their constituent institutions.
DBM is responsible for the state's budget development and supervision, including the Capital Improvement Program (CIP). The fiscal note indicates these bond proceeds are included in the FY 2027 CIP.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget and Capital Improvement Program, which include the projects authorized by this bill.

The Treasurer manages the issuance of State bonds and provides financial oversight; although these are USM revenue bonds and not a general debt of the State, the Treasurer's Office monitors the state's overall debt capacity and financial integrity.
As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees significant state expenditures and the fiscal impact of debt issuance.
The Board of Public Works must approve significant State expenditures and capital projects, which may include the facilities and contracts funded by these bonds.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the University System of Maryland, regarding the legality and form of bond issuances and associated contracts.

As the state's coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission establishes statewide policies and ensures institutions meet financial standards, which relates to the long-term capital planning of academic facilities.

Synopsis: Requiring a federal firearms licensee or law enforcement agency  operating a gun buyback program to destroy each firearm and all its component parts that are traded in as part of a gun buyback program; authorizing a licensee or agency to contract with a law enforcement agency or a business to destroy certain firearms; requiring a law enforcement agency operating a program to determine if a firearm is a crime firearm or has been reported lost or stolen before destroying the weapon; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Gun Buyback Programs - Destruction of Firearms

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Dealers -see also- Motor Vehicle Dealers and Salespeople
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: This bill requires federal firearms licensees and law enforcement agencies that operate gun buyback programs to destroy all surrendered firearms, including all attached components and parts, to ensure they are permanently inoperable. Before destruction, law enforcement must make reasonable efforts to determine if the firearm was stolen or used in a crime. The bill establishes a fine of up to $10,000 for violations and requires the Secretary of State Police to revoke the dealer's license of any licensee who violates these provisions.
responsible_party: Secretary of State Police, law enforcement agencies, and federal firearms licensees
stakeholders: Federal firearms licensees (dealers), law enforcement agencies, and individuals surrendering firearms through buyback programs
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Although the bill establishes a misdemeanor fine of up to $10,000 for violations, no specific dollar estimates for total revenue or expenditures are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police, led by the Secretary of State Police, is the primary agency responsible for regulating firearms dealers. This bill explicitly requires the Secretary to revoke dealer licenses for violations of the new gun buyback regulations and defines the standards for firearms destruction that law enforcement agencies must follow.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this agency is relevant because gun buyback programs are specific public safety initiatives aimed at reducing crime and juvenile delinquency, which falls under their policy development and interagency collaboration mandate.

The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense and fines of up to $10,000 for improper operation of a gun buyback program. The judicial branch will be responsible for adjudicating these cases and managing related court records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of a new criminal misdemeanor for the unauthorized operation of gun buyback programs may require the Office of the Public Defender to represent indigent defendants charged under these provisions.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the Maryland State Police. They would likely be involved in advising on the implementation of the new licensing regulations and representing the state in any legal challenges regarding license revocations.

Synopsis: Repealing a certain provision of law exempting all persons that acquire or are assigned certain mortgages, mortgage loans, or installment loans under certain circumstances from certain provisions of law governing the licensing of providers of certain financial services in the State.
Title: Financial Institutions - Consumer Credit - Application of Licensing Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill repeals a specific exemption from consumer credit licensing requirements for entities that acquire or are assigned mortgages, mortgage loans, or installment loans if they do not otherwise engage in those lending businesses. It is intended as a clarifying corrective measure to repeal a provision erroneously enacted in 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Entities acquiring or assigned mortgages or installment loans; consumer credit lenders; Maryland Department of Labor
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no fiscal impact on local governments or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, is responsible for the licensing and regulation of financial institutions, including consumer credit providers and mortgage lenders. This bill directly repeals a licensing exemption within their regulatory jurisdiction.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the Department of Labor and its regulatory boards. Additionally, the OAG enforces state consumer protection laws which are applicable to the consumer credit and mortgage lending activities affected by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring hospitals in the State to adopt a policy describing the protocol of the hospital when there is an immigration enforcement action at the hospital; and requiring hospitals to make the immigration enforcement action policy available to all staff members and provide annual training to ensure the staff's knowledge and understanding of the policy.
Title: Hospitals - Immigration Enforcement Action - Policy Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires hospitals in Maryland to adopt and implement policies regarding how they will respond to immigration enforcement actions on their premises. These policies must align with guidance from the Attorney General, be made available to all hospital staff, and be supported by annual staff training. The bill also tasks the Health Services Cost Review Commission with developing and publishing a model policy in consultation with the Attorney General and the Maryland Hospital Association.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Hospital staff and administrators, patients, guests, and the Maryland Hospital Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect state or local governmental operations or finances. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the bill relates to administrative policy requirements and training for hospital staff, which do not carry a direct state expenditure or revenue change according to the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) to develop a model policy for hospitals regarding immigration enforcement actions and to publish this policy on its website by October 1, 2026.

The HSCRC must consult with the Attorney General to develop the model policy. Additionally, the bill requires hospital policies to be consistent with guidance already issued by the Attorney General under existing state law.

The HSCRC is an independent agency within the Maryland Department of Health. Furthermore, MDH regulates the hospitals that are required to adopt these policies and was a primary information source for the fiscal note.
The bill includes a technical amendment to the section of law that governs the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, which the MHCC oversees in conjunction with the HSCRC.
As the executive department overseeing state agencies and policy coordination, the Governor's Office is relevant to the implementation of new hospital protocols and the signing of the bill into law.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual who enrolls for coverage or enrolls a dependent for coverage during a certain special enrollment period for pregnancy to choose a certain date option on which the coverage will become effective; and requiring the carrier, if the individual fails to select the effective date, to select a certain date option.
Title: Health Insurance - Special Enrollment Period for Pregnancy - Coverage Effective Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: This bill allows individuals who enroll for health insurance or enroll a dependent during a special enrollment period for pregnancy to choose the effective date of their coverage. The individual may choose to have coverage begin on either the first day of the month in which pregnancy was confirmed or the first day of the month following the selection of the plan. If the individual does not select an option, the insurance carrier is required to select one of these two dates.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Pregnant individuals and their dependents, health insurance carriers, the Maryland Insurance Administration, and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in FY 2027 due to $125 rate and form filing fees. Operational impacts on the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange are expected to be handled within existing budgeted resources. There is no fiscal impact on local governments or the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory body for health insurance in the state. This bill requires carriers to modify their enrollment processes and effective dates for pregnancy-related special enrollment periods, which will require the MIA to review and approve updated rate and form filings.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) administers the Maryland Health Connection, the state's individual insurance marketplace. Since the bill mandates changes to special enrollment periods both inside and outside the Individual Exchange, MHBE must implement system and operational changes to allow enrollees to select their preferred coverage start dates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange. They would be responsible for ensuring that the implementation of the new enrollment rules complies with state and federal insurance laws.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees public health policy and the Maryland Health Care Commission. While MIA and MHBE are the primary implementers, MDH has a general interest in policies that expand or clarify access to maternal health coverage and healthcare practitioner confirmation processes.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain service agreements for residential property entered into before June 1, 2023, if the service provider is not considered in good standing with the State Department of Assessment and Taxation on or after June 1, 2026.
Title: Residential Property - Service Agreement - Defunct Service Providers
bill_summary: This bill voids residential property service agreements made before June 1, 2023, if the service provider is defunct or not in good standing with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation on or after June 1, 2026. It limits the duration of such agreements to two years and prohibits them from creating property liens or binding subsequent owners. Additionally, it allows property owners to sue in circuit court to have such agreements declared void and to seek compensatory damages and legal fees.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Residential property owners and service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. While it creates a cause of action for individuals to seek damages and attorney's fees in circuit court, these private legal actions do not represent a significant fiscal impact on the State or local budgets.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a specific cause of action in Maryland's Circuit Courts, allowing individuals to seek a judicial determination that a service agreement is void and unenforceable. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides the operational and legal support necessary for the judicial branch to handle these new proceedings.

The bill regulates service providers who contract for the maintenance, purchase, or sale of residential property. Many of these providers, such as real estate brokers and home service professionals, are licensed and regulated by the Maryland Department of Labor.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides counsel on the interpretation of the Real Property Article. Furthermore, these types of residential service agreements are often linked to the Consumer Protection Act, which the OAG enforces.

This agency is responsible for ensuring residents have access to secure housing and for managing community revitalization. The bill's provisions regarding the voiding of liens and encumbrances on residential properties directly impact homeownership security and property title integrity.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for providing notice to interested parties when a county or municipal corporation files a complaint for a judicial in rem foreclosure on certain vacant and abandoned property.
Title: Judicial In Rem Tax Foreclosure - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the notice requirements for counties and municipalities when filing for a judicial in rem tax foreclosure on vacant and abandoned properties. It requires that the complaint be served on each interested party in accordance with the Maryland Rules, replacing the specific requirement to mail notices within five days of filing.
responsible_party: Maryland counties, municipal corporations, and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Owners of vacant and abandoned property, mortgagees, lienholders, and local government jurisdictions in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State finances and is not expected to have a material impact on local government finances. Specific expenditure or revenue figures were not provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the procedural notice and service requirements for in rem tax foreclosure complaints filed in the state's Circuit Courts, mandating that service be performed in accordance with the Maryland Rules instead of previous statutory mailing requirements.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to the Judiciary and state agencies regarding the implementation of and compliance with Maryland Rules and statutory service requirements.

This bill relates to tax foreclosure procedures for vacant and abandoned properties, which are critical tools for the community revitalization and housing stabilization efforts overseen by the department.

As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller's office may be an 'interested party' in foreclosure actions if state tax liens are attached to the property; the bill changes how the agency would receive service of the complaint.

The department promotes sustainable growth and provides land use data and technical assistance to local governments; changes in the foreclosure process for vacant lots impact local land management and revitalization planning.

Synopsis: Correcting certain errors or omissions in certain articles of the Annotated Code and the Public Local Laws of Maryland; clarifying language; correcting certain obsolete references; reorganizing certain sections of the Annotated Code; providing that the Act is not intended to affect any law other than to correct technical errors; and providing for the correction of certain errors and obsolete provisions by the publishers of the Annotated Code.
Title: Annual Corrective Bill

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
