bill_summary: The bill corrects technical errors, omissions, and obsolete references in the Annotated Code of Maryland and the Public Local Laws of Maryland. It reorganizes certain sections and clarifies language without making substantive changes to the law.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents, legal professionals, and state and local government agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as it is purely technical in nature and does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes numerous technical corrections and updates to the Education Article, affecting education funding, teacher induction programs, school safety funds, and special education services.

The bill corrects multiple sections within the Health - General and Health Occupations articles, including language regarding the AHEAD Model State Agreement, firearm violence reduction programs, and physician assistant regulations.
The bill contains extensive technical updates to the Transportation Article, affecting modal administrations, zero-emission bus procurement, and emergency vehicle regulations.
The bill includes drafter's notes clarifying the role and definition of the Secretary of Budget and Management regarding capital project planning and performance incentive programs.
The bill clarifies the approval authority of the Secretary of General Services concerning the design and implementation of state capital projects.
The bill explicitly adds definitions for the Secretary and Department of Disabilities to the Human Services Article to clarify the administration of assistive technology and self-advocacy programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects the agency's name in multiple sections of the Annotated Code following its renaming from the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services.
The bill updates sections regarding nonvisual access standards for information technology and the reporting of cybersecurity incidents.
The bill corrects technical errors in the Labor and Employment and Business Occupations articles, including provisions related to unemployment insurance and professional licensing.
The bill updates the Land Use Article to change the term 'visions' to 'planning principles' in alignment with recent legislative changes.
The bill makes technical corrections to the Environment Article regarding groundwater permits, the Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund, and packaging inspections.
The bill updates cross-references within the Tax - General Article that the Comptroller is responsible for enforcing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects language in the Correctional Services Article and updates retirement provisions for correctional officers.
The bill reorganizes definitions related to sustainable communities and the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet within the Housing and Community Development Article.
The bill makes technical corrections to the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding juvenile detention and traffic citation penalties.
The bill updates technical provisions in the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding investment managers and retiree reemployment.
The bill corrects technical errors in the Public Utilities Article regarding community choice aggregators and hazardous liquid pipelines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects the terminology regarding Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation goals in state procurement contracts.
The bill clarifies the use of the Safe Schools Fund for grants and training, which is administered by this center.
The bill identifies the State Police as a coordinating partner in multidepartmental firearm violence reduction efforts.
The bill specifies the Treasurer's role in investing money within the Safe Schools Fund.
The bill repeals an obsolete cross-reference to the Insurance Article within the Health - General Article affecting health maintenance organizations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates language regarding the distribution of proceeds from online sports wagering.
The bill makes multiple corrections to the State Government Article and defines the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet located within the Executive Department.
The bill clarifies that certain guidance and policies are not subject to standard administrative procedures, affecting the OAG's advisory role.
The bill updates the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children, which impacts the families served by this department.
The bill corrects federal law references regarding National Guard members on active duty orders within the Education Article.
As a modal administration of MDOT, it is impacted by technical corrections to road safety and work zone speed control provisions.
As a modal administration of MDOT, it is impacted by corrections to vehicle registration and driver education accounts.
As a modal administration of MDOT, it is impacted by corrections regarding zero-emission bus procurement and reporting.
The bill updates definitions related to transportation facilities projects managed by the MDTA.
The bill makes technical corrections to nonresident tuition exemptions at public institutions of higher education.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2027, and altering the membership and duties of the Workgroup.
Title: Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance – Extension and Alteration of Membership and Duties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: This bill extends the term of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance to June 30, 2027, and expands its membership and specific duties. The workgroup is required to develop concrete, data-driven legislative recommendations to reduce automobile insurance premiums and address rating factors that may cause geographic or racial disparities, with an updated report due to the Governor and General Assembly by January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, private passenger automobile insurance companies, insurance producers, and consumer advocacy organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is expected to handle the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources. There may be a minimal increase in special fund expenditures if the MIA needs to expand its contract with an actuary for additional data-driven analyses. The bill has no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary agency responsible for establishing, chairing, and supporting the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance. The bill expands the workgroup's duties to include specific legislative recommendations regarding rating factors and extends its operational life until 2027.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) is a statutory member of the workgroup. As the state's insurer of last resort, MAIF is directly impacted by findings and legislative recommendations concerning the affordability of automobile insurance, particularly in majority-minority and lower-income communities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly alters the membership, legislative duties, and termination date of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance, which is a state-authorized body tasked with conducting special studies and providing policy recommendations.

The workgroup is required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor. Additionally, the Governor oversees the executive branch, including the primary implementing agency (MIA), and the workgroup serves to inform the Governor's policy initiatives regarding insurance affordability.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program in the Department of Commerce to provide customized, no-cost workforce training as a business attraction tool, to recruit strategic industries and qualified business entities to the State; requiring the Department to partner with not more than two community colleges in the State to deliver training services; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program within the Department of Commerce. The program is designed to attract new businesses and strategic industries to the state by providing them with customized, no-cost workforce training. The Department of Commerce will partner with up to two community colleges to deliver these training services and must report on the program's effectiveness by the end of 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Business entities located outside of Maryland that are in active negotiations to relocate to the state, Maryland community colleges, and individuals receiving workforce training through the program.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by 1,000,000 in FY 2027 and FY 2028, reflecting a contingent appropriation in the FY 2027 budget and assumed discretionary funding thereafter. These funds will support one contractual position at the Department of Commerce and provide training grants to partner community colleges. Minimal expenditures of 42,600 are expected in FY 2029 for final administrative duties. Local community colleges selected as partners will see an increase in revenues and expenditures to develop and deliver the training curriculum.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Commerce as the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and reporting on the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program. Commerce must manage the budget, negotiate with business entities, and partner with community colleges.

The bill creates a workforce training program as an economic development tool. As the chief policy-making body for the state's workforce system, the GWDB is relevant to the strategic alignment of this pilot with state workforce goals.

The fiscal note identifies a need for $1.0 million in general fund expenditures and the creation of a new contractual finance specialist position, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget and personnel management.

The program requires the Department of Commerce to partner with community colleges to deliver training. As the regulatory and coordinating board for higher education, MHEC is relevant to the integration of these programs into the community college system.

The Department of Labor oversees workforce development and adult learning programs. This pilot program provides similar workforce training services, creating a direct overlap or coordination point with Labor's mission.

The bill requires the Department of Commerce to submit a report on the program's effectiveness to the Governor by 2028. The Governor's Office also oversees executive policy initiatives like the state's economic strategic plan mentioned in the bill.

The Department of Commerce must enter into formal agreements with qualified business entities, including performance metrics and reimbursement provisions. OAG provides the necessary legal counsel to draft and enforce these state contracts.

As an agency responsible for conducting fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive branch programs, OLA will eventually be responsible for auditing the financial management and performance outcomes of this pilot program.

The Comptroller, as the state's chief financial officer, is responsible for the collection of revenues and payment of state bills, including the $1.0 million in general fund expenditures allocated for this program.

The Treasurer's Office manages and protects state funds. This includes the disbursement of the $1.0 million in general funds and the handling of any reimbursements from businesses that fail to meet performance metrics.
The team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility. This workforce pilot is directly related to providing pathways for economic opportunity through job training.

The pilot program requires tracking performance metrics such as jobs created and salaries. MLDS links and analyzes student and workforce data, which may be relevant for evaluating the long-term outcomes of the trainees.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones in the 41st legislative district of Baltimore City under the pilot program authorized for Prince George's County, the 45th and 46th legislative districts of Baltimore City, and the City of Takoma Park if authorized by local law.
Title: Baltimore City - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - 41st Legislative District

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Authorizes the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones in the 41st Legislative District of Baltimore City for a three-year pilot program. Fifty percent of the fines collected must be distributed to the Baltimore City local management board to provide youth programming and services for those living in or attending school in the 41st Legislative District.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Motorists in Baltimore City, students and youth in the 41st Legislative District, and the Baltimore City local management board.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5,938 in FY 2027 for one-time programming costs for the Judiciary. State general fund revenues increase minimally from contested citations. Local revenues and expenditures for Baltimore City increase as systems are implemented, with 50% of revenue from $40 civil penalties mandated for specific youth services in the 41st district.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Highway Administration to authorize the use of stop sign monitoring systems on State highways within the pilot program's districts and mandates that the agency place prominent notification signs on those highways.

The Judiciary is responsible for processing citations that are contested in the District Court. The fiscal note indicates a direct cost of approximately $5,900 for one-time system programming to implement the pilot program for the new legislative district.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, MDOT oversees the modal administrations involved in highway safety and automated enforcement policy, and the agency is mentioned in the fiscal note as being involved in the bill's analysis.

The bill directs 50% of the fine revenue collected from the pilot program to the local management board for Baltimore City to be used for youth programming. The Governor's Office for Children coordinates with these local boards and oversees statewide efforts for youth services.

The bill stipulates that if the program's revenue exceeds 10% of the local jurisdiction's total annual revenues, the excess funds must be remitted to the Comptroller, who serves as the state's chief financial officer.
The bill requires a report on the pilot program's costs, performance, and effectiveness to be submitted to the Governor by December 1, 2027, and the Governor signed the bill into law.

The pilot program is specifically limited to school zones. This agency is responsible for a comprehensive approach to school safety and may utilize the data regarding the effectiveness of these monitoring systems in reducing crashes and injuries near schools.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is included in the definition of agencies authorized to issue citations for violations recorded by stop sign monitoring systems, particularly on State highways.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Highway Administration and the Judiciary regarding the implementation and enforcement of the new automated traffic monitoring pilot program.
DBM oversees the state's budget execution, which is impacted by the Judiciary's programming expenditures and potential increases in general fund revenues resulting from contested citations.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide reimbursement for applied behavior analysis services provided by behavior technicians to Program recipients with autism spectrum disorder under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; prohibiting, subject to a certain exception, the Department from requiring as a condition of reimbursement that an individual receive a certain certification to provide applied behavior analysis services as a behavior technician to Program recipients; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Behavior Technicians - Reimbursement
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 867

NarrowSubjects.Name: Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide reimbursement for applied behavior analysis (ABA) services provided by behavior technicians to Medicaid recipients with autism spectrum disorder. The bill prohibits the Department from requiring certification as a condition of reimbursement for the first 150 days an individual provides these services, though it may require technicians to obtain and maintain certification after that period.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Medicaid recipients with autism spectrum disorder, behavior technicians, and health care providers delivering applied behavior analysis services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) can likely conduct administrative oversight of behavior technicians using existing budgeted resources. Any increase in Medicaid expenditures (funded 50% by state general funds and 50% by federal funds) is expected to be minimal and absorbable. The bill is not expected to materially affect revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide reimbursement for behavior technician services under the Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), adopt regulations, and monitor federal compliance.

This agency is responsible for coordinating services for Maryland residents with disabilities; individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), the specific target population for the bill's services, fall under this mandate.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the state budget and Medicaid expenditures. Changes to reimbursement rules for behavior technicians have potential long-term fiscal impacts on the state budget.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the Department of Health and would be involved in interpreting the bill's requirements and ensuring compliance with federal laws to prevent abrogation.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and the implementation of state programs; the bill also requires the Governor's approval for final enactment.
This office focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children; because many recipients of ABA services for Autism Spectrum Disorder are children, this bill aligns with their core policy focus.
The Comptroller acts as the state's principal tax collector and pays state bills; the agency is responsible for the actual disbursement of funds for Medicaid reimbursements.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to support the growth of companies that specialize in regenerative medicine and other advanced manufacturing by providing certain grants; authorizing grant proceeds to be used only for acquisitions, renovations or construction of certain space, infrastructure improvements, and purchase of equipment; etc.
Title: Maryland Technology Development Corporation - Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to provide grants to companies specializing in regenerative medicine and other advanced manufacturing for the acquisition, renovation, or construction of facilities, infrastructure improvements, and equipment.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
stakeholders: Companies specializing in regenerative medicine and other advanced manufacturing, and small businesses providing related equipment and services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5,000,000 annually starting in FY 2027 to capitalize the program. In FY 2027, general fund expenditures increase by approximately $800,000 for administrative costs. Beginning in FY 2028, $5,000,000 in pay-as-you-go general fund expenditures are required annually to capitalize the special fund, a portion of which will then cover ongoing administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and managing the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program and its associated special fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund separately and to invest the money in the fund.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the new special fund and manages the accrual of interest earnings as part of the state's financial oversight.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel. The bill necessitates significant annual general fund and PAYGO appropriations (approximately $5 million) and the addition of new personnel at TEDCO to manage the program.
According to the fiscal note, a significant portion of the initial funding for this program ($3 million) is appropriated through the Department of General Services budget for transfer to TEDCO.

The Governor's Office proposes the annual state budget, which must account for the multi-million dollar capitalization of the new grant program, and oversees the executive department responsible for these policy initiatives.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the program's goal of supporting the growth of companies in advanced manufacturing and regenerative medicine aligns with Commerce's mission, even though TEDCO is the lead implementer.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires TEDCO to consult with the Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission (an independent commission within TEDCO) regarding criteria and regulations for grants involving regenerative medicine.

It man dates that promoters o r participatin g license holders obtain this permit to publicize or host events with 75 or more anticipate d attendees, set s specific application fees and permit cost s base d on venue capacity, and establish e s fine s for noncompliance.

fiscal_impact_summary: The State experienc e s no fiscal impact. Baltimore City will see a minimal revenue increas e from FY 2027 to FY 2028 through application fee s of $50 and permit fee s rangin g from $500 to $1,500 depen din g on venue capacity. Local administrativ e and enforcemen t cost s are expecte d to be manage d usin g existin g resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller's summary explicitly states that the agency is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state revenues. This bill creates a new alcohol permit and involves the regulation of state caterer's licenses, making it directly relevant to the Comptroller's oversight duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission with enforcing certain provisions and imposing fines. This collective entity includes various commissions authorized by the General Assembly to address specific government issues, such as the commission mentioned in the bill.

The bill is specifically designed to facilitate the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave in Baltimore City. The Office of Tourism Development is responsible for promoting Maryland as a premier travel destination and driving the tourism economy, which is directly impacted by the regulation of events related to major conventions.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel to all state agencies and commissions. They would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the new permit requirements and representing the state in any legal disputes or enforcement actions related to these alcohol regulations.

As the parent agency of the Office of Tourism Development, the Department of Commerce oversees efforts to enhance Maryland's competitive position and stimulate the economy. The successful hosting of a major national fraternity conclave is an economic development priority.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The Governor is responsible for signing the legislation and oversees the agencies and commissions tasked with enforcing the bill's provisions.

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to allow the chair of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities to recall former members as temporary substitutes or request the Governor to appoint temporary members or extend existing terms in cases of recusal, disqualification, or term expiration. The bill also withdraws and repeals previous similar legislation from the 2025 session.
responsible_party: Commission on Judicial Disabilities and the Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland State judges, attorneys admitted to practice in Maryland, public members of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities, and Maryland voters.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no material impact on State or local finances. If the constitutional amendment is approved by voters in the 2026 general election, the Commission on Judicial Disabilities may experience operational efficiencies. There is no impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the Governor's constitutional authority by allowing the Governor to appoint temporary substitute members to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities or to extend the terms of existing members upon request from the Commission chair.

The Commission on Judicial Disabilities investigates complaints against judges and recommends disciplinary action to the Supreme Court of Maryland. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides central support to the Judicial Branch and would be impacted by procedural changes in judicial oversight and discipline.

The bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be submitted to the voters of the state for adoption or rejection during the November 2026 general election, which is administered by this agency.

This office assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of candidates for state boards and commissions. It would be involved in managing the process for the new temporary and extended appointments created by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Judicial Disabilities is a permanent body within the scope of this collective entity, and the bill directly modifies its membership rules, vacancy procedures, and term limits.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and state agencies regarding the implementation of constitutional amendments and legal matters related to the regulation of judges and state officials.

As the custodian of official records, the Secretary of State manages the registration of laws, executive orders, and commissions, and plays a role in the administrative processing of constitutional amendments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from requiring or requesting from a prospective tenant certain information relating to criminal history and prohibiting a landlord from considering certain information when evaluating the prospective tenant; permitting a landlord to consider certain criminal history information prior to extending a conditional offer to a prospective tenant; and requiring the landlord to consider certain information provided by a prospective tenant relating to a criminal history records check; etc.
Title: Landlord and Tenant - Residential Leases - Prospective Tenant Criminal History Records Check (Maryland Fair Chance Housing Act)

bill_summary: The Maryland Fair Chance Housing Act prohibits landlords owning or managing five or more residential units from inquiring about a prospective tenant's criminal history before making a conditional lease offer, except for specific serious offenses such as murder or sex crimes. After a conditional offer is made, landlords may consider certain felony convictions from the previous five years but must conduct an individualized assessment and allow tenants to provide evidence of rehabilitation or dispute inaccuracies. The bill also bans advertisements that categorically exclude tenants based on criminal history and establishes a civil penalty for violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs)
stakeholders: Landlords managing five or more residential units and prospective tenants, particularly those with criminal histories.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State or local government finances or operations. It establishes a civil penalty of up to $500 per violation, and the Department of Housing and Community Development is required to adopt regulations and develop model notices using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department's Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs develop and publish a model notice document and adopt regulations to carry out the Fair Chance Housing Act.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like DHCD for regulation development and enforces consumer protection laws; the bill involves housing disclosures and potential complaints under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
The bill addresses discriminatory practices in residential leasing based on criminal history, which aligns with the Commission's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws in housing.
The bill establishes civil penalties of up to $500 for violations and creates a new framework for legal claims regarding residential leases, which would be adjudicated within the state court system.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees DHCD and is responsible for signing the bill into law and ensuring the execution of state housing policy.
DBM is responsible for the fiscal oversight and personnel management related to the implementation of new regulations and agency duties by DHCD.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses for the odd side of the 1000 block of West Baltimore Street and the even side of the 800 block of North Charles Street in the 40th alcoholic beverages district, subject to certain limitations; and prohibiting certain license holders in a certain area of the 40th alcoholic beverages district from selling alcoholic beverages before 10 a.m. or after 10 p.m.
Title: Baltimore City - 40th Alcoholic Beverages District - Authorizations and Revisions
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses for specific restaurant locations in the 40th alcoholic beverages district, subject to memorandums of understanding with local community associations and waivers of minimum seating requirements. It also adjusts the conditions for a Class C license in Eutaw Place and modifies the geographic boundaries that define restricted hours of sale for alcoholic beverages in the district.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurant owners and alcoholic beverage license applicants in Baltimore City's 40th district, the Hollins Roundhouse Association, the Mount Vernon-Belvedere Association, the Bolton Hill Community Association, and residents of the affected neighborhoods.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates there is no State fiscal impact. The impact on Baltimore City finances and operations is considered not material, as the issuance of a small number of new licenses (with annual fees of approximately $2,060 for Class B and $860 for Class C) does not represent a significant change in revenue or administrative expenditure.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal financial officer and regulator of the alcoholic beverages industry, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the enforcement of tax laws and regulations related to the sale of alcohol under the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article amended by this bill.

The bill redefines geographic boundaries and restricts the hours of sale for alcoholic beverages establishments in the neighborhoods surrounding the Pimlico Race Course, an area specifically within the Authority's mandate for community revitalization and public safety oversight.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies regarding the implementation and interpretation of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill implements public safety measures by restricting the hours of sale for alcoholic beverages in specific areas of Baltimore City, aligning with this office's mission to develop policies that reduce crime and enhance public safety.
The bill references services regulated under the Business Occupations and Professions Article, specifically barbering services, which are licensed and overseen by the Maryland Department of Labor.

The bill authorizes new Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses for restaurants, which directly impacts the economic development and small business growth objectives of the Department of Commerce in Baltimore City.

The Maryland State Police provides support to local law enforcement and ensures compliance with state regulatory and criminal laws, including those pertaining to the regulated sale of alcoholic beverages.
The Governor's Office is responsible for the final signing of the legislation and oversees the administrative support for the executive branch in enforcing the state's laws.

Synopsis: Altering the annual salary of the Sheriff of Howard County and altering the annual salary of the State's Attorney of Howard County.
Title: Howard County - Sheriff and State's Attorney - Compensation Ho. Co. 13-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill establishes a new salary schedule for the Howard County Sheriff and the Howard County State’s Attorney, setting specific annual salaries for calendar years 2027 through 2029 and a final rate for 2030 and subsequent years. The changes take effect at the beginning of the next terms of office.
responsible_party: Howard County Government
stakeholders: The Howard County Sheriff and the Howard County State's Attorney
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. According to the fiscal note, Howard County expenditures increase by approximately $48,000 in FY 2027, $96,000 in FY 2028, and at least $104,000 annually thereafter to cover the mandated salary increases. These expenditures do not account for fringe benefits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for the final review and signing of legislation passed by the Maryland General Assembly; the Governor signed this bill into law on May 12, 2026.

The Sheriff and State's Attorney of Howard County are state constitutional officers and typically members of the State Retirement and Pension System. Changes to their annual salaries directly impact the calculation of pension contributions and future retirement benefits managed by this agency.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state officials and reviews legislation for constitutional compliance. This bill involves Article III, Section 35 of the Maryland Constitution regarding salary adjustments for public officers during their terms, a matter requiring OAG legal oversight.

The bill references the salary of a District Court Judge as the baseline for the State's Attorney's compensation for calendar year 2026. The AOC monitors judicial pay scales, and the bill's subsequent decoupling of this local salary from judicial pay is relevant to state judicial compensation records.

bill_summary: This bill modifies various prior authorizations of State debt issued between 2017 and 2025. The changes include extending deadlines for expending or encumbering funds, changing grantee names, altering the authorized purposes of specific grants, and removing certain matching fund requirements for projects throughout Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Local governments, non-profit organizations, educational institutions, and community groups that are recipients of State capital grant funding.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill modifies the conditions under which State grant funds may be used but does not materially affect State finances. While the bill alters specific grant amounts and reallocates funds (for example, increasing a grant for McDaniel College from $22,246 to $2,977,754 and reassigning others), these changes occur within existing State debt authorizations or bond capacity and do not require additional total state debt.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget, including the capital budget. This bill amends prior authorizations of state debt and grants, which are core executive functions.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing state contracts and expenditures, including the certification of matching funds and approval of state debt disbursements modified by this bill.

The Treasurer manages the issuance of State bonds and the protection of state funds. As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer must approve the capital expenditures and debt modifications authorized in this bill.
The bill alters grants for senior centers, such as the Harford Road Senior Center, which falls under the department's mission to improve the quality of life for older adults.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for developing and supervising the state's budget. It was consulted in the fiscal note and oversees the long-term fiscal planning related to these capital grants.

The bill modifies grants for several arts and cultural institutions (e.g., Everyman Theatre, Chesapeake Arts Center, Imagination Stage), which are supported by the Department of Commerce to enhance the state's economic and cultural competitive position.
The bill impacts funding and project scopes for public school facilities, such as Catonsville Middle School and Woodlawn High School, which are overseen by MSDE.

DGS is the primary operational support agency for the planning, design, and construction of state-funded facilities. It is a primary source of information for capital budget modifications and provides technical oversight for state-funded construction projects.
The bill alters grants for healthcare facilities, including the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center, Harford Crisis Center, and Holy Cross Hospital.

The bill modifies grants for community revitalization and infrastructure, such as the Choice Neighborhood Initiative and Park Heights Community Investment, which are often administered or supported by DHCD.
The bill alters grants for local parks and collections (e.g., Calvert Marine Museum, Long Branch Local Park), which relate to DNR's mission to enhance natural resources and recreational public lands.
The bill impacts historic sites (e.g., Historic Gibson Grove) and community revitalization master plans (e.g., Park Heights), which fall under the technical and policy guidance of MDP.
The bill alters grants for transportation infrastructure, including the North Bethesda Metro Station, hiker-biker trails, and bus acquisitions, which are within MDOT's multi-modal scope.

The bill modifies a grant for McDaniel College, a private institution, through the Maryland Independent College and University Association, which falls under MHEC's statewide policy and coordination role.
The BPW is the highest administrative body overseeing state expenditures and must approve the significant state procurements, bond issuances, and contract modifications described in this bill.
The IAC oversees the planning and funding of public school construction projects; several school-specific grant alterations in the bill fall under its domain.

The bill specifically references the Park Heights Master Plan and investments made in consultation with governing bodies associated with the Pimlico Redevelopment Community Compact, which is the focus of this Authority.
